author: joshspeagle
body:
## Summary

This pull request adds `CLAUDE.md`, the instructions that Claude follows in this repository. It also adds templates for pull requests, task issues and phase tracking issues.

Closes #2

## Background

Claude does most of the overhaul work, often without a person who watches each step. `CLAUDE.md` sets the standards for that work: the plan and its approval points, the GitHub and Git process, the pull request steps, and the rules for code, numerics, tests, documentation, measurements, agents and writing. Claude Code reads this file at the start of every session.

The text is adapted from the instructions of the AlphaUniverse project (`hanbangwu/alphauniverse`) and changed for a numerical library. Before you read the decisions, note one fact: Claude works through the lead's GitHub account. Its text is identified by the footer line `_Generated by Claude Code_`, and a person approves by a comment.

## Decisions

The lead made decisions 1 to 8. Claude made decisions 9 to 15. Each decision had an adversarial review: an independent subagent tried to refute it. Two review rounds ran, one before and one after the `/simplify` and `/code-review` passes. No decision is a behaviour change.

| # | Decision | Alternatives | Adversarial review |
| - | -------- | ------------ | ------------------ |
| 1 | Pull requests go into `main`. Claude merges each one when CI passes, no review thread is unresolved, each request has an answer, and each required approval is given. | An integration branch `dev`; the lead merges every pull request. | Revised: the merge conditions are now complete, and local commands replace CI until CI exists. |
| 2 | Claude is the commit author. | The lead as author. | Revised: the rule was missing from the text. |
| 3 | Only the public API has docstrings, in NumPy style. Comments explain only a non-obvious reason. | No docstrings, as in AlphaUniverse. | Revised: methods are included, a module gets one line, and the equation is required only if there is one. |
| 4 | The lead approves only two things: the merge of the Phase 1 (design) pull request, and any tag, release or package upload. | A stop at the end of every phase. | Revised: Phase 1 is named, and the lead can approve on the pull request or on the tracking issue. |
| 5 | A behaviour change does not wait for the lead. It gets three reviewers, a test that shows the old and the new result, and a line in `CHANGELOG.md`. | Each behaviour change waits for the lead. | Revised twice: the definition now covers masks, errors and defaults, any loosened tolerance, and a tolerance looser than 1e-10 against the 2022 outputs. |
| 6 | Merge commits. Before a pull request is ready, Claude folds each fix into the commit that it corrects. | Squash merges. | Revised: the fold uses `--keep-base` and `--force-with-lease --force-if-includes`, and only on branches with no human commits. |
| 7 | Text on GitHub follows rules adapted from ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. | The spartan style of the session replies. | Revised: the rules now also cover comments, decision logs and checkpoint reports. |
| 8 | CI runs only fast tests. Long tests are marked `slow` and run locally, or in CI when started by hand. | All tests in CI. | Revised: tests against the 2022 outputs or against a direct solve are never `slow`, and each CI test step takes under 2 minutes. |
| 9 | All rules are in `CLAUDE.md`. There is no `.claude/rules/` directory. | Path-scoped rule files. | The first design, path-scoped files, was refuted: its paths matched no file, so the rules would not load. The replacement was upheld. |
| 10 | One adversarial reviewer for each decision. A behaviour change gets three reviewers and stands only if at least two uphold it. | Three reviewers for each decision. | Revised: "decision" is defined, the reviewer's brief is specified, and a split vote leads to a revision or a drop. |
| 11 | Branch names are `<issue>-<slug>`, with a lowercase slug joined by hyphens. | `feat/...` prefixes. | Upheld. |
| 12 | Each default label has one stated use. An item that will not be done closes as "not planned" or "duplicate", with a label and a comment. | Labels without stated uses. | Revised: the close reason was added. |
| 13 | A pull request that the lead or a collaborator reviewed or committed to waits for that person's approval. Requests from other accounts get an answer, not action. | No exception for human reviewers. | Revised: a review from any account would have blocked merges, and any account could have given Claude instructions. |
| 14 | The commands and rules for golden tests come with the pull request for #3. | Add them now. | Upheld. |
| 15 | Pull requests have Summary, Background, Decisions, Testing and Checklist. Task issues have Summary, Background and "Done when". Phase issues also have a decision log. | Longer templates with "Changes", "Issues" and "Checkpoint" sections. | Revised: the repeated sections were removed, and phases now have a "Done when" list. |

Two review findings were not adopted:

- A pointer to the specification. The lead decided to keep planning material out of the repository. Step 4 now gives the reviewer "the requirements the change must meet".
- Model names in the rule for agents. No model name is allowed in the repository, so the rule uses "the session's own model".

## Testing

No tests apply: this pull request changes only instructions and templates, and no CI exists yet. Claude checked the text for em dashes, and checked the fold procedure against git 2.43.

<details>
<summary>Findings of /simplify and /code-review high</summary>

`/simplify` ran four reviewers (reuse, simplification, efficiency and altitude).

- Fixed: duplicate rules, the scattered approval gates, the definition of a behaviour change, a fragile reference to step numbers, and the layout table.
- Not adopted:
  - Running `/simplify` before the adversarial review. The lead set this order.
  - Two reviewers instead of three for a behaviour change. A third reviewer can find an objection that the first two missed.
  - Skipping the review passes for small pull requests. The lead wants rigor first.

`/code-review high` reported 10 problems. All 10 are fixed:

- The autosquash form did not work on git 2.43.
- Folding conflicted with the rule against rebasing a human's branch, and the force-push was not described.
- The 1e-10 trigger would have caught every fast-path test at condition number 1e8.
- A rule described CI as if it existed.
- The approval rules contradicted each other, and they assumed that the lead can approve their own pull request.
- Input validation had lost its protection from the leanness rules.
- The rule "never choose silently" was lost.
- The checklist required `docs/`, which does not exist.

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Each decision has the result of its adversarial review.
- [x] `/simplify` and `/code-review high` ran, and each finding is fixed or answered.
- [x] Before ready, each fix was folded into the commit it corrects, or the branch has a human's commits. Every commit passes the commands under Commands (none exist yet).
- [x] The `slow` tests of the changed modules pass locally, or there are none.
- [x] `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` and any docs are current. This change is not user-visible, so `CHANGELOG.md` is not created yet.

author: sunag
body:
Fixes https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/issues/35033

**Description**

Node materials that only differ in `envMap` share the same shader, but `EnvironmentNode` took the PMREM texture from whichever material was built first. Every other material reflected that environment, and assigning a new `envMap` had no effect.

`EnvironmentNode` now reads the current environment texture before rendering and passes it to the PMREM node when it changes. For `material.envMap` it is read per object, and for texture nodes like `scene.environment` it is read per render. `PMREMNode` itself is unchanged.

author: neilp9
body:
Brings `main` up to date with the dataset and eval work since `a8a22a8`.

## What's in it
- **Configurable eval judge**: several judges per run, cross-family judging, and `ajaanai rejudge` to re-score saved transcripts.
- **Shaped reply mode** (`DATASET_REPLY_MODE=shaped`): the synth model writes each reply in his voice from the passage, instead of picking his sentences by number.
- **Provider-neutral LLM helpers** (`src/ajaanai/llm.py`): synth, check, eval caller and judge run on Claude or any OpenAI-compatible API as equal backends, including both providers' batch APIs. Every model setting names its provider, e.g. `SYNTH_MODEL=openai:gpt-5-mini`.
- **Labelled datasets**: results live in `data/datasets/<mode>_<provider>-<model>/`. Each build gets a label such as `verbatim_anthropic-claude-sonnet-5-5_20261014`, which is recorded in its `card.json` and in the `run.json` of every model trained on it. `ajaanai train --dataset <label>` picks a build.
- **`SYNTH_EFFORT`**: reasoning effort for the synth model. gpt-6.x models are treated as reasoning models.
- Earlier commits not yet on GitHub: the responsiveness check, whole-conversation eval, `max_steps` for fine-tuning, and batch logging.

## Breaking changes
- Model settings without a provider prefix (`SYNTH_MODEL=claude-sonnet-5-5`) fail at startup. Use `anthropic:<model>` or `openai:<model>`.
- `JUDGE_BASE_URL` / `JUDGE_API_KEY` are replaced by `OPENAI_BASE_URL` / `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
- Datasets moved from `data/dataset*` to `data/datasets/`. Existing local data and the Modal volume have already been migrated.
- After merging, run `ajaanai secrets-sync` and `ajaanai deploy` so Modal uses the new settings and records dataset labels.

## Testing
- 91 unit tests pass.
- Live sample builds worked with `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5` and `openai:gpt-5-mini`.
- Live batch runs worked on both providers, and resuming them was a no-op.
- 2,000 of 2,000 stored synth hashes still match, so the existing 32k results are reused.

author: tehutahu
body:
Related issue #31

## Behavior
While moving an existing clip, its nearest start/end edge snaps to the live playhead within 8 CSS pixels. Ties prefer the start edge. Alt temporarily bypasses playhead snapping; overlap avoidance and the zero boundary remain in effect. Playback continues, stationary modifier/zoom changes update the preview, and release commits the last rendered position.

Stable timeline pointer capture survives track changes. A cancelled or unchanged drag adds no history. Trim, asset drop and other move APIs keep their existing behavior.

## Placement constraints
Only the UI move helper repairs invalid legacy overlap results with a bounded, monotonic walk across sorted blockers. Valid legacy results stay unchanged. Snapped candidates must be nonoverlapping; the global resolver and move API are unchanged.

## Validation
Added 16 unit cases and a production real-pointer browser suite to required CI. New browser suite passed 20 checks covering start/end, stationary Alt/zoom, CSS-pixel thresholds, playback, cancellation, cross-track capture, exact preview/commit, Undo/Redo, save/load and a decoded export with matching payload/source parts. Lint, type check and production build passed locally (Node 24.19.0, Playwright 1.57 / Chromium 154). Full real-ffmpeg Vitest suite passed: 31 files / 231 tests. The complete browser suite passed: 23 history + 20 persistence + 20 snapping checks (63 total), five real exports, no runtime errors. Independent code review of exact head `e03a41c779f9a45fb6c48120d744c945ee714206` approved with no blocking or material findings.

Independent execution verification of the exact head passed lint/type checking, all 231 tests, 63 browser checks/five exports, plus 11 independent boundary checks and another real decoded export (no runtime errors). Additional checks covered drop/trim remaining unsnapped, blur cancellation with Redo preserved, 3px/zero no-ops, obstructed snapping and preview/commit/Undo/Redo agreement, and save at 4s → move to 7s → load back to 4s → export retaining source parts. Four evidence images were visually reviewed. Local verification used Node 24.19 / Playwright 1.57 / system Chromium 154; required GitHub CI used Node 22.14 and the lockfile-installed Playwright/official Chromium. [Final-head CI run 38839227061](https://github.com/tehutahu/movie_editor/actions/runs/38839227061) passed for exact head `e03a41c779f9a45fb6c48120d744c945ee714206`, including official Chromium installation, lint, real ffmpeg tests, build, type checking, all browser regressions, audit and evidence upload. Independent review, independent execution and final-head CI are complete and successful.

## Integration
Merged with exact head matching using merge commit `369b39d6c8dbb8cd6b3734ff4a15528524228850`. [Main push CI 38839602774](https://github.com/tehutahu/movie_editor/actions/runs/38839602774) passed for that exact merge SHA, including all browser regressions, audit and evidence upload. Main tree matches the reviewed head.

author: keylormr
body:
Cierra la segunda mitad de H-271-3 de la revision adversaria del 15-10: depositar y retirar de una meta de ahorro armaban una llave de idempotencia nueva en cada llamada.

## Que pasaba

El adaptador mandaba un `Idempotency-Key` al azar por pedido, asi que solo protegia el reenvio exacto del mismo pedido, no el reintento de la persona. Si la red se cortaba sin traer la respuesta, el deposito pudo haberse hecho, la hoja decia "No se pudo depositar. Tu dinero sigue en la billetera." y tocar Depositar otra vez lo hacia de nuevo.

Y aun con la misma llave el reintento fallaba en el caso mas probable: depositar todo el saldo. El servidor leia el saldo antes que la llave, veia la billetera en cero y respondia "insufficient balance" por un deposito que si se habia hecho.

## Que cambia

### Servidor (`/savings/goals/{id}/deposit` y `/withdraw`)

- **La repeticion se marca.** Con una llave que ya tiene su asiento, la respuesta es la meta como esta y `replayed: true`, sin mover nada. Sin la marca la pantalla no puede soltar la llave: un segundo deposito identico hecho a proposito el mismo dia viajaria con la llave del primero y se devolveria como hecho sin mover nada.
- **Depositar lee el saldo primero y la llave solo si no alcanza** (la regla del repo para los pre-chequeos de cortesia): el reintento de un deposito que se llevo todo el saldo es aquel deposito, no "sin saldo".
- El reintento de un deposito que despues se retiro sigue siendo la repeticion de aquel deposito: no mueve nada y lo dice. La respuesta es la meta como esta hoy, asi que no afirma un estado que ya no existe.

### Pantalla de ahorro

- La llave la guarda `intentoPendiente` (ambito `ahorro`; firma: meta, sentido y monto), la misma que usan SINPE y el retiro del comercio (y Servicios con #277): sobrevive a cambiar de pestana y a cerrar la app. Se conserva ante cualquier error y se suelta al salir bien o ante la repeticion.
- Sin respuesta, la hoja dice que el movimiento quedo sin confirmar y que reintentar ahora con el mismo monto no lo hace dos veces, en vez de afirmar donde esta el dinero. Los rechazos siguen con su texto de siempre.
- La repeticion se dice: "Ese movimiento ya se habia hecho. No se hizo otra vez; si querias hacer otro igual, intentalo de nuevo."
- Dos textos nuevos en los 7 idiomas.
- `openapi.yaml` documenta depositar y retirar, que no estaban, con la llave y la marca; los tipos generados se regeneraron.

## Pruebas

| Commit | Que | Resultado en CI |
|---|---|---|
| `d1b8eb8` | Pruebas: por la ruta real, el reintento del deposito que se llevo todo el saldo, la marca de la repeticion al depositar y al retirar, y el reintento de un deposito ya retirado; el adaptador manda la llave de la pantalla y lee la marca; la pantalla dice "sin confirmar" tras un corte, reintenta con la misma llave, usa otra despues de salir bien y dice la repeticion | Rojo, lo esperado ([corrida](https://github.com/keylormr/kiramopay/actions/runs/38839226975)): 3 pruebas del servidor (el reintento salia `400 SAVINGS_FAILED`; las repeticiones, sin marca), 6 del frontend y el typecheck (la llave y la marca no existian en el contrato) |
| `65cb605` | Arreglo | Verde, todos los trabajos ([corrida](https://github.com/keylormr/kiramopay/actions/runs/38840115589)) |

## Observaciones fuera de este PR

- El handler de ahorro responde `400 SAVINGS_FAILED` para todo, incluida una falla de la base. La pantalla no muestra el texto del servidor y conserva la llave ante cualquier error, asi que no hay riesgo de cobro doble; darle codigo a cada motivo (sin saldo, mas de lo guardado, meta ajena) queda para otro cambio.
- La llave del libro es `savings:` mas la del cliente, sin la persona: dos personas que mandaran la misma llave chocarian. Con llaves al azar no pasa; quien la fuerce solo se afecta a si mismo (su movimiento se toma por repetido).

author: ayanbinrafaih
body:
## Problem

Capability negotiation for `tail` and `store_id` is an ordinary compatibility path: an older server emits a terminal `protocol_error`, rejects the capability-bearing subscribe request, and the client retries without that option. `PersistentEventStream` forwarded that probe-only frame before the typed rejection proved its meaning. The compatible fallback then stayed live, but consumers had already latched a permanent stream failure and initial fallback emitted no compensating `connected` transition.

Closes #2716.

## Solution

Keep at most one pre-acknowledgement `protocol_error` local to a capability-bearing dial until its handshake settles. A typed server rejection consumes that frame with the failed probe; any transport failure, accepted subscription, or unadorned fallback still publishes the fault normally.

The synchronous `subscribed` frame, rather than the later promise continuation, closes the probe window. This matters when an acknowledgement and terminal fault share one socket callback: post-ack delivery remains inside the transport's observer boundary, so a throwing consumer cannot orphan the acquired handle.

The recovery owner is marked failed while a terminal frame is pending so an explicit recovery cannot be lost in the promise-settlement window. Only a proven capability rejection clears that local failure before its fallback.

**Same flaw elsewhere.** `rg -n "isServerRejection|protocol_error|tail|storeId" clients/libs/transport clients/tui clients/web clients/desktop` found the two compatibility probes owned by `PersistentEventStream`: initial `tail` bootstrap and `store_id` resume. Both use the same corrected dial path. No other client capability fallback forwards an in-band stream fault before classifying its request rejection.

### Design

- **Owner:** `@vibesys/transport` owns persistent subscription negotiation, stream-generation fencing, and fallback. The fix stays in that deep module.
- **Interface:** No public interface or wire contract changes. Existing `StreamTransport.subscribe`, `PersistentEventStream`, and callback contracts are preserved.
- **Direction:** Transport frames continue to flow through `PersistentEventStream` into frontend callbacks. No imports, package dependencies, or `tach.toml` edges were added.
- **Drift:** None. Both known capability probes now share one mechanism, and accepted frames continue through the transports' existing observer-failure boundary.

### Architecture

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant Peer
    participant Transport
    participant Stream as PersistentEventStream
    participant UI as Consumer
    Peer->>Transport: protocol_error before subscribed
    Transport->>Stream: protocol_error
    Stream->>Stream: defer one probe fault
    Peer-->>Transport: typed request rejection
    Transport-->>Stream: rejected subscribe promise
    Stream->>Transport: retry without capability option
    Transport->>Stream: subscribed + event_batch
    Stream->>UI: compatible live stream only
```

## Verification

The regression patch against merge base `51f247f81` failed both capability cases: consumers saw `protocol_error,event_batch` after a successful fallback. The product change on the rebased head emits only `event_batch`. A separate accepted-handshake regression sends `subscribed` and `protocol_error` in one observer turn, throws from the consumer, and proves the returned handle is retired.

### Correctness properties

- A stream fault is hidden only when a typed server rejection proves it belongs to a `tail` or `store_id` probe.
- Transport failures never authorize dropping a capability option or suppressing a fault.
- A fault after `subscribed`, and a fault from the plain fallback, remains visible.
- A deferred terminal frame fences overlapping recovery until its classification is known.
- Every acquired subscription handle is adopted or retired, including when a post-ack observer throws.
- Later real disconnects still report, reconnect, and clear normally after a successful fallback.

### Testing

- `PATH=/tmp/vibesys-bun/bin:$PATH pnpm --dir clients/libs/transport test` — 283 Bun tests and 9 Node test files passed.
- `clients/node_modules/.bin/tsc -b clients/libs/transport/tsconfig.json --pretty false` — passed.
- `clients/node_modules/.bin/biome check clients/libs/transport/src/persistent-event-stream.ts clients/libs/transport/src/persistent-event-stream.test.ts` — passed.
- `pnpm --dir clients check:clients` — 29/29 client package checks passed before the final focused observer-boundary repair; the affected package was rerun in full after that repair.
- `./scripts/check_format.sh` and `./scripts/check_lint.sh` — passed before rebase; changed-file checks passed on the rebased head.
- `git diff upstream/main --check` — passed.

The repository-wide TypeScript architecture command was attempted but did not complete or emit a failure after more than six minutes in this environment. This change adds no import or package edge.

body:
## 요약

`그 사업 예산은?` 같은 후속 질문을 이전 대화로 보완해 검색하고, 재작성한 질문으로 발주기관을 선택합니다. 고려대학교 사업을 물은 뒤 후속 질문을 하면 고려대학교 문서에서 검색합니다.

Closes #15

## 변경 이유

기존에는 이전 대화를 답변 생성에만 전달했습니다. 후속 질문에 기관명이 없으면 재작성과 기관 라우팅이 대상을 복원하지 못해 전체 문서에서 다른 기관의 근거를 가져왔습니다.

## 변경 내용

- `rag/retrieval/rewrite.py`: 최근 질문·답변 최대 10턴을 재작성 모델에 전달합니다. 대화가 없을 때의 메시지와 빈 재작성 출력의 원본 질문 대체 동작은 유지합니다.
- `rag/generation/generation.py`: `answer_question`의 대화 기록을 질문 재작성에도 전달합니다.
- `rag/retrieval/retrieval.py`: 재작성 질문으로 기관을 선택합니다. 요구사항 코드는 원본과 재작성 질문 양쪽에서 모읍니다.
- `tests/test_rewrite.py`, `tests/test_usage.py`, `tests/test_retrieval.py`: 대화 전달 범위, 호출 흐름, 라우팅 입력과 요구사항 코드 보존을 검증합니다.
- `README.md`: 재작성·기관 라우팅 설명을 현재 동작에 맞추고 후속 질문에 기관명을 직접 넣으라는 기존 우회 안내를 교체합니다.

## 검증

- PR 최신 커밋 `ebe010f`: `.venv\Scripts\python -m pytest -q tests` — **497 passed**, RAGAS 관련 사용 중단 경고 14개.
- 최신 `main`(`3930cfa`)과의 GitHub 병합 결과 `14746e8`: 같은 전체 테스트 — **577 passed**, 경고 14개.
- PR 최신 커밋과 병합 결과 모두 `ruff check .`, diff 공백 검사, `CLAUDE.md`·`AGENTS.md` 동일성 확인 통과.
- 실제 색인 100개 문서·18,988개 청크로 질문 화면에서 고려대학교 응답시간 질문 → `그 사업 예산은?`을 확인했습니다. 후속 질문은 고려대학교 사업의 예산 질문으로 재작성되었고, 출처 12개가 모두 고려대학교 문서였습니다. PDF 3쪽을 근거로 `11,270,000,000원 (V.A.T 포함, 3년 분할 지급)`이라고 답했습니다. 재작성 2회·답변 생성 2회의 사용량 기준 예상 요금은 합계 **$0.00403275**입니다. [실행 조건과 상세 결과](https://github.com/LittleBitAI/rfg_rag/pull/52#issuecomment-6206762459).
- 실제 화면 검증은 코드 커밋 `c2b0980`에서 수행했으며, 이후 PR 변경은 README뿐입니다. 해당 대화 1회 검증으로 전체 질문의 검색 품질을 보장하지는 않습니다.

body:
## Summary

- **New deck `convolution-sense`** (20 slides, 13 live canvas animations): grows convolution out of the ReLU kink idea, from one small neuron slid everywhere to (1, −2, 1) turning kinks into spikes and spikes ∗ ramp rebuilding the ReLU line. It then covers convolution as a tied matrix, weight counts, kernels as patch-space folds, and the arithmetic from Dumoulin & Visin's convolution guide: padding, stride, pooling, dilation and receptive field, and transposed convolution.
- **`deep-learning-intuition-en`**: new slide 22, "Kinks and boundaries are hyperplanes". It trains a 2D ReLU classifier live in the browser and shows that the decision boundary is a polygon whose corners sit on creases. Later eyebrow and page numbers shift by one.

author: skyfuller1303
body:
Split out of #321 as suggested in https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/pull/321

Stacked on #626 (S3a, `feat/fig-import-sources`) only through a shared test file (`source_identity_tests.rs` is created there); the production code here does not use anything from S3a, so the two can land in either order (the test file then moves to whichever lands first).

## Problem

- An instance's override rows address the layers of its main by id. A row can carry the key a layer had before its main was edited (`overrideKey`), and rows of an enclosing instance have to win over those of the instances nested in it. The importer matched rows by current id only and applied them in list order, so such overrides were dropped or applied in the wrong order.
- An explicit "no style" on a layer was overridden by the older style field.
- A paint bound to a variable kept the colour it was saved with until the first edit, even when the active mode of the document says otherwise.
- A stroke-only vector that imports as the outline of its stroke lost the stroke's shared style and colour variables (the stroke becomes the fill, the bindings stayed on the hidden stroke).
- Vectors whose single segments carry their own stroke style import without them and without saying so.

## Behaviour

- A row naming a layer by its old `overrideKey` reaches the layer under its current id, when the key is unambiguous in the main and the current id does not exist already. Rows of an enclosing instance beat rows of nested ones; within one instance the wire order is kept, derived layout last.
- An explicit "no style" link detaches the style, also when the older field still names one.
- On any document load (a new session document, a native file, `.fig` and file JSON; `DocState::new`, `load_with`, `link_instances`), paint colours bound to variables take the colours of the active modes, without touching other pending changes or the undo history. This is not limited to `.fig` imports. Other bindings still go through the normal edit pipeline.
- Every stroke-only vector that imports as the outline of its stroke (REST file JSON exported with `geometry=paths` as well as `.fig`) moves the stroke's style and colour variables to the fill it becomes and drops the hidden fill's. The test lives in `rest/import_regression_tests.rs`.
- The note "stroke styles of single vector network segments were left out" is added for networks with styled segments. `network::decode` stays available next to `decode_styled`.

## Evidence

Synthetic messages and documents built in code.

- `crates/format/src/fig/source_identity_tests.rs`: aliases normalise lazily and keep outer wire order; the selected main of a swap owns the alias scope; an ambiguous alias is ignored but a current id still matches; an explicit no-style detach.
- `crates/format/src/rest/import_regression_tests.rs`: the shared stroke style and the colour variable of an outlined stroke-only vector are kept.
- `crates/format/src/fig/tail_tests.rs`: styled segments are counted by `decode_styled` and reported.
- `crates/engine/src/variable_tests.rs`: initial colour bindings settle in the constructor and the loaders; settlement keeps existing dirty nodes.
- Checks on Windows, based on `main` f40c600 with S3a: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, layers, assets and wasm pass; workspace tests 2,418 passed, 9 ignored, and one collab-net session test that failed under parallel load passes when run alone.

## Limits

- Only fills and strokes colours (and gradient stops) settle at load; other variable bindings are applied by the first edit, as before.
- Per-segment stroke styles are reported, not imported (the document model has no per-segment stroke).
- Overlap with #524 (open): in `rest/mod.rs` #524 changes `vector()` to look up `vectorNetworkRef`, and this PR makes `vector()` return whether it used the stroke outline, so the returns and the start of the function conflict; in `fig/map.rs` `network()` uses `decode_styled` here where #524 (which still calls `network::decode`) edits the lines around `blob_id`; `Mapper::new`'s struct literal is edited by both.

author: ndellagrotte
body:
## Problem

With a shader pack on, OpenComputers screens drew wrong. Under BSL 10.1.8 the in-world screen showed no text and the screen's GUI was black. Without a pack both drew correctly. Complementary r5.9.3 happened not to show it.

## Cause

OpenComputers caches screen text in a display list, compiled with `GL_COMPILE_AND_EXECUTE` during the world pass, and toggles `GL_TEXTURE_2D` inside it. GLSM posts `TEXTURE_UNIT_STATE` for those calls, and Iris switches its pass in response (`setInputs` → `matchPass` → `beginPass`). GLSM recorded those GL calls into OC's list: `USE_PROGRAM`, `VIEWPORT`, `DISABLE(BLEND)` and `ACTIVE_TEXTURE`. Every call of the list therefore rebound the world pass's program and viewport. Upstream Angelica has the same code.

## Fix

- `DisplayListManager.postHook` posts a hook with recording paused, the same pause `glEnd` uses for its live draw. All 23 hook posts in `GLStateManager` use it.
- Replay runs the recorded `ENABLE`/`DISABLE(TEXTURE_2D)` through `GLStateManager`, which posts the hook again, so Iris picks the pass for the context the list is drawn in.
- `DisplayListHookRecordingTest` covers it, and fails without the fix.
- `docs/compat/opencomputers.md` describes the bug and how to check it.

## Dev tooling (second commit)

- `-PwithOpenComputers` loads OC 1.8.10, Scalar, Scalar Legacy and Fugue in the dev client, and unpacks the Scala libraries Scalar nests (FML extracts ContainedDeps only from the mods folder).
- New harness steps: `scmd`, `insert` and `use`.

## Testing

- `:test --rerun`: 1200 tests, 0 failures, 2 skipped.
- Dev client, script `ocscreen.txt` (no pack, BSL, Complementary): text and GUI correct in all three. With `-Dangelica.logDisplayListCompilation=true`, none of OC's 81 lists contains `USE_PROGRAM`, `VIEWPORT` or `ACTIVE_TEXTURE`.
- Regression scripts `itemgui.txt` and `gate-accepted.txt` pass.
- Production jars on Cleanroom 0.7.6 in Prism (NVIDIA): the BSL GUI and in-world text are fixed.

author: tiagoemicheli160512-dotcom
body:
## O pedido

> Nos relatórios para WhatsApp, e no PDF dos cards das lojas no painel de gestão, poderia colocar as informações mais clean, tipo nome da loja, quantidade vendida, e valor total (...) pois as vezes os emogis, fica muito informações, pra enviar para a direção da empresa. Só dos cards mesmo, os demais pode deixar como está.

## O que mudou

Um **terceiro recorte**, do mesmo jeito que o "Rodízio/feijoada" já funcionava: os três botões do modal (Gerar PDF / WhatsApp / PDF no Whats) passam a gerar o resumo quando ele está ligado.

**O relatório completo e o de buffet não mudaram.** A saída dos dois sai idêntica caractere a caractere à do `origin/main` — texto do WhatsApp e PDF, com os mesmos dados:

```
IGUAL  compTxt  (710 → 710 caracteres)
IGUAL  compPdf  (8599 → 8599 caracteres)
IGUAL  bufTxt   (504 → 504 caracteres)
IGUAL  bufPdf   (4707 → 4707 caracteres)
```

### Como fica a mensagem do WhatsApp

```
*GN Gestão — Mensal Outubro/2026*

*Faturamento total: R$ 279.361,19*
4 de 5 lojas com faturamento lançado

*Norte Shopping* — R$ 104.420,89 · 62 rodízio/feijoada
*Bangu* — R$ 94.940,30 · 38 rodízio/feijoada
*Pedreira* — R$ 80.000,00
*Maglia* — R$ 51.000,00

*Rodízio e feijoada: 100 vendidos · R$ 7.019,40*
_Já incluído no faturamento de cada loja — não somar de novo._

_Maglia não entra no faturamento total consolidado._

_GN Operações · 16/10 09:12_
```

O PDF é uma tabela de três colunas (Loja · Rodízio/feijoada (qtd) · Faturamento) com linha de total, sem meta, Δ, funcionários, CHK nem manutenção, e sem emoji no título.

## Duas decisões que os dados impuseram

**"Quantidade vendida".** O único número de unidades que o sistema guarda por loja é o de rodízio e feijoada, lançado no fechamento de caixa — não existe contagem de comandas nem de clientes por loja em lugar nenhum do app. Por isso a quantidade vem rotulada e **depois** do valor, nunca colada nele: escrever `Bangu — 142 · R$ 180.432,10` faria parecer que as 142 unidades geraram os R$ 180 mil. No PDF ela pode ter coluna própria porque o cabeçalho diz o que é. Quando nenhuma loja lançou no período, a linha e a coluna somem em vez de virar uma lista de traços.

**A loja fora do consolidado.** Ela aparece na lista mas não soma no Faturamento Total — regra que já existia (`LOJA_FORA_CONSOLIDADO`). Num relatório que vai pra fora da empresa, uma linha que não soma precisa dizer que não soma, senão a conta não fecha pra quem recebe. O recorte escreve a nota; ela some quando as lojas são escolhidas à mão nos cards, porque aí a escolha é explícita e a loja soma. Nenhum comportamento da loja mudou — a nota só mostra o que o app já fazia.

## Detalhe interno

`window._relSoBuffet` (booleano) virou `window._relRecorte` (`''` | `'buf'` | `'dir'`), já que agora são três estados e não dois. O rótulo da pílula do buffet encurtou de "🍖 Rodízio e feijoada" pra "🍖 Rodízio/feijoada" pra as três caberem numa linha a 390px (conferido em captura).

## Testes

```
e2e_relatorio_direcao.js     32 OK, 0 falhou   (novo)
e2e_relatorio_so_buffet.js   21 OK, 0 falhou   (atualizado pra flag nova)
e2e_home_relatorios.js       13 OK, 0 falhou
e2e_relatorio_lojas_legibilidade.js  19 OK, 0 falhou
e2e_mes_anterior.js          17 OK, 0 falhou
```

O teste novo mede, entre outras coisas, que não sobrou nenhum emoji nas três saídas do recorte (mensagem, texto que vira PDF e PDF impresso), que o total é o mesmo número do relatório completo e não um recalculado, e que voltar pro Completo devolve a saída idêntica.

author: cameronbrooks11
body:
Adds `SPEC.md`: draft 0 written up as `docs/adjudications/0001-syntax.md` and `0002-block.md` decide it, with their addenda. Where an adjudication's wording needed scoping, the text marks the reading it takes, and the section below lists each one. Where it and an adjudication disagree, the adjudication wins, and every question the adjudications leave open is listed in §11 instead of being answered.

`README.md`, `AGENTS.md` and `conformance/cases/README.md` said there was no `SPEC.md`. Each now points at it.

## Outline

1. What this format is for
2. What this document decides
3. Encoding and lines (UTF-8; CommonMark's lines and tabs; `\n` in leaf content)
4. The profile
   - 4.1 the base grammar: CommonMark 0.31.2, block level only, what is admitted and what is refused
   - 4.2 inline content is opaque
   - 4.3 tables: GFM pipe tables, the blank-on-both-sides rule, the ambiguous-table addendum
   - 4.4 conflict markers
5. Frontmatter
6. Blocks and leaves: the partition, leaves, leaf content
7. Names: the marker line, what a one-line marker names, regions, duplicate names
8. Resolution: markers before slugs, github-slugger 2.0.0 slugs, slugs resolve but are not durable
9. Refusals, normative: the eleven identifiers from `case-body.schema.json`, and the two refusal orders the addenda fix
10. Conformance: the `parse` case kind and what an accepting case pins
11. Not decided

`[CHOICE]` markers follow rowspec's convention. Each carries the reason its adjudication gave.

## Open questions the adjudications leave undecided

The suite pins these as READINGs (numbered as in `conformance/cases/README.md`). The spec names each one as a reading and does not adopt it:

- **1**: whether a region's nodes include other markers between its pair
- **3**: whether a `:begin` with no `:end`, or the reverse, is `unpaired-region`
- **6**: whether `raw-html` reaches inline HTML
- **8**: leaf content per type, table cells especially (`\|`, padding, truncation)
- **9 (part), 10, 11, 13**: frontmatter ends at the first closing line; it may be empty; no blank line is needed after it; an unclosed block is not frontmatter; YAML is not checked
- **4, 12**: whether the conflict-marker scan reaches inside a fence, and inside frontmatter
- **14**: the exact conflict-marker line (seven or more; what may follow)

No case pins these:

- CRLF fixtures. The rule is decided, but no fixture has CRLF bytes yet
- a byte-order mark, and bytes that are not UTF-8 (no refusal code)
- whether a heading slug transcludes the heading or its section (0002 §4)
- the anchor format, including the disambiguator for a leaf that was already repeated when the anchor was made, and range anchors (0002 §2)
- how `SPEC.md` ranks against the suite
- how refusal identifiers evolve (retirement, reuse)
- whether 0001's proposed second-opinion parser runs in CI

## What was scoped, read or decided

Where the adjudications' wording does not give one answer, the text says so:

- **The ambiguous-table order is scoped to one table's lines (read as).** The three-defaults addendum states `ambiguous-table` before `table-not-blank-above` in general terms. The ambiguous-tables addendum states it for one pair of lines, and the general sentence is read that way. Across different tables the order is unspecified, and the reader refuses whichever problem comes first.
- **A marker indented four or more spaces is indented code only where a block can start (read as).** In paragraph context it is lazy continuation text, as CommonMark, markdown-it, pandoc and the reader all read it. 0001's addendum wording is read that way.
- **Conflict markers inside a fence and inside frontmatter** are the suite's readings 4 and 12, listed together in §11, and §4.4 no longer states them as decided.
- **A non-paragraph line directly above a table** is decided by 0002's *Decision* text ("a blank line, or its container's edge, on both sides"). The suite's reading 2 is therefore not listed as open.
- **U+0000 becomes U+FFFD**, decided by the pinned grammar (CommonMark 0.31.2 §2.3).
- **UTF-8** is `DESIGN-BRIEF.md` §1's decision. A non-UTF-8 file has no refusal code yet, which is listed as open.
- **The transclusion unit** from 0002's *Decision* is in §2. Whether a heading slug names the heading or its section stays undecided, as in 0002 §4.
- **A lazy delimiter line** is paragraph text, which §4.3 now says explicitly.

The cases README's note claiming that `.gitattributes` normalises fixtures to LF was false (`conformance/cases/** -text` exempts the tree). It is corrected in its own commit.

## The reference reader against the text

Each normative statement in §3 to §9 was checked against the case that pins it, and inputs no case pins were run through `reference/blockspec/document.py`.

**Reader bug, to fix separately:** the reader keeps U+0000 in leaf content, where the pinned grammar replaces it with U+FFFD (§3). This PR does not change the reader.

Some unpinned inputs fall under the questions §11 leaves open. The reader's current behaviour on them is recorded here and not adopted:

- a leading BOM is kept as a character of the first line. So `\ufeff# Title` is a paragraph, and a BOM before frontmatter turns the opening `\ufeff---` into paragraph text, after which the closing `---` reads as a setext underline and the document is refused as `setext-heading`
- `======= x` is a paragraph

```
$ just check
All checks passed!
$ just conform
0 failure(s) across 237 case(s) in the fixture tree
$ just tree
0 problem(s)
```

No case and no line of `reference/` changes.

author: whysosuresh
body:
The second of three steps: the keyboard. Hold Caps Lock and press a key to bring an app forward, land on a site's tab in its Chrome account, snap the front window, or open a link.

```yaml
keys:
  s: { app: iTerm }
  g: { site: github }
  left: { window: left-half }
  f: { window: maximize }
  w: { url: "slack://open" }
```

**Config**
- `keys:` maps a key name (`a`–`z`, `0`–`9`, `f1`–`f12`, `left`, `right`, `up`, `down`) to exactly one of `app`, `site`, `window` or `url`. Every problem is reported at once with its line, and a key bound twice is refused by the YAML parser.
- Caps Lock is the one key, with no setting to pick another. A file without `keys:` leaves Caps Lock alone, and `sites:` is now optional.

**Core** (pure, all tested)
- `Keys.swift`: the key table. `f1`–`f12` also match the Magic Keyboard's top row as measured: key codes 145, 144, 160, 177, 176, 178 and media keys 20, 16, 19, 7, 1, 0.
- `KeyRules.swift`: the tap's decisions. Caps Lock (as F18) is swallowed. A bound key runs once and an unbound one does nothing while Caps Lock is held. A swallowed press swallows its key-up and repeats, and a missed key-up can't stick a key.
- `WindowLayout.swift` gives the frames; `KeyBindings.swift` holds the actions and the app-name search.

**CapsJumpSystem** (new, live)
- `KeyMapping`: Caps Lock → F18 through the HID event system's public `UserKeyMapping` property. It adds and removes only its own entry.
- `KeyLayer`: one active session event tap. It switches itself back on if macOS disables it.
- `ConfigWatcher`: FSEvents on the config file's path, so edits apply on save.
- `WindowMover`: moves windows through Accessibility.
- `Launcher`: opens apps and links through NSWorkspace.

**App**
- The keys start on every launch, and by themselves once Accessibility is granted. Caps Lock is mapped only while the tap runs.
- Caps Lock is given back on quit, logout, SIGTERM, SIGINT and `brew uninstall`; the cask gains `uninstall quit:`.
- `capsjump setup` registers a login item. Accessibility is enough for the tap; Input Monitoring isn't needed.
- `capsjump check` lists every key: the app it finds, or the app that opens its link. It also reports whether the app runs and Caps Lock is mapped.

**Verified locally**
- `swift test`: 69 tests in 10 suites pass. `scripts/bundle.sh` builds.
- With the app installed on a Mac Studio with a Magic Keyboard:
  - 16 app keys, 7 site keys, 3 window keys and two links all ran. Jumps took 262–397 ms.
  - A broken edit kept the keys and posted one notice.
  - Removing `keys:` gave Caps Lock back without a restart, and restoring it took Caps Lock again.
  - A normal quit and SIGTERM both gave Caps Lock back.
  - The mapping survived the keyboard being switched off and on.

body:
## Resumo
Rotulagem do avaliador B para a validação manual (S02-O2.3).

- `rotulos/B.csv`: 60 repositórios (`tipo_projeto`, `entregas_reais`) e 300 releases (`corretiva`).
  - tipo_projeto: 27 aplicação/serviço, 23 biblioteca/framework, 8 ferramenta CLI, 2 outro
  - entregas_reais: 58 sim, 2 incerto
  - corretiva: 128 sim, 172 não
- `validacao/enriquecer_planilha.py`: adiciona à planilha a descrição, o README, as notas e os commits de cada release, para apoiar a leitura.
- `validacao/pre_rotular.py` + testes: pré-rotulagem por palavras-chave que preserva rótulos já preenchidos e marca casos duvidosos para revisão.

author: ningendo7
body:
## Problem

Three things about the networking around RDS went wrong for consumers:

- **Leaving deadlocked.** Removing `rds.consumes`, or deleting a consumer CR, tried to delete the consumer's pod security group first. The instance owner's ingress rule still named that group, so AWS refused with `DependencyViolation`. The owner only revoked the rule once the consumer's ledger entry disappeared, which only happened after the delete succeeded. `RDSReady` stayed `False`, or the CR stuck in Terminating.
- **Pods lost their normal traffic.** With Security Groups for Pods, the groups in the `SecurityGroupPolicy` replace the pod's own. The consumer's group has no ingress rules, so adding `rds.consumes` could cut the app's pods off from Service, load balancer and probe traffic the next time they restarted.
- **Instance security groups leaked.** Instances are only ever deleted by hand, and the instance's security group was never deleted. It counted against the VPC quota and its rules blocked consumers from deleting their own groups.

## Changes

- **Release order for consumers.** The consumer's pod group is first marked as releasing, which makes it read as unpublished so the owner revokes the rule naming it. The `SecurityGroupPolicy` and ServiceAccount label are then dropped, and the group is deleted. While AWS still refuses, the entry is kept and the section shows `WaitingForRuleRelease` and retries.
- **Owners only grant ingress to consumers that want it.** A consumer being deleted, or one that doesn't list the instance in its own `rds.consumes`, no longer gets access. Naming a CR in `sharedWith` was previously enough.
- **Base security groups.** New `manager.podBaseSecurityGroupIds` chart value (manager flag `--pod-base-security-group-ids`, validated at startup) lists groups the consumer's pods keep next to the database group. Unset, behaviour is unchanged and the operator warns with `PodBaseSecurityGroupsUnset`.
- **Instance security groups are recorded and cleaned up.** Each is tracked in the ledger (existing instances pick it up on the next reconcile) and deleted once its instance is gone, after the ownership-tag check.
- The Makefile's `helm-generate` recipe re-applies the new chart template and values entries, as it does for `extraEnv`.

## Not changed

Discovering the cluster security group automatically when the list is unset is a planned follow-up.

## Tests

- Unit tests for each change, each confirmed failing without it. The fake EC2 now refuses to delete a group another group's rule references, as AWS does, so the deadlock is reproduced and shown resolved.
- The chart workflow checks the value reaches the flag and that nothing is added by default.
- No e2e: LocalStack's community edition has no RDS.

author: pnz1990
body:
Fixes #1077

## Problem

`spokes:disable-kro` sources `scripts/argocd-refresh-token.sh` before its `argocd app sync --prune`. go-task's shell interpreter can't parse that script (line 11 is zsh-only syntax), and `2>/dev/null || true` hides the error. So the refresh has never run from the Taskfile: the CLI sync fails `Unauthenticated` and every teardown prunes through the `kubectl patch` fallback.

Making the script parse isn't the fix either. It signs in with Playwright through IAM Identity Center, which is one per account. With two workshop stacks in an account, the identity source can be the other stack's Keycloak, so a working refresh would send this stack's password there mid-teardown. Details in #1077.

## Fix

`workshop/Taskfile.yaml`, `spokes:disable-kro`: remove the `source … argocd-refresh-token.sh` line and its comment. A short comment says why there is no sign-in here.

- The `argocd` CLI branch stays. It uses whatever Argo CD session the caller already has (for example, a token from the IDE's refresh timer).
- The `kubectl patch` fallback is unchanged. It is what pruned the spokes in every teardown so far.
- `scripts/argocd-refresh-token.sh` itself is untouched. No other Taskfile cmd sources it, and the IDE's `argocd-refresh-token` shell function is separate.

**Test:** `workshop/scripts/tests/test_disable_kro_no_sso_refresh.py`:

1. no Taskfile cmd (or `sh:` var) sources or runs the token refresh;
2. with go-task on PATH, every repo script a Taskfile cmd sources parses under go-task (a parse-only probe);
3. the go-task mechanism itself: `source` of a file with `${(%):-%x}` fails before the file's first line runs, even when that line is fine;
4. the task's cmd, read verbatim and run under go-task against a local bare fleet-config repo (real git and yq; fake `aws`, `argocd`, `kubectl`, `python3`, `sleep`, and an `rm` that only records). With no Argo CD session, it prunes through `kubectl patch`, cleans up the marker, the fleet member and the CARM mapping, de-registers the spoke, and never calls `python3`.

## Validation

- `workshop/Taskfile.yaml` parses (`yaml.safe_load_all`).
- New tests: **2 fail on `main`** (1 and 2: `spokes:disable-kro[0]: source "{{.REPO}}/scripts/argocd-refresh-token.sh" 2>/dev/null || true`, and `parameter expansion flags are a zsh feature; tried parsing as bash`). All 4 pass with the fix. Tests 3 and 4 also pass on `main`: there too the sign-in never starts, because the `source` fails.
- `python -m pytest workshop/scripts/tests scripts/tests -q`: 105 passed (101 existing + 4 new), with go-task 3.53.1 on PATH. Without go-task, tests 2-4 skip.

**Live, on our test stack:**

Verified by local reproduction under go-task, plus the live teardown output from `main`'s code. The change only removes a line that never ran, so the live path (the `kubectl patch` fallback) is the one a real teardown already takes.

**Before, live** (`main`'s `spokes:disable-kro`, run by `task destroy` on the workshop IDE, go-task 3.54.0, no Argo CD session), for each spoke:

```
▸ Pruning app clusters-kro-<prefix>-spoke-dev — this DELETES the live cluster <prefix>-spoke-dev + its VPC.
time="…" level=fatal msg="rpc error: code = Unauthenticated desc = no session information"
⚠ argocd prune failed (auth?). Falling back to kubectl patch...
application.argoproj.io/clusters-kro-<prefix>-spoke-dev patched
✓ Cleaned up <prefix>-spoke-dev marker, fleet member, overlay + multi-acct mapping.
✓ De-registered <prefix>-spoke-dev from Argo CD (clusters-kro-<prefix>-spoke-dev, fleet-secret-<prefix>-spoke-dev, cluster Secret).
```

The token automation's stderr file (`/tmp/argocd-token-debug.log`) did not exist afterwards: the sign-in never started. Both spoke clusters were then deleted through the patched sync.

**Why, local** (go-task 3.53.1, the script from `main`):

```
$ task probe REPO=<repo>     # source "{{.REPO}}/scripts/argocd-refresh-token.sh" || echo "SOURCE-FAILED rc=$?"
source: <repo>/scripts/argocd-refresh-token.sh:11:63: parameter expansion flags are a zsh feature; tried parsing as bash
SOURCE-FAILED rc=1
after source
$ bash -n scripts/argocd-refresh-token.sh && echo ok
ok
```

**After, local** (`test_disable_kro_no_sso_refresh.py`, the task's cmd run verbatim under go-task 3.53.1 against a local bare fleet-config repo, no Argo CD session): exit 0, `Falling back to kubectl patch...`, the `kubectl patch application clusters-kro-peeks-spoke-dev … "prune":true` call, the post-prune cleanup commit, the de-registration, and no `python3` call.

```
main:   2 failed, 2 passed  (no cmd runs the token refresh; sourced scripts parse under go-task)
branch: 4 passed; full suite 105 passed
```

## Notes

- No behaviour change on a working path: under go-task the removed line never did anything.
- Merges cleanly with the open PRs that touch `workshop/Taskfile.yaml` (#1068, #1043).
- `scripts/argocd-refresh-token.sh` line 11 could become bash/POSIX-only, or the script could be removed, if nothing outside the Taskfiles sources it. Left for a separate change.

## GF-2: the golden corpora record what a phone computes from the kernel (format 3)

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/engine-split/gf2-kernel-overlay-design.md` (owner rulings Q1–Q6, 2026-10-15). Batch review: `docs/superpowers/specs/engine-split/reviews/gf2.md`.

### What changes
- **Corpus format 3.** Every stream now records a per-step summary digest (`summaries`), the kernel overlay (`overlay`: stoppage, squads, settlement, expunge, level withdrawal, decider), effective `outcome`/`summary`/`deltas` (Q3), and final `playerStats` (Q2). The reformat commits are data only: every pre-existing field is byte-identical.
- **Fold-epoch guard.**
  - `summaries` and `overlay` changes owe a MAJOR; `playerStats` changes owe a MINOR (Q2).
  - Newly recorded fields owe nothing only if the PR touches no fold-affecting code (Q1 freeze rule).
  - The format never falls (judged per corpus).
  - Unknown stream keys and malformed or hybrid formats exit 2.
- **Golden floor.**
  - New tokens: `overlay:<fact>:set|cleared`, `undo:core.settle` and `stats:award:<declared key>`.
  - Settle, expunge and award stories are appended in every sport.
  - Floor reproduction is batch-scoped, so a config added later cannot change an earlier batch.
- **Retirements.**
  - The `core.settle` floor exemption is gone.
  - `OVERLAY_CLAIMS` keeps only `note` (nothing computes from a note) and `award` in the 8 sports with no declared award key.
  - GOLDEN-POLICY "what the guard cannot see" is rewritten to match.
- **S2 phone contract** (`capture-s2-handoff.md`): a phone must not compute or render player stats.
- **Reformat route.** A format-1 stream whose module value differs from the effective one cannot be reformatted. The refusal names the route: start from main's format-3 corpus and re-append with `EXTEND_GOLDEN=1`.

### Teeth
Each check below uses a real kernel or stats mutant, then `REBASELINE_GOLDEN=1`; the guard names exactly the sports reached.

| Mutant | Sports named | Bump owed |
|---|---|---|
| suspend drops its reason | 11 | MAJOR |

| fold never sets expunged | 11 | MAJOR |
| position reducer no-op | 11 | MAJOR |
| `outcomeOf` ignores a level withdrawal | 6 | MAJOR |

| `awaitingDecider` | boardgame | MAJOR |
| `levelWithdrawal` drops `eventId` (batch review) | the 6 level sports | MAJOR |
| substitution not counted (batch review) | 11 | MAJOR |
| settlement drops `eventId` (batch review) | 11 | MAJOR |
| award credit | football, hockey, icehockey | MINOR |
| counted stat | 11 | MINOR |
| summed stat | cricket, generic | MINOR |

Before GF-2, the stoppage-reason change moved no recorded byte.

author: skyfuller1303
body:
Split out of #321 as suggested in https://github.com/storytold/figcraft/pull/321

Stacked on #627 (S3b, `feat/fig-import-overrides`), which is stacked on #626 (S3a). Until they merge the diff shows all three.

## Problem

A text layer that links a shared text style keeps its own copy of the typography, which can be stale when the style changed. The importer put the style above everything, so:

- an instance override of the font size lost against the shared style;
- a case, decoration, paragraph spacing or paragraph indent set on the layer itself (including "original", "none" and zero, which clear what the style has) lost against the style;
- an explicit "no style" on a text layer was overridden by the older style field;
- letter spacing given as a percentage of the font size came in as a fixed pixel value;
- a text property value on an instance inherited the character styles written for the main's text, which count other characters.

## Behaviour

- Order of precedence for a text layer: override rows of the instance, then the shared style (typography), then the layer's own copy. For the typography (font, size, line height, letter spacing) the layer's own copy is treated as possibly stale. For case, decoration, paragraph spacing and paragraph indent the file cannot tell a stale copy from a deliberate local value, and "original", "none" and 0 could never be set on a layer if the style always won, so a value the layer or an override sets itself is taken as deliberate and wins over the style's; a value the importer does not know leaves the style's in place. The rule is stated in a comment at that code and pinned by `local_case_decoration_and_paragraph_values_beat_the_shared_style`, which also checks that the style's size and family still beat the stale copy.
- An explicit "no style" unlinks the layer.
- Percent letter spacing stays a percentage in `.fig` imports; the private `_letterSpacingPercent` field is read only by the `.fig` import path, so ordinary REST file JSON is unchanged.
- When an instance gives a text property value for other characters than the main's, the main's character styles are dropped and only the value's own apply.

## Evidence

Synthetic messages built in code, import only (`crates/format/src/fig/text_style_tests.rs`): local case/decoration/paragraph beat the shared style and clear it, unknown values and absent fields fall back, the shared definition is not changed; instance override beats the style, explicit no-style detach; property text drops the main's run styles while the main keeps them; percent and pixel letter spacing; the private percent is ignored by the public REST import. They fail on the base branch.

Checks on Windows, based on `main` f40c600 with S3a and S3b: fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, workspace tests (2,424 passed, 0 failed, 9 ignored), layers, assets and wasm pass.

## Limits

- Hyperlinks with an empty URL need no change here: main already keeps the empty URL and `rest/text.rs` clears the link.
- Round trips through the `.fig` writer (case, decoration and paragraph values written back) belong to the exporter work.
- Overlap with #524: none beyond `fig/map.rs` being edited in different functions.

author: hanthor
body:
## What happened

The `bazzite-deck:stable` branded E2E [38832644743](https://github.com/tuna-os/wootc/actions/runs/38832644743) gets through the GUI install, the deploy, MokManager, Phase 2 under Secure Boot and the return to Windows. It ends inconclusive with "the Phase-2 guest agent never answered". The deployer had logged:

    [WARN] ntfs-3g or qemu-guest-agent still absent from localhost/wootc-ntfs-injected:latest after injection

## Cause of that warning: the probe, not the image

- **Both images ship both tools.** The published layers of `ghcr.io/ublue-os/bazzite-deck:stable` and `bazzite:stable` both contain `usr/bin/qemu-ga` and `usr/bin/ntfs-3g`. In each image they sit in the same layer and point at the same ostree objects. The layer annotations (from the rpmdb) list `qemu-guest-agent` and `ntfs-3g` in both images. I read this from the registry without pulling either image.
- **The passing run has the same warning.** `bazzite:stable` run [38792319332](https://github.com/tuna-os/wootc/actions/runs/38792319332) logged the identical `[WARN] ... still absent ... after injection`, and then its guest agent answered and user data passed. So this warning does not tell the two runs apart.
- **Injection should not have run at all.** These images already have `ntfs-3g`. The first capability probe failed anyway, so injection ran.
- **The two probes that fail share a shape no working probe has.** The first probe and the verify probe were the only `podman run`s in the deployer without `--network=host`. The first one also ran before the image was pulled, inside a 60s bound. Every probe that passes (injection, backend probe, btrfs probe, fallback NTFS probe) uses `--network=host` on an image that is already local.

Not established: the exact podman error. Neither probe saved its stderr, and the run's artifacts cannot be downloaded here. This PR makes the next run record it.

## Change

- `probe_image`: every probe in the NTFS section now uses one shape. It passes `--network=host`, has a 300s bound, and saves podman's stderr. `NTFS_DRIVER_PROBE` is the single capability test, and both call sites run it.
- `ensure_ntfs_support` pulls the image before it probes. It skips the pull when offline.
- `verify_injected_tools` prints `ntfs-3g=<path> qemu-ga=<path>` and `rpm -q`. It looks on PATH first, then in `/usr/bin`, `/usr/sbin`, `/usr/libexec` and `/usr/local`. Everything goes on one `[WARN]` line, because the E2E serial relay forwards only the last `[WARN]` line of each chunk. When the probe cannot run, it says so and includes podman's stderr. It no longer reports that case as "absent".
- When injection succeeds, it now logs the tail of the install output and the tail of stderr, so you can see which step succeeded.
- `run-e2e.sh`: the Phase-2 check that the agent answered was a single probe. It is now repeated inside the existing 120s poll. When the agent stays silent, the harness prints the serial lines about the agent and its virtio port.

## What this does not claim

The `bazzite:stable` run passed with the same warning, so this fix alone may not make the deck guest agent answer. With these changes, the next deck run should skip injection ("Image already has an NTFS driver"). If its agent is still silent, the job log will contain the serial lines that show why.

## Tests

- New `tests/unit/deployer-injected-tools.bats` (9 tests): probes pass `--network=host`; the image is pulled before the probe; one capability test serves both call sites; resolved paths are logged, including a path off PATH; ABSENT and the rpmdb view appear on one `[WARN]` line; a probe that cannot run is reported with podman's stderr; the in-image probe script works in `sh`; the install output is logged. All 9 fail against `main`'s `deploy.sh`.
- Updated: `backend-detection.bats` (the shared capability test), `e2e-failure-ledger.bats` (the agent check is repeated inside the poll).
- Local: all bats suites pass. The only failure, `userdata-persistence.bats` #10, needs the fisherman submodule, which is not checked out here. shellcheck `-S warning` is clean. The Python unit failures are the same set as on `main` (environment).

author: dastratakos
body: ## Summary The ask: make the video call look good at its aspect ratio, whatever the width of the Call tab. Before this change, the video tile filled the whole width of the Call tab, less 16px on each side, at 16:9. In a narrow panel that was fine. In a wide one, such as a full-screen panel, the tile was wider than the transcript column under it (the 720px reading width). It also grew to about 600px tall and squeezed the transcript; in a short window it could take the entire tab. Its `flex: none` meant nothing ever shrank it. The change is one CSS rule (`apps/desktop/src/renderer/styles/call.css`), shared by the tile and the video-off strip: ```css width: min(100% - 2 * var(--space-16), var(--reading-width), max(240px, 70vh)); margin: var(--space-4) auto var(--space-8); ``` - The tile matches the transcript column below it (`min(100% − 32px, --reading-width)`) and is centred over it, so its edges line up with the lines under it. - `70vh` of width at 16:9 is about two fifths of the window's height, so a wide, short tab still leaves the transcript room. The tile narrows instead of cropping (`object-fit: cover` never crops). - The 240px floor keeps the still frame and Restart video readable without running into the corner's Video off button. - The strip uses the same width, so the Video on/off button doesn't move sideways when video is turned off. At the panel's minimum (280px) and default (400px) widths, the tile is the same as before. ## Evidence - Platform-independent checks: `pnpm check:affected` exits 0 (typecheck, lint/knip/discarded-effect, repository checks, desktop vitest 149 files / 1271 tests). - Layout measured in Chromium (Playwright), with the real `base.css`, `planning.css`, `desktop.css`, and `call.css` around the Call tab's DOM. Tile width × height at each tab size: | Tab | Before | After | | --- | --- | --- | | 280×700 | 247×139 | 247×139 | | 720×800 | 407×229 | 407×229 | | 1400×850 (full-screen panel) | 1087×611 | 595×335, centred over the transcript | | 1400×480 (wide, short) | 1087×611, taller than the tab | 336×189 | ![Call tab video tile before and after, full-screen and wide-short panels](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ReviewStage/luke/pr-assets/pr-3016/call-video-tile.png) The ratio is 1.778 in every case. Not checked on a Mac: the packaged-app capture (`scripts/evidence.sh`) is macOS only. ## Invariants - [x] `./scripts/check.sh` green. (CI) - [x] JSON Schema goldens unchanged. - [ ] Every behavior change has, in this PR, the test that fails without it: **no test added.** This is a layout-only CSS change, and the suite's jsdom does no layout, so the only test possible would assert the rule's text, which is a change-detector test. The Chromium measurements above are the evidence. - [x] Gateway envelope goldens unchanged. - [x] No new `as` type assertion. - [x] No `Effect.run*` outside the edges. - [x] No new raw async primitives. - [x] No discarded Effect. - [x] Test count unchanged. - [x] No hand-rolled file replaced. - [x] No `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` sentence names the changed part. - [x] `PRIVACY.md` unchanged. - [x] Package deps unchanged. - [x] Barrel/door rule untouched. ## Notes - Blockers or follow-up verification: check it by eye in the app with Settings › Experimental › Video calls on, at full screen and at a narrow panel width. - The height cap is a judgment call. Raise `70vh` if the tile should take more of a tall window. Made with [Luke](https://tryluke.dev) --- --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes the Call tab's video tile so it always renders at 16:9 regardless of tab width, instead of stretching to fill the whole tab and potentially crowding out or overgrowing the transcript. - A single shared rule caps the tile and the video-off strip at the transcript column's width and two fifths of the tab's height, centered over the transcript. - The video-off strip stands at the tile's own width, so the toggle stays put. - Tile size is unchanged at the panel's minimum (280px) and default (400px) widths. - Verification by eye is recommended in the app at full screen and a narrow panel width. Written for commit ab51576211067a6380bf43c37d910aa7bc14bca5. Summary will update on new commits.

author: tdavidson
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"tdavidson"} -->
_Requested by **Taylor** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016pG6q64inLqNWpaoCrkirA?thread=cmsg_016pG6q64inLqNWpaoCrkirAQvqyNvsnTVhFCpCG4NkkEu)_

Before: a fund could receive email through Postmark or Mailgun, and Mailgun was also an outbound option, though nobody uses it. Sender trust rested on the From address alone. Postmark posts attachments inside the webhook body, and Vercel caps that body at 4.5 MB.

After: Settings → Inbound email and the onboarding wizard offer **Postmark or Resend**. With Resend, a fund enters its inbound domain, a full-access Resend API key and the webhook signing secret, then points an `email.received` webhook at `/api/inbound-email/resend`. Mail to any address on that domain is processed like Postmark mail. Mail whose From fails DMARC is dropped. Mailgun is gone everywhere.

Resend's webhook carries only metadata, so after verifying the Svix signature the route reads the body and attachments back from Resend's API. If that read fails, it answers 503 and stores nothing, so Resend retries.

**How**
- `app/api/inbound-email/resend/route.ts` replaces the Mailgun route. It resolves the fund by recipient domain (`resend_inbound_domain`) and verifies the signature with the fund's secret (or `RESEND_WEBHOOK_SECRET`). It checks member and authorized-sender status before calling Resend. Then it fetches the email and attachments (`lib/resend/inbound.ts`), drops it on a DMARC `fail`, and reuses the existing dedupe, storage, scan and `runPipeline` steps via `normalizeResendEmail` → `toPostmarkPayload`.
- The Resend API key reuses `resend_api_key_encrypted`, so the fund's inbound and outbound mail live in one Resend account.
- `20261016020000_resend_inbound_email.sql` adds `resend_inbound_domain` and `resend_webhook_secret_encrypted` and allows `'resend'` in the inbound check, keeping `'mailgun'` so it is safe to apply before deploy. `supabase/pending-deploy/drop_mailgun.sql` drops the Mailgun columns and narrows the checks; move it in once this release is live.
- Mailgun is removed from `lib/email.ts`, Settings, onboarding, setup, `lib/credentials/env.ts`, the agent setup tools, docs and `package.json` (`mailgun.js`, `form-data`).
- Settings PATCH now encrypts every email secret in one save under the same data key. Before, a fund without a data key that saved two secrets at once got two keys, which broke the first.
- The route is registered in `UNGATED_ROUTES`. The proxy matcher already skips `/api/inbound-email/*`, and that is now pinned in the test.

**Tests**: `lib/resend/inbound.test.ts` (domain matching, DMARC policy, attachment paging and download, normalization) and `tests/inbound-email-resend-route.test.ts` (bad signature, unauthorized sender, DMARC fail, 503 on Resend error, happy path). The full suite passes (517 files, 5075 tests), `tsc` is clean, and eslint reports 0 errors.

author: bdstark
body:
## Why

In the field test the agent ran `gma3_build_phaser` once, then generated its effects in Python and built them in Lua: 18 moves, 10 colour patterns × 3 modes on 132 items, and 16 Festoon patterns × 3 modes on 72 cells. The tool:
- refused more than 128 fixtures (its own cap, not the console's);
- could not express sync/follow/mirror versions, a per-fixture inversion, a phase step per fixture, shuffle, shapes in degrees or strand patterns.

The agent's hand-written builder lost step timing, so 30 presets had to be rebuilt. Checking the phase spread took a programmer read of about 21,000 lines.

## Probe

[docs/probes/su-13-phaser-builder-macos-2.5.1.md](docs/probes/su-13-phaser-builder-macos-2.5.1.md), onPC 2.5.1, in Preview:

| Behaviour | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| Step value written on part of the selection | changes only those fixtures |
| `At Phase 0 Thru 1260` on 8 cells | reads 0…720, then −540, −360, −180: phases are kept within ±720, so they are compared modulo 360 |
| `XShuffle` | permutes the phases, and the set is unchanged |
| A wing of one fixture | gets the `to` end of the distribution |
| Step width | above **3200 %** it is clamped silently; widths are kept to 0.1 % |
| `measure` | the beats one cycle lasts (MA help) |

## Change (`src/tools/phasers.ts`; `presets.ts` scope cap)

- **No cap below the console's**: up to 1024 fixtures or cells, of several fixture types. `gma3_store_preset`'s scope cap is raised to match.
- **Phase forms**: `{from, to}`, `{from, step}` (a step per fixture) or `"spread"`, plus `shuffle: seed`.
- **`mirror {attributes, wings}`**: inverts the attributes on every second wing. Relative and physical values are negated; percent becomes 100 − v.
  - The per-fixture values are written on those fixtures once every step exists.
  - The whole selection is restored before the timing and phaser layers.
  - The check expects each fixture's own value.
- **`variants: [sync, follow, mirror]`** builds consecutive presets named `"<name> <variant>"`:
  - sync: no phase spread;
  - follow: the phase, or an even spread;
  - mirror: the spread mirrored about the centre (wings 2), with Pan (or `mirror.attributes`) inverted on the second half.
- **Templates**:
  - position shapes in degrees around a centre: circle, figure8, cone, fan (per-fixture pan spread), bounce;
  - dimmer patterns for rows: runner, comet, alternate, thirds, fill, sparkle.

  Widths are scaled to the console's 3200 % and rounded to 0.1. A scanner is not expressible as one phaser; this is documented.
- **`effects`**: several effects in one call, at most 64 presets.
  - All are inspected first; nothing is sent if one is refused.
  - All are built in one Preview session, with a confirmed Preview and ClearAll between them.
  - A failed effect does not stop the others; an unknown step does.
  - The result has one line per preset; `detail: true` gives every step.
- **Compact results**:
  - each preset reports its phases from the build check's own scan, as `{first_phase, step}` or a list;
  - a single effect's result is compact by default (steps that did not succeed, counts, a command count). A 140-fixture rig went from **80 KB to 3.5 KB**; `detail: true` gives everything.
- **The descriptions say what `measure` means.** Steps refuse widths over 3200.
- SU-12's "several effects per call" is met inside the tool, because this branch comes from `main`. It can move to `src/batch.ts` once #58 merges.

## Testing

- **Unit** (`test/phasers.test.ts`, 28 tests, all SB-04 tests unchanged except one that now asks for `detail`):
  - phase forms and modulo-360 comparison;
  - mirror and spread overrides;
  - override command ordering;
  - the shuffled-set check;
  - phase summary, including console-wrapped values and a 116-fixture spread;
  - shape and pattern expansion, including the width cap;
  - variants;
  - tool runs of variants into named presets, a mirror inversion, a 132-fixture rig with a compact-size bound, and an effects list.
  - The test console now models preset names and the groups/wings/blocks MAtricks.
- **Live** (`test/live/phaser-builder.live.ts`, README row added): 1/1 in 48 s on the throwaway show, with every preset matched.
  - circle variants on the beams, named, with mirror's Pan inverted;
  - a fan;
  - on 40 Festoon cells in one call: a runner with 180° per cell, a comet and a shuffled sparkle;
  - a chase on **140** fixtures and cells of three types, phases `{first_phase: 0, step: 2.5712}`.
- `npm run ci` (624/624) and `npm run test:lua` pass. Track B held the console lock until it released it on request; the lock was held for the probes and released afterwards.

## Review round 1

Fixed in a9dd80c, after merging `main` (SU-12 and the bridge 0.30.1 index-0 scan fix are kept). Each regression test fails on 6970e68 and passes now.

1. **[P2] Shuffled phases on every attribute.** With shuffle, `verifyBuild` now checks two things:
   - the attributes of each fixture share one phase (one `At Phase` sets every active attribute, step-preset and activation-group channels included);
   - for every attribute, the set of phases over the fixtures is the unshuffled set.

   Test: the reviewer's case, Dimmer 0/180 next to ColorRGB_R 90/90, now reports both problems.
2. **[P2] Partially completed stores count as work.** The multi-preset outcome is `partial` whenever a preset was stored, even when a later step of it failed or got no reply. Each compact line keeps its failed or unknown steps (including those inside the store) and `uncertain: true`, and the summary says a step got no reply. Tests:
   - two effects whose name writes are rejected: both lines and the call are `partial`;
   - a name write without a reply: the call is `partial`, the line is `uncertain`, and its unknown step is listed.

The docs are updated (`docs/tools/phasers.md`). `npm run ci` 660/660 and `npm run test:lua` pass. The SU-12 dependency is in `main` now. The effects list keeps its own one-Preview-session runner, which follows the same rules as `src/batch.ts` (an uncertain step stops the build, and the whole call holds one lock span).

## Review round 2

Fixed in b9859ee.

- **[P2] A subset-only attribute is checked against the shuffled fixture phases.** The round 1 check expected each attribute's phases to be the unshuffled subset at its own fixtures' positions, which rejects a valid shuffle on a mixed rig. With shuffle, `verifyBuild` now requires:
  - every attribute of a fixture (activated siblings and step-preset channels included) shares that fixture's phase;
  - over the whole selection, the fixtures' phases form the unshuffled set.

  The new RGB/RGBW regression test fails on a9dd80c and passes now: a valid shuffle with W aligned to its fixture's R is accepted, and W out of phase with its own fixture is still caught. The round 1 cases are still caught: they are reported as fixtures out of phase, and a wrong distribution with every attribute aligned is reported by the full-set check. Docs updated. `npm run ci` 661/661.

## Review round 3

Fixed in 8897e09.

- **[P2] Missing phase read-back on a participating attribute.** With shuffle, every participating row (explicit, activated sibling or step-preset channel) must now carry a finite phase; a row without one, missing or null, is reported as "no phase read". It is then compared with its fixture's phase. The subset-only channel behaviour from round 2 is kept. The regression test covers the reviewer's case (ColorRGB_R rows with no phase field), a null phase and a numeric mismatch; it fails on b9859ee and passes now. `npm run ci` 662/662.

body:
## A pinned toolchain never queries for updates on fleet hosts

**Why.** In the m1 mise rollout step (step 1b, 2026-10-16), both binaries reached out on their own:
- The pinned mise printed `mise version 2026.10.10 available`. `mise --version` asks GitHub for a newer release unless the update warning is off.
- rustup checked for its own update on `toolchain install`, and by default it also installs that update.

**Changes.**
- `mise_pin.py` asks the binary its version with `MISE_DISABLE_UPDATE_WARNING=1`.
- New profile table `[rustup]`: `path` (the host's rustup) and `auto_self_update = "disable"`.
  - The installer runs `rustup set auto-self-update disable` before any LaunchAgent is written, then reads rustup's own `settings.toml` back.
  - A rustup that does not record the setting refuses the install with exit 3, naming the recorded value and the fix.
  - A profile without `[rustup]` leaves the host's rustup untouched.
- Only m1's profile carries the table.

**Host and rollback.**
- Host: m1 only. It takes effect at m1's next self-update or install.
- Rollback: delete the `[rustup]` table, then run `rustup set auto-self-update enable` on m1.

**Proof. Everything ran on m1 in a scratch HOME with `env -i`, `ulimit -u` and `nice`; nothing ran on a gate host.**
- `test_rustup_settings` (6 tests):
  - apply sets the value and reads it back;
  - a rustup that exits 0 but records nothing is refused (the control);
  - a missing rustup names the fix;
  - schema checks;
  - with no table the host is untouched;
  - the installer applies the setting before writing agents.
- `test_mise_pin`: a stand-in mise reports the pinned version only when the update check is off.
- `test_install_macos_fleet`, new tests: rustup is set to never self-update; a rustup that keeps self-update refuses the install with exit 3 before any fleet LaunchAgent. The mise, rustup and pinned-interpreter install tests pass, 5 of 5.
- Mutants, 3 of 3 killed: dropping the installer's apply call, skipping the read-back, and dropping mise's env.
- Real rustup 1.29.1 on m1, against a scratch `RUSTUP_HOME`: `rustup set auto-self-update disable` writes `auto_self_update = "disable"`, which the read-back parses as `disable`.

Companion Pulp PR: Generous-Corp/pulp#10389, which turns off mise's update check in `.mise.toml` and in the toolchain scripts' probes, and adds the rollout check flags `--fleet-path` and `--require-tools`.
