author: vincentkoc
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Preliminary intake labels wait for target-source checkout even though intake only classifies the submission. Runs that lose the exact-review reservation also prepare runners and source unnecessarily.

## User Impact

Preliminary labels become visible before target checkout, while the full review continues through source preparation. Held or superseded reservations skip runner and source preparation. Disabled or unavailable intake still allows the full review.

This saves the source-preparation wait on the path to initial labels and avoids setup for duplicate work. It does not make the deep model review faster or establish a measured reduction in model cost.

## Why This Change Was Made

The exact-review workflow owns this ordering. Reserve ownership first, retain trusted scanner setup before intake, publish intake labels, prepare source, then announce and start the full review. Keeping scanner setup ahead of intake prevents cold scanner installation from consuming the inference deadline.

Intake keeps its own live source and queue fences. The automatic reviewing acknowledgement remains after successful preparation, so setup failures do not announce a running review. Receipt recovery still precedes the full-review ledger finalizer.

No model, credential, API, dependency, or configuration surface changes. Workflow production delta is +8 comment lines; existing step blocks move and their provisioning predicates reuse the posted reservation. Test delta is +70 lines. No new runtime TypeScript or parallel label writer.

## Documentation Impact

Updated the active `docs/intake-triage.md` runbook and its workflow-ordering verification/update triggers. Added one changelog fragment.

## Evidence

- Candidate: `843412261e62b05ad044339aee1066bb147b2d7f`; base: `76085db0243085d4bcbddc36001ab47ed28ba357`.
- 27 focused tests passed, covering reservation, provisioning predicates across both runners, intake configuration and admission, source drift, receipt recovery, and oversized exclusions.
- Full `corepack pnpm run check` passed: 5,872 tests passed, 22 skipped, zero failed/cancelled; builds, lint, formatting, documentation, and coverage gates passed. Crabbox run `run_fcc39db22692`.
- Fresh pre-commit and committed-branch Codex reviews: no actionable P0–P2 findings.
- Direct upstream dependency inspection: Codex `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`, `codex-rs/cli/src/main.rs:1371`, `codex-rs/cli/src/login.rs:198` and `:424`. Login and status use the configured Codex home; they do not require the target checkout.

## Real Behavior Proof

**Claim and surface:** the changed workflow publishes intake before target checkout, skips preparation without a posted reservation, preserves optional-intake continuation, and does not announce or enter full review after preparation failure or a denied status fence.

**Executed fixture:** a disposable replay parsed the actual workflow YAML and ran its reservation, intake, receipt-recovery, target-checkout, and status shell steps. It used the compiled intake/status CLIs, the installed trusted scanner, real ledger receipts, and a local Git repository. Each scenario had an isolated compiled workspace and ledger.

**Command/environment:** `crabbox run --id cbx_59210b7bd00b --no-sync --no-hydrate --keep -- node --input-type=module -e '<workflow replay>'`; AWS Linux, image `ami-04beed173f1785931`, Node `24.19.0`, pnpm `12.4.1`. All four changed files were checked against local SHA-256 values before execution. Successful replay: `run_9c16ebabffe5`. Workflow SHA-256: `8289f62118a5a824409514cc6c8954ce8913966c5b1d6b9cd1d00714c7e0a240`.

**Observed trace:** all eight scenarios passed.

| Scenario | Observed result |
| --- | --- |
| Published | Reservation → runner eligibility → intake label publication → actual target checkout → fenced reviewing status → full-review admission. The fixture README existed after checkout and the human label was preserved. |
| Held / superseded | Reservation only; no runner setup, intake, target checkout, or review. |
| Disabled intake | No preliminary label; checkout and full-review admission continued. |
| Runner failure | No intake, checkout, reviewing status, or full review. |
| Checkout failure | Preliminary label was already visible; no reviewing status or full review. |
| Intake failure | Receipt recovery ran before checkout; full-review admission continued. |
| Status fence denied | Intake and checkout completed; no reviewing status or full review. |

**Limits:** GitHub, queue, and provider responses were controlled boundaries. Runner installation was represented by eligibility markers; scanner installation was real. Full review was an admission marker. This proves the changed shell/CLI ordering and failure behavior, not hosted cold-cache latency or end-to-end model performance.

### Post-merge hosted verification

Production run https://github.com/openclaw/clawsweeper/actions/runs/38862977335 uses merge commit `dc342ca89dbc364957a5075d3cc8f800da7356f3`. Its exact-review job `116849287489` exercised the new ordering on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/142556:

- Reservation succeeded at 06:45:38 UTC on October 16, 2026; real runner/scanner setup succeeded at 06:45:48.

author: erik668
body:
Stacked on #1 (`pace/prelogon-notice`). Review that first; this diff is the three commits after it.

## Summary

Callers couldn't tell where a connect failed, or whether a failure could have cost a login attempt. This PR reports both and bounds the phases before the password is sent.

**Phases.** `connect` records `dns`, `tcp`, `rdp_negotiate`, `tls`, `rdp_connect` and, when NLA is off, `logon`. Each phase has a start time, duration, outcome (`ok`, `failed` or `timed_out`) and an allowlisted detail:
- resolved addresses, and the address tried
- the selected security protocol
- the SPKI pin, and whether it matched
- the error code

The detail never holds a username, password or screen content. The phases ride on the `connected` data and on a failed connect's `error`. SDK: `ConnectResult.phases`, `RdpError.phases`.

**Credential boundary.** `credential_boundary` (`none` | `rdp_connect` | `logon`) is the first phase in which the credentials may have reached the server. A failed connect with `none` cannot have cost a login.
- NLA off: the boundary is the Client Info PDU, so `logon`.
- NLA on: CredSSP sends the credentials at a point IronRDP doesn't expose, so all of `rdp_connect` counts as past the boundary.

SDK: `ConnectResult.credentialBoundary`, `RdpError.credentialBoundary`.

**Pre-password timeouts.** All of these fail as `connection_failed`, never as a failed login:
- DNS: 5 s.
- TCP connect: 10 s, total across all resolved addresses.
- RDP negotiation and TLS: 10 s each.
- NLA off, `rdp_connect` up to Client Info: 10 s.

**After the boundary.** The 20 s logon window starts as Client Info leaves, and a failure there fails closed as `logon_unconfirmed`. NLA on, `rdp_connect` is bounded by the same 20 s and a stall fails closed.

The worst case is about 65 s, so the CHANGELOG tells callers to pass a request timeout above the SDK's 30 s default.

**Known and accepted:**
- With NLA on, a close or reset during `rdp_connect` still returns `connection_failed`. The `rdp_connect` boundary marks it.
- There is no overall connect deadline.

## Tests

- `cargo test --locked --workspace`: daemon 126, protocol 75, CLI 8.
- SDK: `tsc` and `node --test` pass, 14/14.
- Mock-server tests cover each phase timeout, each boundary, and fail-closed after the boundary.
- Handler and SDK tests check that phases and the boundary reach both the error and the success responses. These were fault-checked by removing the plumbing.

Live on the CyberArk PSM sim (psm02 NLA off, psm01 NLA on), every case matched and the password appeared 0 times in all output:

| Case | Result | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| wrong password | `logon` timed out at 20,001 ms after a 70 ms `rdp_connect` | `logon` |
| good password | `logon` 1,310 ms | `logon` |
| refused, blackhole (tcp timed out at 10,001 ms), dns, pin mismatch | `connection_failed` / `certificate_mismatch` | `none` |
| NLA on (psm01) | connected | `rdp_connect` |

author: spy4x
body:
<!-- agent -->

**Stacks on #164** (`feat/design-by-default`): this branch starts from it, so merge #164 first, then this one.

## In short

The owner asked for this in chat on 2026-10-16:

> I want you to (refactor/rewrite/optimize) dotfiles/ai-harness and ai-memory documents and instructions. Also, we need to save instructions/rules of how we keep/write/modify instructions and rules themselves. What we do today should rule how we improve in the future. Also, increase max session context window - I think 250k might be not enough for coordinator. Maybe 400k again?

> the coordinator session should be aware about the direction document, absolutely. That would allow it to direct subagents to do what MATTERS.

This PR covers the dotfiles half. The ai-memory half (`direction.md`, `decisions/`) is a separate branch. Changes:

- The compaction window goes from 250k to 400k.
- Every Claude Code session now loads `~/sync/code/ai-memory/direction.md`. The `harness-rules` mod adds it as a `prompt.context` block and skips it silently when the file is missing. OpenCode loads it through `instructions`. DSH has no setting for an extra file, so a DSH lead reads it by hand.
- The global rules gain a **Direction** section and a **Rules about rules** section. A request the owner makes in chat starts now, whatever a plan says. Final reports gain **Decisions**.
- Rule history moved out to `ai-memory` and is linked from the rules; every rule is kept. Five incident stories had no home there yet; spy4x/ai-memory#44 adds `incidents/agent-rule-stories.md`, and the five rules link to it. The file is reflowed to 100 columns, and a test holds it to 850 lines and 56,000 bytes.
- The mod now refuses four more rule breaches: `ulimit -u`, `gh pr merge --admin`, `gh pr merge` without `--repo`, and a Write or Edit that adds a version 4 UUID call to a JS, TS or SQL file.
- The reviewer now blocks a rule lost or weakened without the owner's request.

## Why it matters

A coordinator that knows the direction can brief its subagents on what matters. Rules about rules keep later edits from piling up history and duplicates. Machine checks catch breaches that wording alone did not stop.

## Decisions

- **Rules about rules is a section in the global AGENTS.md, not a separate file.** Every harness loads that file, so every agent sees the section. A separate file would be read only on demand, by an agent that already knows to look for it.
- **The direction is loaded through `prompt.context`, not `session.start`.** `session.start` cannot add context; `prompt.context` adds it to the first message, beside CLAUDE.md.
- **The size budget is 850 lines and 56,000 bytes.** DSH reads at most 64 KiB of rules, a repo's AGENTS.md included. The template's AGENTS.md is about 7 KB, so the global file must stay well under that limit.
- **Trial dates are unchanged**, including the README's mod experiment date of 2026-10-15, which has already passed.

## Moved passages

| Passage | Where its meaning lives now |
| --- | --- |
| Outside-authors story | Clause: "an agent once merged a stranger's PR as its own lane" |
| Busy-loops story | Short clause kept, full story in `incidents/agent-rule-stories.md` |
| Scratchpad wipe story | Clause: "other agents' worktrees can live there" |
| Fake rsync story, "500 until 2026-10-14" | Linked to `experiments/tasksmax-4000.md`; trial date 2026-10-28 and the row rule kept |
| Seven-hour wait story | Clause: "since a run can finish or die unseen" |
| systemd kill story | Clause: "a wrong PID can end the whole desktop session" |
| Opus, Sonnet 5 and Fable numbers | Linked to `experiments/model-comparison/` |
| Haiku 61% figure | Linked to `experiments/haiku55-and-mods.md` |
| Sonnet implementer history | Linked to `sonnet55-vs-opus55-paired.md` and `sonnet55-implementer.md` |
| Reviewer trial numbers | Linked to `sonnet55-reviewer.md` |
| Deno and Cloudflare reason | Shortened to "Deno gets fixes only until about October 2027" |
| Commits line | Merged into Language style |
| One-source paragraph, "Rules are mine", repo AGENTS.md paragraph | Moved into Rules about rules |

These five stories now live in `ai-memory/incidents/agent-rule-stories.md` (spy4x/ai-memory#44), and each rule keeps a short clause plus the link: the outside PR merged as an agent's lane, 32 busy-loops for 11.5 hours, a reviewer's cleanup that wiped two worktrees, a seven-hour wait on a finished run, and a parent-PID misread that logged the desktop out.

The `one-thing` skill no longer asks for the three weekly money numbers, the 60/25/15 split target or a frozen `situation.md`; it plans against `direction.md`. The owner said in chat on 2026-10-16 that money nudges do not work and asked for schedule gates to go.

## Tests

Each line names the mutation, the test it broke and that test's first failure. Every mutation ran in a throwaway detached worktree, through `claude plugin test` on the mod or `deno test` on `source.test.ts`.

- Mutation: rules.ts ulimit flag regex `/^-[A-Za-z]*u/` → `/^-u$/` → refuses ulimit -u in any spelling and allows other ulimit flags → (fail)
- Mutation: rules.ts `--admin` check → `--admin-x` → refuses gh pr merge with --admin → (fail)
- Mutation: rules.ts the missing `--repo` check → `if (false)` → refuses gh pr merge without --repo and allows one with it → (fail)
- Mutation: rules.ts `startsWith('--repo=')` → `'--repo=='` → refuses gh pr merge without --repo and allows one with it → (fail)
- Mutation: rules.ts count comparison `after <= before` → `after <= before + 1` → refuses a write that adds a version 4 UUID call to a code file → (fail), and both register tests that refuse
- Mutation: rules.ts `CODE_FILE` without the `i` flag → refuses a write that adds a version 4 UUID call to a code file → (fail)
- Mutation: rules.ts `after <= before` → `after < before` → allows keeping an existing call and writing one outside code files → (fail); lets a Write through that keeps the file's existing call → (fail)
- Mutation: rules.ts `CODE_FILE` → `/./` → allows keeping an existing call and writing one outside code files → (fail)
- Mutation: rules.ts `directionBlock` accepts blank text → frames direction.md as a context block and skips a missing or empty one → (fail)
- Mutation: register.ts reads `personal.md` instead of `direction.md` → adds direction.md to the conversation's context, reading only that file → (fail)
- Mutation: register.ts `prompt.context` returns the context without the block → adds direction.md to the conversation's context, reading only that file → (fail)
- Mutation: register.ts a missing file becomes the text `x` → starts without direction.md when the file is missing → (fail)
- Mutation: register.ts Edit compares `new_string` with itself → refuses an Edit that adds a version 4 UUID call to a TypeScript file → (fail)
- Mutation: register.ts Write counts the new content as the old → refuses a Write that adds a version 4 UUID call to a file that had none → (fail)
- Mutation: register.ts Write ignores the existing file → lets a Write through that keeps the file's existing call → (fail)
- Mutation: source.test.ts `RULES_MAX_LINES` 850 → 800 → the global rules stay within their size budget → `AssertionError: AGENTS.md has 822 lines; the budget is 800`
- Mutation: source.test.ts `RULES_MAX_BYTES` 56_000 → 50_000 → the global rules stay within their size budget → `AssertionError: AGENTS.md has 52922 bytes; the budget is 50000`

author: roboomp
body:
## Repro
`read` of any RSS 2.0 or Atom feed (directly, or via a page's feed alternate) returned `# RSS Feed` / `# Atom Feed` and one `## Untitled` per item, dropping descriptions, dates, summaries, and RSS item links; only the Atom `<link href>` survived. Reproduced on `main` by serving the reporter's RSS/Atom fixtures from a local `Bun.serve` and running `bun packages/coding-agent/src/cli.ts read http://127.0.0.1:<port>/rss.xml` (and `/atom.xml`); the real feed `https://fluxer.app/blog/rss.xml` showed the same output.

## Cause
`parseFeedToMarkdown` in `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/fetch.ts` read every field through `querySelector(...)?.text`. Since the linkedom → `@oh-my-pi/pi-utils/dom` migration (`e9888367d1`), `Element.text` is a compatibility getter that always returns `undefined` (`packages/utils/src/dom/core.ts`), so every field fell back to its placeholder. Separately, `parseInto` in `packages/utils/src/dom/parser.ts` already detects RSS/Atom documents (`xmlLike`) but still applied HTML void-element rules, so RSS `<link>https://…</link>` became an empty void `<link>` followed by a stray text node.

## Fix
- `packages/utils/src/dom/parser.ts`: for feed (`xmlLike`) documents, an element closes immediately only on explicit `/>`; HTML void rules no longer apply. HTML parsing is unchanged.
- `packages/coding-agent/src/tools/fetch.ts`: added `feedField(parent, selector)` reading `textContent` through `cleanFeedText`, and used it for every RSS/Atom field.
- `packages/coding-agent/test/tools/fetch-feed.test.ts`: `ReadTool` against local RSS/Atom servers asserts channel/feed titles, item titles, dates, CDATA HTML descriptions stripped to text, RSS `<link>` body, and Atom `summary`→`content` fallback.
- Changelog entries in `coding-agent` and `utils`.

## Verification
- `bun test test/tools/fetch-feed.test.ts test/tools/fetch-http-status.test.ts` (coding-agent): 4 pass.
- `bun test test/dom.test.ts` (utils, includes the linkedom golden Atom extraction): 5 pass.
- `bun test test/web` (coding-agent, includes the arxiv Atom scraper path): 216 pass.
- `bun check`: `check:ts` passes; `check:rs` fails in this sandbox on a cargo-cache `PermissionDenied` in `zstd-sys` build.rs (no Rust in this diff).
- Manual: the repro now prints `# RSS_CHANNEL_TITLE`, `## RSS_ITEM_TITLE`, the `pubDate`, description, and `[Read more](https://example.test/rss-item)`; Atom prints title, `updated`, summary, and link. `read https://fluxer.app/blog/rss.xml` now prints `# Fluxer blog` / `## Mobile clients and Fluxer v2` with its description.
- Skipped pre-publish gate (`skip_checks`): `bun run test` fails independently of this diff — directory-listing tests (`workspace-tree.test.ts`, `root-path-alias.test.ts`, `read-directory-range.test.ts`, …) crash on `result.unreadableDirectories.map` because the local `@oh-my-pi/pi-natives` binary predates #15769 (`listWorkspace` returns only `entries`, `agentsMdFiles`, `truncated`), plus an unrelated `usage-cli.test.ts` failure. Also, `bun run fix` rewrites the maintainer-owned `packages/coding-agent/src/prompts/review-request.md` on `main` (`MUST NOT` → `NEVER`), and that change does not belong in this PR.

Fixes #15954

## 무엇이 틀렸나
컷의 정렬 키는 신호·설명 순위가 같으면 파일 경로·줄 순으로 떨어지고 파일 다양성을 보지 않는다. 그 사실이 `_order_and_cut` docstring에 없었고 D97도 「경로 사전순 앞 8개」라고만 적었다. 실서빙 `run_20261015_0001`(arvo:1065)에서 `signal_rank` 1 다섯 자리가 전부 `apprentice.c`였다.

## 무엇을 바꿨나
코드 동작은 바꾸지 않았다. 문서 둘뿐이다.
- `src/orchestrator/runner.py` — `_order_and_cut` docstring에 5줄: 같은 순위 안은 경로·줄 순이고, 위 run의 분포, 라운드로빈·파일당 상한을 안 넣은 이유.
- `docs/open-questions/D/D97.md` — 새 ⏵(2026-10-16): 분포 표, 안 고친 이유, 다시 여는 조건, 받아들이는 비용.

## 결정 경위
이슈 #696의 선택지 (a) 라운드로빈 · (b) 파일당 상한 · (c) 그대로 두고 문서화 중 (c)다. council(2026-10-16) Skeptic·Pragmatist·Critic이 셋 다 (c)였고 진행자의 첫 입장 (a)는 철회했다. 사용자가 확정했다. 판정 코멘트: https://github.com/0xM1yu/whitehat-boss/issues/696#issuecomment-6208386837

## 근거
| 순위 | 후보 수 | 파일별 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `signal_rank` 2 | 3 | apprentice.c 1 · cdf.c 1 · softmagic.c 1 |
| `signal_rank` 1 | 78 | apprentice.c 46 · cdf.c 25 · softmagic.c 5 · vasprintf.c 2 |

- 출처: 그 run 핸드오프 `trace.jsonl`의 `target_planned` 8 + `target_skipped` 158 [실측 · 산출물은 저장소 밖].
- 계산값: 비례 추첨이면 apprentice.c 기댓값 약 2.9자리, 다섯 자리가 전부일 확률 약 6.5%(비복원). 증거의 세기가 아니라 한 run의 산술이다.
- `funcs.c`는 `signal_rank` 0이라 파일 다양화로도 8칸에 못 든다. 거기 닿게 하는 것은 #695다.

## 이 변경이 다음 full run의 어느 단계를 어떻게 바꾸는가
바꾸지 않는다. 컷 동작·trace 필드·ID 발급 순서가 그대로다.

**`remote::tailscale::tests::the_probe_tells_a_listener_from_nothing`**

- **Symptom.** `cargo test -p orchestra-app --lib` on `main` failed in 4 of 15 runs on macOS 27 (Apple Silicon), always on the second question: `left: Some(true)` where `Some(false)` was expected. Alone, the test passed. I found no sign of it in the last 40 failed CI runs.
- **Cause.** The test dropped its listener and probed the port at once. A diagnostic run showed what happened in that moment:
  - the v4 connect "succeeded", but the socket was already `CLOSED` and had no peer (`peer_addr` gave `EINVAL`);
  - `lsof` showed nothing listening on the port.

  On macOS, a connection made right after a listener closes can complete and then be reset, and `listening` counts the completed connect.
- **Fix.** The test now asks first about a port that never had a listener: it takes the number from a socket that is bound and dropped without ever listening. Then it asks about a listener of its own. It passed 15 of 15 full runs.
- **What does not work.** A port held bound but never listening: macOS drops the connection instead of refusing it, so the probe timed out (`None`, 15 of 15).

**`crash::tests::the_hook_writes_the_panic_it_saw`**

- **Symptom.** It failed in the same full run as the probe test.
- **Cause.** The test installs the process-wide panic hook for a moment. The probe's panic, on another thread, was written to its file after its own, and `take_previous` read that one back, so one failure showed as two.
- **Fix.** Once installed, the hook is narrowed to the test's thread before the test panics. Other threads' panics go to the hook that was there, and the exact original hook is put back at the end.
- **Verified with a forced panic.** I added a panic on another thread in that window, temporarily and not committed. The old test failed 3 of 3, and the new one passes 3 of 3.

## What I did not do

- **Change `listening` itself.** The app does not probe a port the moment a listener there closes, so the window matters only to this test. Checking `peer_addr` after the connect would narrow the window, but not close it.
- **Run on Windows or Linux.** The reasoning for both is below under Reviews; CI runs them.

## Checks

- [x] `npm run check` — UI types
- [x] `npm test` — UI unit tests
- [x] `npm run check:i18n` — ko and en hold the same keys
- [x] `npm run check:readme` — the two READMEs still have the same shape
- [x] `cargo test --workspace`
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` — no new warnings
- [x] `npm run build` (needed before any cargo command on a fresh clone)

Notes on the above:

- Run on macOS 27 (Apple Silicon) only; Windows and Linux are left to CI.
- `cargo test --workspace`: 434 passed.
- The 4 clippy warnings are the ones already on `main`: `conductor.rs:2807`, `lib.rs:250`, `remote/server.rs:91`, `crates/agents/src/lib.rs:936`.

## Tests

- `the_probe_tells_a_listener_from_nothing`: a port with no listener is `Some(false)`, and a listener is `Some(true)`. Full runs of the app's tests: 11 of 15 passed before, 15 of 15 after (macOS).
- `the_hook_writes_the_panic_it_saw`: unchanged in what it checks: the block's shape, the mask, and the next run reading the panic back. It now holds while other tests fail on other threads.

## Reviews before this PR

- **open-code-review**, delegation mode, on a copy without the `.gitignore` allow-list lines (see #96).
  - No High or Medium findings. One comment was made exact: there is a moment between `install` and the narrowing, but a panic from another thread in that moment lands before the test's own, and the last block is what is read.
  - The reviewer stress-tested copies of the code. The probe ran 300 times while other tasks opened and dropped listeners, with no wrong answer. The wrapper ran 2000 rounds with four threads panicking non-stop: the original hook always came back, and the test's panic was always last.
  - On reading, the reviewer found the same answers on the other platforms: Linux, Windows (a refused loopback connect there takes about 2 s, within the 3 s `LISTEN_PROBE`, as before), and machines without `::1`.
- **Codex**: no findings.

author: mahtradr
body:
## Problem

`;hmr xml` stops Lich from reading frontend input.

`HMR.reload` reloads every `$LOADED_FEATURES` entry that matches the pattern. That includes files that belong to Ruby itself and to installed gems. Lich loads rexml at boot (`lich.rbw:68`, `lib/common/gameobj.rb:4`), so `/xml/` also matches about 34 rexml files.

- **The overflow.** Re-running those files overflows the stack in `REXML::XMLDecl#encoding=` (rexml 3.4.4, Ruby 4.0.7).
- **REXML stays broken.** Every later REXML parse in the session raises `SystemStackError` as well.
- **Nothing catches it.** The per-file `rescue => exception` only catches `StandardError`, and `SystemStackError` is not one. It escapes `HMR.reload` and gets past both bare `rescue`s in the client thread (`lib/main/main.rb`). That kills the client thread, so the frontend's input is no longer processed.

The same gap affects the most common reload failure. A typo in the file being edited raises a `SyntaxError`, which is a `ScriptError`, so it is not caught either and also kills the client thread.

## Repro (upstream/main fc03e4d3)

This calls the real `Lich::Common::HMR.reload` with rexml loaded, as in production:

```
candidates: 38 (34 rexml)
ESCAPED HMR.reload: SystemStackError: stack level too deep
REXML after: SystemStackError stack level too deep
```

With this branch:

```
candidates: 38 (34 rexml)
reload returned normally
REXML after: ok hi
```

## Change (`lib/common/hmr.rb`)

- **Gem and Ruby files are skipped.** A match is skipped if it lies under one of these, compared by realpath because Homebrew records gem files under `Cellar/` while `full_gem_path` uses the symlinked prefix:
  - RbConfig's library dirs: `rubylibdir`, `rubyarchdir`, `site*`, `vendor*`
  - `Gem.path`
  - an activated gem's `full_gem_path`

  Paths are compared as bytes: RbConfig's strings are BINARY and feature paths are UTF-8, so under a non-ASCII directory a plain `start_with?` raised `Encoding::CompatibilityError`.

  Built-in features that Ruby records without a path (`thread.rb`, `set.rb`) are skipped too. HMR then prints `skipped N file(s) that belong to Ruby or an installed gem:` followed by the first 5 basenames and a count of the rest. Their bodies are not written to be re-run, and HMR exists to reload code you are editing, not third-party libraries.
- **Wider rescue.** Each file's reload now rescues `StandardError, ScriptError, SystemStackError`, so one bad file is reported and the remaining files still reload. `NoMemoryError`, `SignalException` and `SystemExit` still propagate.
- **Bounded backtrace.** A failed reload prints at most 25 backtrace lines plus a count of the rest. A stack overflow's backtrace repeats one frame about 10,000 times, and printing it all sent roughly 640 KB to the frontend.
- **Help text.** The `;hmr` line in `;help` now says files from Ruby itself or an installed gem are skipped.

The skip is what fixes `;hmr xml`. The wider rescue on its own would keep Lich alive, but REXML would still be broken for the rest of the session.

I chose a denylist (skip gem and Ruby files) over an allowlist (only `LIB_DIR`/`SCRIPT_DIR`). The help text says HMR reloads "a Ruby or Lich5 file". A denylist keeps that working for files that scripts `require` from anywhere else, and it keeps the existing tmpdir reload spec passing unchanged.

## Tests

The new examples in `spec/lib/common/hmr_spec.rb` run the real `HMR.reload`. The first 8 fail on main and pass here; the rest pin the path comparison and the backtrace cap:

- a `SyntaxError` in the reloaded file is reported, not raised
- a `SystemStackError` raised during a reload is reported, not raised
- a failing file does not stop the files after it from reloading
- rexml (an installed gem), a `rubylibdir` file and a path-less built-in feature are not reloaded. These cases stub `load`, so a regression cannot really re-run gem code in a shared rspec worker.
- a pattern that matches both a Lich file and a gem file reloads only the Lich file
- the "skipped" message is printed when every match is a gem or Ruby file, and it names the first 5 skipped files and counts the rest
- the backtrace printed for a `SystemStackError` is capped, and the failing file's own frame still comes first
- the path comparison: a `Gem.path` entry given through a symlink, a gem file required through a symlink, a sibling directory whose name extends a gem directory's name (still reloaded), a path gem outside `Gem.path` found through `Gem.loaded_specs`, a loaded file that has since been deleted (reported, not raised), and Ruby plus the loaded file both under a non-ASCII directory (compared as bytes, so no `Encoding::CompatibilityError`)

Other checks:

- Full suite: `bundle exec parallel_rspec -n 4 -o "--seed N" spec` with seeds 1234 and 98765 gives 8627 examples each. The only failures are the 16 in `spec/lib/global_defs_spec.rb`, which also fail on main locally because of a Bundler "missing extensions" warning on stderr in this environment.
- `bundle exec rubocop` is clean on the touched files.

author: ishcodebellz
body:
Two follow-ups to the redesign, from an audit of what the handoff didn't cover.

## Icons

The favicon and Apple touch icon were still on the retired palette (`#123B66`, `#1A4C7D`) with a Georgia serif "HF" — visibly off-brand next to the new `#0F3459` / Jost site.

Both are now generated from `public/havenflow-mark.png` itself: trimmed to its ink and centred on a `#FEF9FA` field at 512×512. The favicon keeps a rounded tile with tight padding so the portrait mark fills the available height; the Apple icon is full-bleed with more margin, since iOS applies its own corner mask. The hardcoded `icons` metadata is dropped so Next's file convention is the single source of truth.

Checked at 512 / 192 / 64 / 32 / 16 against both white and a dark tab bar. Tradeoff: being portrait, the mark reads tall and narrow in a square tile and is finer at 16px than a blockier abstraction would be — but it's the authentic artwork and looks better at every size that modern displays actually use.

## Structured data

New `components/StructuredData.tsx` emitting `LocalBusiness` JSON-LD: contact details, `addressLocality: London`, `areaServed`, `foundingDate: 2024`, Companies House number, Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00, all four social profiles in `sameAs`, and an `OfferCatalog` generated from `lib/services.ts` so it tracks the service list automatically.

Deliberately omitted: any street address beyond the locality the site actually publishes, and any `aggregateRating` — inventing review data is a manual-penalty risk.

## Verification

`npm run lint` and `npm run build` clean, 21/21 pages. Served HTML confirmed to carry `<link rel="icon" href="/icon.png" sizes="512x512">`, `<link rel="apple-touch-icon">`, and JSON-LD parsing as `LocalBusiness` with 6 services and 4 social links. No console errors.

Note for after deploy: browsers cache favicons hard, so the old "HF" icon may persist in existing tabs for a while.

author: iskwang
body:
Implements PRD-sre-lab milestone M1 / requirement B from M0 commit `fabf904`. Root workspaces, scripts and filtered Docker installs use Bun 1.3.14 with shared built first; services and build/test tools remain on Node 20. The verifier uses npm with ignored install scripts and explicit local tool paths (no package downloads during execution), retaining timeouts/cwd/AbortSignal and cleaning up POSIX child process groups. Cleanup errors produce a fixed warning rather than escaping event listeners and crashing the worker. The generated `world.ts.template` TS2322 (`role = entry.role`) is fixed by narrowing a local before assignment, with a type-check test. Operator commands are updated; generated ZIP contents and version pins are unchanged.

### Verified

- Fresh `bun install --frozen-lockfile` and typecheck/lint/test/build under Node 20.20.2. Backend **244 passed / 5 skipped** (M0: 236 / 5); frontend **11 passed**. Lint has zero errors and four existing warnings.
- All **770** unique registry name/version pairs and **40** direct dependency declarations match the old lockfile: no resolved-version differences.
- Both images build. Rebuilt in an isolated Compose project (`docker compose -p m1-accept up --build`): backend `/health` ok, frontend HTTP 200.
- Independent npm/Cucumber 11.0.0/Playwright 1.60.0/Chromium check with the **real generated world template** (`M1_USE_GENERATED_WORLD=1`): smoke passed, syntax-only passed, abort left **0** live browser processes (6 before).
- Real LLM jobs (saucedemo.com, OpenRouter claude-haiku-4.5, `smoke`, 2 Scenarios): 1 of 3 passed verification (one `docker run` job completed; two Compose jobs failed). In all three, explore/generate/verify ran end to end with real Cucumber and Chromium, `tsc --noEmit` passed and `steps.ts` had no XPath. The two failures were the final `Then` asserting descriptive text that is not on the page, i.e. LLM assertion-text variance, not a package-manager or container defect.
- API key is absent from backend logs and `/storage`; it is in the Redis `job:{hash}` record by documented design (`docs/PRD.md:480`, 7-day TTL).
- Remaining executable pnpm commands are confined to the documented ZIP/video/historical-review exemptions.

### Known limits

- **PRD B acceptance: owner decision.** "`docker compose up` completes one real job" is satisfied only in the sense that the pipeline runs end to end in Compose; the two Compose jobs ended `failed` on generated assertion text. The owner accepted this reading. Improving generated `Then` assertions is out of M1 scope and is tracked as a backlog item in `docs/PROGRESS.md`.
- **Parent shutdown (M2):** detached verifier processes may survive dev Ctrl+C, ts-node-dev restart or backend stop outside a container. In Compose, stopping the container terminates every process in its PID namespace. Documented in both READMEs and `.agents/self-test.md`.
- **Timeout (M2):** group cleanup depends on npm exiting after SIGTERM; no independent forced-kill deadline. Windows process-tree cleanup is not verified. `init: true` for the backend service is also an M2 item.
- No M2–M7 work, Redis/storage deletion, or ZIP contract changes.

Detailed evidence and the review disposition: [M1 verification report](docs/reviews/2026-10-16-m1-bun.md).

author: hihenen
body:
## 배경
13:36 폰 Slack 에서 누른 게이트 승인 버튼이 데몬에 도달하지 않았다. 로그에 `Slack interactive payload received` 가 없고 TCP 는 ESTABLISHED — half-open 소켓 의심. 또 #38 은 토큰 읽기 실패까지 캐시해, 키체인 창에서 '거부' 한 번이면 재시작 전까지 Slack 이 영구 단절된다.

> ⚠️ **#38(`HyeongDoYun/knock-keychain-cache`) 위에 쌓인 PR** — #38 이 아직 머지 전이라 diff 에 그 커밋(`aec90c3`)이 함께 보인다. #38 머지 후 이 PR 만의 변경이 남는다. (master 와 CHANGELOG 충돌은 머지로 해소)

## 변경
- **소켓 생존 감시**: 30초마다 WebSocket ping, 90초 동안 어떤 프레임(pong·ping·envelope)도 없으면 끊긴 것으로 보고 기존 reconnect(backoff) 경로로 재연결. Slack 서버 ping 에는 tungstenite 가 pong 응답
- **토큰 실패 캐시 만료**: 실패는 1분 → 2분 → … 최대 15분 backoff 동안만 캐시, 이후 다시 읽는다. 성공 캐시는 #38 동작 유지(세대 변경 때만 무효화)
- **상태 노출**: 연결됨 / 재연결 중 / 토큰 없음 / 꺼짐. 트레이 메뉴 한 줄, `knock ctl status`(신규) 와 `ctl list` 의 `slack` 필드. 끊김 5분 초과 시 macOS 알림 1회(같은 끊김 동안 반복 없음)
- **로그**: connecting / connected / hello / disconnect / socket ended / 생존 타임아웃을 `knock.log` 에 한 줄씩 (토큰 값 없음)

## 테스트
시간 주입(`Instant` 인자)으로 sleep 없이 검증: 생존 타임아웃·ping 주기·프레임 수신 시 시계 리셋, 토큰 실패 backoff 만료/성공 캐시/세대 변경, 끊김 알림 1회성.
`cargo test`(93 통과, 병렬 기본) · `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` · `cargo fmt --check` 통과. 프런트 변경 없음.

## 확인 못 한 것
실제 half-open 상황 재현과 트레이 메뉴 화면 확인은 하지 않았다(데몬 재시작 필요). 머지 후 `knock ctl status` 와 트레이 표시를 눈으로 확인 필요.

author: sukantratnakar
body:
**Approved by Sukant on 16 Oct 2026, after checking the preview.**

## What and why
The live site serves files that aren't meant for visitors (`/.git/config`, `/.git/HEAD`, `/.git/index`, `/.git/logs/HEAD`, `/wrangler.jsonc`). `wrangler.jsonc` serves assets from `"."` (the whole repo) and there was no `.assetsignore`.

This PR:
1. Adds `tests/check_public_files.sh <base-url>`. It checks HG-01 to HG-03 with `curl`, including the byte count and SHA-256 of `/`. It also checks offline that every repo file is either a visitor file or hidden.
2. Adds `.assetsignore`, which hides all dot-files and dot-folders except `.well-known` (so `.git`, `.gitignore`, `.assetsignore`, `.github`, `.claude`, `.wrangler`, `.env` and `.dev.vars` are all covered). It also hides `/wrangler.*`, `/tests`, `*.md`, `/package*.json` and `node_modules`.
3. Adds `"previews": {}` to `wrangler.jsonc` (a435b8a) and changes nothing else in that file. Preview builds now run `npx wrangler preview`, which stops without a `previews` block. That is why the first two preview builds failed.

`index.html`, `article.html` and all images are unchanged.

## Requirements
- **HG-01:** nothing under `/.git/` is served.
- **HG-02:** `/wrangler.jsonc`, `/.assetsignore`, `/.gitignore` and `/tests/...` are not served.
- **HG-03:** every visitor file still loads, and `/` is byte-for-byte unchanged (61,004 bytes).
- **HG-04:** nothing else changes. **Amended by Sukant (16 Oct 2026)** to allow exactly one change to `wrangler.jsonc`: adding `"previews": {}`.

## Test results
- **Live site, before the fix:** 40 passed, 6 failed. Five `/.git/*` paths and `/wrangler.jsonc` fail, as expected.
- **Local `wrangler dev` of this branch:** 46 passed, 0 failed. Planted future files (`.github`, `.claude`, `.dev.vars`, `README.md`, `.npmrc`) return 404. `.well-known/security.txt` and `robots.txt` stay public.
- **`wrangler@4.151.0 deploy --dry-run`, before and after adding `previews`:** same output, no bindings, and the same 34 files to upload, with `.git`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `.assetsignore` and `tests/` ignored. Production is unaffected.
- **Cloudflare preview build of a435b8a:** passed. The test gives **46 passed, 0 failed** against both the branch preview link (`fix-hide-repo-files-changeanesthesiology.sukantratnakar.workers.dev`) and the build link (`c6742196-changeanesthesiology.sukantratnakar.workers.dev`).
- The earlier preview builds (9037a66, d4eb340) failed only because the `previews` block was missing.

## Independent review
A separate agent checked the patterns against every repo file using both git's matcher and Wrangler's own matcher (`ignore@5.3.1`). It found no visitor file hidden. Its should-fix points (future repo-only files, a test that could falsely pass without git, and new files nobody classified) are fixed in 1bb23e5 and d4eb340.

author: dominion5254
body:
Fixes #4263.

This only fixes delivery: a publishing request from a VPN client now reaches the router. Whether it is accepted is unchanged and is #4266's permission check.

A StartOS server joined over a StartWRT inbound VPN could never publish its DNS records. Two independent defects each blocked it:

- The nft divert `redirect`s a `wg_*` arrival to the WireGuard interface's own address (the profile's `.254`), but the 9554 listener bound the profile gateway (`.1`), so every update hit a closed port. The listener now binds the address read from the wg interface. The same divert carries every DNS-over-TCP query from a VPN client, so those were refused too and now reach the relay.
- Client configs carried `Address = <ip>/32`. StartOS sends updates to the first host of the client's own subnet, so a `/32` left it nothing to send to. Configs now carry the profile's `/24`, as StartTunnel's do; the router still routes only the peer's `/32`, and the `/24` is already inside every peer's `AllowedIPs`. A client added on an earlier release must be deleted and re-added to publish; the pending fragment says so.

**Relation to #4266.** That PR makes an inbound VPN peer need the DNS-publishing permission; this one makes publishing reach the router at all. Neither is sufficient alone, and both must land before the 1.3.0 tag. #4266 has merged and this branch is rebased onto it: the `wg_lan` test fixture keeps both sides' additions, and the pending fragment takes #4266's wording plus the re-add bullet here.

Verification: `make start-wrt-test` (674 + 18 passed) on the rebased branch, rustfmt and prettier clean. Benched on the K1 with a StartOS client joined over the inbound VPN: both failures reproduced on the previous binary. On the rebased binary, with the peer's permission off the update reaches the `.254:9554` listener and is refused, and StartOS marks the gateway unsupported; with it granted the record is published, resolves from LAN and VPN clients over UDP and TCP, and StartOS marks the gateway supported; revoking it drops the record at once. DNS-over-TCP queries from the VPN client to outside names resolve. `bench.sh smoke` green; the 9553 LAN listener is unchanged.

author: jppittman
body:
JP, 2026-10-16: "No to register allocation out of the allocator. Ever." and "put a sonnet on that typed register number thing." Regalloc plan v2's S3 then S6, byte-identical on all three targets, plus the boundary rule that keeps it so.

## Three commits

**S3 `refactor(codegen): the frame is one operand; architectural registers have one spelling`.** On x86, `frame(slot)` returns the `[rsp + slot]` base and displacement and every spill and reload uses it; `add_rsp`/`sub_rsp` share `rsp_imm32`; the `Mem` doc no longer calls `rsp` a value. On NEON, `abi::XZR` and `abi::LR` sit beside `abi::SP`, and the words for `mov`, `mvn`, `ret`, `SUB_SP`, `ADD_SP`, `SUB_SP_PAGE` and `STR_XZR_SP` are built through `rn()`/`rm()`/`rd()`, so a grep for a register finds them.

**S6 `refactor(codegen): a hardware register number has a type`.** `RegNo<F>` in `resource.rs`: `Copy`, the file in its type, returned by `Reg::number()`, its bits read in one place per backend. Every encoder register field takes one (`rrr`, `rr`, `rm`, `rip`, `rm_scaled4`, `vsib_scaled4`, `masked`, `X86::ones`, the ModRM/SIB helpers, `spill_into`/`reload_into`; NEON's `rd`/`rn`/`rm`/`ra`). The fixed registers are typed constants (`gpr::RSP/RDI/RSI/RDX`, `abi::X0/X1/X2/SP/LR/XZR`, `K0`); an opcode's `/digit` is `Digit`, which fills ModRM.reg but is not a register; the EVEX writemask is `Option<RegNo<OpmaskFile>>` rather than a byte where 0 means none. `rrr(0, 1, 2)` no longer compiles, and neither does `rex_w(0, rsp)` for a digit, which the compiler caught in the first draft.

**`ci(codegen): a fixed register is declared once, and the boundary check says so`.** `RegNo::architectural` must stay `pub(in crate::emit)` for the backends to declare their constants, so nothing in the types stops a call elsewhere in `emit/`. Rule E of `check_emit_boundary.py` now flags it anywhere but the right-hand side of `const NAME: RegNo<File> = RegNo::architectural(N);`, with eight self-test cases. `regalloc/intent.md` lost its last **Behind** line about the bare `u8`, gained the type and the rule under **Enforced by**.

## Judged, not followed

- The x86 vector encoders are generic over each operand's file (real instructions mix files: `vcvttss2si`, `vmovq`, the `k` family); the memory base and SIB index are fixed to the general file, the VSIB index and gather mask to the vector file, `masked` to the opmask file.
- `rex_w`, `modrm_rr` and `rr` stop being `const fn` (trait methods are not callable in `const` on stable); none had a `const` caller.
- `Members` lists and `Lent::number()` stay `u8`: they declare which numbers a file has and feed the allocator's own bitmask, and `Pool::mint` is where a number becomes a register. `local.rs` is untouched.

## Byte gate and checks

`byte_probe` output recorded on `f30ef3b5` before any change, on AVX-512, AVX2 and NEON (the last from an unmodified main under qemu): identical after S3 and after S6, 107 rows each. x86: `cargo test -p pixelflow-codegen` 157 passed; aarch64 under qemu 141 passed; `cargo check --target aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu --all-targets` clean; fmt, clippy `--all-features -D warnings`, `cargo doc -D warnings --document-private-items` clean; `check-emit-boundary.sh` (74 self-test cases), `check-intent.sh`, `check-cfg-encapsulation.sh`, `check-cl-metadata.sh` pass. Rebased onto 5574374a (docs-only delta) before the third commit; fmt and clippy re-run clean there.

author: knowlet
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to merged PR #1 and its [P2 DesktopSize review finding](https://github.com/knowlet/ironvnc/pull/1#discussion_r4269371245). PR #1 remains merged; this new fix PR is based on `edfb9fc840723e30bb60dedfb1735ffcff8eeade`.

- Remove the last-rectangle-only restriction. Apply DesktopSize immediately, retaining size validation and the dirty-list reset, then validate and decode subsequent rectangles against the resized framebuffer.
- Send exactly one FramebufferUpdateRequest after consuming the complete update: non-incremental when resized, otherwise incremental. Multiple resizes use the final dimensions. This replaces the old full-plus-incremental pair and prevents premature requests during partial payloads.
- Bound DesktopSize allocation and UI-event work **before resizing or publishing an event**: at most 16 resize markers and 32 Mi pixels of cumulative framebuffer reallocations per update. Counters reset per update and are independent of the existing decoded-pixel budget, so a maximum-size resize plus a full frame is not charged twice. This also addresses the [follow-up resource-exhaustion review](https://github.com/knowlet/ironvnc/pull/2#discussion_r4291158656).
- Preserve decoder implementations, compression state, CopyRect source checks and existing size/pixel/rectangle limits. The production client changes by 23 additions / 6 deletions; the only other file is the new test module. No dependencies or workflows change.

[RFB 7.7.4](https://github.com/rfbproto/rfbproto/blob/master/rfbproto.rst#desktopsize-pseudo-encoding) recommends, but does not require, DesktopSize last. Because resizing discards pixels, the next request is non-incremental. The resize count and cumulative allocation caps are client resource policies, not protocol ordering requirements.

## Regression coverage

13 new Rust loopback tests exercise the production `VncClient::connect` with synthetic RFB 3.8 packets:

- DesktopSize alone, last, first and between old/new pixel rectangles; discard stale dirty regions when shrinking.
- Decode Raw, Hextile, Tight and CopyRect using expanded dimensions and stride; preserve stateful ZRLE before/after resize and across the next update.
- Fragment headers/payloads; defer requests until complete consumption; exactly one full request after resizing, then incremental requests for ordinary/empty updates; coalesce multiple resizes and stay quiet without another server response.
- Reject 40 invalid destination-header cases across all five decoders without waiting for absent payloads; reject CopyRect sources outside new bounds, invalid dimensions and truncated Raw without publishing partial pixels or requesting refresh.
- Verify subsequent Bell/clipboard sentinel framing.
- Accept exactly 16 resizes per update and reset the budget for the next update; reject the 17th before another allocation/UI event/request.
- Accept exactly 32 Mi cumulative resized pixels plus subsequent independently budgeted pixel data; reset the budget for the next update; reject even one additional resized pixel before reallocating/publishing its size.

## Validation — four complete native jobs passed; two still running

**Verified head: `9505fb983d3babd92c962a0f5e254d2e9f9ce299`.**

[Exact-head Native binaries CI](https://github.com/knowlet/ironvnc/actions/runs/38855975818), observed 2026-10-16 after 05:36 UTC (13:36 Asia/Taipei):

| Native target | Current-head status |
| --- | --- |
| x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu | Complete: success |
| aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu | Complete: success |
| aarch64-apple-darwin | Complete: success |
| x86_64-pc-windows-msvc | Complete: success |
| aarch64-pc-windows-msvc | Native release-test step in progress |
| x86_64-apple-darwin | Native release-test step in progress |

All six formatting checks passed. Every completed job passed native release tests, release binary build, actual-binary RFB loopback fixtures, smoke/packaging, and artifact upload. **The overall six-platform run is not yet complete; no all-platform pass is claimed.**

The [current-head macOS ARM64 log](https://github.com/knowlet/ironvnc/actions/runs/38855975818/job/116827409851) was inspected directly and reports:

- `69 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; 0 measured; 0 filtered out` (56 existing + 13 new tests).
- All 13 DesktopSize tests are listed as passed, including both resource-budget boundary tests.
- `All 15 synthetic loopback interoperability cases passed.`

CI commands:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo test --locked --release --all-targets --target "$NATIVE_TARGET" --jobs 2
cargo build --locked --release --bin ironvnc --target "$NATIVE_TARGET" --jobs 2
python3 scripts/rfb_fixture.py --binary "$binary"
```

The compatibility-only head `93e87c65c284faf41528d2c7b7d9fb4ab79e48ad` previously passed all six jobs with 67 tests. That is historical evidence only, **not** a substitute for the current hardened head's run.

Earlier iterations stopped at rustfmt; all reported formatting changes were applied. Source-hash/diff verification also caught an accidentally omitted fixture payload append during the resource-test update; it was restored before final validation. Current source blob hashes match the intended files: client `0e50e83ec579879eaf298e461f49796de36db7f2`, tests `45e77db642ee55b64f4c11506ce1aeb6aa0f7558`.

No local Cargo execution is claimed: this editing environment has no Rust toolchain and cannot clone via network. No new unsafe code is introduced. Runtime tests are not a formal memory-safety proof; no Miri, sanitizer, real-server or visual GUI validation is claimed.

## Review and merge status

The [original PR #1 finding](https://github.com/knowlet/ironvnc/pull/1#discussion_r4291083933) links this follow-up and is still unresolved: the code-level ordering issue is addressed here, but **main remains affected until this PR merges**. PR #1 was not reopened. PR #2 is open, ready for review, and not merged.

Sourcery has independently marked the [new repeated-resize finding](https://github.com/knowlet/ironvnc/pull/2#discussion_r4291158656) addressed in `8601b254b9037ffa8d7cd88099070af471694845` and resolved that thread. The [fix reply](https://github.com/knowlet/ironvnc/pull/2#discussion_r4291226507) now includes current-head runtime evidence. This is not a claim that the original merged main or all outstanding CI jobs are complete.

## Summary by Sourcery

Fix DesktopSize handling so framebuffer updates remain valid and synchronized when the server resizes the framebuffer mid-update.

Bug Fixes:
- Allow framebuffer rectangles to follow DesktopSize rectangles and validate them against the resized framebuffer.
- Send a single correctly scoped full or incremental framebuffer update request after each complete update.

Enhancements:
- Add comprehensive loopback regression coverage for resize ordering, decoder behavior, compression state, fragmented updates, invalid bounds, and request coalescing.

Tests:
- Add production-client wire-level tests covering DesktopSize interactions across supported framebuffer encodings and malformed or truncated updates.

author: continuum-beta-iad[bot]
body:
Query\-frontend handler buffers the whole request body unconditionally and logs every request parameter untruncated

## Risk assessment

**Severity: Low**

**Likelihood: High · Impact: Very low**

| Dimension | Recorded assessment | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reachable from attacker | Yes | Inferred |
| Configuration required | No | Finding |
| Access required | ANY\_AUTHENTICATED | Finding |
| User interaction required | No | Finding |
| Attacker gains | Neither | Finding |
| Blast radius | Cross\-tenant | Finding |
| Target value | Low | Finding |

<details>
<summary>Assessment reasons and what could change this assessment</summary>

### Reachable from attacker

Cortex query\-frontend exposes HTTP routes \(\/prometheus\/api\/v1\/query\_range\, etc\.\) via RegisterQueryAPI as tenant\-facing API endpoints\. The finding\'s steps\_to\_reproduce describe POSTing to \'https\:\/\/<frontend>\/\.\.\.\' with tenant credentials\, implying external reachability typical of multi\-tenant Cortex deployments\. Graph has no explicit exposure claims\.

**What could change this assessment:** Explicit deployment topology confirming the query\-frontend is behind an internal\-only load balancer rather than an internet\-facing one would flip this to false\.

### Configuration required

The primary defect \(unconditional body buffering \/ defect 1\) is exercisable with SHIPPED DEFAULTS — the finding explicitly states \'\-frontend\.log\-queries\-longer\-than\=0\, \-frontend\.query\-stats\-enabled\=false\, \-frontend\.max\-body\-size\=10485760\' \(all defaults\) are sufficient to reproduce the memory issue\. Only defect 2 \(log amplification\) requires a non\-default flag\.

**What could change this assessment:** If only defect 2 were considered \(requires \-frontend\.query\-stats\-enabled\=true or \-frontend\.log\-queries\-longer\-than\!\=0\, both default off\)\, this would be true\.

### Access required

The finding requires \'X\-Scope\-OrgID\: <tenant\-id>\' accepted by the AuthMiddleware \(AuthenticateUser → ExtractOrgIDFromHTTPRequest\)\. Any valid tenant identity suffices\; no privileged role or admin scope is required\. In Cortex\, any provisioned tenant can issue query requests\.

**What could change this assessment:** If the deployment front\-loads an additional authZ layer \(OPA\/role check\) restricting query POSTs to a specific operator role rather than all tenants\, this would be \'privileged\'\.

### User interaction required

The attacker \(authenticated tenant\) drives the entire exploit chain alone by issuing crafted POST requests with large bodies and slow queries\. No other user needs to click\, view\, or trigger anything\.

### Attacker gains

CWE\-770 resource exhaustion \/ log amplification\. No code execution\, no data read\/modify\. Impact is memory pressure on the shared query\-frontend and potentially inflated log lines — degraded availability only\.

### Blast radius

The query\-frontend is a shared multi\-tenant component \(Cortex\)\. Heap exhaustion \/ log pipeline saturation on this shared frontend caused by one tenant\'s requests degrades service for all tenants on the same frontend\, per the finding and proof\-of\-exploitability walk \(\~2 GiB per\-tenant\-per\-frontend ceiling with no per\-tenant memory quota\)\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the deployment is single\-tenant or that a per\-tenant memory quota exists upstream would reduce to own\_scope\.

### Target value

The affected resource is query\-frontend process heap and log pipeline\/disk — operational\/availability resources\, not credentials\, PII\, or business data\. Logged content is the requesting tenant\'s own query parameters\.

**What could change this assessment:** If logs were shown to contain cross\-tenant secrets or auth tokens\, this would rise to high\.



</details>

## Remediation

Fixed pkg\/frontend\/transport\/handler\.go\.

<details>
<summary>Recorded change details</summary>

1\) Compute shouldBuffer \= \(LogQueriesLongerThan \!\= 0 \|\| QueryStatsEnabled\) before the round trip\. The io\.TeeReader is now installed only when buffering is actually needed\; otherwise the body streams through unmodified \(still bounded by http\.MaxBytesReader\)\. This eliminates the per\-in\-flight heap retention on the default configuration where neither slow\-query logging nor query\-stats is enabled\.

2\) When buffering\, the tee writes into a new limitedBuffer that caps retained bytes at 10 KiB \(maxBufferedQueryBytes\) regardless of \-frontend\.max\-body\-size\. The wrapper always reports the full length written so the TeeReader keeps forwarding the full body downstream\; only the retained copy is capped\.

3\) formatQueryString now caps output\: at most 32 params per log record \(maxQueryStringParamsLogged\) with a param\_truncated\_count overflow field\, and each value is truncated to 1024 bytes \(maxQueryStringValueLogged\) with a \"\.\.\.\(truncated\)\" suffix\. One request can no longer produce a multi\-megabyte log line\.

Public interfaces preserved\: NewHandler\, Handler\.ServeHTTP\, HandlerConfig\, flag names\/defaults\, response shape\, and the param\_<name> log key format are unchanged\. The slow\-query\/stats gate is kept and additionally gated on shouldBuffer\, so logging behavior is identical when flags are on\, aside from the new output bounds\.

No Go toolchain in sandbox to run tests\; manual review confirms the diff uses only existing imports and preserves existing TestHandler\_ServeHTTP paths\.

</details>

## Proof

**Recorded evidence level: Static proven.**

Recorded source analysis; patch execution results are not included in this evidence.

<details>
<summary>Recorded source analysis</summary>

Source artifact: 01a142d8889479268e87cf78126ead4d · Issue 01a142c9035a7316a759a335e7327323.

```python
# Layer 2 — Annotated entry->sink walk (SOURCE_ONLY)
# Finding 01a142c0 — Cortex query-frontend unbounded request-body buffering, aggregated within the per-tenant queue.
# CONTEXT LEVEL = SOURCE_ONLY: source-grounded reachability/guard/quantification walk; 'not executed' is complete at this level.
#
# ATTACKER BOUNDARY: authenticated tenant POST /prometheus/api/v1/query_range, X-Scope-OrgID:<tenant>,
#   Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded, body ~<10 MiB, deliberately slow query= .
#
# WALK (real file:line):
#  1. pkg/api/api.go:370           RegisterQueryAPI -> /api/v1/query_range to the single shared frontend Handler (auth=true)
#  2. pkg/api/api.go:143           RegisterRoute wraps ONLY AuthMiddleware (+optional gzip/header mw)
#  3. vendor/.../middleware/http_auth.go:11   AuthenticateUser only ExtractOrgIDFromHTTPRequest -> any valid X-Scope-OrgID passes
#  4. pkg/frontend/transport/handler.go:131    COPY #1: MaxBytesReader(MaxBodySize=10MiB) then io.TeeReader(r.Body,&buf)
#  5. pkg/frontend/transport/handler.go:136    f.roundTripper.RoundTrip(r) — Handler goroutine stays on stack holding buf
#  6. pkg/frontend/transport/roundtripper.go:35 grpcRoundTripperAdapter.RoundTrip -> server.HTTPRequest(r)
#  7. vendor/.../httpgrpc/server/server.go:156  COPY #2: body,_ := ioutil.ReadAll(r.Body) -> httpgrpc.HTTPRequest.Body (also fills buf via Tee)
#  8. pkg/frontend/transport/roundtripper.go:39  RoundTripGRPC(ctx, req): copy #2 carried into blocking gRPC round trip
#  9. pkg/frontend/v1/frontend.go:163            request{request: req, response: chan(1)} references req (copy #2)
# 10. pkg/frontend/v1/frontend.go:334            queueRequest -> EnqueueRequest (ONLY concurrency gate)
# 11. pkg/scheduler/queue/queue.go:96            non-blocking select: overflow -> default -> ErrTooManyRequests -> HTTP 429 (buffers NOT freed)
# 12. pkg/scheduler/queue/user_queues.go:110      channel size = maxUserQueueSize = MaxOutstandingPerTenant

author: vincelwt
body:
Linear: GLO-866

## What was wrong

After the close, Gloom Cloud picked the Gainers and Losers candidates by each quote's latest print, after-hours trades included. Since #1860 (GLO-863) the list re-ranks rows by the regular-session move, but only within the ~50 rows the server sends, so a stock that closed up big and fell after hours could miss Gainers entirely.

## Fix

The server now selects and ranks by a `session` the client names (vincelwt/gloomberb-platform#1188): `regular`, the last completed regular session's move, or `extended`, the latest print. This change sends it explicitly:

- The MOST pane and `fn MOST` ask for `regular`, the basis `rankMoverQuotes` ranks by, so the server's candidates are the session's movers.
- `movers gainers|losers` asks for `regular`, or `extended` with `--session extended`.
- Pro (`/market/screener`) and free (`/market/movers`) requests both carry it; Most Active and the session lists (pre-market, after-hours, gaps) send none.
- The client cache keys each session apart (`screener:day_gainers:count=50:session=regular`), so a regular list is never served from an extended one.

An older server ignores the param (production answers 200 with `session=regular`) and keeps its latest-print candidates; the app's own regular-session ranking from #1860 still applies on top, as today. No layout or text changes.

## Verification

- `bun test src/plugins/builtin/market-movers src/cli/commands/overview-sessions.test.ts src/api-client`: pass.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run knip`: clean.
- New test in `integrity.test.ts`: the request carries `session` for Gainers and Losers and not for Most Active, Pro or free; the regular and extended lists are cached apart; the pane and MOST ask for `regular` unless `extended` is asked.

Merge after the platform PR.

## TR-023 — Companies House (P2-011، تفعيل المالك التسجيل المجاني 2026-10-16)

**ماذا:** محوّل TR-023 (شركة/اسم شركة ← بيانات التسجيل البريطانية) منفذ بنمط إصلاح TR-028: المفتاح المجاني يُقرأ من `IR_COMPANIES_HOUSE_TOKEN` وقت التشغيل ويسافر في ترويسة Authorization (Basic بالمفتاح) لا في الرابط أبداً؛ بلا مفتاح فشل-مغلق قبل أي استدعاء نقل [مقيس: صفر طلبات]؛ البيان يعلن `env` فيسلّم المشغّل المعزول الاسم وحده عبر IPC.

**التصميم:**
- عمليتان: رقم تسجيل ← الملف+المسؤولين+PSC (3 طلبات، النشط فقط)؛ اسم ← بحث (طلب واحد) يعيد أرقام تسجيل تطابق نمط `uk_company_number` (تتغذى التوسعة على مسار الرقم).
- نوعا كتالوج جديدان: `uk_company_number` (Finance، `^\d{8}$|^[A-Za-z]{2}\d{6}$`، مطبّع upperCompact) و`company_name` (Documents، متعدد الكلمات مع `context.required` — درس TR-036). الكتالوج 383 نوعاً (مقيس، بلا ازدواج)؛ الاختبار الذهبي 10/10.
- حساسية `natural_person_gate` (المسؤولون وPSC أشخاص طبيعيون — بوابة المحرك E-02). 404 سلبية لا خطأ؛ 401 يرفض التشغيل؛ قيمة لا تطابق نمط نوعها تُتخطى (D-018).

**حد جديد اكتشفه الاختبار المعزول وأُصلح أحمر أولاً:** مسار العزل كان يسقط ترويسات الطلب (رسالة IPC `op:"fetch"` كانت method+url فقط) — فشل اختبار TR-023 المعزول للسبب الصحيح (Authorization وصلت undefined). الإصلاح: الترويسات تمرر عبر IPC في الاتجاهين مع تحقق صارم من شكلها، والأدلة المسجلة لا تتضمن الترويسات فلا يصل المفتاح السلسلة.

**الأحمر أولاً:** إصلاح ترويسات IPC فشل قبله اختبار معزول للسبب الصحيح؛ جولة القيمة الاصطناعية العالية الإنتروبيا رصدها فحص الأسرار المحلي (generic-api-key) فاستُبدلت بقيمة منخفضة الإنتروبيا `ch-key-2026` وفق سابقة TR-028 (لا ترميز ولا إخفاء) وأُعيد بناء الفرع نظيفاً من main.

**الإثبات:** 9 اختبارات عقد (7 داخل العملية + 2 معزولتان على مسار الإنتاج)؛ السلسلة الكاملة [مقيس]: 114 ملفاً / **1602 ناجحاً/6 متخطاة**؛ lint/typecheck/build/governance exit 0؛ gitleaks نظيف على نطاق الفرع.

**التسجيل:** REGISTRY (uk_company_number/company_name مع فحص مدخل قبل فتح القضية) + تقييم TL-4b0199a8 محدث بسجل التنفيذ؛ STATUS/WORKLOG محدثان في كل إيداع.

ملاحظة: الفروع السابقة للـPR (TR-034/TR-032) مدموجة — هذا الفرع نظيف فوق main@84a47a0 بثلاثة إيداعات (تنفيذ + دورتا تصحيح موثقتان).

author: diego-choi
body:
## Problem

`New` / `NewWithBytes` return `Invalid JPEG header` for a JPEG that other decoders (libjpeg, Go's `image/jpeg`) open fine.

The file I hit has an XMP APP1 segment at offset `0x40b6` whose length field says 32031, but the segment data actually continues for 16,611 more bytes (libjpeg reports `Corrupt JPEG data: 16611 extraneous bytes before marker 0xee` and carries on). After seeking past the declared length, the next real marker (APP14, then DQT) starts at an even offset, while the seek landed on an odd offset (48599).

## Cause

`readMarker()` reads two bytes per call (`Read(mark)`) and, if they are not a `0xFF xx` pair, reads the next two. So after the seek only odd offsets are ever tested as a marker's first byte, and a marker that starts at an even offset is stepped over. The scan then misreads RST markers (`FFD0`..`FFD7`) in the entropy-coded data as segments with a length, skips around, hits EOF, and returns `ErrInvalidJPEG`.

The two-byte step was introduced in 1777f74 ("add New() with io.SeekReader"), when `bytes.Reader.ReadByte()` was replaced by `io.ReadSeeker.Read`. It stayed hidden because in a well-formed file the length field is exact, so the position after a seek is always the start of a marker.

## Fix

Three fix commits, plus two small follow-ups:

1. `readMarker()` now scans one byte at a time, following libjpeg's `next_marker()`: discard bytes until `0xFF`, skip further `0xFF` fill bytes, ignore `0xFF 0x00` (stuffed byte), otherwise return the marker. Any read failure, EOF included, still returns 0, so callers still return `ErrInvalidJPEG`. Segment bodies are still skipped with `Seek`; the byte-wise scan only runs between segments. The quality formula and public API are unchanged.
2. `New()` SOI check: `sign[0] != 0xff && sign[1] != 0xd8` became `||`. With `&&`, input starting with `FF xx` or `xx D8` was accepted.
3. `cmd/jpegq`: remove the call to `jpegquality.SetLogger`, which no longer exists since the move to `log/slog`, so `go vet ./...` and `go build ./...` work again.
4. Tests: assert that the fixture's DQT is at the offset the new cases rely on, and keep failure messages readable.
5. README: the "Custom logger for debug" section still showed `SetLogger`; it now shows `slog.SetDefault` with a debug-level handler.

No API change; no new API beyond what the repo already requires (`log/slog`, Go 1.21+). The `go` directive in `go.mod` is untouched.

With the fix, the original file reports quality 98 from both `NewWithBytes` and `New(*os.File)`; before it failed with `Invalid JPEG header` on both.

## Tests

All added to `jpegquality_test.go` as subtests that modify the existing `jpegData1` fixture, so no new fixture was added. The existing expectations (76, 88) are unchanged.

Expect quality 76:
- odd-length garbage after APP0
- even-length garbage after APP0 (regression guard; passes before the fix too)
- a single `0xFF` fill byte before DQT (`FF FF DB`)
- garbage containing `FF 00`, odd total length
- APP0 length field one byte short

Expect `ErrInvalidJPEG` (the branch where `readMarker` returns 0):
- EOF after garbage, after a lone `FF`, after `FF FF`, after `FF 00`

Expect `ErrInvalidJPEG` (SOI check):
- input starting `FF 00`
- input starting `00 D8`

## Benchmark

Measured with a throwaway harness outside the repo (`testing.Benchmark`, median of 5 runs per row), same source for before (`3f50304`) and after (this branch). Go 1.27.2, darwin/arm64, Apple M1 Max (10 cores). `slog` output was discarded (`slog.NewTextHandler(io.Discard, nil)`), so logging cost is not included. `os.File` rows seek to 0 before each iteration and reuse the file. No `Benchmark*` functions are added to the repo.

Inputs: `jpegData1` (14,061 bytes, well-formed); the real-world file above (4,807,978 bytes, 16,611 extraneous bytes); and "garbage + EOF" = the first 0x14 bytes of `jpegData1` (SOI + APP0) followed by 1 MiB of `0x20` and nothing else (1,048,596 bytes). Garbage + EOF is rejected in both versions; the original file only succeeds after the fix, so its "before" time is the time to fail.

| Input | Reader | Before (ns/op) | After (ns/op) |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `jpegData1` (14,061 B) | `NewWithBytes` | 253 | 278 |
| `jpegData1` (14,061 B) | `New(*os.File)` | 4,138 | 5,119 |
| original (4,807,978 B) | `NewWithBytes` | 693,400 (fails) | 100,207 (quality 98) |
| original (4,807,978 B) | `New(*os.File)` | 98,254,878 (fails) | 7,836,838 (quality 98) |
| garbage + EOF (1,048,596 B) | `NewWithBytes` | 1,695,430 | 6,293,472 |
| garbage + EOF (1,048,596 B) | `New(*os.File)` | 245,949,066 | 492,271,111 |

Iteration counts per run (before / after): `jpegData1` bytes \~4.7M / \~4.3M, file \~290k / \~235k; original bytes \~1,735 / \~10,000-12,000, file 12 / \~150; garbage bytes \~705 / \~190, file 5 / 2-3.

Reading: for well-formed input the cost is essentially unchanged with an in-memory reader (+25 ns); on `*os.File` it goes from about 4.1 µs to 5.1 µs because the gap between segments is now read byte by byte. The cost grows with the number of non-marker bytes the scan has to step over: on a bare `os.File` each byte is one `read` syscall (about 0.5 µs per byte here, so \~0.5 s for 1 MiB of garbage, 2x the old 2-byte step), and with `bytes.Reader` about 6 ns per byte.

If you scan untrusted files through `New(*os.File)`, load the file with `os.ReadFile` and call `NewWithBytes`. That avoids the per-byte syscalls entirely. I did not add buffering inside the library, because it would have to keep the buffer position consistent with `Seek`, which is a larger design change.

## Known issues not addressed here

Left as-is to keep this PR focused:

- 16-bit precision DQT detection: `tableindex` is masked with `& 0x0f` before `tableindex>>4` is tested, so the 16-bit branch is never taken.
- The result of `rs.Read()` is not checked for short reads.
- No buffering inside the library: on an unbuffered `io.ReadSeeker` such as `*os.File`, the byte-wise scan costs one read call per byte between segments (see Benchmark).
- The README "Output example" still shows the pre-slog log format.
- When a DQT segment lists the chroma table before the luma table, `cumsf` / `cumsf2` are not reset and keep accumulating.
- Standalone markers (SOI `D8`, EOI `D9`, RST `D0`..`D7`, TEM `01`) carry no length field, but `readQuality()` reads a length after every marker. If the garbage before a DQT contains a byte sequence like `FF D0`, it is taken for a segment (`ErrShortSegment` or a wrong `Seek`). The recovery added here therefore covers garbage that contains no `FF` followed by a marker-like byte other than `00` or `FF`. The file that motivated this PR meets that condition (the extraneous bytes are leftover XMP text).

author: zhiyao
body:
## Summary

Website copy catch-up for the `herdcats-bridge` Timeline host helper (v0.1.4). Existing security claims ("no relay / no cloud daemon") stay true — the helper runs on demand over SSH only while Timeline is open — but the site never disclosed that the app can now install optional companion software on the host. This PR closes that gap across four pages (review findings F1–F9).

```diff
 web/app/
 ├── support/page.tsx   # F1: "other software" FAQ explains why Timeline needs the helper
 │                      # F7: new troubleshooting entry for missing/failed installs
 │                      # F8: new FAQ "What is the Timeline helper, and why does Timeline need it?"
 ├── privacy/page.tsx   # F2: §4 paragraph — what the helper reads, GitHub download, removal
 │                      # F3: §1 summary bullet · F4: §9 adds GitHub to third parties
 ├── terms/page.tsx     # F5: §4 optional companion installs · F6: §8 adds GitHub
 └── about/page.tsx     # F9: "no relay or companion server" → helper-aware wording
```

Copy leads with *why* (a terminal pane is a scrolling log; the helper reads the structured transcript for a readable conversation) and keeps optionality explicit (Terminal, Compose, voice, and photos never need it). Wording mirrors the in-app setup sheet.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `herdcats-bridge` appears nowhere on the site; the support FAQ claims only `quota-axi` is optional; Privacy/Terms have no helper or GitHub-download disclosure.
  **After:** `bun run build` passes with all 16 routes prerendered; rendered HTML confirms the two new support sections, sidebar anchors matching their heading ids (`using-app-what-is-the-timeline-helper-and-why-does-timeline-need-it`, `troubleshooting-timeline-helper-missing-or-install-failed`), the Privacy §1/§4/§9 additions, and both "Last updated" dates bumped to 16 October 2026.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way — website copy only, trivially revertible.

**Blast Radius:** marketing/legal pages only. No app, bridge, or protocol code touched. The landing page intentionally stays unchanged (its copy makes no daemon/relay claim).

author: offgridwithjd
body:
Stacked on #1473 (merge after it). Two commits: `2a698cd6` (the twin and the shell fix) and `8d36c7a4` (the ledger seed).

## What was wrong
The suite pins the descriptor's bytes and then claims the table "reads back". With `PgColumnarEncdescReadEntry` taking rawLen and encLen from each other's offsets (a reader-side drift), **the shell stayed 16/16 green**:
- the bytes on disk were right, so every byte arm passed;
- `count(*)` and `sum(a)` are answered from the catalog and the zone maps' sums, without decoding a page.

A decoding read of the same table fails (`native chunk length does not match descriptor`). **"every row reads back as the generator wrote it (a decoding read)"** compares every row's text with the generator's, and goes red.

## Mutations of the codec (PG18)
| mutation | old shell (16) | new shell (17) | twin |
|---|---|---|---|
| the reader swaps rawLen and encLen | **green** | red: the decoding read | red: same |
| the writer swaps rawLen and encLen | red: both rawLen arms | and the decoding read | red: rawLen |
| NO_VALIDITY never set | red: the 3 flags arms | and the decoding read | red: flags |
| version and flags bytes swapped | red: the 6 version and flags arms | and the decoding read | red: version |

## The twin
`test_native_encdesc_golden.py` carries all 17 checks by the shell's name (`compare_to_bash`: 8 literal, 3 template, 0 missing). The per-column arms use the shell's `column $col …` names.

## Runs
Head is 17/17 in both twins on each of 15, 16, 17, 18 and 19.

## Ledger
- The suite had no rows. All 17 enter, and 9 are dated.
- Eight arrive never:
  - the vectorCount, valueCount, length and trailer arms, which no mutation here moves;
  - the count and sum read-backs, which never decode.
- `suites_not_covered` 206 → 205. The census is 3956 / 2854 / 1102.
- `pgc_ledger.py gate` returns rc 0.

## Counts and guards
- `cluster_tests` 694 → 695, and pytest collects 695.
- `COMPLETE` gains the suite, and TESTS.md gains §160.
- The NO_CLUSTER guards pass (438), `harness_selftest.sh` passes, and `docs_style.sh` passes.
