author: hreddygayam
body:
## Why

The File Format API TCK (apache/iceberg#15415) has no concrete binding for the generic (`Record`) object model — only Spark and Flink, whose engine row types cannot represent several Iceberg types. As a result, type coverage that only the file formats + generic model support (for example geospatial) could not be exercised at all. This adds the generic binding and closes the V3 **geometry/geography** coverage gap.

## What

- **`TestGenericFormatModel`** — a `BaseFormatModelTests<Record>` binding that runs the full TCK matrix against Avro, ORC and Parquet with the generic object model.
- **`Geometry` / `Geography` data generators** (default `OGC:CRS84`), registered in `DataGenerators.ALL`.
- **`FEATURE_GEOSPATIAL`** feature gate: ORC has no geospatial object-model support (`IllegalArgumentException: Unhandled type GEOMETRY`), so it is declared missing and `supportsGenerator` skips the geo generators for ORC. Avro and Parquet round-trip geospatial values and are covered.
- Spark/Flink engine bindings add `GEOMETRY`/`GEOGRAPHY` to `UNSUPPORTED_TYPE_IDS` so the geo-only generators are cleanly skipped there (via the existing `assumeThat` path).
- The generic binding normalizes nested non-`Record` structs — the `_partition` metadata column materializes as `PartitionData` — back into `GenericRecord` for comparison.

## Testing

`./gradlew :iceberg-data:test --tests "*TestGenericFormatModel"` → **420 tests, 0 failures, 26 skipped**. All 28 geometry/geography parameterizations pass on Avro and Parquet; ORC is gated out. `:iceberg-data:spotlessJavaCheck` passes.

Empirically-confirmed geo round-trip support (generic engine):

| Format | geometry | geography |
|--------|----------|-----------|
| Avro | PASS | PASS |
| ORC | unsupported (gated) | unsupported (gated) |
| Parquet | PASS | PASS |

> Note: the data module is verified here. The Spark/Flink changes are two-constant additions to existing `Set.of(...)` exclusion sets; their module test suites should be run before merge.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Non-default CRS / `EdgeAlgorithm` round-trip coverage.
- Wire ORC geospatial object-model support, then drop `FEATURE_GEOSPATIAL` from ORC's missing set.

Relates to apache/iceberg#15415.

author: coryfinnegan
body:
Closes #112

## What changed
`POST /api/v1/scan-sessions/{id}/identify` is real (viewer, like `barcodes`). The phone posts what it read (text and fields, never an image) and gets candidates grounded in the catalogue.

- **Snap:** one `scan_snaps` row per `snapId` (trigger, engine, item count, fallback reason; `asset_id` null). Idempotent per `snapId` under the session lock: a retry or concurrent twin gets the same candidates, none new. A `snapId` used by another session is 409 without saying whose.
- **Grounding** (`Application/Scanning/Identify/IdentifyGrounding`, session-free so EVAL-1a can call `GroundAsync`): local trigram search, then providers (cached by the provider layer), scored with `MatchScorer` and the live `IOptionsMonitor<ScoringOptions>`. `TextSearchResolver` (SearchForCandidate.cs) was split into `FindLocalAsync` / `AskProvidersAsync` / `Score` (pure, static); `SearchAsync` composes them with unchanged behaviour. Provider failure with nothing good found is `Pending`, not `NotFound`.
- **Never trust the model alone:** the phone's kind/format/platform only tune the weights; an item the catalogue and providers can't support is `NotFound`; `Matched` only comes from the scorer. Extra fields like `confidence` are ignored.
- **`localMatchReleaseId`:** honoured only for a global release or one owned by the session's library (explicit check, not just the query filter); otherwise ignored, never echoed, and the item is resolved by text.
- **Ownership and defaults:** reuse `CandidateResolver.ApplyAsync` (exact owned: Skip; otherwise Add; user decisions never overwritten).
- **Immediate vs pending:** items resolve in parallel inside `ResolveBudget` (2 s); the rest stay `pending` and `ResolvePendingIdentify` (job `scan.identify_resolve`) finishes them from the read stored in `inferred`; `candidate.updated` reaches the SSE feed through the existing cursor. A job that still can't answer sets `error`.
- **Limits:** the body is read inside the handler, after the 404/403 filters, bounded to 256 KB (413); non-JSON/image is 415; more than 40 items or an item over 16 KB is 400; control and invisible format characters are stripped. No text, titles or keys in logs or traces (the trace holds provider, outcome, latency, score, profile).
- **Contract (deliberate):** `IdentifyItem.format` (`ReleaseFormat`), `IdentifyItem.year`, `IdentifyRequest.fellBackFrom` (`FallbackReason`). Without the format a VHS and a DVD of one film are indistinguishable. Snapshot updated for these, plus the new 409/413/415 responses and the endpoint no longer being a 501 stub.

### Scoring-profile rules (first row that fits wins; `ScoringProfileSelector`, pure, table-driven)
1. Tape format (VHS/Betamax) with completeness `cart_only` or `disc_only` -> **BareLabel**
2. Completeness `disc_only` -> **BareLabel**
3. Completeness `cart_only`, or a cartridge/card format with no stated completeness (null / `n_a`) -> **LooseCartridge**
4. 4 or more items in the snap -> **ShelfSpine**
5. Otherwise -> **Cover** (a boxed game, a sleeve, a DVD case, a single book)

## Tests added
- Locked (first commit, red then green): high confidence without support is `NotFound`; a below-threshold read is never auto-accepted and commit ignores it; a foreign/missing/other-library `localMatchReleaseId` is ignored and never echoed (including for a user in both libraries); a viewer identifies and sees ownership but gets 403 on accept/search/commit; 404 for another library's or user's session, 401 signed out, 200 for every role; same `snapId` re-post and 6 concurrent posts make one set; log capture and trace check for item text, titles, local ids and provider keys.
- Behaviour: profile table (Application.Tests); VHS vs DVD; invented title; provider timeout leaves only that item pending, job then `error`; job resolves pending; job never overwrites a decision; near-miss pair with the right one first; exact owned = Skip, other format = Add; valid `localMatchReleaseId` is Matched; snap row contents; source mapping; inferred chips; control characters; limits (41 items, 17 KB item, 280 KB body, image, bad JSON, missing fields); closed session; snap id in another session.

## Gate
`scripts/check.ps1`: restore, build (warnings as errors), format, 1634 tests, app check all green. `origin/main` merged afterwards (app-only changes).

## Notes for the lead
- **Hot-file touches (small):** `Api/Scanning/ScanningEndpoints.cs` (identify mapping), `ScanningRequests.cs` (the three contract fields), `ScanningServices.cs` (one line: `services.AddIdentify();`, registrations live in `Api/Scanning/Identify/IdentifyServices.cs`), `Application/Scanning/SearchForCandidate.cs` (the `TextSearchResolver` split above). Possible conflicts with #115 in `ScanningEndpoints.cs` / `ScanningServices.cs`.
- **Authorization matrix:** the `identify` row now has `allowed: BadRequest` (`{}` has no `snapId`, so the handler is reached) instead of the 501 stub default. Role coverage for identify is also in `IdentifyLockedTests`.
- **`contracts/openapi.json`:** regenerated (the build step needs `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development`). Will conflict with other round-1 PRs that change the contract; regenerate after merging.
- **docs/04 change to make** (row for `identify`): body `{ snapId, trigger, engine, fellBackFrom?, items: [{ localId, text, title?, creator?, edition?, completeness?, kind, format?, year?, platform, localMatchReleaseId? }] }`, at most 40 items, 16 KB per item, 256 KB per body (413), JSON only (415). Returns `{ candidates }`; slow items are `pending` and arrive as `candidate.updated`. The "top candidates' `artworkUrl`s" sentence belongs to SCAN-2b.
- **No migration**, no new packages. `IOptionsMonitor<ScoringOptions>` resolves defaults until SCAN-2d binds the live options; no code change needed here then.
- The duplicate rule is the barcodes one (exact owned = Skip, else Add); a soft "you own this on another format" hint is not added to the candidate (no field for it today).

## Check at the next checkpoint
POST a hand-written read of a loose cart with curl (`completeness: "cart_only"`, `format: "game_cartridge"`, `platform: "Nintendo 64"`, a title) and see the card arrive; the app side is CAM-3b.

_Requested by **Fabricio** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01R5YHT6eSVhXu3cne3jdExN?thread=cmsg_01R5YHT6eSVhXu3cne3jdExNHxsKN1UHLvhuHRT8Rt34A2)_

Before: with maven-surefire-plugin 3.5.3 and older, a JUnit4 `initializationError` run by the vintage engine (for example an invalid test class with a parameterized `@Test` method) came without a test name and was printed as `✘ null`.

author: choughton
body:
## Summary

Test-only change. Adds `test_epic_close_sends_the_finalizer_the_configured_commit_mode`, which checks that `run_epic_close` builds the finalizer prompt from `config.commit_mode`. In dispatcher mode the prompt says "Dispatcher commit mode is on" and tells the finalizer to leave the handoff uncommitted.

## Why

A self-host finalizer committed `docs/handoff/HANDOFF.md` on local main (2026-10-15). The investigation found the fix was already on main in #48 (9f7b5de):

- `ledger_updater_prompt(handoff_path, commit_mode)` gives the finalizer the dispatcher-mode commit instruction. The finalizer does not go through `_with_commit_mode_instruction`, because its commit instruction is part of its prompt.
- After the finalizer runs, `undo_planner_handoff_commits(..., role="finalizer", may_commit_other_files=True)` undoes a commit that holds only the handoff and stops the loop when a commit mixes the handoff with other files.

The incident run used a pinned dispatcher at 67066c0 (#46), which predates #48. The existing tests cover the prompt text and the guard, but not the step where `run_epic_close` passes the configured mode into the prompt. This PR adds that test.

## Test plan

- `python -m pytest tests -q`: 1418 passed, 18 skipped (before this test was added)
- Mutation check: with the `commit_mode` argument removed from `run_epic_close`, the new test's `dispatcher` case fails.

No CHANGELOG entry, because no behavior changes.

author: dmontagu
body: > Stacked on #10292; will be retargeted to `main` when that merges. ### Why #10292 lets a plain function be used as an evaluator, but a dataset using one can't be saved to a file. This saves a function evaluator under the function's name, the same name already recorded as the result's `source`, so dataset files, hosted datasets and traces identify it the same way. Loading takes the functions back in `custom_evaluator_types`; nothing is imported from the file. ### New public surface None. `custom_evaluator_types` on `Dataset.from_file`, `from_text`, `from_dict`, `to_file` and `model_json_schema_with_evaluators` now also accepts evaluator functions, type-checked against the dataset's type parameters. ### User-visible behavior ```python dataset = Dataset[str, str, Any]( name='shouting', cases=[Case(inputs='hello world', evaluators=[word_count])], evaluators=[FunctionEvaluator(exact_match, evaluation_name='matches', version='v2')], ) dataset.to_file('shouting.yaml', custom_evaluator_types=[exact_match, word_count]) # used to raise loaded = Dataset[str, str, Any].from_file('shouting.yaml', custom_evaluator_types=[exact_match, word_count]) ``` ```yaml evaluators: - word_count evaluators: - exact_match: evaluation_name: matches version: v2 ``` - The JSON schema lists each function with its optional `evaluation_name` and `version`. - Only a plain `def` function can be saved. A lambda, bound method, `functools.partial` or other callable has no name that identifies it (a bound method's or partial's name doesn't capture its instance or arguments), so saving a dataset that uses one still raises, as does passing one in `custom_evaluator_types`. - A function whose name clashes with another custom evaluator raises a `ValueError` asking to rename it; like a custom class, a function may replace a default evaluator of the same name. - The "not in the provided `custom_..._types`" error now says "include it" instead of "include its type". Follow-up outside this repo: the Logfire SDK's hosted-dataset upload builds evaluator specs with `dataclasses.asdict` rather than the evaluator's own serialization, so it fails on a function evaluator with "Object of type function is not JSON serializable"; it will be switched to the evaluator's serialization separately. ### Verification [`tests/evals/test_function_evaluators.py`](tests/evals/test_function_evaluators.py): YAML/JSON round trip with case- and dataset-level, sync and async functions next to a class evaluator, re-serialization stability, JSON schema, `from_dict`, unnamed callables, name collisions, load errors, and pyright-checked `custom_evaluator_types` typing. The docs example in `docs/evals/evaluators/custom.md` pins the saved file. ### What changes for existing users Nothing, other than the error-message wording above. ### Checklist - [x] No **breaking changes** in accordance with the [version policy](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/docs/version-policy.md). - [x] Any permitted **compatibility impact** has a label, warning, migration, release note, and exact API-check waiver. - [x] **PR title** is fit for the [release changelog](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/releases).

author: continuum-beta-iad[bot]
body:
Raw Postgres driver errors returned in gRPC status and span status of ListProducts\/SearchProducts

## Risk assessment

**Severity: Low**

**Likelihood: Moderate · Impact: Very low**

| Dimension | Recorded assessment | Basis |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reachable from attacker | Yes | Code |
| Configuration required | Yes | Finding |
| Access required | None | Code |
| User interaction required | No | Finding |
| Attacker gains | Read | Finding |
| Blast radius | Own scope | Finding |
| Target value | Low | Finding |

<details>
<summary>Assessment reasons and what could change this assessment</summary>

### Reachable from attacker

src\/frontend\-proxy\/envoy\.tmpl\.yaml exposes \/jaeger\/ on the public Envoy listener \(lines 48\-52\) with no auth filters in the http\_filters chain \(only fault \+ router\)\. The frontend\-proxy publishes ENVOY\_PORT to the host\. An anonymous internet caller can browse product\-catalog traces and read the span status description containing the raw Postgres error\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the frontend\-proxy is not actually bound to a public interface in the deployed environment\, or that an upstream ingress enforces auth on \/jaeger\/\.

### Configuration required

Two non\-default conditions must hold\: \(1\) the optional observability profile \(compose\.observability\.yaml\) must be running so Jaeger and the \/jaeger\/ Envoy route resolve\; \(2\) a database fault \(missing schema\/table\, permission error\, dial failure\) or the productCatalogLockContention flag must be present\, because loadProductsFromDB\/searchProductsFromDB use static SQL with bound parameters — request input cannot induce a pq error\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the observability profile is enabled by default in the target deployment AND that routine DB errors are already generated under normal load would make this FALSE\.

### Access required

The \/jaeger\/ route on the public Envoy listener has no authentication filters — the http\_filters chain contains only envoy\.filters\.http\.fault and envoy\.filters\.http\.router \(no ext\_authz\, jwt\, basic\_auth\, rbac\)\. Jaeger UI itself is served unauthenticated\. Anonymous internet users can read span status descriptions\.

**What could change this assessment:** Discovery of an ext\_authz \/ JWT \/ basic\-auth filter on the Envoy listener or on the Jaeger upstream would raise this tier\.

### User interaction required

The attacker directly browses \/jaeger\/\, selects the product\-catalog service\, and reads the errored span\'s status description\. No other user needs to click\, approve\, or render anything\. The attacker can also trigger errors themselves via the publicly reachable flag UI or by waiting for ambient DB faults\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that only an authenticated operator can navigate the Jaeger UI or that traces are only rendered on operator action\.

### Attacker gains

The finding demonstrates that an anonymous user can read raw Postgres driver error messages \(schema\/table names\, DB role\, internal host\:port\, driver diagnostics\) via the unauthenticated public Jaeger UI span status descriptions\. This is purely an information disclosure — no code execution or state modification\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the leaked error messages contain actual credentials \(e\.g\.\, full password in a connection error\) rather than just topology\/schema metadata would still keep this as \'read\'\; nothing in the finding shows modification capability\.

### Blast radius

The disclosed information is operational metadata about the product\-catalog service\'s own database connection \(schema name \'catalog\.products\'\, role \'astronomy\_user\'\, host \'astronomy\-db\:5432\'\)\. It is not another user\'s data — all users would see the same shared internal infra details\. The validation also notes these values are already in the public \.env file of this open\-source demo\. No cross\-tenant boundary\; this is a single\-tenant demo application\.

**What could change this assessment:** Evidence that the error messages leak per\-user data \(e\.g\.\, another customer\'s query parameters or PII in error context\) would elevate to other\_users\_in\_tenant\.

### Target value

The exposed data is operational metadata\: internal DB hostname\, port\, role name\, schema\/table names\, and driver diagnostic text\. These are internal identifiers and configuration\, not credentials\, PII\, financial data\, or auth state\. The validation notes the same DSN\-derived server\/port\/db\-name is already in every otelsql span and in the repo\'s committed \.env file\, so the error\-text leak adds no credential\/PII exposure beyond topology hints\.

**What could change this assessment:** If the pq error text actually included authentication secrets \(e\.g\.\, echoed password in a \'password authentication failed\' message with the password visible\) that would raise to high\; the finding only lists username\, not password values\, in the example messages\.



</details>

## Remediation

Updated ListProducts and SearchProducts in src\/product\-catalog\/main\.go so they no longer leak the wrapped lib\/pq error through the gRPC status message or the OpenTelemetry span status description\. Both handlers now\:

<details>
<summary>Recorded change details</summary>

\- Log the detailed wrapped error server\-side via \`logger\.Error\(msg\, slog\.Any\(\"error\"\, err\)\)\` \(same slog pattern already used elsewhere in the file\)\. \- Set a generic span status description \(\`\"failed to load products\"\` \/ \`\"failed to search products\"\`\)\. \- Return \`status\.Error\(codes\.Internal\, msg\)\` with the same generic string\.

This matches the existing house pattern used by GetProduct \(which returns a stable \`codes\.NotFound\` message and never includes the raw DB error\) and addresses CWE\-209 by preventing Postgres driver diagnostics \(schema\/table names\, role name\, internal host\:port\, auth failures\) from reaching anonymous Jaeger UI users or any gRPC caller\.

Compatibility\: no changes to function signatures\, RPC methods\, response shapes\, or legitimate success paths\. The gRPC error code remains \`codes\.Internal\`\; only the free\-text message is now stable and generic\. Existing callers already treat these as opaque Internal errors\.

</details>

## Proof

**Recorded evidence level: Static proven.**

Recorded source analysis; patch execution results are not included in this evidence.

<details>
<summary>Recorded source analysis</summary>

Source artifact: 01a143032dca71eb93c4314466122f40 · Issue 01a142eaae327468b3cb4faff85b9198.

```markdown
# Annotated source->sink walk (SOURCE_ONLY, infra level 1) — vuln 01a142e...
# SOURCE: product-catalog span status (ListProducts main.go:377-381, SearchProducts 430-434)
# SINK:   unauthenticated observability control plane on the public Envoy listener
#         (/jaeger/ read, /otlp-http/ ingest write, /opamp/ agent-config control)
#
# ATTACKER BOUNDARY: anonymous internet HTTP caller hitting the frontend-proxy
#   (Envoy) listener, which compose.yaml PUBLISHES ${ENVOY_PORT} to the host
#   (container_name: frontend-proxy, ports: '${ENVOY_PORT}:${ENVOY_PORT}').
#
# ---- NODE 1  src/product-catalog/main.go:377-381 (ListProducts) / 430-434 (SearchProducts)
#   products, err := loadProductsFromDB(ctx)
#   if err != nil {
#       span.SetStatus(otelcodes.Error, err.Error())   // <-- raw wrapped lib/pq error into span status
#       return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to load products: %v", err)
#   }
#   err chain: loadProductsFromDB (main.go:224-250) wraps pq error with %w
#   DSN (compose.yaml:546): postgres://astronomy_user:...@astronomy-db/astronomy_db
#   => leaked recon: schema catalog.products, role astronomy_user, host astronomy-db:5432
#   GUARD on path: NONE (service has no auth; reflection.Register advertises API at main.go:203)

body:
## What this fixes

The native MCP relay and the daemon's direct hook path both derive the portable Git identity of the workspace a call names, so they can compose that identity's saved decisions with the local ones exactly as `resolve_policy_decision_lookup` (`store_portable_project_memory.py`) does.

Until now both of them first scanned the whole store and handed the call back to the Python proxy whenever they found a row bound to another workspace or to another project's portable identity:

- `mcp_relay_decide_saved.rs` deferred with `mcp_relay_saved_remote_policy` or `mcp_relay_saved_portable_workspace`;
- `hook_direct_saved_portable.rs` deferred the saved decision.

A developer with two Git checkouts has rows for both projects in one store, so every relayed MCP call and every hook paid the handoff — a stopped tool call each time — for a store that is entirely ordinary.

## Why the scans protected nothing

Every workspace selector a lookup binds is the probe's own: `policy_decisions` matches `scope = 'workspace' and (workspace = ? or workspace = ?)` against the probe's workspace and its policy key, and `guard_local_once_approvals` matches `workspace is null or workspace = ?`. A row bound to another workspace, or under another project's `git-project:v1:` identity, is read by no lookup of this one. The other scopes — artifact, publisher, harness, global — never read the workspace column at all, in Python or here.

Both paths now answer whenever the identity resolves exactly. A workspace whose identity the resident cannot reproduce still defers (`PortableIdentity::Unknown`), so the fail-closed boundary is unchanged.

## One mirror of `_portable_project_workspace`

The identity is now read through `project_identity::portable_workspace`, with `is_portable_project_identity` beside it: the prefix followed by exactly 64 lowercase hex digits. That also covers the case both paths used to refuse outright — a workspace that already names a portable identity is its own identity, and `resolve_policy_decision_lookup` then returns that identity's restrictive-only lookup *alone*, with no local authority composed beside it. Both paths short-circuit on it now, as `policy_lookup_groups::candidate` already did.

## Tests

- `project_identity_tests.rs`: the predicate's boundaries (63 and 65 digits, an uppercase digit, a digit outside the alphabet) and the workspace that is its own identity, space-stripped.
- `mcp_relay_decide_saved_tests.rs`: a row bound elsewhere answers as a miss instead of deferring; a third project's identity leaves the checkout's own block as it was; a workspace that already names an identity reads that identity alone, so its portable allow never lowers enforcement.
- `hook_direct_saved_portable_tests.rs`: the same two shapes for the hook path.

Rust builds, clippy and the full test suite run in CI.

author: dhe-eraj-s
body:
Closes #52.

#52's last open item is the Windows recipe, and the issue's own last comment says it needs a design decision first. A Job Object limits processes and memory but not file access, so it cannot confine writes the way the systemd, macOS and Docker recipes do. Real write confinement on Windows would need a low-privilege account with NTFS ACLs, or an AppContainer, plus a CI check that a write outside the workspace is refused. The second is close to the issue's own "not writing a sandbox" non-goal.

This PR takes the cheaper path that is honest about it:
- `examples/deploy/README.md` says to get OS isolation on Windows by running MELRA in one of the existing recipes: Docker Desktop with the Docker recipe, or WSL2 with the systemd unit (`systemd=true` under `[boot]` in `/etc/wsl.conf`). It also says why there is no native recipe.
- `melra doctor`'s `isolation` line on native Windows points to those recipes instead of mentioning a Job Object; macOS keeps its "a sandbox profile cannot be read from inside".
- `docs/INSTALLATION.md` and the CHANGELOG say the same.

A native Windows recipe (low-privilege account plus ACLs, with a `windows-latest` smoke) can be its own issue if Windows service deployments come up.

Tests: the isolation unit test still checks that an unreadable platform says "not visible", and on Windows CI it also checks that the line names WSL2. `docs:check` and the CLI typecheck pass.

author: mikolalysenko
body:
LLM Description written by Claude Code:claude-opus-5-5
-----

Fixes #1598

## Summary
A yarn `portal:` / `link:` / `file:` copy whose `package.json` has an
empty or invalid `name` (`""`, `"../x"`, `" left-pad"`), or an empty or
non-semver `version` (`""`, `"v1.3.0"`), is now treated as naming no
package or no version. This is the same rule #1586 applies to a missing
key. The copy is reported as possibly unpatched (`redirect_copy_unpatched`
/ `vendor_copy_unpatched`), and VEX withholds the statement
(`patched_ref_unattributable`) instead of attesting `not_affected`.

## Root cause
`CopyRef::identity` (`formats/yarn/copy.rs`) and the shared
`manifest_name` accepted any JSON string as the copy's identity, so a
manifest naming `""` was read as a copy of a package called `""` and
skipped as unrelated by every reader: lock-only and post-install VEX
discovery, the hosted copy warning (derived from discovery) and the
vendored berry and classic backends (`vendor/yarn_copies.rs`).

## Fix
- `package_name` validates with `is_registry_package_name`
  (validate-npm-package-name's `validForOldPackages`, already used by the
  vlt reader). `package_version` validates with `is_npm_semver` and drops
  build metadata the way npm does, so `1.3.0+build` is 1.3.0.
- `manifest_name` moved next to them in `copy.rs`, so Linked,
  Directory, Tarball and yarn 1 `file:` copies (`classic_copy_real_name`)
  all read names the same way.
- `docs/ecosystems.md` documents the rule.

## Tests (red → green)
| Issue variant | Test |
| --- | --- |
| `portal:`/`link:` + empty / `../x` / leading-space name, hosted | `hosted_memory_engine::issue_1598_berry_invalid_manifest_name_or_version_is_named` (CLI) |
| `portal:`/`link:` + empty / `v` version | same, plus `vex::discover::yarn::tests::issue_1598_invalid_manifest_name_or_version_contests` |
| berry `file:` directory with empty / invalid name | `issue_1598_invalid_manifest_name_or_version_contests` |
| yarn 1 `file:` directory and tarball with an invalid name | `issue_1598_invalid_manifest_name_or_version_contests` |
| real-binary disk scan of the same project | `hosted_memory_engine::issue_1598_berry_invalid_manifest_name_or_version_is_named_on_disk` |
| unit: every copy kind, npm-invalid names, non-semver versions, build metadata | `formats::yarn::copy::tests::invalid_manifest_name_or_version_identifies_nothing` |

Without the fix (core changes stashed), the CLI test fails with
`portal {"name":"","version":"1.3.0"}: [] left: 0`, and both core tests fail
(`linked "" left: Some(("", "1.3.0"))`). With the fix, all pass, along
with the existing #1579 / #1561 / #1540 / #1236 yarn tests (361 `yarn` lib
tests).

Local gates on `a3a6d63`:
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`: clean. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-features -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --no-fail-fast`: 14584 passed, 10 failed. All 10 come from the sandbox, not this diff. Eight are
  read-only-permission tests that can't fail when run as root (e.g.
  `copy_tree::relax_loop_must_not_traverse_symlinked_root`,
  `pypi_requirements::wire_failure_rolls_back_already_written_files`).
  `e2e_bun_lockb::binary_shared_bundled_record_hosted_pin_is_managed`
  needs `patches-api.socket.dev`, which the sandbox proxy blocks. None of them
  touch yarn code.
- `scripts/yarn-classic-vex-matrix.sh 1.22.22`: pass.
- `scripts/yarn-berry-vex-matrix.sh 4.18.0`: can't run here, because corepack can't
  fetch yarn 4.18.0 behind the sandbox proxy. CI's `yarn-berry` job covers it.

/code-review high: two findings (names npm can't carry, such as zero-width
space, `?` or `@/x`; versions with build metadata or numbers too large for npm)
were fixed in `a3a6d63` by reusing the existing npm validators. The
helper-cycle cleanup was applied too. Not fixed: one extra JSON parse per
linked copy (negligible), and npm package-lock `file:` entries reading
`name` literally (`vex/discover/npm.rs`). That is a different lock format and
reader, and it's left as a follow-up rather than widening this PR.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes shared Yarn copy identity logic used by hosted scans, vendoring, and VEX discovery; behavior is well-covered by new tests but affects security-relevant attribution of linked installs.
> 
> **Overview**
> Fixes **#1598** by tightening how Yarn copy `package.json` identity is derived: empty or invalid npm `name` values and empty or non-semver `version` values are treated like missing keys (#1579), so the copy no longer gets a bogus identity such as `""@1.3.0`.

author: shane-3
body: Fixes #207 ## Problem A run replay starts the project's rerun command with `spawn(…, { shell: true, cwd })` and listens only for `close`. When the registered folder no longer exists, Node emits `error` on the child process instead, and with no listener that error stops the whole neatroots process: collector, steering, MCP and the app. Registering a rerun command never checked the folder, so a typo or a later-deleted folder (a removed worktree) leads straight to it. ## What changes - **`replay/replay.ts`**: listen for the child's `error` event. The replay is marked `failed` through the existing `startRun` catch, the kill timer is cleared, and neatroots keeps running. When the cause is a missing folder, the message says so and how to fix it (`the rerun folder … doesn't exist. Register it again: neatroots rerun add …`) instead of Node's `spawn /bin/sh ENOENT`; any other spawn error keeps Node's message. - **`server/api-explore.ts`**: `POST /api/projects/:project/rerun` refuses a command `cwd` that isn't an existing folder (400 `no such folder: …`, nothing saved), worded like the agent-chat check. - **`cli/data.ts`**: `neatroots rerun add --cwd` checks the folder too, since it writes `config.yaml` itself when the server isn't running. The `error` listener is the actual fix: a folder can disappear after it was registered, so the registration checks only catch mistakes earlier. ## Tests Two regression tests in `test/replay-explore.test.ts`: - `fails the replay, not the server, when the rerun folder is gone`: without the fix this test hits the same unhandled `ENOENT` error. - `refuses to register a rerun command in a folder that doesn't exist`: 400 and nothing saved for a missing folder, 200 for a real one. ## Validation Run on Windows 11 (Node 22.19.0, Git Bash): - `npx vitest run test/replay-explore.test.ts -t "rerun folder is gone|refuses to register a rerun"`: both fail on main (`2 failed`, unhandled `spawn … ENOENT`), both pass with this change. - `npx tsc --noEmit` (packages/neatroots): no errors. - `git diff --check`: clean. - End to end with the CLI (`neatroots start`, send a run, `rerun add --cwd` then delete the folder, `neatroots replay`): on main the server exits; with this change the replay fails with the folder message and `/health` still answers. Not run: the full `pnpm test` suite and the Playwright e2e. On native Windows the full suite has unrelated failures on main too (`EBUSY` when tests delete the store, POSIX paths), so I'm relying on CI for Linux and macOS. No UI changes. ## Impact No stored-data or API shape changes. `POST /api/projects/:project/rerun` and `neatroots rerun add` now refuse a `cwd` that doesn't exist, where they used to save it.

author: vinayakss007
body:
## What

#2688 scoped seven widgets and keyed `lib/dashboard/widget-cache.ts` by caller.
`widgets/stats/revenue/route.ts` — "Revenue MTD", live in the registry at
`components/tenant/dashboard/widget-registry.ts:23-24` — is the eighth, and it
got neither half.

It is a `SUM(amount)` over **deals** (`:44-56`) filtered on tenant, tombstone,
the tenant's "won" stage and `date_trunc('month', now())`, wrapped in
`withCache(tid, 'stats-revenue', 300, …)` with the default `scopeKey` of
`'tenant'` (`lib/dashboard/widget-cache.ts:27`). So both #2688 defects were
still open here:

1. A rep whose pipeline tile *beside it* — `widgets/stats/pipeline/route.ts:49`,
   the same deals read, and it does carry
   `ownerScope(auth, 'deals.view_all', deals)` — showed only their own won
   revenue, saw the workspace's number.
2. Whichever caller computed it first served that number to every other caller
   in the tenant for up to 300 s.

The two are the reason #2688 refused to split the fix: a per-caller predicate
behind a shared cache key is a second leak that only shows up under traffic.

## How

Mirror the pipeline widget, invent nothing: `const auth = ctx` before the
closure (the `let ctx` narrowing does not survive into it — the TS2345 that
#2688 hit seven times), `ownerScope(auth, 'deals.view_all', deals)` inside the
`and(...)`, and `ownerCacheKey(auth, 'deals.view_all')` as `withCache`'s fifth
argument. A `deals.view_all` holder gets `undefined` from `ownerScope`, which
`and()` skips, and `'tenant'` from `ownerCacheKey`, so managers keep sharing one
entry and their SQL is byte-identical — both asserted, not assumed.

**One extra finding, folded in:** the tile also counted **archived** deals,
which #2684 hid from every other deals read (`notArchived()` at
`widgets/stats/pipeline:43`, `deals/route.ts:53`). A won deal retired last
week still padded Revenue MTD here. `notArchived()` joins the same `and()`.
This one was not in the issue body — it surfaced while writing the third test.

The `deal_stages`/`pipelines` lookup (`:31-36`) stays tenant-wide on purpose:
stage definitions are tenant configuration, not records with an owner. Pinned
by a test so the next reader does not scope it too.

## Test evidence

Red before green at `57ded7e2`: **4 of 7 assertions failed** — the owner
predicate, the archive term, and both `scopeKey` cases (a rep's `MINE`, a
manager's `'tenant'`, which the route was leaving `undefined`). The 3 controls
that passed before and after: the won-stage/month/tombstone terms it already
had, a manager's unscoped SQL, and the config lookup staying unscoped.

Asserted on the SQL drizzle renders (`new PgDialect().sqlToQuery`) *and* on the
arguments the route hands `withCache` — the same double assertion #2688's suite
uses, because a route can carry the right predicate and still be answered from
the first caller of the TTL window. `can()` is left real; the rule under test
is exactly the permission check.

97 tests green across the dashboard / widget suites (9 files) — #2688's own 32
and the cache-key 7 included, so the shared `withCache` signature did not move.
`tsc --noEmit`, `eslint`, `guard:filesize`, `guard:register-drift` clean.

Closes #2695

author: steveash
body:
## Task

T-1677 (docs/tasks/M2/T-1677-move-and-or-and-xor-onto-the-shared.md): AND, OR and XOR read their arguments through the SPEC-0009 walker, with no change in any result.

## What changed

- `logical_nary` now calls `walk_aggregate_args` with a `const` policy `LOGICAL_ARGS` (`ArgReading::InContext`, `ErrorRule::First`, empty arguments kept). A boolean visitor is keyed on `ItemSource`. The function no longer matches `CalcResult::Range` or `CalcResult::Array` itself.
- New `ArgReading::InContext` (`evaluate_in_context_arg`) keeps today's `evaluate_node_in_context` reading. It turns a cross-sheet range into `#VALUE!` and a direct LAMBDA into `#N/IMPL!`; both are direct errors returned at once, as before. Using `Aggregate` instead would change results for a text "TRUE" cell picked by IF, INDEX, XLOOKUP or LET, which is unprobed, so T-1683 is filed to probe it.
- Direct text is now cast from the value already read, not evaluated a second time.
- SPEC-0009: new consumer-mapping row and an as-built bullet.
- New engine test. It passes on the old code too, which shows the results did not change.

## Evidence

body:
A coloured line at the bottom of every interlaced picture, and each field's first row missing: the Pocket leaves out an interlaced field's first line of DE.

**What it was** (read off a capture of the Dock's HDMI output, `il_test` with a bar code of each row's number and a 240-line window)
- In an interlaced frame, output line k showed the picture's row k + 3: each field's first line was dropped, the frame shifted up one line of the field, and the frame's last two lines were never written, so they showed whatever the scaler's memory held.
- A progressive picture checked the same way shows every line, the first included.

**The fix:** each field of a serrated picture has one line of DE more, black, before its 240 (DE from the line before the field's first). On the Pocket all 480 lines now show the picture's rows 1 to 480, and the bottom edge is black.

**Also in this PR**
- `tb_vi`: a serrated frame has 241 lines of DE, the first black; `tb_soc`'s woven frames leave it out as the Pocket does. `sim/vi_filter/regress.sh`: 42 runs, 0 failed.
- `il_test`: `FULLWIN`, `FLASH` (two pictures in turn, for catching a tear) and `PROGONLY`.
- `docs/resolution.md`: the line, and the tear the Dock shows on a change of picture in 480i. Measured with `FLASH`: the Pocket writes each field over the picture it shows, and its 60.00 Hz output against the 59.94 Hz fields makes the meeting point cross the picture for about 0.75 s every 16.7 s. A progressive picture, the same test, shows no tear in 1,200 frames (the Pocket repeats a frame instead).

**Fits** (`projects/fits.json`): seeds 9, 4, 14 and 5 close; the best, 9, at +0.107 ns over the 128 analyses. 17,151 to 17,207 ALMs.

author: ppeerttu
body:
## Summary

Adds three Gladia settings that the AssemblyAI integration already has equivalents for:

| Attendee setting (`transcription_settings.gladia`) | Sent to Gladia as | AssemblyAI equivalent |
| - | - | - |
| `custom_vocabulary` (+ `custom_vocabulary_default_intensity`) | `custom_vocabulary: true`, `custom_vocabulary_config: {vocabulary, default_intensity}` | `keyterms_prompt` |
| `custom_spelling` — `[{"from": [...], "to": "..."}]` | `custom_spelling: true`, `custom_spelling_config: {spelling_dictionary: {"<to>": [<from>...]}}` | `custom_spelling` (same input shape) |
| `model` — `solaria-1` / `solaria-3` / `solaria-fusion` | `model` | `speech_models` |

`custom_spelling` takes the same input shape as the AssemblyAI setting, so callers can reuse one list for both providers. The adapter converts it into Gladia's dictionary form. Entries that share the same `to` are merged, and duplicate variants are dropped.

Settings that `solaria-3` can't serve are rejected with a 400 when the bot or async transcription is created, instead of failing on every utterance later:
- code switching, from `code_switching: true` with several languages, or from the deprecated `enable_code_switching`
- any language outside `en`, `fr`, `de`, `es`, `it`

Builds on #1073 (language_config). Until that merges, this diff includes its commits.

## Gladia API reference this relies on

From [`POST /v2/pre-recorded`](https://docs.gladia.io/api-reference/v2/pre-recorded/init):

> `custom_vocabulary` (boolean) — "**[Beta]** Can be either boolean to enable custom_vocabulary for this audio or an array with specific vocabulary list to feed the transcription model with"
> `custom_vocabulary_config.vocabulary` — "Specific vocabulary list to feed the transcription model with. Each item can be a string or an object with the following properties: value, intensity, pronunciations, language."
> `custom_vocabulary_config.default_intensity` — "Default intensity for the custom vocabulary" (0–1)
> `custom_spelling` (boolean) — "**[Alpha]** Enable custom spelling for this audio"
> `custom_spelling_config.spelling_dictionary` — "The list of spelling applied on the audio transcription", e.g. `{"SQL": ["Sequel"]}`
> `model` — enum `solaria-1`, `solaria-3`, `solaria-fusion`. "The model used to process the audio. "solaria-1" is used by default."

On the same page, about `solaria-3`:

> **Languages:** English, French, German, Spanish, Italian
> **Single language only** — pass exactly one language in `language_config.languages` (no code switching).

The [models page](https://docs.gladia.io/chapters/introduction/models) disagrees about the language count: "With `"solaria-3"`, there is no code switching. You can pass languages in `language_config.languages` (for example `["fr"]`, or several from EN/FR/DE/ES/IT) so the model can pick among those covered languages." So this PR enforces only what both pages agree on: no code switching, and only the five languages. It doesn't reject several of those five languages. `solaria-fusion` appears in the API enum but isn't described anywhere else in Gladia's docs, so it's passed through without extra checks.

Custom spelling semantics, from the [custom spelling page](https://docs.gladia.io/chapters/audio-intelligence/custom-spelling): keys are "the spelling to write (case-sensitive)" and values are "variant strings to find (case-insensitive; can be multiple words)".

**Not verified against the live API:** I didn't have a Gladia API key. Everything above comes from Gladia's docs and OpenAPI spec (`https://api.gladia.io/openapi.json`).

## Example request body

`{"model": "solaria-3", "languages": ["de"], "custom_vocabulary": ["Kubernetes", {"value": "Jyväskylä", "pronunciations": ["yuvaskula"], "intensity": 0.6, "language": "fi"}], "custom_vocabulary_default_intensity": 0.4, "custom_spelling": [{"from": ["sequel", "s q l"], "to": "SQL"}]}` sends:

```json
{
  "audio_url": "https://api.gladia.io/file/...",
  "language_config": {"languages": ["de"], "code_switching": false},
  "model": "solaria-3",
  "custom_vocabulary": true,
  "custom_vocabulary_config": {
    "vocabulary": ["Kubernetes", {"value": "Jyväskylä", "pronunciations": ["yuvaskula"], "intensity": 0.6, "language": "fi"}],
    "default_intensity": 0.4
  },
  "custom_spelling": true,
  "custom_spelling_config": {"spelling_dictionary": {"SQL": ["sequel", "s q l"]}}
}
```

Empty `custom_vocabulary` / `custom_spelling` lists send nothing, and `default_intensity` is left out when it isn't set.

## Tests

The new tests in `GladiaProviderTest` check the exact request body for model, vocabulary (with and without default intensity), and the spelling conversion, including merging. Schema tests cover valid and invalid values. The `solaria-3` limits are tested on both async transcription creation and bot creation. Against the previous code, every new test fails except the one checking that empty lists send nothing, which guards existing behavior.

author: matejkozlovsky
body:
Stacked on #1631, so the diff includes it until that lands.

On top of #1631, also from #898.

Adds `Accelerator::comp_frame_yuv420_async`: render, submit, return. Planes come later in a per-frame callback from `poll_readbacks`, so the next frame can record while the previous copy runs. Nothing calls it yet; export still uses the sync path. Switching needs a small reorder buffer, I'd do that separately once the API looks right.

- `done` runs exactly once: planes, or `None` on failure/device loss (uses the context's existing bounded readbacks).
- Declined or can't start → `Err(done)`, callback untouched, caller can go CPU. (`GpuContext::try_map_readback`; `map_readback` wraps it.)
- Staging ring of 4; buffers go back only after unmap.
- Max 4 frames in flight, slot reserved before rendering; the 5th call polls (and sleeps briefly if the other frames are still rendering) until one frees.
- `done` runs on whichever thread polls, outside locks. Don't block in it or call back into the accelerator.
- `poll_readbacks` uses a new opt-in `poll_readbacks_busy_ok`, where a wait timeout means "busy". Everything else, `wait()` included, still retires on timeout. (Adds a crate-private `Gpu::wait_for(Duration)` for that test.)

Tests:
- `frames_in_flight_each_get_their_own_planes`
- `in_flight_cap_holds_across_threads` (8 threads × 6 frames, never >4 pending)
- `a_device_failure_fails_every_pending_readback_once`
- `cancelled_readbacks_return_their_buffers_only_once_unmapped`
- `wait_past_its_deadline_retires_but_the_yuv_poll_does_not`
- `declined_async_frames_hand_the_callback_back_unused`
- `async_yuv_defaults_to_the_synchronous_conversion` (render crate)

**Kind: off unless set.** It changes anything only with `LAMP_SPOKEN_TO=on`. Without it the room counts as before.

**Why:** a tool call sets the session's first output, so no `Unanswered` comes, and `RoomTold::spoke` ran only on forwarded audio. A request answered by a call alone ("lights off", then "brighter", each done without a word) was counted as left alone. - `docs/attention.md`: the count also begins afresh after an answer made by a call alone.

**Tests:** `room_told::tests::with_the_switch_a_line_answered_by_a_call_alone_is_no_talk_past_the_lamp` plays the sixth's sequence. With the switch, "a bit more" still rides on the conversation. Without it, the two calls count, as before.

body:
## 概要

Fixes #200

OWASP ZAP のスキャン (EC-CUBE/ec-cube#7190) で、動的クライアント登録 (`POST /register`) への攻撃 222 件のうち 26 件が 500 (システムエラー) になっていました。クライアントの入力の誤りを、保存や値オブジェクトの生成で例外にしたまま返していたことが原因です。RFC 7591 のエラー (400) を JSON で返すよう直します。

## 変更内容

| ファイル | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `Controller/ClientRegistrationController.php` | `client_name` を、保存先の列 (`oauth2_client.name`、`varchar(128)`) に接頭辞 `DCR:` ごと収まる 124 文字に切り詰める。従来は 200 文字で切り詰めており、保存時に DB のエラーで `server_error` (500) になっていた |
| 同上 | `RedirectUri` の生成で例外を捕捉し、`invalid_redirect_uri` (400) を返す。従来は捕捉されず、JSON ではなくシステムエラーの画面になっていた |
| 同上 | 空白・制御文字を含む `redirect_uri` は `invalid_redirect_uri` で拒否する。URI に現れない文字であり、末尾の改行は `RedirectUri` の検証を通って保存され、NUL は PostgreSQL の TEXT 型に保存できない |
| 同上 | `redirect_uris` の件数 (10 件) と 1 件あたりの長さ (2000 バイト) に上限を設ける。保存先は TEXT 型 (MySQL では 65535 バイト) のため、超えると保存時に失敗する |
| 同上 | 本文が JSON の配列 (list) の場合は `invalid_client_metadata` で拒否する。RFC 7591 のメタデータは JSON オブジェクト |
| `Tests/Web/ClientRegistrationControllerTest.php` | 上記の入力検証のテストを追加 |

`grant_types`・`scope`・`token_endpoint_auth_method`・`response_types` は、従来どおり読まずに MCP の固定値で登録します。どの型で送られても 500 にならないことをテストで固定しました。

`league/oauth2-server-bundle` v1.2.3 の `RedirectUri` は、正規表現で空白を含む値を拒否します (Issue 本文では `FILTER_VALIDATE_URL` と書きましたが、この版では正規表現です)。空白・制御文字は値オブジェクトに渡す前に拒否するため、現在の版で例外の捕捉に到達する値は確認できていません。依存の版が変わったときに 500 に戻らないよう、捕捉は残しています。

## テスト

- 追加したテスト: 長い `client_name` が 124 文字に切り詰められて登録されること、不正な `redirect_uri` (空白・タブ・改行・NUL・長すぎる値・件数超過) と不正な本文 (JSON でない・文字列・数値・配列・`redirect_uris` の欠落や型違い) で 400 と JSON のエラーを返すこと、登録で使わない項目がどの型でも 201 になること
- 修正を外した状態では、追加したテストのうち 9 件が失敗することを確認しました (500、または不正な値のまま登録される 201)
- `Tests/` 全体: 159 件中 158 件成功 (EC-CUBE 4.4・PHP 8.2・PostgreSQL 18)。失敗する `SchemaTest::testMutationUpdateStock` は 4.4 (95de337) でも同じく失敗し、この変更とは関係ありません
- PHPStan: `GraphQL/Query/SingleResultQuery.php` の既存のエラー 1 件のみ (4.4 の CI でも同じエラーで失敗しています)。変更したファイルにエラーはありません

author: vpetersson-bot
body:
### Issues Fixed

Sentry `ANTHIAS-C` — `OperationalError: no such table: assets` out of `anthias_viewer.scheduling.generate_asset_list`, reported as "Viewer crashed."

### Description

anthias-server owns the database: its start script runs a dbbackup → migrate pass, with a dbrestore fallback that drops and re-creates every table. The viewer starts in parallel with that, and `main()` builds its `Scheduler` as soon as `wait_for_server` returns.

That wait does not establish that the schema exists:

- it polls `/splash-page`, which the server answers while the migrate/restore is still running, and
- it gives up **silently** after `SERVER_WAIT_TIMEOUT` (60s) and returns anyway — easily reached by a restore on a slow SD card.

`Scheduler()` queries `assets` on construction, so landing in that window kills the viewer on the way up. The container restarts and races again, which is why a single device produced 78 events.

This is the same race, and the same signature, that `wait_for_migrations` has guarded on the celery side since `ANTHIAS-1`. The probe and the polling loop move to `anthias_common/migration_wait.py` so both services share one implementation (the viewer image ships no celery, so the shared module must not import it), and the viewer waits on the schema before constructing its scheduler.

The wait is deliberately unbounded, matching the celery side: a bounded wait is exactly what leaves the caller querying a half-restored schema, and a viewer with no database can do no useful work. It logs on the first miss and every 30s after, naming which service is waiting.

The ordering is asserted directly — a wait placed after `Scheduler()` would be useless, so the viewer test checks that the schema wait happens first.

### Checklist

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code.
- [x] New and existing unit tests pass locally and on CI with my changes.
- [ ] I have done an end-to-end test for Raspberry Pi devices.
- [ ] I have tested my changes for x86 devices.
- [x] I added a documentation for the changes I have made (when necessary).

body:
The ninth fix from the second fidelity audit: a dead crew member can be neither given a post nor trained, as in the original.

## Problem

Since crew members can die (#414 and before it), the Starport's panels still treated the dead as crew:
- **Crew Assignment:** cycling through the files with Left and Right gives the post to each file shown, so passing a dead crew member's file gave them the post. An empty post started on the first file, dead or not.
- **Personnel:** Train offered a dead crew member's skills for training at 300 M.U. a session.

The original refuses both (CONFIRMED in the decompiled code):
- **ASSCREW-OV `WF395`:** a file is assigned only if its status is that of a living crew member (`(status & 3) == 1`). Otherwise `WF2B1` prints "YOU CAN'T ASSIGN " and the crewmember, or "THIS FILE IS EMPTY".
- **PERSONNEL-OV `WF3A3`:** training goes on only for a living crew member. Otherwise `WF192` prints "YOU CAN'T TRAIN ...", or "THERE IS NO ONE HERE TO TRAIN".

author: romange
body:
## Summary
In cache mode every lookup records the entry for a bump in `OnCbFinishBlocking`. Each one hashed the key up to four times, looked it up a second time, and the set was reallocated in every callback. This trims that work without changing which entries move.

## Changes
- `FindInternal` hashes the key once and reuses the hash for `fetched_items_`; new `DashTable` overloads of `Find`, `CVCUponBump` and `BumpUp` take the precomputed hash and assert in debug builds that it matches.
- Entries in the first slot of a regular bucket are not recorded, since a bump leaves them in place.
- The bump lookup compares the full hash instead of accepting any entry with a matching fingerprint, so it no longer bumps a different key and the hash it passes to `BumpUp` is correct.
- `OnCbFinishBlocking` gives the set's allocation back to `fetched_items_` after the loop.

author: ppeerttu
body:
## Summary

Attendee deletes the Gladia transcription (which also deletes its uploaded audio) only when a job finishes successfully. When a job fails, ends with an unknown status, or times out, the audio and job data stay on Gladia for the account's whole retention period. Each of those failures is retryable, so every retry uploads the audio again and leaves another copy behind.

This PR:

- deletes the Gladia transcription on every outcome where a job was created: done, error, unknown status, and polling timeout.
- keeps Gladia's response body (`response_text`) in the failure data when `POST /v2/pre-recorded` is rejected, as the OpenAI, Sarvam and ElevenLabs adapters already do. Until now, a 400/422 caused by invalid settings was stored only as a status code.

## Gladia API reference this relies on

[`DELETE /v2/pre-recorded/{id}`](https://docs.gladia.io/api-reference/v2/pre-recorded/delete): "Delete a pre-recorded transcription and all its data (audio file, transcription)." It returns `202`.

[`POST /v2/upload`](https://docs.gladia.io/api-reference/v2/upload/audio-file) is the only operation on `/v2/upload` in `https://api.gladia.io/openapi.json`. There is no API call that deletes an uploaded file on its own. So if the upload succeeds but `POST /v2/pre-recorded` is rejected, no job exists to delete, and the uploaded file stays until Gladia's retention deletes it.

[Data retention](https://docs.gladia.io/chapters/limits-and-specifications/data-retention): on paid plans, "Audio input | 3 weeks" and "Transcription output | 3 weeks"; on the free plan, 1 year.

**Not verified against the live API:** I didn't have a Gladia API key. In particular, I couldn't check whether Gladia accepts a DELETE for a job that is still `queued`/`processing` when Attendee's polling times out. If it refuses, the failure is logged, as before.

## Tests

New tests in `GladiaProviderTest`:
- an `error` job, an unknown status and a polling timeout each send exactly one DELETE, to the job's result URL;
- a rejected transcribe request stores the Gladia response text and sends no DELETE, since there is no job.

All four fail against the previous code.

author: mesejo
body:
## What

A post-rewrite for both DataFusion compilers, `hoist_sort_keys_out_of_subquery` in the vendored `backends/sql/rewrites.py`. When a plain projection reads a sorted subquery, the sort moves up:

```sql
-- before: DataFusion ignores the inner ORDER BY
SELECT t1.l AS x FROM (SELECT * FROM t ORDER BY m, SUM(k) OVER ()) AS t1
-- after
SELECT t1.l AS x FROM (SELECT *, m AS __sort0, SUM(k) OVER () AS __sort1 FROM t) AS t1
ORDER BY t1.__sort0, t1.__sort1
```

The hidden columns never reach the output. Every reference to the old subquery is rebound field by field, so a correlated reference or an IN needle follows it, while a subquery that reads the old relation as its own input keeps its schema.

- `rewrites.py`: the rewrite. `backends/xorq_datafusion/compiler.py`, `compilers/datafusion.py`: one line each in `post_rewrites`.
- `test_select.py` in both backend test directories: executed row order for both triggers, plus correlated, scalar and IN subqueries over the sorted select.

## Why

`merge_select_select` refuses to fold a projection into a sorted Select when a window function is among the sort keys or the parent is distinct, so the ORDER BY stays in a subquery, and DataFusion drops a subquery ORDER BY. `t.order_by([t.m, t.k.sum().over()]).select(x=t.l)` and `t.distinct().order_by("a").select(a=t.b)` returned unsorted rows with exit 0; duckdb returns the requested order. One rule for the mechanism covers both triggers and any other that keeps a projection out of its sorted parent.

## Verification

`pytest -m "xorq_datafusion or datafusion"` over both backend test directories: 1035 passed, 11 skipped, 3 xfailed. With the rewrite left out of `post_rewrites`, the four trigger cases fail.

## Not addressed

- A sorted or distinct outer Select keeps the subquery ORDER BY as written.
- A window function among the sort keys of a relation reused inside a scalar subquery hits a DataFusion planner limit; same on main.
- A correlated subquery over a Select that `merge_select_select` merges away fails on every backend on main.
- Builds on the shadowed-alias split without changing it.

author: hello-alexmcc
body:
## What

`SMG_VLLM_SERVICER_IMPL=rust` with `python -m vllm.entrypoints.grpc_server` never engaged the servicer switch on vLLM 0.28 and 0.29. On those releases that module is the gRPC launcher itself, so `python -m` runs it as `__main__`: it is never in `sys.modules` under its name, and neither the import-time hook (the launcher's own import of this package) nor the meta-path finder reaches it. The launcher built the AsyncLLM, initialized the engine completely, and only then the Python servicer's guard refused with `RuntimeError: ... the switch ... never ran`. From 0.30 the same command runs a 27-line shim whose `from vllm.entrypoints.launchers.grpc_server import main, serve_grpc` is caught as it loads, which is why the switch worked on one engine build and not on the other; `python -m vllm.entrypoints.launchers.grpc_server` on 0.30+ had the same gap as 0.28.

The hook points are identical from 0.28 through 0.31 (the launcher file is byte-for-byte the same from 0.24.0 to 0.29.0; 0.30 moved it under `launchers/` and left the shim; 0.31 only changed gRPC options and a logging call): the servicer classes imported at module level, then `async def serve_grpc(args)`, then a `main()` that builds the parser with `AsyncEngineArgs.add_cli_args` (which loads this package's plugin), parses, and runs `uvloop.run(serve_grpc(args))`. So the fix is one more place to bind, not a per-version hook:

- `launcher_switch.install_launcher_switch()` also binds the launcher that is the process's `__main__` (`launcher_main()`: runpy names the module in `__main__.__spec__`), by rebinding `serve_grpc` in its namespace, which is what the launcher's `main()` reads. It does so from the two moments this package runs inside `main()` after the body defined `serve_grpc`: vLLM's load of the plugin while the launcher builds its parser (`register()`), and the plugin's parse step on the launcher's own parse (new call there, for a vLLM that loaded the plugins during the launcher's imports). The module object is left as it is; only the dict entry changes.
- One table for the launcher layouts: `LAUNCHERS` (`vllm.entrypoints.launchers.grpc_server`, 0.30 and later; `vllm.entrypoints.grpc_server`, 0.28 and 0.29), `LAUNCHER_MODULES` derived from it, `HOOK_ATTRIBUTE`, `SUPPORTED_VLLM_RELEASES` (`0.28 through 0.31`), `launcher_for_release()` for messages, `supported_launchers()` for a refusal line. Binding goes by what is loaded, never by the version: a main-branch build between two releases carries the next release's layout under the earlier version.
- `--servicer-impl` joins the stock launcher's own parser the way the `--mm-*` flags already do (both key on `serves_grpc`), so the flag form works on `python -m` as well as on `vllm serve`.
- The Python servicer's guard names what is left unreached (a launcher run as a file path, or with the plugin left out of `VLLM_PLUGINS`) and the forms the switch binds.
- README: a "Supported vLLM releases" section with the table, the entry forms, and how to run the smoke.

Per engine: SGLang's and TokenSpeed's switches live in this package's own entry points (`sglang/server.py`, `python -m smg_grpc_servicer.tokenspeed`), which read the selection before any engine process starts; neither has an upstream launcher to bind, so neither changes.

## Tests

- `grpc_servicer/scripts/launcher_switch_smoke.py`: a CPU smoke that runs vLLM's gRPC launcher the way its entry points run it, through to the servicer construction, against a stub engine, one fresh interpreter per case: `python -m` on every launcher module the release has, and `vllm serve <model> --grpc` (the CLI's import of `serve_grpc` after its parse); Rust selected by the variable and by the flag, and the Python default. Rust must hand the process to `serve_rust` before any engine is built (a stand-in returns exit code 7, which the switch raises); Python must build the (stub) engine and construct the servicer on it, running the real guard. Sources: `--launcher-tree` (a `vllm/` tree holding only the launcher files, the rest of vLLM stubbed; this package's modules are the real ones, so the switch installs itself from the launcher's own import exactly as in production) or `--installed` (the installed vLLM with only the engine stubbed; a CPU-only container is enough, no model is read).
- `grpc_servicer/tests/launchers/`: byte-identical copies of the upstream launcher at v0.28.0 (the same file through v0.29.0), v0.30.0 and v0.31.0 with the shim (README with provenance; excluded from ruff like the other vendored upstream file).
- `grpc_servicer/tests/test_vllm_launcher_switch_main.py` (10 tests): the launcher as `__main__` is bound in its namespace for both module names and left a plain module; a `__main__` mid-body is bound by the plugin's parse step; a `__main__` that is not the launcher (the console script, a file path) is untouched; the table and `launcher_for_release`; the guard's message; the flag on the stock launcher's parser; and the smoke on each vendored layout (every form, Rust by variable, Python default: 16 launches) plus the flag form on the 0.28 launcher.
- The existing switch tests (`test_servicer_switch.py`, `test_vllm_rust_servicer.py`) are unchanged and green.

## Release note

The vLLM servicer switch now engages when the gRPC launcher module is run with `python -m` (vLLM 0.28 and 0.29, where `vllm.entrypoints.grpc_server` is the launcher itself; the 0.30+ module by its own name), so `SMG_VLLM_SERVICER_IMPL=rust` takes the Rust path there instead of failing in the Python servicer after the engine initialized; the supported range (vLLM 0.28 through 0.31) and its launcher layouts are documented and smoke-tested on CPU.

## Numbers

The smoke on the vendored upstream launchers (`python -I grpc_servicer/scripts/launcher_switch_smoke.py --launcher-tree grpc_servicer/tests/launchers/<layout> --servicer-root <tree>`; one fresh interpreter per case, CPU only, no vLLM installed), before = this package at `main`, after = this branch:

| launcher layout | cases | before | after |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.28 (`vllm.entrypoints.grpc_server` is the launcher) | 6 | 4 pass; `python -m ... [SMG_VLLM_SERVICER_IMPL=rust]` builds the engine, then exit 1 from the guard; `[--servicer-impl rust]` unrecognized | 6 pass |
| 0.30 (`launchers/` module + shim) | 9 | 6 pass; `python -m vllm.entrypoints.launchers.grpc_server [rust]` builds the engine, then exit 1; the flag unrecognized on both `python -m` forms | 9 pass |
| 0.31 | 9 | 6 pass (same three) | 9 pass |
| `pytest -q grpc_servicer/tests` (generated proto stubs, no engine) | | 978 passed, 33 skipped, 1 failed | 989 passed, 33 skipped, 1 failed (the same test, `test_sglang_health_cleanup.py::test_terminal_probe_finishes_before_rpc_cancellation`, fails on `main` in this environment and is in an untouched suite) |

The same smoke on the launcher files of two main-branch builds, one of each layout (0.28.1rc1.dev388 and 0.29.1rc1.dev347, fetched from upstream at those commits): 6 of 6 and 9 of 9 after. Wall time of the smoke: about 1.6 s per layout.

## Owed

The live proof on an engine: `SMG_VLLM_SERVICER_IMPL=rust python -m vllm.entrypoints.grpc_server --model <model> --port <port>` on a vLLM 0.28/0.29 host reaching the Rust servicer, and the `--installed` smoke in a CPU container of an engine image of each layout (`python -I grpc_servicer/scripts/launcher_switch_smoke.py --installed`, which drives the real CLI, parser and plugin loading with only the engine stubbed). This PR is the compatibility; the start-up refusal of a launcher the switch cannot bind is a separate PR, whose probe must report a bound `__main__` launcher as bound (the second of the two to merge rebases on the first).

author: deehw
body:
A test-only fix: the voice's paced duplex test failed once in a full serial run on this Mac, and its harness could make a block gap the detector refuses. It closes nothing, and the voice itself is unchanged.

**The failure:** on 16 October at 13:40, in one of my full serial gate runs (`--test-threads=1`, with the audio, voice, voice-eval and memory tests), `coordinator::tests::duplex::first_words_older_than_the_provider_takes_are_dropped_before_the_commit` (#936) panicked at `duplex.rs:234`: `called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: Custom { kind: Other, error: "capture discontinuity" }`. Run alone three times it passed each time (2.5 s each).

**The cause:** the harness's `at()` read a paced block at the host clock, once it was at least the paced gap (40 ms) after the previous read. A host late to wake, on a loaded runner, could make the gap longer than 50 ms. The detector refuses a gap that long, as a discontinuity, as it should on a lamp.

**The fix** (`crates/voice/src/coordinator/tests/duplex.rs`, `Harness::at`): a paced block is read exactly the paced gap after the previous one, once the host clock has reached that time. What reads the block judges it by that time, not the host's. An unpaced block is read strictly after the previous one, as before.

**Not shown:** I couldn't reproduce the failure under synthetic load, so the fix rests on reading the code. The time the test takes is unchanged.

**Gate** (Fourth's Intel Mac, macOS 26.6.2, i7-10700K, Rust 1.96.0), on the head `7da61bcb8` (`lamp-voice` `eb905bdab` plus this one commit):
- format of the changed files, Clippy (`--workspace --all-targets -D warnings`) and `cargo build --workspace`: passed.
- Tests on the three heads together (#1030, #1069 and #1070 on `lamp-voice` `eb905bdab`, `585e2d549`): `cargo test --locked -p lamp-same-voice -p lamp-voice -p lamp-voice-eval -p lamp-memory --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=1` gave Same-voice 3, Voice 1,601, Voice-eval 521 and Memory 208 passed, none failed, 15 ignored.
- ARM64 run 38873381159 on the head: 5,551 tests run, all passed, 143 skipped.

Known flaky tests, named and not used to hold this back: the voice's timed process tests (#739), `lamp-policy` `program.rs:363` (#783), the log relay losing a part's last line (#862).

author: codeskop-io
body:
Events v2 phase 1: fixes bugs 3, 4, 5, 6 and 8 from the event model review.

- **Bug 3 (beacon 401):** batches sent on page close keep the key in \`?key=\`, which backend v0.29.2 accepts for public keys. The body is now sent as \`text/plain;charset=UTF-8\`, which is CORS-safelisted, so there's no preflight while the page is closing. **Release after backend v0.29.2 is in production.**
- **Bug 4 (stale page):** \`context.app.page\` is read when each batch is built, not once at init. \`api_error\` and \`api_timing\` payloads carry the \`page\` they happened on.
- **Bug 5:** \`recordException(err, attrs)\` sends \`attributes\` on the exception payload, cleaned like \`track\` properties. \`cleanProperties\` moves to \`core/properties.ts\`.
- **Bug 6 (web):** \`context.app.environment\` is sent, defaulting to \`production\`.
- **Bug 8:** \`pagehide\` also triggers the unload flush. If both \`visibilitychange\` (hidden) and \`pagehide\` fire, only one flush runs; it re-arms on visible or \`pageshow\`.

**Also**
- Version 1.4.3 (\`package.json\`, \`SDK_VERSION\`). The React adapter is unchanged.
- API report updated for \`environment\` and \`attributes\`.

body:
Before: the logo next to "Julendly" was still Kairos's K, and public pages could only follow the device's light or dark setting.

After: the mark is a J (the logo and the favicon). Public pages, the friends link included, have a sun/moon button in the top right corner (bottom right on phones, clear of the "Powered by" ribbon). It switches light and dark, and the choice is remembered on later visits. Until a visitor uses it, pages still follow the device setting.

How: the choice is stored in a `kairos_public_theme` cookie. The root layout sets it as `data-public-theme` on `<html>` in the server response, so a reload never flashes. In `globals.css`, the public dark tokens (classic and friends) now apply under the device media query unless the visitor chose light, and under `data-public-theme="dark"` whatever the device says. `DarkReaderLock` adds its meta whenever the page is dark, chosen or automatic. Embeds and pages with branding background or text colors stay light and show no toggle.

Tests: a new e2e test in `e2e/booking-pages/dark-mode.spec.ts` covers light on a dark device, the choice surviving a reload, dark on a light device with the Dark Reader lock, and the friends page, with axe checks. The dark mode and friends specs pass (7 tests), along with tsc, eslint and the foundation unit tests.

body:
### Agent

- [x] Opret `ewald/1969` med seks underbind efter modellen `aarestrup/1976`.
- [x] Placer de 88 eksisterende DSL-tekster i bind I–V i trykkets rækkefølge; markér udgaven og bindene som ufuldstændige.
- [x] Bevar tekst-id'er, bidragsoplysninger, kvalitetsmærker, variantrelationer og sidehenvisninger ved flytningen; bevar 1770/1779 i teksternes noter.
- [x] Tilføj og kontrollér seks titelblade med transskription af den trykte ordlyd; alle seks består titelbladsskillens geometriske QA.
- [x] Kontrollér bibliografi, digitale kilder og kildearv; bevar de tre dokumenterede andre tekstudgaver.
- [x] Generér, synkronisér og kontrollér otte komplette facsimileserier med 2.778 billeder og thumbnails.
- [x] Gennemgå variantkandidater og bevar de oprindelige udgivelser som tomme værkposter med intakte værklinks.
- [x] Gennemgå bind I’s trykte rettelsesliste og indfør den relevante rettelse med erratamarkering.
- [x] Kontrollér XML, formattering og alle berørte id'er; kør `make test`.

### Bruger

- [ ] Gennemgå værkstruktur, titelblade og bibliografiske oplysninger.
- [ ] Foretag afsluttende stikprøvekontrol mod facsimilerne.

### Resumé

Ewalds eksisterende digte manglede 90 bibliografiske kildeangivelser. Alle 91 berørte tekster har nu en kilde. De 88 tekster, som følger DSL's udgave, er samlet under **Samlede Skrifter (1969)** med underbind I–VI, ligesom Aarestrups 1976-udgave. Bind VI har et komplet facsimile, men endnu ingen transskriberede tekster.

Fixes #1967

### Kilde

Johannes Ewald: *Samlede Skrifter*, I–VI, ved Hans Brix, V. Kuhr, Svend Aage Pallis og Niels Møller, oprindelig 1914–1924; 2. oplag, fotografisk optryk, Gyldendal, København, 1969, med *Tillæg 1969* ved Erik M. Christensen. [KB, bind I](https://tekster.kb.dk/text/adl-texts-ewald03val-root); links til alle bind, kolofonoplysninger og sidemapping findes i [kildedokumentationen](https://github.com/thabz/Kalliope/blob/ewald-kilder-1967/docs/kilder/ewald.md).

Komplette facsimiler: [I](https://kalliope.org/facsimiles/ewald/1969-1.pdf), [II](https://kalliope.org/facsimiles/ewald/1969-2.pdf), [III](https://kalliope.org/facsimiles/ewald/1969-3.pdf), [IV](https://kalliope.org/facsimiles/ewald/1969-4.pdf), [V](https://kalliope.org/facsimiles/ewald/1969-5.pdf), [VI](https://kalliope.org/facsimiles/ewald/1969-6.pdf), [Tillæg 1969](https://kalliope.org/facsimiles/ewald/1969-6-tillaeg.pdf), [Udvalgte digte 1998](https://kalliope.org/facsimiles/ewald/1998-udvalgte-digte.pdf).

*Til Sielen* bevarer Kielberg/Ravn, DSL/Borgen 1998, s. 96–100. *Hedningernes Frelse* bevarer *Den danske lyrik*, bind I, 1963; *Da den høysalige Konge blev udført* bevarer *Gyldendals Bibliotek, Dansk Lyrik*, bind I, s. 63–65.

### Arbejde udført af Agent

- Opretter hovedværket og seks underbind; fordeler 88 tekster med henholdsvis 6, 14, 37, 1 og 30 tekster i bind I–V. *Fiskerne* får en samlet linkbar sektion i bind III; *Philet* ligger i bind II. De oprindelige udgivelser bevares som tomme, ufuldstændige værkposter i `1770.xml` og `1779.xml`, med noter der henviser til DSL-teksterne. Både digtenes og de oprindelige værkers eksisterende URL'er bevares.
- Tilføjer 1969-optrykkets seks titelblade som `1969-1-p1.jpg`–`1969-6-p1.jpg`, med den trykte ordlyd i `<transcription>`. Geometrisk behandling og QA følger `prepare-kalliope-titlepage`.
- Forkorter de strukturerede kildetitler ved at udelade undertitlen *Efter Tryk og Haandskrifter*. Kilderne angiver `2. oplag`; forklaringen om det fotografiske optryk af 1914–1924-udgaven står én gang i en note på hovedværket.
- Fjerner forklarende noter om ufuldstændighed og sideudvalg fra 1969-værket og bindene; visningen bruger den automatiske statusbesked.
- Tilføjer samme vejledning om historiske udgivelser som tomme placeholders til Brorson-issue #1968.
- Lader de to andre udgaver blive i `andre.xml` og bevarer *Hedningernes Frelse* særskilt i `1771.xml`. *Vingesus* (1985) får en struktureret værkkilde med forfatter, titel, udgiver, sted, forlag og år; alle syv tekster arver kilden gennem `<source pages="…"/>`, med deres eksisterende sidetal og ordlyd bevaret.
- Tilføjer kontrollerede bind, sidetal og digitale links. Indfører afgrænsede tekstrettelser efter DSL som aftalt, uden særskilt registrering af forskellene. Flytningen til 1969-udgaven ændrer ikke tekstindholdet yderligere.
- Tilføjer komplette facsimiler af alle seks DSL-bind, tillægget og DSL/Borgens 1998-udvalg: 2.778 billeder med PDF-filer og thumbnails. Bevarer alle sider i KB’s billedindeks, herunder titelblade, forord, kommentarer og blanke sider; udelader én ugyldig indeksreference i bind II. Bruger faste sideoffset som hos Aarestrup, så flere digte kan tilføjes uden at udvide eller omnummerere serierne.
- Registrerer *Samtlige Skrifter*, København, 1780, som struktureret værkkilde til `ewald/p1780` (*Fortale til Læseren*) med eksplicit kildearv på teksten; bevarer ordlyd og den eksisterende note om tekstens oprindelse.
- Gennemgår bind I’s trykte rettelsesliste, s. 383–384, og indfører den relevante rettelse `Din] din` i *Sørge-Digt over Frue Rahbek*, s. 138, med `<errata>` og en erratafodnote.
- Gennemgår antologiforekomster og variantkandidater. Det eneste nye kandidatpar er et allerede dokumenteret uddrag, *Alnaturens Glæde*; det forbindes ikke som en fuldstændig variant. Fire eksisterende variantforbindelser bevares.
- Dokumenterer konkordans, udgaveoplysninger og sidemapping i `docs/kilder/ewald.md`; Ewalds restmængde under #1912 er opdateret.

### Udestående

- Præcis udgaveidentifikation/digital scanning af *Gyldendals Bibliotek, Dansk Lyrik* og sidetal/scanning af *Hedningernes Frelse* i 1963-antologien følges særskilt i #1969.
- En fuld transskription af de seks DSL-bind ligger uden for denne kildeopgave. Alle bind har komplette facsimiler; bind VI har endnu ingen tekst, og de øvrige bind indeholder udvalg.
- Brugerens afsluttende review ovenfor.

### Usikkerheder og redaktionelle valg

DSL 1969 er valgt som tekstgrundlag med brugerens godkendelse; det dokumenterer ikke den oprindelige indtastningsudgave. *Til Sielen* dateres 1998 efter den kontrollerede kolofon og den eksisterende indtastningsnote, selv om KB's portal siger 1999. Kilde- og sidetalskontrollen er ikke en fuld ny korrektur; teksternes kvalitetsmærker er bevaret, og der erklæres ingen komplette interne sideskift eller fuld gennemgang af alle bogsider.

### Validering

- `make test`: bestået, 125 testsuiter og 1.999 tests; 1 suite og 9 tests sprunget over.
- Sammenligning før/efter flytningen: samtlige 91 berørte tekst-id'er, tekstindhold (bortset fra den dokumenterede trykte rettelse ovenfor), eksisterende tekstmetadata og trykte sidetal bevaret; de 88 DSL-tekster arver samme bibliografi, og alle 89 berørte facsimilehenvisninger peger på de samme bogsider i de nye komplette serier. Alle seks forældre-/bindreferencer er kontrolleret.
- Alle seks titelblade består geometrisk QA; de trykte ordlydstransskriptioner er kontrolleret mod billederne, og alle billeder er med i de genererede værkdata.
- `p1780`: kildearv til *Samtlige Skrifter*, København, 1780, er verificeret i den genererede tekstpost.
- Vingesus: alle syv tekst-id’er, tekstindhold, kvalitetsmærker og sidetal bevaret; struktureret kildearv verificeret i de genererede data.
- Placeholder-værkerne 1770/1779 er tomme og ufuldstændige, bevarer oprindelige årstal og har henvisninger til DSL-teksterne.
- De seks binds forklarende noter om ufuldstændighed og sideudvalg er fjernet; ufuldstændighed vises gennem den automatiske statusbesked. Hovedværket har én fælles bibliografisk note om det fotografiske optryk.
- Variantkontrol kørt på alle seks underbind; kandidat og eksisterende relationer gennemgået.
- Alle 2.778 sidebilleder og deres 2.778 thumbnails i 250-pixel-bredde er kontrolleret på den offentlige server med HTTP 200 og `image/jpeg`; alle ni thumbnailbredder er genereret lokalt.
- Sideantal og ubrudt billednummerering kontrolleret for alle otte PDF’er/serier; alle 25.002 thumbn
