body:
The original planner stored data separately in each browser. This branch adds an encrypted EU D1 workspace with pairing keys, revision-protected saves, field-level merging and conflict review, plus responsive PIMP/HOE-inspired planning tools.

The workspace covers projects/goals/milestones/dependencies, routines, mood/diary/values, budget/time tracking, abstinence/time-since trackers, analytics and Google Calendar/Tasks exchange. Tasks support Urgent · Priority 0, automatic overdue urgency, grouped reminders, custom title colors, category icons, project color inheritance and confirmed completion with retained notes. Apple integration is excluded.

Diary photos use separate encrypted image storage for cross-device display. Google Drive can receive normal JPEG copies and encrypted full backups; the requested destination is configured privately. Artlook's read-only gatekeeper is reused through an authenticated fixed-folder service binding. Real-account Google write authorization and uploads remain unverified: no real Drive uploads/backups are claimed. Daily backups require an open app and active authorization.

Version 2.2.1 fixes Journal history navigation: View day remains in Journal and shows the selected day's full notes/images. History includes selected-day records and has explicit pagination beyond 30, with labels/previews and safe handling of undated records. No saved entries were rewritten.

Version 2.2.3 refines category icons to compact, thinner rounded outlines with white strokes and coordinated glows. More space separates icons from text, title/category left edges align, and entry titles are larger. Noto Sans Mono is bundled and served locally, including graph labels, with its SIL license retained.

Version 2.3.0 makes the planner installable on Android with regular/maskable launcher icons, standalone display, an Install control and menu guidance. A versioned public-only service-worker cache supports offline reopening, keeps API/images/Google off the cache, and waits for old windows to close before updating. Existing local edits sync on reconnect. No native APK, store listing or closed-app push is added.

Version 2.3.1 includes existing and new mood/feeling observations in Journal daily entries and history, with context, rating, Vienna timestamps and direct editing of the same record. New check-in timestamps remain stable after editing; no duplicate diary records or migration is needed. Focused mood checks cover phone layout, editing and second-device sync; the 42-record Journal regression passed.

Version 2.3.2 changes urgent badges, summary headings/actions, row markers and overdue deadline text to vivid alarm red, preserving custom title/category colors. The build, 16 automated tests and 63 responsive browser checks passed; desktop and phone screenshots were inspected. Google authorization was not tested or modified.

Version 2.3.3 adds Remove due date to task editing and preserves empty deadlines when reopening. Saving an undated task clears deadline time/reminders; automatic overdue urgency clears while manual P0 remains. The build, 16 automated tests and focused deadline browser regression passed, including cancellation, reopen persistence and second-device sync. The phone editor screenshot was inspected.

Validation: focused PWA checks returned zero Chromium installability errors, verified PNGs/manifest, exercised synthetic install prompting and saved/reloaded a note offline before reconnect sync. The phone install dialog was visually checked. Physical Android OS installation is not claimed. The latest build and 16 automated tests passed; the 2.3.0 release also passed 63 responsive browser checks, including icon size/stroke/glow, spacing, title/category alignment and loaded-font assertions and overflow checks across desktop, simulated iPad and phone layouts. Desktop and phone screenshots were visually reviewed. The targeted Journal browser regression first reproduced the failure, then passed same-day inclusion, 42 records through pagination, selected-day navigation, historical-note editing and phone-width layout. The preceding 2.2.0 release passed 63 Chromium checks across desktop, simulated iPad portrait/landscape and phone, including image sync and mocked Drive writes. Those Google fixtures are not real account tests. Physical Safari/iPad, real OAuth/Picker consent, OS notification delivery and interrupted large uploads remain unverified.

author: hello-hayden-slaughter
body:
## What changes

"Open Pip" no longer throws the demo up full screen. The desk in "Go on, have a play" turns into Pip's window, in place, as in the prototype ([Pip Demo Window](https://claude.ai/artifact/XmLBwn5ko7jTzn5JVKZygz)):

- **Opening:** the desk's things drift out and fade, the page glides until the section sits under the header, then the desk grows into a window centred on the screen. The page dims behind it.
- **Size:** the window takes the Mac app's shape (16:10). It is as big as the screen allows, never past the demo's natural 1280 × 800, so the app draws at its own layout, just scaled.
- **Window controls:** macOS's three buttons sit where the Mac app has them, over the empty top of Pip's rail (`trafficLightPosition` 16, 18 in electron.js). Nothing else is drawn on the demo.
  - **Red:** puts Pip back on the desk.
  - **Yellow:** tucks Pip into a little dock at the bottom of the screen, so you can read on. The desk's button reads "Back to Pip", and the dock tile brings the window back.
  - **Green:** fills the browser window, with the app laid out at the screen's shape. Green again, or Esc, comes back.
- **Keeps your place:** Pip stays where you left it through close, minimise and full screen for the whole visit, because the frame is never reloaded.
- **Under the window:** "Like what you see?" and the trial button. When the demo is slow or silent, that line becomes "Not opening? Try a new tab".

## What goes

- **The full-screen takeover and its bar:** both are removed.
- **The first-time "This is the real Pip" card:** removed too. The demo's own welcome note now says the same thing (no live AI, replies written in advance, nothing leaves the browser).

## Also

- **Poster:** `assets/img/pip-demo-note.jpg` is retaken from the live demo. It now matches what loads ("You've landed in Pip"), so the swap from the still to the real thing doesn't jump.
- **Dock icon:** `assets/img/pip-app-icon.png` is the Mac app's icon (from `desktop/build-resources`).
- **`view.screen()`:** a new export, so the window and the dock land on the visitor's screen in a frame stretched to the page's height (the review page).
- **README:** the demo paragraph now describes the window.

## Checked

Checked in headless Chromium against a local server, with the live demo loading in the window.

- **Sizes:** at 1440 × 820 the window is 1146 × 716, with the app at 1280 × 800. At 1920 × 1000 it's the full 1280 × 800. At 1280 × 640 it gets smaller to fit.
- **Keeping your place:** opened Sales 2026 in the demo, minimised, scrolled 1,200px, brought it back from the dock: still on Sales 2026. Same after closing and reopening.
- **Full screen:** the app re-lays out at 1440 × 820, and comes back to 1280 × 800 after Esc. Yellow is greyed out in full screen, as on a Mac.
- **Closing:** returns focus to Open Pip, removes every `inert`, and leaves the desk fully below the header. A click on the dimmed page also closes.
- **Phones:** no Open Pip button and no sideways scroll. Narrowing to a phone's width puts Pip back on the desk from any state, minimised and mid-move included.
- **Edge cases:** reduced motion, and a cross-origin frame stretched to the page's full height.
- **Errors:** none on the page.

One whole-diff review ran before this PR. Its five findings are fixed in the second commit:

- the desk now visibly clears before the window grows;
- narrowing to a phone's width while minimised or mid-move is handled;
- the dialog now wraps the line under the window, so VoiceOver can reach the trial button;
- the window controls come before the demo in tab order;
- a smooth scroll still running at the click is stopped first.

**Known limit (unchanged from the takeover):** once you've clicked into the demo, Esc doesn't reach the page, because the demo is on another origin. The red and green buttons always work.

mlx-lm 0.32.2 adds its own Muse Spark model, and its checkpoints use a different layout from the one #4573 loads: q, k, v and the attention output gate are one `qkvg_proj` with interleaved q and k rows, the experts sit under `mlp.experts`, and the residual gates and zero-centered norms are stored as their fixed coefficients and gains. The vision tower also stores q, k and v as one `qkv_proj`. The mlx-community Muse Spark Open quants are now built for mlx-lm 0.32.2, so oMLX needs to read this layout, and oQ output should load in mlx-lm too.

## What changes

- **Loading**: checkpoints in the mlx-lm layout load on the mlx-lm and mlx-vlm paths. The fused projections are split back, and the norms and residual gates use the stored gains and coefficients as they are, so the logits match exactly. On the mlx-vlm path, `quantization_path_aliases` maps the per-module bits. Checkpoints in the earlier layout still load.
- **oQ**: Muse Spark Open output is written in the mlx-lm layout.
  - q, k, v and the gate of a layer get the widest bit width among them, since the layout stores them as one projection (+0.40 GB on oQ3e).
  - The lm_head stays in BF16. mlx-lm 0.32.2 casts the lm_head input to the weight dtype, so a quantized lm_head gives wrong logits there (+1.55 GB on oQ3e).

## Validation

- Round trip: a model saved in the mlx-lm layout and loaded back through the mlx-lm and mlx-vlm loaders gives identical logits, including with an image input. An oQ run on a small HF checkpoint writes the layout with one bit width per fused group and loads back.
- mlx-community/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-3bit, converted with mlx-lm 0.32.2: text, image and tool-call requests work in oMLX.
- The new mlx-community/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-oQ3e (371.5 GB) on an M3 Ultra (512 GB), 1024-token prompt and 128 generated tokens:

| | Prefill (tok/s) | Decode (tok/s) |
|---|---|---|
| mlx-lm 0.32.2 | 223.5 | 20.55 |
| oMLX | 224.5 | 20.68 |

  In oMLX, text, image, tool calls and reasoning effort from low to xhigh behave as before. Decode is 2.9% slower than the previous oQ3e (21.30 tok/s), mostly from the BF16 lm_head.
- The new mlx-community/Muse-Spark-Open-816B-A42B-oQ4e (477.6 GB, NVFP4 experts passed through) loads strictly in mlx-lm 0.32.2 and in oMLX on both paths, and layers 0-2 on real weights agree between the two within the BF16 difference of oMLX itself (cosine 0.9995 or higher).

## 개요

규모 곡선을 A안(총 부하 고정)·B안(로봇당 부하 고정) 둘 다 돌리도록 문서를 바꾼다. 10/16 하연 결정: A만으로는 곡선이 평평할 가능성이 커 논문에 쓰기 어렵고, B는 문제가 있지만 분석적으로 쓸 수 있다.

- [x] docs: 문서

- [ ] chore: 빌드·설정·CI

author: jazzenchen
body:
Every mark that turns into a bot now acts out what its agent is doing, not just "working or not".

## What the HUD shows

- **Looks** (one at a time, per mark): a waiting request (permission › question › plan), compacting (Claude, automatic only), working (thinking, edit/command, reading, a long command, or plain work for clients whose logs carry no tool calls), no news (in flight with no sign of life for 30 min: a half-faded logo), idle (logo with a visit every 20–35 s) and asleep (every session idle for an hour: a doze every 3–5 min).
- **Events** played over the look: start (a prompt after 5 min of rest), a failed turn, a turn stopped by a usage limit.
- **Badges** that need no timer: × after a failed turn, ⧗ while a limit holds. With Reduce Motion or bot logos off they sit on the still logo, as do the request signs ! ? ≡.
- **Several sessions, one mark**: a sticky owner session; a new working look shows after two reads and holds at least 6 s; thinking only after 10 s with no tool. Done stays on the reply card, where the dock is hidden anyway.
- **Reminder cards** act out what they are about: approval, question or plan; the reply (Clawd dances for a turn of 10 min or more); a reset or credit card.
- **Clawd plays Claude's own sprites**: the Clawd Quest animations that ship inside Claude.app (thinking bubble, laptop, desk, light bulb, pointing, facepalm, dizzy, meditating…). The 18 the clips use are bundled as `Resources/clawd-sprites.json`, copied unchanged from Claude 2.37337.1 and credited in `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt`; `scripts/clawd-sprites.py` copies them again from an installed Claude.app. They are decoded once and baked to whole device pixels, in the demo and recordings too; only a mark too small for them gets the drawn Clawd.
- **The other bots** act each state with their own parts and a 5×7 sign over the head (! ? ≡ × ⧗ … z); DeepSeek's bot becomes a chubby fish: a swept fin on its back and a small triangular fin on each side that flaps with its work.
- The shared bot clock steps on one grid (1/24, 1/12, 1/6 s), wakes only when a picture changes, and leaves out bots nobody can see (covered window, sleeping displays, inactive session).

## Signals (Core)

- Claude: tool calls and results, thinking, API errors (with the limit's reset) and retries are read from line heads; an API-error line ends the turn as failed or limited instead of leaving it running for 30 min. Turns carry an outcome: completed, interrupted, failed or limited.
- Codex, DeepSeek, Grok CLI, Copilot, Pi, Kimi and OpenClaw give outcomes where their logs give a structured reason; Codex, DeepSeek and Grok report open calls.
- `ReportView.queueMarks` hands each mark its sessions' live facts and waiting requests; `queueVendors` is unchanged.
- Claude's automatic compaction is heard through a `PreCompact` hook. It runs the existing `--session-origin-hook claude` command, which every build since 0.4.36 already handles quietly, so an older copy at the hook's path never starts whole on a flag it does not know.

## Docs

`docs/hud.md` (Bots) rewritten; the compaction hook and turn outcomes in `session-lifecycle.md`, `command-line.md`, `architecture.md`, `data-access.md`, `providers.md`; CHANGELOG Unreleased lines.

## Checks

- Full suite: AgentHUDDesktopTests 651 tests (3 skipped), AgentHUDCoreTests 1370 tests (4 skipped), 0 failures.
- An adversarial review (Core signals, Desktop behaviour, cost, spec conformance) produced 24 findings; every fix was first proven by a failing test (13 fixed, 3 deferred as low-impact, 4 owner questions).
- `scripts/check-source-boundaries.py` passes.

## Owner decisions folded in

- Clawd's frames are bundled into Open; the app never reads Claude.app.
- Interrupted turns and session ends play no animation; asleep dozes every 3–5 min.
- A hook command with a `--…-hook` flag or client this build does not know exits 0 quietly instead of starting the app (a host's own hook flags must run before `HookEntry.handle`; agent-hud does so since fc694d9). `--install-completion-hook` with an unknown client prints an error and exits 1.
- On a top or bottom dock that separates its agents, Clawd stands with its request's sign (a plan holds its lit bulb) by its card instead of pointing past it.

body:
Two defects from the SLA-860 multiplication smoke (deck 45047a9e).

**1. `scene` was refused in create mode.** `VARIABLE_INPUT` was built from `VARIABLE_FIELDS`, which leaves out `scene`. It now uses `TESTED_VARIABLES`, so the input matches what SKILL.md documents (`["hook","character","concept","scene"]` in exploration). The planner was already mode-agnostic: `isEditArm` sends any scene arm to baseline-edit with baseline QA. The existing schema rules still apply: scene on its own in controlled mode, never together with `slides`.

**2. Edit-mode scene had no control arm.** The stored direction was `Scene: <new setting>. Change only…`, so the planner staged arm A in the new setting as well. Changes:
- `editSceneDirection` (moved to `schema.ts`) tells the planner that arm A reproduces every source frame as it is (person, outfit, pose, setting, progression) and that the new setting applies to the alternate only.
- `contractInputOf` rebuilds that direction from `sceneOverrides` at plan time. Drafts stored before this fix (`278afe69`) therefore re-plan correctly.
- Workspace locks (`universalLocks()`) now apply to edit-mode scene, both when the draft is stored and at plan time, so `hardLocks` is no longer empty.
- When the user fixes the setting, the alternate uses the model's per-slide re-staging, which keeps each slide's outfit and pose. The bare setting is the fallback. The baseline-edit opener now keeps outfit and pose and changes only the setting and props.

Tests: the planner-input unit test for an edit-mode scene draft stored the old way checks the direction, the locks and `hardLocks`. Other new tests cover create-mode scene acceptance and the re-staging path. `bun test src/experiments src/tools/experiments.test.ts`: 1116 pass. The 13 failures are composite/overlay tests that fail on a missing `opentype.js` in the local node_modules, which this diff doesn't touch. `tsc` is clean.

author: awgn
body:
## Overview

This PR optimizes the connection and request routing hot paths by replacing per-connection and per-request linear scans with precompiled lookup structures built once at configuration load time.

## Key Changes

### 1. Precompiled 5-Level Decision Tree for Filter Chain Selection
Previously, every incoming TCP connection matched its `FilterChain` by linearly scanning all configured `FilterChainMatch` rules across 5 passes and allocating a candidate bitmap.

`FilterChains<T>` now compiles the rules upfront into an immutable 5-level decision tree that strictly follows Envoy's evaluation hierarchy without backtracking:
1. **Destination Port:** $O(1)$ hash lookup with wildcard fallback.
2. **Destination IP Prefix Ranges:** IPv4 and IPv6 Longest Prefix Match grouped into hash buckets ordered by descending prefix length, with host bits masked at build time.
3. **Server Names (SNI):** $O(1)$ exact hash lookup, followed by wildcard suffix lookups scanning dot boundaries from longest (most specific) to shortest.
4. **Source IP Prefix Ranges:** IPv4 and IPv6 Longest Prefix Match grouped by descending prefix length.
5. **Source Ports:** $O(1)$ hash lookup with wildcard fallback and build-time ambiguity detection for overlapping chains.

### 2. `VirtualHostTable` and Precompiled Per-Route HTTP Filters
In `HttpConnectionManager`, virtual host resolution previously iterated over every virtual host and domain pattern on each HTTP request.
- **`VirtualHostTable`:** Compiles domain rules into an $O(1)$ `AHashMap` for exact host matches (short-circuiting on `host:port` before falling back to the port-stripped host), length-sorted slices for suffix and prefix LPM matching, and a direct wildcard fallback index.
- **`RuntimeRoute` & `RoutingState`:** Per-route HTTP filter overrides are now resolved and compiled ahead of time when `RoutingState` is constructed, removing the lazy `OnceLock` wrapper from the request path and sharing `Arc<HttpFilter>` pointers directly when routes do not override a filter.

### 3. Minor Allocation Cleanup in `FilterDecision`
Updated `FilterDecision` response helper constructors (`internal_server_error`, `bad_request`, `not_found`, etc.) to accept `impl Into<String>` instead of `&str`, avoiding extra `.to_owned()` allocations when callers already hold an owned `String` (such as formatted errors in the Wasm filter).

## Testing

Added comprehensive differential and Cartesian-product unit tests verifying 100% behavioral equivalence against the reference implementations:
- **`FilterChainMatcher`:** Exhaustive verification across all $2^5 = 32$ optional field combinations (both isolated and compiled simultaneously), multi-specificity IPv4/IPv6 CIDR hierarchies (`/0` through `/32` and `/128`), multi-label SNI wildcards, and Proxy Protocol connection metadata.
- **`VirtualHostTable` & `RoutingState`:** Cartesian product of domain rule archetypes (exact, suffix, prefix, wildcard, port-only `*:port`, host + wildcard port `host:*`, IPv4/IPv6, trailing dots) against HTTP/1.1 `Host` headers and HTTP/2 `:authority` URIs, plus a $2^9 = 512$ power-set differential test, per-route filter override checks, and all $2^3 = 8$ header mutation hierarchy combinations.

Sprint64 Selection explicitly classifies this as green-first write-tests, not new product behaviour or refactoring. Independent PO canonical gate remains pending; **do not merge**.

## Complete Scope

[Complete owned-file diff](https://github.com/akmaier/agent-m/pull/565/files):
- `tests/mail-protocols.test.mjs`: fixture preparation extracted only. Original header and the entire TST-420001..005 declaration/body/assertion/expected-result block are byte-identical to base, verified by direct comparison.
- `tests/mail-protocols-fixture.mjs`: the same fixture, reused only by MOD-mail-protocols unit tests (DRY/one responsibility).
- `tests/mail-protocols-privacy.test.mjs`: four new privacy guards, TST-420101..104, with literal inputs/preconditions/expected results and unchanged public mailHandlers route.

**No production, API, dependency/lockfile, workflow, shared helper, header reassignment, SPEC/UC/architecture or docs/job changes.** No real mailbox/credential inspection, off-computer mail service, package install inside tests or paid request. Exact Bridge packages were staged outside tests with `npm ci --prefix src/bridge-build --omit=dev --ignore-scripts`.

## Actual Failure Nodes

`privacyCase:51 -> owned fixture runTest -> public mailHandlers()[POST /v1/mail/test] -> testMailbox -> real imapflow/nodemailer -> loopback STARTTLS fixtures`. Success, no-encryption, login-refused and not-found outcomes are positive controls before the privacy assertions. Certificates and listeners precede observation. Fixture protocol arrays are never classified as product logs.

author: nickruigrok
body:
Closes GRA-634.

`pageOf` opened a browser context per page and nothing closed them, so every context a test opened stayed open (session, `/rpc` socket, live subscriptions) until the worker's browser shut down. #549 fixed this for `e2e/unknown-outcomes.e2e.ts` only.

## What changes

- `e2e/contexts.ts`: the tests' `test`, with two fixtures:
  - `newContext(options?)`: a browser context of the test's own.
  - `pageOf(person, options?)`: a page signed in as `person`, in a context from `newContext`.
  Every context they open is closed when the test ends, passed or failed.
- `e2e/csp.ts` builds its CSP-checking `test` on it, so every file that used `pageOf` keeps its import.
- The three browser-policy files that use plain `test` (screen-attacks, package-artifacts, product-page-scripts) take it from `contexts.ts`.
- All 30 callers move to the fixture, along with the raw `browser.newContext()` calls in languages, page-recovery, decisions and intake. Their hand-written `context.close()` calls go: those ran only when the test passed, and decisions never closed its context at all. The tracking helper from #549 in unknown-outcomes goes too.
- `pageOf` is gone from `people.ts`, so there's no untracked way to open a page left.

## Tests

- `e2e/contexts.e2e.ts`: in one worker, a test that passes and a test that fails (`test.fail()`) each open contexts with `pageOf` and `newContext`. The next test checks that none of them is in `browser.contexts()`. Checked by mutation: without the closing loop, the last test fails.
- Locally on the installed Chromium with 2 workers, the `chromium`, `package-approvals` and `playbook` projects pass: 184 tests in 6.0 minutes. Firefox and WebKit weren't run locally; CI runs them.

## Review

OpenCodeReview: 0 findings across 34 items.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Tests**
  * Improved isolation across browser-based tests by managing test contexts consistently, including when a test fails.
  * Added coverage to verify that test contexts are closed after use.
  * Existing end-to-end scenarios and their expected results remain unchanged.

<!-- end of auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## How much it leaked

On main, a test run last in a 1-worker chromium run found 76 browser contexts, 76 pages and 120 frames still open, each with its live connection to the one local core. Those leaks are the likely cause of the load behind GRA-617, GRA-618 and GRA-620. I found no race of their own; the evidence is on each issue.

author: lassetyr
body:
## Problem

Exchanges that never complete ("leaked" inflight exchanges) are only visible when a pod shuts down: Camel then waits for them until the shutdown timeout, and logs how many there are per route. With the default configuration Camel only tracks *counts* per route, so even the shutdown log cannot say where the exchanges are stuck. There are no route metrics either, as `camel.metrics.enable-route-policy=false`.

Leaked exchanges in the VM pipeline make the shutdown wait for the full timeout, and the pod can be killed before Hazelcast has left the cluster - stalling processing on the remaining pods until the member is detected as dead.

## Changes

- `camel.main.inflight-repository-browse-enabled=true` - tracks each inflight exchange, including the route and node it is currently at. The overhead is one map insert/remove per exchange.
- New `CamelInflightMonitor`, runs every 5 minutes (`anshar.camel.inflight.monitor.interval.seconds`):
  - Gauge `app.anshar.camel.inflight{routeId, endpoint}` - inflight exchanges per route. Only routes that have had inflight exchanges get a time series.
  - Gauge `app.anshar.camel.inflight.oldest.seconds` - age of the oldest inflight exchange.
  - Logs up to 10 of the oldest exchanges that have been inflight for more than 5 minutes (`anshar.camel.inflight.monitor.stuck.threshold.seconds`), with route and endpoint they started in, route/endpoint/node they are currently at, time at that node, body type and exception, if any.

This makes it possible to see leaks build up, and where they happen, without restarting pods.

## Testing

- `CamelInflightMonitorTest` - blocks an exchange in a nested route, and verifies the gauges and the reported route/node.
- `CamelShutdownConfigurationTest` - verifies that the browse setting binds from `application.properties`.
- Full suite: 597 tests, 0 failures.

body:
### Context
`handsontable/src/plugins/manualRowResize/__tests__/manualRowResize.spec.js` › "should autosize selected rows after double click on handler and move mouse to the next row" was flaky: `Expected 100 to be around 26` on 2026-10-07 (two attempts, "passes alone"); its sibling "should autosize selected rows after double click on handler" shares the gesture and failed on the one run that moved every row height by a pixel.

**Why.** The autofit does not run on the double-click: the first press arms a 500ms timer and the fit happens when it fires. The Jasmine cases waited a fixed 38 and 63 animation frames, a different clock, so on a loaded runner the check came before the timer.

Both are now `tests/e2e/manual-row-resize-autofit.spec.ts` (fixture `manual-row-resize-autofit.html`: `createSpreadsheetData(9, 9)`, row headers, `manualRowResize`; page object `ManualRowResizeAutofitPage` extending `ManualResizePage`), tagged `THEMES_TAG` because the row heights are theme sizes. The gestures are the user's: a real drag on the handle to stretch a row, a press-move-release over the row headers to select rows 1–3, `locator.dblclick()` on the handle; the second test moves the pointer onto the next header right after the double-click. Heights are read in one evaluate together with the grid's default row height (`stylesHandler.getDefaultRowHeight()`, 29/37/26 on main/horizon/classic) and compared within the same inclusive 1px the Jasmine `toBeAroundValue` used; every test asserts its premise first (the stretched heights, the header selection, the handle sitting on the target header's boundary), so it cannot pass on a grid whose rows never moved.

The rule (2026-10-13): a flaky Jasmine spec is migrated to Playwright and the Jasmine case deleted, never patched. The Jasmine suite is frozen and has no quarantine.

### Test evidence (required for source changes)
- Unit tests added/modified (`*.unit.js` or `*.unit.ts`): none – test-only change
- E2E tests added/modified (Playwright `tests/e2e/*.spec.ts`): `tests/e2e/manual-row-resize-autofit.spec.ts`, `tests/fixtures/pages/ManualRowResizeAutofitPage.ts`, `tests/fixtures/demo/manual-row-resize-autofit.html`
- Type tests (`*.types.ts`) updated if public API changed: none
- For a bug fix – the spec that fails without this fix: n/a (a test migration; the Playwright cases pin the same behavior the Jasmine cases did)
- Demo page / recorded trace (for UI changes): none
- Visual spec added/modified (`visual-tests/tests/**/*.spec.ts`, only for pixels no DOM probe can express – in addition to, never instead of the E2E above): none

**Jasmine cases deleted:**
- `handsontable/src/plugins/manualRowResize/__tests__/manualRowResize.spec.js`: "should autosize selected rows after double click on handler" and "should autosize selected rows after double click on handler and move mouse to the next row" (49 lines, nothing else touched)

**What the Playwright cases carry, and what changed:**
- Carried with the same numbers: rows 1–3 (first case) and row 1 (second case) end at the default row height, tolerance 1px inclusive, same grid.
- Changed: the default height is read from the grid instead of `getThemeLayout()`; real pointer events instead of simulated ones (the Jasmine `resizeRow` border compensation is not needed, the drag target is the rendered height); `expect.poll` on the heights instead of 38/63 frames; the second case waits until the handle is on row 1's boundary before pressing it (the handle is attached once and moved from header to header, so "visible" does not mean "on this header").

## 1. Show every secondary output and its odds
Chance outputs were hidden: machine panels showed only the main outputs, and sifting showed "?" until a by-product had been found. Players couldn't tell where items like copper flakes came from.

- **Machine panels:** every chance output is listed beside the main outputs, with its odds per cycle (perks included), plus the lucky ×2 chance. The inventory also lists chance items waiting inside the machine.
- **Sifting Frames:** their by-products are shown with odds instead of "?".
- **Trees:** what each gather gives — the fixed yield, the fiber, sapling and amber odds, and the extra fruit from a hive next door.
- **Treewrights:** everything the trees and grass around them can give.
- **Drills and islet hearts:** each find with its odds.
- **Hand crafting:** recipes list any "sometimes" outputs.

## 2. Fuel-burning machines top up from the stash
A kiln smelting copper (or making bricks, or an oven baking) also needs fuel, but only its main input was obvious.
- **Before:** fed copper flakes alone, a kiln never started. Pressing Load fuelled it for about a dozen cycles, then it stopped again.
  - Reproduced in the sim: 0 copper in 5 min from flakes alone, versus 51 when charcoal is also fed.
- **Fix:**

author: n-losse
body:
## What

Builds the provider and exporter with Go's native FIPS 140-3 mode so the binaries link the **CMVP-validated Go Cryptographic Module (certificate #5247)** in approved mode. All crypto on the Go standard-library path (`crypto/tls`, `crypto/ecdsa`, `crypto/rand`, …) routes through the validated module.

The module is compiled **into the binary**, so this needs no base-image change: the binaries stay pure-Go (`CGO_ENABLED=0`) and the runtime image remains `distroless/static`.

## Changes

- **Makefile** — `export GOFIPS140 ?= certified`, so every `go build`/`go test` run through the shared build submodule selects the latest CMVP-certified module. Overridable to `off` for local troubleshooting.
- **.goreleaser.yaml** — `GOFIPS140=certified` for the GitHub-release binaries, matching the image build.
- **cmd/provider** — logs `crypto/fips140.Enabled()` and `.Version()` at startup as runtime proof of approved-mode crypto. (The exporter is FIPS-linked via the build flag too, but has no runtime banner — a CLI writes its output to stdout; use `go version -m` to verify its binary.)

`certified` resolves to the latest module with a CMVP certificate (today **v1.0.0**) and rolls forward automatically as newer modules certify.

author: yasyf
body:
On Oct 16 the orca desk's incident clock launched an Opus fallback for an evidence lane twice, in cci #80942 at 12:54 AM and #81126 at 1:18 AM Pacific. Each `<lane>-evidence-opus` did nothing and was stood down. Evidence lanes never post a mechanism or open a PR, so the clock could only misfire on them. This is cc-notes papercut 3dfdc2f.

## Cause

`desk-launch.py incident <name> <fix-brief> <evidence-brief>` launches both lanes as `NOW incident xhigh`. The runner clocks every launch on the `incident` alias unless its brief's `ccx:` line names a role other than `fix` or `incident`. A hand-written evidence brief without `ccx: role=evidence` therefore ran on the fix lane's 10-, 15-, and 20-minute thresholds.

## Fix

- The launch line takes an optional `role=<role>` before `brief=`. The runner records it on the launch, and the `launch` command takes the same value as `--role`.
- `incident_fix` reads the launch's own role beside the brief's. A launch whose line or brief names any role but `fix` or `incident` is never clocked.
- `desk-launch.py incident` posts `role=fix` and `role=evidence`, so the exemption no longer depends on what the brief says. `lane` launches post no role.
- Launch records written before this change carry no role and are read as before.
- `orca-desk-brief.md`, SKILL.md, and both script docstrings describe the role.

Evidence lanes get no clock of their own. The evidence brief does not ask for `evidence` records on cci, so a threshold on them misfires the same way.

## Tests

- `test_an_evidence_lane_launched_with_its_role_passes_each_threshold_unclocked` covers each threshold at 10, 15, and 20 minutes. A fix lane and an evidence lane launch through cci lines with `role=fix` and `role=evidence` on plain briefs. The fix lane logs the threshold and gets its fallback; the evidence lane logs nothing and gets none.
- The launch grammar test gains a `role=evidence` line and asserts the parsed role.
- `test_desk_launch.py` asserts the incident pair's lines carry `role=fix` and `role=evidence`.

Ruff is clean on the touched files.

author: gmh5225
body:
## Summary

LLVM-C units now hold the records they name, as the program's local types define them, the same way HighC units do since #1136. A function decompiled through LLVM-C now compiles on its own and reads its records by the members the user sees in Local Types.

**Definitions.** LLVM-C writes the unit first, then asks the local types (`CEmitterOptions::RecordDefinitions`) for every name its text spells:
- a record's or an enumeration's name;
- an enumerator of an enumeration the decompiler displays, which stands for that enumeration.

Before the body it then prints:
- a `typedef` for each record tag it spells by name (`typedef struct _KDPC _KDPC;`);
- the definitions, rendered by `renderEmbeddedC` exactly as for HighC;
- a `typedef` for each enumeration it spells, placed after that enumeration's definition.

The definitions are left out, with a comment saying so, if one of their names is also the name of one of the unit's own functions or objects (`CProjectionIdentifierAllocator::holds`).

**Agreement.** `LocalTypesDebugContext` now remembers the members and enumerators that the debug information itself gave to records and enumerations named in the library. A record or enumeration is defined only where all of these agree with the library. Otherwise it stays declared only, so the unit fails to compile at that point instead of reading a member the definition does not have.

**Typed signatures and conversions.** LLVM-C computes with integers. In a unit that holds the definitions:
- Parameters and results that the debug information or a prototype types as a pointer are now declared as that pointer, so LLVM-C signs as HighC does: `void KeInitializeDpc(_KDPC* Dpc, void (*DeferredRoutine)(void*, void*, void*, void*), void* DeferredContext)`.
- Such a parameter converts to the integer wherever the code computes with it, as a record-pointer parameter already did.
- A pointer member that the code reads as an integer converts to that integer.
- A store to a pointer member casts with `(__typeof__(member))`. A pointer parameter stored whole is stored as its address.
- A result returned whole is returned as a pointer.

**Members through every parameter.** Before this change, LLVM-C named members only through the first parameter. It now names them through every parameter typed as a pointer to a named record, in units that hold the definitions: `Packed->Count` and `Thread->MiscFlags`, where it used to print `*(uint16_t *)((void*)((uint64_t)Packed + 5))`. Units without local types keep their previous output.

**HighC.** A pointer parameter stored whole into a pointer member is now stored as the parameter, not through a `uintptr_t` round trip: `Dpc->DeferredRoutine = (__typeof__(Dpc->DeferredRoutine))(DeferredRoutine);`.

Example, `PsGetProcessId` through LLVM-C:
```c
void* PsGetProcessId(_EPROCESS* Process) {
    return (void*)Process->UniqueProcessId;
}
```

## Not in this PR

- **Other LLVM-C compile errors**, which this PR does not touch and which predate it (see the sweep below):
  - forward declarations that take every argument register while the calls pass the callee's arity (`too few arguments`);
  - `memset` and other runtime calls without declarations, or assigned as integers;
  - undeclared intrinsics such as `__readgsqword`.
- Whole-image emission (`neverd_decompile_all`), Rust and Go views, and enumerators renamed in Local Types, as listed in #1136.

## Verification

- **`scripts/check_decompiled_types.py`** now checks both routes; `--route` picks one. It decompiles each function and compiles the unit for the Windows target with clang and mingw-w64's headers. Before this change, LLVM-C failed all six kernel functions: `_KDPC`, `_EPROCESS`, `_KSEMAPHORE` and `_OBJECT_ATTRIBUTES` were unknown type names, and integers were converted to pointers implicitly. Now all six compile in both routes (`KeInitializeDpc`, `KeSetImportanceDpc`, `PsGetProcessId`, `PsGetProcessCreateTimeQuadPart`, `KeInitializeSemaphore`, `NtCreateFile`), and so does the typed-PDB fixture's `use()`.
- **Kernel sweep.** I decompiled 200 named ntoskrnl functions through the C API, in both routes, with the dev engine and with this one, and compiled every unit the same way. For each unit whose text changed, I compared its errors by kind:
  - HighC: 2 of 200 units changed, with no change in errors.
  - LLVM-C: 9 of 200 units changed. 13 `unknown type name` errors are gone, and no error kind is new.
  - One `too few arguments` error now shows in `IoGetDeviceInterfaceAlias`. It was already there: clang reports it now that the argument has a type.
  - Units that fail: HighC 76 before and 76 after, LLVM-C 92 before and 90 after. What still fails is listed under "Not in this PR".
- **`NeverDSessionCAPITests`.** `FunctionsHoldTheRecordsTheirPDBTypes` runs on the fixture in CI and now covers LLVM-C:
  - the tag typedefs come before their definitions, and the enumeration's typedef comes after its definition;
  - the signature spells `_SIGNED_KIND Kind`;
  - `Device->Size`, `Thread->MiscFlags` and `Packed->Count` are named;
  - renaming `_PACKED.Count` to `Items` reaches LLVM-C's code and its definition.

  `SessionCAPIKernelInputs.KernelFunctionsHoldTheRecordsTheyName` checks, in both routes:
  - `KeInitializeDpc`'s signature with the prototype's pointers;
  - the `__typeof__` stores of the parameters;
  - `void* PsGetProcessId(_EPROCESS* Process) { return (void*)Process->UniqueProcessId; }`;
  - a user rename of `DeferredRoutine` reaching LLVM-C.

  21 session tests that touch LLVM-C or local types pass, with the kernel inputs set.
- **Other suites:**
  - `NeverDLocalTypesDebugContextTests`: 2 tests pass.
  - `NeverDTypesTests`: 73 tests pass.
  - `NeverDLiftTests`: 1038 tests pass in the debug-type, display and source suites (`X86_64_DebugParams`, `X86_64_DebugRecords`, `X86_32_DebugHighC`, `LLVMCPointerAddresses`, `SourceABI`, `CSourceDefinitions`, and others).
  - The worker's `local_types_test.py` passes.
  - Style and localized-docs checks pass.
- **Workbench fold.** The workbench folds the definitions with the prelude in both routes: on the fixture, the LLVM-C page reports a 202-line prelude that ends where `use()` begins.

author: viktorkhan
body:
## Summary
A visual failure, real or flaky, used to cost a full ~10-minute re-run, and nothing showed which one it was. This PR:
- caches npm downloads in both CI workflows;
- cancels superseded PR runs;
- retries a failed visual test once in CI and reports any test that passes only on its retry as flaky (job summary, warning annotation, trace upload);
- uploads Playwright's JSON report on every run;
- adds a manual run that repeats a filtered set of tests with no retries, to confirm or rule out a flake.

Closes #263

## Changes
- `test-n-build.yml` (`test` job) and `visual-regression.yml`: `cache: npm` on `actions/setup-node`.
- Both workflows: a `concurrency` group. PR runs share one group per ref and cancel the run in progress. Push and manual runs each get their own group (`github.run_id`), so they are never cancelled, queued or replaced.
- `playwright.config.ts`: `retries: process.env.CI ? 1 : 0`, so `trace: "on-first-retry"` now records traces in CI. Adds a JSON reporter writing `reports/visual-results.json`, outside `test-results/` and `playwright-report/`, which Playwright empties. `html` and `list` are kept, and `/reports` is git-ignored.
- `scripts/report-flaky-tests.mjs` (new, no dependencies): walks the JSON report and collects every test with `status === "flaky"` (project, file, full title). It then:
  - writes a markdown list to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`;
  - prints one `::warning title=Flaky visual test::<project> › <title>` per test;
  - sets `flaky=true|false` in `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`.

  A missing or unreadable report becomes a notice. The script always exits 0.
- `visual-regression.yml`:
  - runs the flaky report step (`id: flaky`) and uploads the JSON report (`playwright-visual-results`, 14 days, `if-no-files-found: ignore`), both under `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`;
  - uploads `test-results/` as `playwright-flaky-traces` (7 days) when `steps.flaky.outputs.flaky == 'true'`;
  - leaves the existing failure-only upload unchanged.
- `visual-regression.yml`: a `workflow_dispatch` trigger with three inputs: `grep` (optional), `project` (`all`/`mobile`/`desktop`) and `repeat_each` (default 1). A manual run uses `--retries=0 --repeat-each=N`, plus `--grep` when set and `--project` unless `all`. The inputs reach bash through `env:` and the arguments are built as an array; `${{ inputs.* }}` is never interpolated into `run:`. A `repeat_each` that is not a positive integer fails with an error annotation. Other events run `npm run test:visual` exactly as before.
- `CONTRIBUTE.md`: a new "Continuous integration" section. It covers retries (1 in CI, 0 locally), what a flaky entry means and that it must be followed up, and how to use the manual run (`repeat_each = 20`), including that it runs the selected branch's HEAD at trigger time and how the warmup tests count.

## Decisions
- **`retries` was 0, reporters `html` + `list`, no JSON reporter** — confirmed in `playwright.config.ts`.
- **No `cache:` and no `concurrency` in either workflow** — confirmed.
- **Warmup runs with `--project` and `--grep`** — confirmed. `--project=mobile --list` lists both `[warmup]` tests first. `--project=mobile --grep "users page" --list` lists 3 tests: 2 warmup + `[mobile] users page`. `--grep` does not drop dependency projects. In addition, `--repeat-each` does **not** repeat them. The JSON listing reports `repeatEach: 1` for `warmup` and N for `mobile`/`desktop`, so a run of one test on one project with `repeat_each = 20` reports 22 tests. `CONTRIBUTE.md` documents this measured behaviour.
- **Script location** — `scripts/` already exists (`scripts/generate-mutation-hook-list.mjs`, linted by ESLint), so the new script lives there; `.github/scripts/` was not created.
- **Concurrency group differs from the originally proposed `workflow-event-ref` group.** That group put every push to `main`/`develop` into one group. GitHub keeps at most one *pending* run per group, so runs on `main` would serialize, and a third quick push would cancel the queued second run (pending, so AC3 technically held, but that commit's visual result would be lost). The same would happen to repeated manual runs on one ref. Keying non-PR runs by `github.run_id` keeps cancellation strictly to superseded PR runs. The reason is also recorded in a one-line YAML comment.
- **`!cancelled()` instead of `always()`** on the report step and the JSON upload: with superseded PR runs now cancelled, `always()` would report and upload partial results from a cancelled run.
- **Flaky-traces upload uses an implicit `success()`**: a run that is flaky *and* has a real failure already uploads `test-results/` through the unchanged failure step, so it is not uploaded twice.
- **No summary entry when nothing is flaky**: the script prints "No flaky visual tests." and sets `flaky=false`; the job summary stays empty in that case.

## How to verify
Locally:
```bash
npm run lint                                   # 0 errors (22 warnings, all pre-existing on main)
npx tsc -b
CI=1 npx playwright test --list | tail -1      # Total: 328 tests in 21 files (unchanged)
CI=1 npx playwright test --list --reporter=json | node -e 'let s="";process.stdin.on("data",d=>s+=d).on("end",()=>console.log(JSON.parse(s).config.projects.map(p=>p.name+":"+p.retries).join(" ")))'
# -> warmup:1 mobile:1 desktop:1 ; without CI -> all 0
npx playwright test login-and-home --project=desktop   # 4 passed; writes reports/visual-results.json
GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY=/tmp/s.md GITHUB_OUTPUT=/tmp/o.txt node scripts/report-flaky-tests.mjs reports/visual-results.json
# -> "No flaky visual tests.", flaky=false, exit 0
node scripts/report-flaky-tests.mjs /nonexistent.json; echo $?   # notice, 0
git status --porcelain tests/visual/__screenshots__/             # prints nothing
```
Already done during development:
- A hand-made report with one `flaky`, one `expected` and one `unexpected` test produced a single warning (`desktop › Visual baselines › row empty-value error`), a one-entry summary and `flaky=true`.
- An unparsable report produced a notice and exit 0.
- The dispatch `run:` script was executed locally with `--list`:
  - `grep="row empty-value error" project=desktop repeat_each=20` → 22 tests (2 warmup + 20);
  - `project=all repeat_each=1`, no grep → 328;
  - a `grep` containing `$(touch /tmp/pwned)` was passed literally and executed nothing;
  - `repeat_each=0` → error, exit 1.

`actionlint` is not installed here, so it was not run. Both workflows were only checked to parse as YAML.

In CI, on this PR:
- **AC1**: on a second run of either workflow with an unchanged `package-lock.json`, the setup-node step logs `Cache restored from key: …` (npm cache hit).
- **AC2**: pushing again to this PR while its runs are in progress shows the earlier run of each workflow as *cancelled*.
- **AC7**: a successful visual run has a `playwright-visual-results` artifact.
- Neither workflow shows "Invalid workflow file" in the Actions tab. `actionlint` was not run, so expression errors only show up here.

After merge, on main:
- **AC3**: pushes to `main` never show a cancelled run, and none is replaced while pending.
- **AC8**: Actions → Visual regression tests → Run workflow on `main`, with `grep = users page`, `project = mobile`, `repeat_each = 3`. The log shows `--retries=0 --repeat-each=3 --grep=users page --project=mobile` and 5 tests (2 warmup + 3). This check waits for the merge because GitHub only fires a `workflow_dispatch` trigger once the workflow declaring it is on the default branch. Before that, neither the "Run workflow" button nor `gh workflow run` works for this branch.

**AC5/AC6** cannot be forced without touching a test spec. They follow from the code paths verified above with the hand-made report. The first real flaky test in CI is their live verification.

## Upgrade actions
None.

## Out of scope / follow-ups
- After merge, verify the two flake candidates from the issue with a manual run on `main`, `repeat_each = 20`: `[desktop] coefficient-editor › row empty-valu

author: saworbit
body:
Fixes #1186

A Pull or a variant switch rebuilt a copy around the centre of its nodes that were still there. With part of the copy deleted, that centre is not where the copy was placed, so the whole copy came back moved. Two leaves at x 9 and 11, the second deleted, came back at x 8 and 10.

`HFPrefabSystem._instance_placement()` reads the placement back from a node that is still there: its position less its record's offset from the prefab's centre. Nodes pair with records by index and class, as `_kept_names()` already pairs them; the class checks are now `_brush_matches()` and `_entity_matches()`, shared by both. A copy with every node in place is measured as before, by `_instance_centroid()`. So is one where no surviving node pairs with a record.

Known limit: after a Push from another copy, the source offsets are the pushed copy's. If that Push moved the surviving node's record within the prefab, a partly deleted copy shifts by that move. A copy would need its own placement in its record to avoid that, and the case did not seem worth a format change.

Tests: two in `tests/test_prefab.gd`, a Pull with the second leaf deleted and a variant switch with the first deleted. Both fail on main, shifted one way and the other.

author: jojohoch
body:
The player reports its runtime errors under the codes of the player specification, and player and editor name a unit definition they cannot load by those codes too. Refers to #1578.

## What changes
- **Codes to the host:** `GEOGEBRA_NOT_LOADING`, `GEOGEBRA_TIMEOUT`, `IMAGE_NOT_LOADING`, `MEDIA_TIMEOUT` and `MEDIA_DURATION_ERROR` instead of the kebab-case codes. `GEOGEBRA_TIMEOUT` is still `GEOMETRY_TIMEOUT` in the specification; the rename is iqb-specifications/plugin-player#1. The editor's hints area follows with its keys, the texts stay.
- **Unit definition errors:** the translation keys are named after `UNIT_DEFINITION_NOT_READABLE`, `UNIT_DEFINITION_NEWER` and `UNIT_DEFINITION_OUTDATED` (`errorMessage.<CODE>` in the player, `unitDefError.<CODE>` in the editor), and the console names the code before the original error. A missing definition is warned about as `UNIT_DEFINITION_MISSING`. None of these goes to the host.
- **Not readable** is any failure in reading the definition: the JSON, the migration, building the unit. Until now the dialog showed the parser's English message in some of these cases; it shows the text now, and the message stays in the console. What fails afterwards keeps its message: in the player reading the unit state, in the editor everything after the unit is swapped in. For that the editor's `loadUnit` is split into `replaceUnit` and `settleUnit`. The migration after the sanitization dialog stays outside the catch, as before.
- The editor gets the text for a definition it cannot read, the player's.
- Unused player keys removed: `errorMessage.unitDefinitionNeedsEditorUpgrade`, `dialogTitle.*`, `dialogContent.*`.
- The geometry template, touched for its code, uses `@if` instead of `*ngIf` (rules.md §8).
- Release notes under `## next`; the entry for #1526 now names `MEDIA_TIMEOUT`.

## Tests
- Unit tests for the codes, for where "not readable" ends (a broken unit state in the player, a failure after the swap in the editor) and for the missing definition; each checked against a mutation of the code it covers.
- End-to-end: `simple/geometry`, `simple/image` and `simple/video` check the new codes in the message to the host. The new `simple/unit-definition-errors.spec.cy.ts` loads an unparsable, a newer and an outdated definition into player and editor and reads the dialog text, which holds the renamed keys and the translation files together; it fails when a key is missing from `de.json`. author: shadowfps
body:
In der Records-Liste stand bei MX, NS und TXT immer `0s`, nur A und AAAA hatten eine echte TTL. Der Grund: `node:dns` liefert die TTL nur für A/AAAA (`{ ttl: true }`). `resolveMx`, `resolveNs`, `resolveTxt` & Co. geben nur die Daten zurück, und `lookupSingleType` hat für alle anderen Typen eine `0` als Platzhalter eingesetzt. Bei SOA stand das `minttl`-Feld in der Spalte. Das ist aber die TTL negativer Antworten (RFC 2308), nicht die des Records: mittwald.de zeigte 3600 statt 300.

## Was sich ändert

- **TTL per DoH:** Für MX, NS, TXT, CAA, SOA und CNAME holt der Server die TTL jetzt über die DoH-JSON-API von Cloudflare, also beim selben Anbieter wie der primäre Resolver. Die Abfrage läuft parallel zu jeder `node:dns`-Abfrage und hat einen eigenen Timeout von 1,5 s (`TTL_LOOKUP_TIMEOUT_MS`). A und AAAA bleiben unverändert.
- **Zuordnung pro RRset:** Die Zuordnung läuft über den Typ, nicht Wert für Wert, denn alle Records eines RRsets haben dieselbe TTL (RFC 2181 §5.2). Ein Abgleich der einzelnen Werte wäre an TXT-Quoting und am CAA-Format gescheitert. Weichen die TTLs innerhalb eines RRsets doch voneinander ab, gilt die kleinste.
- **Aliasse:** Die TTL ist das Minimum aus der CNAME-Kette und dem RRset des Ziels, so wie `node:dns` (c-ares) sie auch für A/AAAA berechnet. Die Antwort für den gefragten Namen gilt nur so lange wie ihr kürzestes Glied. Antwortet DoH nur mit der Kette und ohne RRset, bleibt die TTL unbekannt.
- **SOA:** Die Spalte zeigt die TTL des SOA-Records und nicht mehr `minttl`. Der Wert `minttl` steht weiter im Record-Inhalt.
- **`DnsRecord.ttl` ist jetzt `number | null`:** Die Records selbst kommen weiter aus `node:dns`. Fällt DoH aus (Netzwerk, HTTP-Fehler, kaputtes JSON, Timeout, Antwort ohne RRset), bleibt jeder Record sichtbar, nur die TTL ist dann `null`.
  - Wir nehmen `null` statt eines optionalen Felds, damit der JSON-Export `"ttl": null` enthält, statt den Schlüssel stillschweigend wegzulassen.
  - Wir nehmen `null` statt `0`, weil `0` eine gültige TTL ist und „nicht cachen“ bedeutet.
- **Liste:** Eine unbekannte TTL steht als „—“ in der Liste. Screenreader lesen „TTL unbekannt“ vor und nicht „Gedankenstrich“. Eine echte `0` bleibt `0s`.

## Geprüft

- **Tests:** 12 neue Tests, insgesamt 264. Abgedeckt sind die TTL je Typ, die SOA-Korrektur, ein Alias mit zweigliedriger Kette (das kürzeste Glied ist einmal ein CNAME und einmal das RRset), eine Antwort, die nur aus der Kette besteht, und ein uneinheitliches RRset. Dazu kommen vier Ausfallarten und die Timeout-Grenze, geprüft mit Fake-Timern. In der Liste werden eine bekannte TTL, eine unbekannte TTL und eine echte 0-TTL geprüft. `node:dns` und `fetch` sind an der Außengrenze gemockt, das echte DoH-Parsing aus `doh.ts` läuft mit.
- **Live** (Commit-Body des Umsetzers): mittwald.de MX/TXT/SOA 300, NS 115; google.com CAA 77060, NS 344862; www.wikipedia.org CNAME 86400.
- **Live im Review nachgeprüft:** mittwald.de (MX/TXT/SOA 300), google.com (CAA, NS, SOA mit eigenen Werten) und www.github.com als Alias (A 20, MX/TXT 300, CAA 3600, CNAME 3600). Ein kompletter Lookup dauerte 32–94 ms.

## Review

**Codex:** Keine Befunde. Der Typecheck war grün. Die Tests konnte Codex in seiner schreibgeschützten Sandbox nicht ausführen; lokal laufen sie grün (siehe oben).

**Eigene Befunde:**

1. **TTL bei Aliassen (behoben, 7b52fd9):** MX, TXT und CAA eines Alias bekamen bisher nur die TTL des Ziel-RRsets. `node:dns` meldet für A/AAAA dagegen das Minimum aus der CNAME-Kette und dem A-RRset. Das habe ich gegen einen lokalen Test-Resolver geprüft: CNAME 60 und A 3600 ergeben 60. Bei einem Alias mit kurzlebigem CNAME stand so A mit 60s und MX mit 3600s in derselben Liste. Jetzt gilt für alle Typen das Minimum aus Kette und RRset. Der angepasste Test schlägt mit der alten Zuordnung fehl (900 statt 60).
2. **Alle Verwender von `ttl: number | null` geprüft (keine Änderung nötig):**
   - Server: Nur `dnsLookup.ts` und `doh.ts` setzen die TTL, sonst liest sie niemand.
   - Client: Nur `RecordsList` zeigt sie an.
   - Export: Der Export ist ein `JSON.stringify` des Reports und enthält damit `"ttl": null`.
   - History (`src/lib/lookupHistory.ts`): Sie speichert keine TTL, und `isHistoryEntry` prüft keine.
   - Typen: `src/types/dns.ts` und `server/types.ts` reexportieren nur `shared/types/dns.ts`.
3. **Last und Latenz (akzeptiert):** Ein ungecachter Lookup schickt sechs DoH-Abfragen an Cloudflare.
   - Sie laufen innerhalb von `cached('records:…', 60 s)`, werden also mit den Records gecacht. Parallele Anfragen auf dieselbe Domain teilen sich eine Produktion.
   - Fällt DoH schnell aus (Netzwerk- oder HTTP-Fehler), kostet das keine Zeit.
   - Hängt DoH, wartet der Lookup höchstens einmal 1,5 s, weil alle Abfragen parallel laufen. Der Fake-Timer-Test deckt diese Grenze ab.
   - Liefert `node:dns` keine Daten (ENODATA), bricht `Promise.all` sofort ab. Die DoH-Abfrage läuft dann im Hintergrund bis zu ihrem Timeout weiter, ohne den Lookup aufzuhalten.
   - `includeCommonSubdomains` (eine sequenzielle zweite CNAME-Runde) ruft niemand auf.
4. **Eine TTL-Lücke wird 60 s mitgecacht (verworfen):** Fällt DoH einmal kurz aus, bleibt `null` so lange im Cache wie der übrige Records-Snapshot. Das ist dasselbe Verhalten wie für alle anderen Daten des Lookups.
5. **Unterschiedliche Cache-Sicht (verworfen):** `node:dns` kann auf 8.8.8.8 ausweichen, und auch bei Cloudflare antworten unterschiedliche Cache-Knoten. Die Restlaufzeit kann deshalb um einige Sekunden von der des Datensatzes abweichen. Sie ist ohnehin nur eine Momentaufnahme; bei A/AAAA war das schon immer so.
6. **Datenschutz (keine Änderung nötig):** Cloudflare-DoH steht schon auf der Datenschutzseite und in `docs/COMPLIANCE.md`.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run verify` lokal grün: Lint, Typecheck, 264 Tests, Build, Smoke-Test und Bundle-Budget. Wegen #89 lief der Check in einer Kopie ohne Punkt-Ordner.
- [x] Live-Lookups für mittwald.de, google.com und www.github.com (Alias) liefern plausible TTLs für alle Typen.
- [ ] CI grün. Die CI läuft erst, wenn #75 gemergt und dieser PR auf `main` umgestellt ist.
- [ ] Nach dem Deploy auf diggydns.cloud z. B. mittwald.de nachschlagen: MX, NS, TXT und SOA zeigen echte TTLs statt `0s`.

Closes #76

body:
## O que muda (CI, lint e documentação; nenhum código do app)

As travas do web, para nada piorar enquanto refatoramos (E3 do programa de saúde do código):

1. **Regras de import com dependency-cruiser 18.6.0** (MIT, só devDependency, nunca vai para o app, então não entra no NOTICE). O arquivo é `web/.dependency-cruiser.cjs` e o comando, `npm run depcruise` (uns 4 s). Ficam proibidos:
   - ciclos de import;
   - `core` → `pages`, `core` → `shell` e `shared` → `pages`;
   - uma página importar arquivos de outra página.

   As 100 violações de hoje estão em `.dependency-cruiser-known-violations.json`, e só uma nova falha. O PR seguinte (o nó de imports) zera essa lista.
2. **Lint contra espera real nos specs:** `setTimeout(` num `*.spec.ts` falha, com a mensagem apontando para `nextTurn()`/`settle()` (`src/test-settle.ts`, #404). Os 7 lugares de hoje estão registrados com `--suppress-rule`, que é o jeito que o CONTRIBUTING prevê para ligar uma regra nova.
3. **Piso da cobertura do web:** o job `coverage` agora decide o verdict. O piso é `coverageThresholds` em `web/angular.json`: 89% das linhas, 88% das instruções, 84% dos ramos e 83% das funções (os números de hoje, arredondados para baixo). Na nuvem, duas rodadas passaram (90,0/88,2/84,4/83,5) e uma com o piso 1 ponto acima falhou, como deve.
4. Também corrige a frase do CONTRIBUTING sobre concorrência no `main`. Um push nunca cancela uma rodada que já começou, mas o GitHub só guarda uma rodada esperando por workflow. Numa sequência de merges, um commit do meio pode ficar sem rodada própria; aconteceu esta noite com o a8046365.

Feito numa sessão na nuvem, que rodou a suíte do web. Revisei aqui, juntei o `main` (um conflito na tabela do CI do CONTRIBUTING) e rodei localmente `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, `tsc` (app e spec), `npm run lint`, `format:check` e `npm run depcruise`.

## Testes

Nenhum teste novo; o CI roda a suíte do web com e sem cobertura.

## Documentação

`CONTRIBUTING.md`: os linters do web (as regras de import e a regra dos specs), a tabela de comandos, a linha do `make web-test` e da cobertura, a linha do web em "What CI checks" e a frase da concorrência. `docs/architecture.md`: um parágrafo sobre as camadas (`core`, `shared`, `pages`, `shell`) que o CI agora cobra.

author: mahtradr
body:
## Problem

Three settings spec files fail every example when they load before any file that requires `spec_helper` in the same process:

| File | Failures when loaded first |
|---|---|
| `spec/lib/common/settings/sessions_settings_spec.rb` | 24 of 24 |
| `spec/lib/common/settings/instance_settings_spec.rb` | 22 of 22 |
| `spec/lib/common/settings/settings_proxy_script_name_spec.rb` | 13 of 13 |

Each failure is the same:

```
Failure/Error: Script.current = nil if defined?(Script)
NoMethodError: undefined method 'current=' for module Lich::Common::MockScript
```

Under `parallel_rspec`, this happens whenever a worker's file list puts one of these files ahead of every `spec_helper` file. It is a latent flake: it depends on how the runtime log splits the files.

## Repro (on main, fc03e4d3)

```
bundle exec rspec spec/lib/common/settings/sessions_settings_spec.rb spec/lib/common/buffer_spec.rb --order defined
# 27 examples, 24 failures: every sessions_settings example (buffer_spec adds 3)
```

Swap the two file arguments and the run passes.

## Root cause

These settings specs deliberately skip `spec_helper`, as the `mock_database_adapter.rb` header and two of the files say. Each one calls `stub_const('Script', Lich::Common::MockScript)` in its own `before` hook.

When `spec_helper` loads after a group is already defined, RSpec's `Configuration#before` attaches the new config hook to existing top-level groups with `group.before`. That *appends* it after the group's own hooks (`add_hook_to_existing_matching_groups` in rspec-core). So spec_helper's reset hook runs after the stub, and `Script.current = nil` lands on MockScript, which has no writer. When `spec_helper` loads first, config hooks run before group hooks, so the reset hits the real Script mock.

## Fix

Register spec_helper's per-example reset hook with `config.prepend_before` instead of `config.before`. For groups defined before spec_helper loads, `Configuration#prepend_before` attaches the hook with `group.prepend_before`, so the reset runs before the group's own hooks. That matches the order every group already gets when spec_helper loads first.

For groups defined later, config hooks still run before group hooks. The reset now also runs ahead of config `before` hooks registered earlier in the process: spec_helper's metadata-filtered `allow(GC)` hook, and `update_spec_helper.rb`'s `LIB_DIR` stub when an update spec loads before spec_helper. Neither touches what the reset touches.

Alternatives I rejected:
- Requiring `spec_helper` in these files: this reverses their documented decision to stay isolated from it.
- Adding `current=` to MockScript: a writer that matches the reset's intent would clear `current_name` after the file set it up.
- Adding `respond_to?(:current=)` to the reset line: this only hides the Script symptom. The reset would still run after the file's own setup for every early-loaded group.

## Verification

- **Ordering sweep:** I ran each of the 50 spec files that do not require `spec_helper`, followed by `spec/lib/common/buffer_spec.rb`, with `--order defined`. Before the fix, the three files above fail and the rest pass. After the fix, all 50 pass. A wider sweep over all 90 files with no direct spec_helper require (adding those that load only a helper such as `update_spec_helper.rb`) gives the same result.
- **Settings files, both orders:** each settings spec file passes both before and after `spec/lib/common/settings_spec.rb`.
- **Full suite:** `bundle exec parallel_rspec -n 4 -o "--seed N" spec` with seeds 1, 31337 and 4242: 8607 examples. The only failures are 16 in `global_defs_spec.rb`, which are local only (a Bundler "missing extensions" warning on stderr) and also fail on main.
- **Regression spec:** `spec/spec_helper_load_order_spec.rb` runs a probe file through a child RSpec process. Its first groups are defined before spec_helper loads; each stubs `Script` with a module that has no `current=` and fills `$_SERVERBUFFER_` in its own `before`. On main those groups fail (the `current=` NoMethodError, or an emptied buffer). With this change they pass, as does a control group defined after spec_helper.
- **RuboCop:** `bundle exec rubocop` reports no offenses.

## Interaction with #1720

#1720 also edits `spec/spec_helper.rb`, adding its globals guard just above this hook. The two branches merge cleanly. On the merged tree:
- the three settings files pass when loaded first;
- `spec/spec_helper_globals_guard_spec.rb` passes;
- a full parallel run with seed 7 shows only the same 16 local `global_defs_spec.rb` failures.

#1720's report flagged this bug as pre-existing and out of scope. It named only `sessions_settings_spec.rb`, but the sibling files fail the same way.

body:
Part 3 of bringing the docs up to date with Burn 26.1.0-experimental-7 and the JIT: tooling, the start pages and the remaining mentions of Rust.

  - source builds need a C compiler, tar and xz instead of Rust;
  - `--install-rust` is removed from the options;

author: knowme-app
body:
A third way to show a profile, between "everyone in the feed" and "hidden".
A donor or surrogate can open her profile only to the agencies, clinics and
intended parents she liked; everyone else sees it neither in the feed nor in
search. The note next to the button warns that this trades offers for
anonymity: fewer agencies will see the profile, so fewer programmes.

- Profile: publish: false + publishAudience: 'liked'; card: feedDate: false +
  audience: 'liked' (rule forbids audience next to a date, so the feed query
  never returns it).
- Access is the like itself: rules open the card, profileDetails and
  profileContacts to whoever is in multiData/favorites/{owner}, and close it
  the moment the like is removed.
- multiData/likedAudience/{viewer}/{owner} is a reverse index the owner writes
  only while the mode is on, so the viewer's feed can find the card. It is an
  address, not a grant.
- readProfileFromNodes / readProfileContacts check membership before asking
  private nodes; the card read alone proves nothing (root matchingCards read).

author: victorpaleologue
body:
The view's multisample anti-aliasing becomes an option. A page can now mount without it:

```ts
await mount("#vizijs", { msaa: 1 }); // or 4, the default
```

## Change

- `ViewOptions` gains `msaa: Msaa`. The target's clear camera and every face's camera take it, so all of a target's cameras agree.
- The browser module's mount options take `msaa`: `1` (`Msaa::Off`) or `4` (`Msaa::Sample4`, the default when absent). Any other value is refused with `msaa: 1 or 4, not …`. `@vizij/runtime`'s `MountOptions` types it as `msaa?: 1 | 4`.
- The desktop app, the headless tests and the `frame_cost` example keep 4×. Native rendering is unchanged.
- Changeset: an `@vizij/runtime` minor.

## GPU-process CPU, 1× against 4×

Method: the study runner `cmp.mjs`, with system Chrome `--headless=new` and `--use-angle=metal` on the real M1 GPU. The display was awake: `caffeinate -u -t 600` during each run, and powerd's "display is on" assertion checked before and after. The page has Quori filling a 1280×800 canvas at device pixel ratio 1, with its program running. Each phase gets 10 s to settle and 20 s of measurement, and the runs alternate 4, 1, 4, 1. The figures are CPU cores per process.

| run | msaa | GPU process, idle | GPU process, speaking | renderer, idle | main thread busy, idle |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| a | 4 | 0.096 | 0.095 | 0.437 | 0.394 |
| a | 1 | 0.093 | 0.092 | 0.438 | 0.395 |
| b | 4 | 0.097 | 0.095 | 0.429 | 0.386 |
| b | 1 | 0.092 | 0.093 | 0.438 | 0.389 |

Turning MSAA off saves about 0.003 core in the GPU process, about 3%. The GPU process's CPU is the command processing; the multisampled target and its resolve are GPU work. So MSAA is not what separates this view's GPU-process CPU from three.js's. The cameras and the uploads remain the candidates.

## How the edges look

Screenshots of Quori from the runs above, full frame and a 4× crop of the left eye, are with the report to Victor. At 1× the eye's and the head's outlines step visibly at device pixel ratio 1. On a 2× display, each step is half as large.

## Tests

- The browser snapshot test also renders Quori mounted with `msaa: 1`. It stays within the reference metric (mean 32×32 difference 0.58, max 10; 0.53 at 4×), and 3,039 pixels differ from the 4× frame, along the edges.
- The rest of `test:browser` (runtime and authoring) passes, and so do the Node smoke, reset and registries tests.
- The harness page takes `?msaa=1`.
- The pre-commit and pre-push hooks pass. The native snapshot references are untouched: native rendering keeps 4×.

author: martina-occhetta
body:
## What
A `scrna-toolkit` command-line interface (also `python -m scrna_toolkit`) for GEO inspection and download, end-to-end preprocessing from a YAML config, summaries, and QC reports. Intended for HPC batch jobs.

## Why
Batch/HPC jobs need the same mechanics as notebooks without writing a script per dataset.

## Changes
- `cli.py`: argparse (stdlib, no new dependency) with subcommands `geo-info`, `download-geo`, `preprocess`, `summarize`, `qc-report`
- `__main__.py`
- `pyproject.toml`: `[project.scripts] scrna-toolkit = "scrna_toolkit.cli:main"`
- `tests/test_cli.py`, README section

## Public API
```
scrna-toolkit [-v] [--version] <command>
  geo-info ACC [--samples] [--include-samples] [--refresh]
  download-geo ACC --output DIR [--pattern GLOB]... [--kind processed|raw_archive|sequence]... [--include-samples] [--overwrite]
  preprocess --input PATH --output OUT.h5ad [--config YAML] [--report-dir DIR] [--format F] [--orientation O] [--prefix P]
  summarize INPUT [--groupby COL]...
  qc-report INPUT --output DIR
```
- `preprocess` runs `load_scrna` → `harmonise_obs(config.metadata)` → `calculate_qc_metrics` → `filter_cells`/`filter_genes(config.qc)` → `preprocess(config.preprocessing)`. It stores `qc_config` and `preprocessing_config` in `uns` and passes through `qc.allow_non_integer_counts`.
- `summarize` opens h5ad files in backed mode, so `X` is never loaded.
- `qc-report` on a processed file computes QC from `layers["counts"]` (with `ensure_raw_counts`, `X` there would be rejected).
- Exit codes: 0 on success, 1 on error (logged as `Type: message`; `-v` adds the traceback), 130 on Ctrl-C, 2 for argparse usage errors.

## Testing
`tests/test_cli.py` (5 tests): `preprocess` end to end with a YAML config and report (checks harmonised columns, embeddings, counts layer, stored configs, report files), `summarize` output, `qc-report` files, `geo-info`/`download-geo` with GEO mocked, non-zero exit on a missing file, argparse error on an unknown command. Manually ran `scrna-toolkit --version`, `geo-info GSE165897` and the missing-file error path. ruff check, ruff format --check and mypy pass locally; the full suite runs in CI before merge.

## Example
```bash
scrna-toolkit preprocess --input data/raw/dataset.h5 --config preprocessing.yaml --output data/processed/dataset.h5ad
```

## Out of scope
Job-scheduler integration (SLURM scripts), multi-file `preprocess` input (use `load_samples` in Python).

author: wodoro
body:
## Why this is needed

The trusted node image for Umbrel and StartOS builds bisq2 from source, but the build has no git history, so the node reports its commit hash as `unknown`. bisq2 now lets such a build take the commit as a `BUILD_COMMIT` build argument (bisq-network/bisq2#5033). This workflow now passes the bisq2 commit it checked out.

## What this changes for users

- A node image built from a bisq2 commit that contains bisq-network/bisq2#5033 logs its real commit hash (10 characters) instead of `unknown`. This takes effect once `bisq-api-commit` points to such a commit. Images built from older bisq2 commits do not change.

## Decisions & Reasoning

**The commit comes from the checkout, not from `bisq-api-commit`.** `bisq-api-commit` is passed to `actions/checkout` as a ref, so it could also be a tag or a branch name. bisq2 accepts only a hex commit hash of 10 to 40 characters and fails the build on anything else. `git -C bisq2 rev-parse HEAD` always gives the full hash of what is built.

**The workflow also works with older bisq2 commits.** Their Dockerfile does not declare `BUILD_COMMIT`, and Docker ignores a build argument that the Dockerfile does not declare. I checked this with buildx v0.37.2: the build succeeds. So this PR can be merged before or after bisq-network/bisq2#5033.

## Notes for reviewers

- I did not run the workflow. I checked that the YAML parses, and that the new step and the image build are in the same job, so `steps.bisq2_commit.outputs.sha` is available to the image build.

author: seblindfors
body:
## Range tint stuck red

LibActionButton 167 moved range checks from a 0.2s poll of every button to ACTION_RANGE_CHECK_UPDATE keyed by action slot. button.outOfRange now persists between events and UpdateAction never clears it. ConsolePort swaps every button's action on each modifier layer, so one out-of-range action on a key painted every layer of that key red, and actions with no range never received an event to clear it. Retargeting fires events for ranged slots only, which is why it sometimes cleared.

The wrapper in ConsolePort/Libs/Local/ActionButton.lua hooks OnButtonCreated and wraps UpdateAction to clear outOfRange when the action or type changes. Reset only, no direct range query, since range reads can be secret on 12.x clients. Blizzard's own buttons carry no range state across action changes.

## Module enable state

GetAddOnEnableState with no character returns the all-characters aggregate, while EnableAddOn and DisableAddOn with no character only touch the current one (WoWUIBugs #156). A module unticked on one character read as Some, IsEnabled said on, LoadAddOn failed, and the Config toggle showed enabled. Blizzard's in-game addon list defaults to UnitGUID("player"), so Modules:GetCharacter returns that and every call passes it, including the two slash command sites. Both paths now read and write one record.

Keyboard turned on for everyone because the toc lost DefaultState: disabled in 2022, so existing addon lists had it enabled, and the 3.3.4 repair only wrote the off case when keyboardEnable was saved. A per-character one-shot (ConsolePortSettings.moduleStateCharacters[guid]) now switches off modules that default off and logs where to turn them back on. Anyone who ticked Keyboard on since 3.3.4 loses it once.

## To verify in game

- UnitGUID("player") is non-nil during ADDON_LOADED on each client. If nil, GetCharacter falls back to the aggregate read for the initial module load.
- Re-entering a layer whose action is out of range turns red again, which depends on EnableActionRangeCheck re-emitting state for an already enabled slot.

author: itsuhsko14
body:
Every img now has width and height taken from the actual file, 188 images in total. Without them the browser doesn't know the size until the photo loads, so the page jumps. That shows up in Cumulative Layout Shift, one of the Core Web Vitals Google uses for ranking.

A global img { height: auto } keeps the existing CSS widths (width: 100% and similar) scaling proportionally. Rules that set an explicit height, like the swiper slides, still win over it.

Stacked on #11. Checked with screenshots of all 33 pages at 375, 768 and 1440px: all 99 are pixel-identical to master.

body: Fixes #380: values whose unit has no suffix rendered with the word `undefined` after them, and currency units lost their symbol. ## Change Grafana's `getValueFormat(unit)` returns `{ prefix?, text, suffix? }`. `none` (the node tooltip default) has no suffix, and currencies put the symbol in `prefix`. Four places in `src/WeathermapPanel.tsx` joined the parts as `` `${text} ${suffix}` ``. They now go through one helper, `formatValueText`, which joins prefix, text and suffix and treats a missing part as empty: - node tooltip metrics; - link tooltip extra metrics; - link value labels and the tooltip's Usage line (`currentValueText`); - the tooltip's Bandwidth line (`currentBandwidthText`). Units that have a suffix keep their exact current output (e.g. `5 b/s`), so existing labels don't change. ## Tests New `src/WeathermapPanel.valueText.test.tsx`: | Test | `main` | This PR | | --- | --- | --- | | Node tooltip metric with no unit shows `Latency: 5` | fails (`5 undefined`) | passes | | Node tooltip metric keeps a suffix (`5 ms`) | passes | passes | | Node tooltip metric keeps a currency prefix (`$5`) | fails | passes | | Link tooltip extra metric with unit `none` shows bare numbers | fails | passes | | Link labels and tooltip Usage line with unit `none` never show `undefined` | fails | passes | The full suite (459 tests), lint and typecheck pass. Closes #380 --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #380: values whose unit has no suffix rendered with the word `undefined` after them, and currency units lost their symbol. Grafana's `getValueFormat(unit)` returns `{ prefix?, text, suffix? }`; `none` (the node tooltip default) has no suffix and currencies put the symbol in `prefix`. Four places in `src/WeathermapPanel.tsx` joined the parts as `` `${text} ${suffix}` ``. They now all go through a single `formatValueText` helper that treats a missing prefix or suffix as empty — node tooltip metrics, link tooltip extra metrics, link value labels, and the tooltip's Usage and Bandwidth lines. Units with a suffix keep their existing output (e.g. `5 b/s`).
