author: endartstudios
body:
Continua a fila de dados do catálogo (T-DADOS-01 → 02 → **03**). Achado que define a fatia (produção, 2026-10-16): `media_score.score_critica` existe em **183 de 16.667** títulos (o bucket Crítica é o diferencial do produto e está vazio) e, dos **4.996 GAME**, só **50** têm `avaliacao_fonte.fonte='igdb'` — enquanto os 4.996 têm `igdb_publico`. Sonda read-only na API do IGDB (`where id = <fonte_id>`): **9 de 9** games amostrados têm `aggregated_rating` real (91,5–100). Ou seja, **o dado existe e nunca foi coletado** — não é ausência honesta.

migration: `20261016140000_critica_igdb_watermark` — **aditiva e não-destrutiva**: só `midia.critica_igdb_em` (nullable, `TIMESTAMP(3)`, sem backfill; o próprio job popula e marca). Nenhuma coluna/tabela existente é alterada ou removida (não há `DROP`/`ALTER COLUMN`/`NOT NULL`), nenhum dado pré-existente é tocado.

## O que muda

- **`mapearCriticaIgdb` (função pura)** — primeiro item da resposta do IGDB → `{ rating, votos, url }`. Só retorna quando `aggregated_rating` é número finito **> 0** (`null`/`0`/negativo/não-numérico → `null`: o IGDB devolve `null` para jogo sem nota da imprensa); `votos` = `aggregated_rating_count` **inteiro > 0** (senão `null` — nunca fabrica volume); `url` = `https://www.igdb.com/games/<slug>` quando há slug. **Nunca lança.**
- **Job `enriquecerCriticaIgdb(limite ≤ 5000)`** (mesmo padrão dos jobs do D-576: `guardaDisco()`, estado próprio, nunca lança por título, log de alvo e de resumo):
  - alvo: `deleted_at IS NULL AND tipo='GAME' AND fonte='igdb' AND critica_igdb_em IS NULL`, ordenado por `id` → **retomável, não repete título**;
  - **lookup EXATO por id**: `POST https://api.igdb.com/v4/games` com `fields name, slug, aggregated_rating, aggregated_rating_count; where id = <fonte_id>; limit 1;` e headers idênticos ao adapter (`client-id` / `authorization: Bearer` / `accept: application/json` / `content-type: text/plain`);
  - **token Twitch** (`client_credentials`) com cache de módulo idêntico ao do `igdb.adapter.ts`. O `obterTokenTwitch` do adapter **não é exportado**, então o cache foi replicado no serviço (como o `prisma/igdb-http.ts` já faz) em vez de alterar o adapter nesta fatia; credenciais nunca aparecem em log;
  - **throttle ≥ 300 ms** antes de cada chamada ao IGDB (medido: 429 após ~22 requisições em rajada) e **retentativa única em HTTP 429** com espera de ~1,5 s; se persistir (ou qualquer outro erro), conta como **falha e não marca o watermark** — o título volta na próxima rodada;
  - com crítica: `avaliacaoFonte.upsert` na chave `{ midia_id, fonte: "igdb" }` (`create`/`update` de `rating`, `media_fonte: 100` e `desvio_fonte` da escala 0–100 via `estatisticas("0-100")` — exatamente como o adapter —, `votos`, `url`) e **então** `mediaScore.recalcularEPersistir(m.id)`, para o `score_critica` do título refletir o dado novo;
  - sem crítica: ausência honesta, **não** grava avaliação e **não** recalcula;
  - **grava `critica_igdb_em` SEMPRE** ao fim do título (com ou sem crítica) — evita fila presa nos jogos sem nota de imprensa; exceção de rede/API não marca;
  - `fonte_id` não-inteiro não é consultável no IGDB → tratado como "sem dado" (marca o watermark, não trava a fila).
- **Fila nova**: `contarPendentes()` ganha `criticaIgdb` (count de `midia` ativa `tipo='GAME' AND fonte='igdb' AND critica_igdb_em IS NULL`); `drenarLote()` consome a 6ª fila por último (é a mais lenta: ~300 ms/título); `backfill-drain.service.ts` inclui `criticaIgdb` **no `total()`** e no `ultimoResumo.pendentesDepois` — foi exatamente o defeito pego no T-DADOS-01 (fila que não entra no `total()` nunca é drenada).
- **DI**: `AdminModule` passa a importar `MediaScoreModule` (exporta `MediaScoreService`, mesmo serviço usado pelo `MediaScoreJobService`); sem ciclo de módulos.
- **Sem rota nova** (o `status()` do admin já expõe o job e o drain o dispara) e **web/UI não foi tocado**.

## Testes

`apps/api`: `npx vitest run` → **169 arquivos, 1480 testes, todos verdes** (1467 no T-DADOS-02 → **+13** novos/estendidos). Cobertura da fatia: mapper (extrai `aggregated_rating`/`_count`/`slug`; `null`/`0`/negativo/não-numérico/array vazio; votos inválidos não invalidam a crítica; sem slug → `url` null), lookup por id (corpo exato, sem `search`, headers `client-id`/`authorization`), `avaliacao_fonte` com `fonte: "igdb"` + `recalcularEPersistir` **do mesmo título** + watermark, watermark **sem** crítica (título sai da fila), `fonte_id` não-inteiro, **429 → espera e repete uma vez** (e 429 persistente → `falhas++` **sem** watermark; erro de rede idem), credenciais ausentes, guarda de disco e as 6 filas em `contarPendentes` + no `total()`/resumo do drain. Mocks fiéis ao driver (D-447); `postJson` mockado — **nunca a rede**.

## Limitações (e follow-ups — filas separadas)

- **O adapter NÃO foi alterado**: `apps/api/src/modules/media-score/adapters/igdb.adapter.ts:72` continua buscando com `search "<titulo>"`, e a relevância devolve **DLC/porta/expansão no lugar do jogo base** — casos reais medidos: id `7346` (Breath of the Wild → *The Champions' Ballad*, DLC, agg 83 em vez de 97,6); id `74` (Mass Effect 2 → *Lair of the Shadow Broker*, DLC, agg 65 em vez de 95,6); id `1070` (Super Mario World → *Super Mario Advance 2*, port GBA). Esta fatia usa `where id = <fonte_id>` e **não** repete o defeito, mas **`igdb_publico` já gravado pode estar contaminado por DLC/porta** (4.996 linhas) — o reparo desses dados é **outra fila**, não escopo aqui.
- **Frescor/repetição**: esta fatia entrega a **primeira coleta** de crítica com watermark. Re-coleta periódica (a crítica da imprensa muda com o tempo) não está implementada — follow-up.
- **Escopo**: só `tipo='GAME' AND fonte='igdb'`. Crítica de outros domínios (filmes/séries/livros) depende das fontes de crítica correspondentes — fora do escopo.
- **Volume**: `aggregated_rating_count` do IGDB é modesta por natureza (dezenas de notas da imprensa), então o "Volume" da confiança do MEDIA Score sobe pouco por esse eixo — é o dado real da fonte, não um defeito.

## Rollback

Reverter o merge deste PR devolve `schema.prisma`, o `MediaScoreModule` no `AdminModule`, o job e o drain ao estado do T-DADOS-02. No banco, a migration é **aditiva e não-destrutiva** (um único `ALTER TABLE "midia" ADD COLUMN "critica_igdb_em" TIMESTAMP(3)`; nenhum `DROP`, nenhum `NOT NULL`, nenhuma reescrita de tabela): nada a consome depois do revert (nenhum caminho de leitura usa a coluna), então o rollback seguro é o revert do código. Se for necessário remover do schema, `prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back 20261016140000_critica_igdb_watermark` seguido de `ALTER TABLE "midia" DROP COLUMN "critica_igdb_em"` — a coluna só contém watermarks de coleta (nenhum dado de produto é perdido; as avaliações de crítica já gravadas em `avaliacao_fonte` são preservadas de propósito, pois são dado de fonte válido). O banco tem backup diário (7.7) como última linha de defesa.

## Gates locais

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → 0 erros
- `npx vitest run` (workspace `apps/api`) → **169 arquivos / 1480 testes, verdes**
- `npx eslint` nos 5 arquivos + `npx prettier --check` → limpos
- `npx prisma validate` (com `DATABASE_URL` dummy; validação não abre conexão) → `The schema at prisma/schema.prisma is valid`
- Guards de migration rodados **localmente** antes do push: `migration-safety.mjs` (contrato B1) e `migration-destructive-guard.mjs` → liberados; no CI, `Migration Safety (B1)` verde (a label entrou no payload via close+reopen).
- CodeQL: o primeiro run acusou 4 alertas `js/incomplete-url-substring-sanitization` — falso positivo do próprio **teste** (`String(url).includes("api.igdb.com")` como filtro de mock); trocado por igualdade exata com as constantes de URL. Run seguinte: **verde, 0 alertas novos**.
- Nenhum arquivo fora dos 7 desta fatia foi tocado (o working tree da máquina tem mudanças de outro programa, **não** incluídas no commit — commit por pathspec).

author: nicolasbissig
body:
## What this changes, and why

Closes #6.

`claude-runway --json` reported `session_5h` and `weekly`. `/usage` also shows a Fable weekly window and a usage credits meter. The data was already in the response, but `parsePayload` read only the keys in `bucketKeys`.

**Per-model weekly windows.** Each `limits[]` entry with `kind == "weekly_scoped"` becomes a `weekly_<model>` row, with the model taken from `scope.model.display_name`. The name is lowercased and anything outside ASCII `a-z0-9` becomes `_`, so a display name with a comma cannot shift the columns of a TOON row. The row gets `100 - percent` left, its own `resets_at`, severity, and a pace judged against seven days. It takes part in `verdict` and `tightest`. A model that already has a top-level window (`seven_day_opus` as `weekly_opus`) is not listed twice. The top-level row keeps its numbers and takes the scoped entry's severity when no `weekly_opus` limits entry exists.

**Usage credits.** `--json` gains a top-level `credits` object with `enabled`, `used`, `limit`, `currency`, `percent_left` and `severity`. Amounts are major units carrying the currency's decimal places (`21.50`, not `21.5`). The source is `spend` (`amount_minor / 10^exponent`), with `extra_usage` as the fallback when `spend` is missing or incomplete. An explicit `spend.enabled: false` is final. The object is omitted when credits are off or any number is missing, so no zero stands in for "unknown". `spend_limit_reached` is ignored because it read `false` on a payload where used (21.50) was already over the limit (20.00).

Credits are a paid reserve the user keeps for time-sensitive work. They never change `verdict` or `tightest`. Agents read `--brief` without the docs, so the TOON line states that rule itself:

```
because: weekly has 3% left
credits: reserve, 0% left (21.50 of 20.00 EUR used), not budget and not part of the verdict
```

MCP `check_usage` returns the same line, since it renders the brief TOON. The tool description, the help text, README and the skill all say that `stop` means stop whatever credits show, and that an agent continues on credits only with the user's explicit authorization for the task.

**Cache.** Credits are stored as derived amounts, never the payload, under cache `version` 2. A version 1 file is ignored and replaced on the next live read, the same path any unreadable cache file already takes. Read as current, it would have reported "no credits" for up to the 6h stale ceiling.

Nothing touches the transport. All new paths run against fixtures built from the payload shape in #6, including one pass over an `httptest.Server` through `--json` and MCP.

## Checks

- [x] `go test -race ./...` passes
- [x] `gofmt -l .` is empty and `go vet ./...` is clean
- [x] `golangci-lint run ./...` exits 0 (run locally with v2.14.0, not the v2.12.2 that CI pins)
- [x] Commit messages follow Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `build:`). The prefix is not cosmetic: `.goreleaser.yaml` filters `docs:`, `test:` and `chore:` out of the generated release notes.

`go mod tidy` leaves `go.mod` unchanged and no `go.sum` appears. `nix build` passes with the suite in the sandbox. `govulncheck` reports nine standard library findings for the local go1.26.8 toolchain, all fixed in 1.26.9 and identical on `main`.

## Invariants

These are contracts, each with a test asserting it. Confirm your change keeps them, or say which one you are deliberately changing and why.

- [x] No failure path renders anything a caller could mistake for a percentage. "I could not find out" must never look like "nothing left".
- [x] An HTTP 429 from the usage endpoint reads as the meter refusing to be read, never as an exhausted subscription.
- [x] The cache holds only derived numbers. No token, ever.
- [x] The OAuth token is never logged and never placed in a process argument list.
- [x] Errors go to stdout as structured `error:` and `help:` lines. stderr stays empty.
- [x] Exit codes hold: 0 for a reading or a definite non-answer, 1 for a runtime failure, 2 for a usage error.
- [x] `go.mod` still has zero dependencies. Adding one needs an argument in this description.

## Authorship

- [x] This change is substantially agent-authored.

Most of this repository is, and that is fine. Ticking the box is not a confession, it is
metadata for the reviewer. What is expected either way: you ran it, you read the diff, and
you can explain why it is correct.

Johno's second tab-strip request from the v0.1.53 test: the GUI title bar cut tab names short (`2026-0…n-guide.md`) while about 260 px lay empty before Raw | Rendered.

**Stacked on #341** (`7c31155`, the scrolled strip's gap before →). Until #341 merges this PR shows its commit too; I'll rebase onto main when it does. The new commits are `74d3fc5` and `60168e5`.

## Cause

Two caps:
- `gui.Editor` gave its tabs at most two thirds of the bar (`TitleLeadingShare(2.0 / 3)`).
- The host (AutoDoc) cut every tab at a fixed 24 cells (`SetMaxTabWidth`).

## Change

- **gui/widget/editor.go:** the strip takes the bar's room up to the switch, with one blank cell before it (the Panel gives a leading widget the free width when no share is set). `TitleLeadingShare` stays for other panels.
- **tui/widget TabStrip.SetLabelFit(min, fit)**, an addition to the API:
  - Each tab shows its whole label while they all fit.
  - When they don't, every label too wide is cut, by the host's `fit(id, w)`, to the widest width at which they all fit (a binary search in `fitTabs`), never under `min` cells including padding.
  - Under that the strip scrolls between ← and → as before.
  - The strip asks for its tabs whole (`width`), so a strip that grows wider shows them whole again.
  - With no fit, `SetMaxTabWidth` is unchanged.
- AutoDoc follows with its middle cut (extension and marks kept) as the fit, and 24 cells as `min`.

## Tests

- `TestATabStripFitsItsLabelsToItsRoom`: one strip at four widths:
  - 120: whole labels, fit never asked;
  - 60: three tabs of 19 cells, cut by fit, no arrows;
  - 30: the minimum, with arrows;
  - 120 again: whole.
- `TestTheEditorsTitleBarHoldsTheHostsTabs`: the tabs now pass column 81 and reach a blank cell before the switch.

## Evidence (VM43, golang:1.25)

- Against #341's `gui/widget/editor.go` (the 2/3 share), the Editor cell fails.

author: deconstructo
body:
Closes #288. Closes #289. Closes #291. Closes #293. Closes #294. Closes #295.

LLVM JIT correctness fixes for a stable release. All of these exist on main; the build without LLVM was never affected.

## Wrong results / crashes fixed

| Issue | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| #289 | A lambda created in JIT code failed with "apply: not a procedure" when passed to `map`/`for-each`/`apply` -- ordinary code once auto-JIT compiled it. JIT functions also never checked their argument count: too few arguments read past the caller's argument array. | `apply()` handles `T_JITCLOSURE`; every JIT function checks argc at entry (`emit_arity_check`) and raises `wrong-number-of-arguments`; `codegen_procedure` binds rest parameters. |
| #291 | Closures with captured variables were compiled with the variables' values at compile time baked in: a hot `set!` counter returned 50 instead of 1001; a closure missed a sibling's `set!`. JIT'd functions whose inner lambdas `set!` a shared variable returned `(1 0)` instead of `(1001 1001)`. | Closures with upvalues stay on the bytecode VM; `reject_captured_assignment` refuses (falls back to bytecode) when a local variable is both `set!` and captured, including Akkadian/cuneiform spellings. |
| #293 | A hot function containing `case` data like `((lambda) ...)` or a quasiquote template like `` `(let ,b ,@body) `` segfaulted the process. | `collect_free_vars` checks each form's shape before reading it; nesting deeper than 2,000 falls back to bytecode instead of overflowing the C stack. |
| #294 | `let*` inside a nested lambda read the global instead of the outer binding (101 instead of 2). | `let*` inits are walked before their name is bound. |
| #295 | `jit-compile!`/`curry-jit-call` compiled `define-library` procedures and `let-syntax` closures that the auto-JIT refuses ("unbound variable"). | Same refusals as the auto-JIT. |
| #288 | Every new closure instance was compiled again; LLVM keeps every module. The repro grew to 722 MB. | Compiled code is cached once per chunk (`Chunk.jit_shared`, CAS) and shared by auto-JIT, `jit-compile!` and `curry-jit-call`. The repro stays at 46 MB; 20,000 fresh hot closures: 0.12 s / 46 MB (was 15.8 s / 378 MB). |

## Cost

Closures with captured variables, and functions that `set!` a captured variable, now run on the bytecode VM. `examples/bench_jit.scm` is unchanged or faster (fib(25) 5.5 ms vs 10.9 ms on a pre-#290 main build).

## Testing

- `tests/jit_tests.scm` sections 11b/11c: every issue above, including the auto-JIT shapes. They fail on main. 1,137 checks pass.
- ctest: 138/138 (default build), 139/139 (`BUILD_LLVM=ON`).
- Independent reviews (fresh subagents, per CLAUDE.md): code + security review of the first two commits; review of the third commit. Their findings are the third and fourth commits (#293, #294, #295, the Akkadian bypass, a `jit_val` race, the depth limit). The fourth commit is small and covered by its own tests; it was not reviewed separately.

## Known limits (not changed here)

- `emit_expr` has no depth guard of its own; the 2,000-level pre-check keeps it safe.
- `collect_free_vars` copies its bound set per scope (memory grows with the square of nesting depth); bounded by the depth limit (worst case seen: 37 MB).

body:
Apple CI restored a Rust cache but deleted its compiled dependencies with `cargo clean` before saving. In run 38864174445, the Apple job restored 101 MB and still compiled Rust tests for 12m37s and the host FFI for 4m45s. The ARM64 release slice already had a useful cache hit and built in 1m30s.

This change removes Intel macOS and Intel iOS Simulator release slices and targets ARM64 throughout the app project and XCFramework packaging. Host bridge tests run in a separate job that retains Rust dependency objects, while app packaging consumes the three revision/digest-verified ARM64 slices. A shared composite action caches SwiftPM repository and binary downloads across Apple jobs, keyed by OS, architecture and package inputs. It excludes toolchain-dependent build state and duplicate multi-GB workspace clones. The private-video macOS test now uses the same SourcePackages directory as the other Xcode builds.

Validation: `make check` passed locally (451 Rust tests, 70 Swift tests, 24 infrastructure tests; 14 Rust integration tests remain ignored by the ordinary suite). Normal commit and push hooks remain enabled. All three ARM64 release-slice CI jobs passed. Local `make apple-build APPLE_RUST_BUILD_ARGS=--package` passed in 61.16s using those CI artifacts on merge revision `0aa63c7fb1e445018ca58b3b0e1a4114a9c83b50` (tree identical to PR head `84721c4`). The XCFramework contains only macos-arm64, ios-arm64 and ios-arm64-simulator; iOS Simulator and macOS app builds both passed. Both Intel slice arguments are rejected before compilation. Xcode also fetched LiteRT-LM from the shared cache during dependency resolution. The complete hosted CI suite is still running. New cache keys start cold; warm-run speedup has not yet been measured. Simulator suites, native tests and slice provenance checks are retained.

author: dumbris
body:
## Summary
Windows stdio and launcher children are now created `CREATE_SUSPENDED`, assigned to the instance Job Object, and only then resumed (`NtResumeProcess`). A child therefore runs no code, and forks no descendant, before it is inside the Job, so a retired instance cannot leave a process running between start and Job assignment.

- `internal/winjob`: `MarkSuspended`, `IsSuspended`, `Resume`, `Job.AssignAndResume` (no new dependencies; ntdll via x/sys/windows lazy proc).
- stdio/Docker (`createProcessGroupCommandFunc`, `assignProcessTree`) and launcher (`applyProcAttrs`, `createJob`) use it, inside the existing admitted sections. Assignment or resume failure closes the Job and fails the start; the existing containment-failure path kills the child. The non-admitted `extractProcessGroupID` fallback kills a suspended child it could not contain.
- tasks.md: T093b and T085b ticked; architecture.md retirement barrier note.

## Tests
- New Windows-tag tests: `internal/winjob/suspended_test.go` (child does not run until assigned+resumed; failed assignment never resumes) and `internal/upstream/core/process_windows_job_test.go` (T4.12: suspended until Job assignment, retirement kill reaches the grandchild). These run on CI windows-latest; they cannot run on the macOS dev host.
- Verified locally: `GOOS=windows go build ./...`, `GOOS=windows go vet` on touched packages, `go test -race` for `internal/upstream/launcher` and `internal/upstream/core`, golangci-lint (bare, server tag, GOOS=windows; only pre-existing findings remain).

author: riderx
body: ## Summary - **iOS**: after a background download (silent push / background fetch / cold background launch) the bundle was only queued as next. `installNext` only runs from `appMovedToBackground`, which a background launch never posts, so the user opened the old bundle. Now `installNextIfInBackground()` installs it right away when `appInBackground` is true. Safe with #947: the notifyAppReady rollback check stays deferred until foreground. - **Android**: `HeadlessUpdateWorker` called `updater.shutdown()` after handing over to the live plugin, writing its empty stats queue (`[]`) over the plugin's newer pending stats file. New `shutdown(boolean persistStats)`; the worker skips the write once `CapacitorUpdaterPlugin.instanceLoaded`. Found in Codex/Grok review of Cap-go/capgo.app#3627 (Capgo native notifications background updates). ## Test plan - [x] iOS `UpdateLifecycleTests` (16/16), new: `testBackgroundDownloadInstallsRightAwayWhileInBackground`, `testForegroundDownloadWaitsForTheNextBackground` - [x] Android `CapacitorUpdaterUnitTest` + `HeadlessUpdateTest` (214/214), new: `shutdownWithoutPersistKeepsAnotherInstanceStatsFile` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need. ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Fixed iOS automatic updates so a downloaded bundle installs when the app is in the background. Foreground downloads remain queued until the app returns to the background. * If an iOS installation attempt fails, the previous bundle remains active and the downloaded bundle stays queued for retry. * Improved iOS update completion reporting to reflect the current bundle. * Improved Android update-stat handling during background updater shutdown, preserving pending information and transferring it to the active updater when available.

- \`grand-canyon.ts\`: a street line and a hip/quarter pipe on the flat rim, a kicker at the lip and a named \`Canyon Drop\` gap over the first cliff. The level test drives it at 24, 27 and 32 m/s and it clears every time.

**How hard was it:** fetching is trivial and automatic. The cost is the level: someone has to read the heights, find the flat shelf and the cliff, and write the spec (about 40 lines, the gap needed no tuning). For "all the US ones" and user requests, the next step is a level generator that does this from the heightmap (flat patches for kit, steepest drop for the gap, spawns on flat ground). Not in this PR.

Request-your-location also needs a form, a place to keep the requests and a cap on fetches. Not in this PR either.

author: thegorgeousivorchival
body:
## Summary

- `Decoder::decode` answered with a `Vec<(Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>)>` — a name and a value allocated for every field of every block, which each consumer read from and dropped. It now walks the block and hands each field to a visitor as it is read: an indexed field gives up the table entry it already names, a plain literal gives up its own run inside the block, so a field that is only read costs neither an allocation nor a copy.
- What is **not** removed: the pair a dynamic entry keeps (two allocations per inserted field where the old shape costed four, because the table entry *is* the field now), and one copy into the decoder's warm buffer for a Huffman string.
- gRPC keeps a `Gate` of four `Option<bool>` judged as the fields pass (`Self::find` and the header list are gone); xHTTP/H2 captures `:method`, `:path` and the head lines during the single visit, and `synth_head` asks for exactly the bytes it carries, so it never grows.
- Rows and prose ship with the change: `header-field-copies-per-head`, `table-entry-copies-per-indexed-field`, `decoder-buffer-writes-per-borrowed-field`, `header-field-allocations-per-inserted-field` on `carrier-grpc`, and `head-buffer-reallocations-per-request-head` on `carrier-xhttp`.

## Witnesses

All four new claims are gated by addresses, not bytes: a plain field's base has to lie inside the caller's block at the offset its own bytes occupy; the pair a dynamic entry is has to be the pair the consumer was handed, for the insert and for the index that names it; buffers warmed by a Huffman literal keep pointer and capacity across the borrowed block that follows and end it empty; and `synth_head` reads `capacity == len` for both stream shapes. Mutating the decoder back to the copy fails the first and the third locally; the head test fails on `49 != 29` with the old `+32`.

## Test plan

- [x] `./scripts/check.sh` green on this machine through `method docs` (205 counts agreed), `ci scope`, `method matrix` and `cargo test --workspace` (490 ferrox-app tests, 33 in the three touched modules).
- [ ] **Operation counts are CI-only here**: `count-ops.sh` exits at `valgrind not installed` on darwin/aarch64, so `append_pem 1205` is unverified locally. Four tests join the same `ferrox-app` bin, and this file's history says a test-count move shifts that probe by ~13 Ir — so the `ops.yml` `check exact counts` step is expected to print a measured number here. I will read that diff and re-bless in a follow-up commit only if the moved count is explained by the added tests and nothing else.
- [ ] CI: `vless-grpc` and `vless-xhttp` cells, conformance and Miri as the scope plan names them.

author: victorzakharov
body:
Fixes #243 (the first part: what the phone's steady frame draws).

**What the report pointed at:** on the phone the forest's top view drew 1.17M triangles with no foes, and the GPU set the pace (25 ms frames on 9.5 ms of CPU). three.js culls an instanced mesh only whole, by the sphere round all its instances, so the trees round the clearing, the thicket, the grass and the ferns were drawn whole in every view and in the shadow map: 661k of the top view's 1.31M triangles lay outside the view of the pass that drew them.

**The fix:**
- `world/culling.ts`: each of those meshes' instances sorted into cells at build (a tree each, the thicket in slices of the ring, the grass and ferns in 8 m squares). Before each render the cells in the camera's view are packed to the front of its instances, and sent to the GPU only when they change. One draw a mesh as before, of what is in view. (Splitting them into meshes of their own cut as many triangles but drew 45 to 60 more times a frame.)
- What casts a shadow casts it from a copy drawn by the shadow map alone, its instances outside the shadow map's box let go at build (40-45% of the trees). The biome's baked static caster is drawn by the shadow map alone too: it was drawn in the frame as well, 16k triangles for nothing.
- The 23 empty rubble pools (and the particles' points) were set up by the renderer every frame with nothing in them, in the frame and the shadow pass: 23 to 46 draws a frame of nothing. Hidden while empty, shown through the boot's warm-up so every program still compiles.

**Measured** (`npm run lab -- perf maelstrom,glacialNova --screen 832x384@3.75 --quality low@518400`, the phone's screen and Auto's lowest, against the commit before the fix, both sides run fresh):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| triangles, standing with 10 foes | 1.47M | 0.89M |
| draws (GL) | 377-387 | 375-385 |
| scene pass, GPU (desktop) | 4.8-5.9 ms | 4.4-5.0 ms |

`lab draws`, no foes: 1.31M → 0.54M triangles in the top view, 1.30M → 0.57M in the third person view, 1.12M → 0.39M in the first person view, with 4 fewer draws in each. With 10 foes, 227 → 204 renderer draws in the frame and 186 → 163 in the shadow pass. The world's pictures in the forest are the same as before in all nine of `lab light`'s views (only the "Wave 1" banner was caught at another moment).

The desktop's GPU time falls less than the triangles do: there the GPU waits on the page's commands (the scene pass's GPU time matches the render's CPU time). The phone's GPU sets its pace, so it should gain more. **Please check on the phone:** the FPS standing in the forest's top view (it was 36-40), and the performance report after Maelstrom and Glacial Nova.

**The lab:**
- `lab perf <skills>` (new): skills cast in turn with the foes coming, every frame timed as the game's performance report times it, by phase: the frame, the update by stage, the render, the GPU by pass, the draws and triangles. `--quality` builds the hero at the level's detail, as a phone whose Auto settled on Low builds him. It has a canary.
- `lab draws`: the triangles drawn outside the view of the pass that drew them, and the draws that drew nothing, both with canaries.

**Round two, after the owner's phone report** (standing 60 fps and Maelstrom fixed; Glacial Nova still at 34-36 fps, and one shader compiled mid-run):
- **Particles were 3 times too wide on the phone.** They were sized by the canvas's height (1440) while drawn into the scene's target (483 high), so every particle filled 9 times the pixels it should. Glacial Nova's particles filled **7.7M pixels a frame, 15 times the scene's own pixels** (up to 9M); now **0.69M, 1.4 times**. Standing: 2.3M to 0.15M; Maelstrom: 3.3M to 0.25M. They're sized in the scene's pixels now (`pointScale()`). On a desktop at 100% nothing changes (all 18 of `lab light`'s views are the same); on the phone, particles now look as they do on a desktop: a third as wide as before.
- **The shader compiled mid-run** was the forest's wood rubble's shadow. three's shared shadow material takes each caster's texture but builds a new program only when instancing or skinning changes between draws, so the shadow programs depended on the order casters are drawn in. This PR's shadow copies changed the order. Now the texture is let go for casters that don't test alpha (it does nothing there), so the programs no longer depend on order (`steadyShadowPrograms`).
- The lab: `lab compiles` (new) breaks a prop of every kind and fights the first wave in each biome (foes dying, which no other check let happen), and names each late program with the draw that first used it. `--boot low@518400` boots the page as a phone's Auto settled there. `lab perf` now reports the particles' fill.

**Please check on the phone:** Glacial Nova's FPS, and that the report says `compiled after load 0`. The particles will look smaller than you're used to on the phone; that's their real size, as on a desktop.

**Left for later in #243:** the hero's update is up to 7 ms on the phone, mostly the mage's cloth (the robe's drape, the sleeves) and the arm IK, done on the CPU every frame. Cutting it on Low would change how the robe moves, so I left it for you to decide.

author: abzum-admin
body:
Part of #2727 (P5c). **Stacked on #2759** (P5b, `lead/p5b-one-publish`). It also merges #2752 (Studio frame, step 1), because it edits the Data tab that PR added.

## What changes

**Module drafts are gone as a separate concept**
- Only an Application has a draft. `save_draft`, `restore_release_draft` (system path) and `validated_builder_draft_write_context_internal` now refuse Module roots. The store's `saveDraft` refuses a Module source, and the restore command schema is Application-only.
- Publication still stages each inline Module's lowering in its internal root before compiling and releasing it (the root keeps its identities). It now does that with the new `vortex_definition.stage_owned_module_source`, which replaces its use of `save_draft`. The rule is the same as before: authority over the owning Application, an ordinary owner for a person, and the source must equal the owner's inline Module (`is_owned_module_source_internal`). `stageOwnedModuleSource` replaces `saveOwnedModuleSource`.
- Migration `20261014011400_modules_edited_inside_application.sql` runs between `set local role vortex_owner` / `reset role` and holds the four canonical bodies.

**Studio edits a module through the app draft**
- The Data panel lists the application's own `modules` from the draft source, with a Fields editor for each. Used modules (`uses`) are listed separately with a Read-only badge and "Owned by <app>".
- The Fields editor (rewired `module-fields-editor.tsx`) adds a field, or changes a field's label, type or required flag, in `source.body.modules[<key>]`. The change is applied as one edit of the application draft history (busy key `moduleField`) and is saved by the normal Save. It is published with the application. The pure transform is `changeInlineModuleField` in `module-field-shape.ts`, checked by the application source schema.
- Opening a used module shows a note saying it is read-only here and is changed in its owner's Studio. It links to the owner's Data tab with the module open (for example CRM → Organisation Administration for `vortex.system_directory`).
- `?tab=data&module=<key>` opens a module directly.

**Deleted**
- Routes `/studio/modules/[organizationId]/[moduleRootId]` (root, fields, queries, before-save), `_lib/module-address-redirect.tsx`, `_lib/studio-module-owner.ts` and `_lib/studio-module-tools.ts`.
- Components `studio-module-editor`, `module-fields-workspace`, `module-fields-agent-tools`, `module-field-label-editor`, `module-text-field-settings-editor`, `module-query-filter-editor`, `module-before-save-condition-editor`, `module-publication-editor` and `module-editor-dirty`.
- Server actions `studio/module-field-label-actions.ts` and the `modules/**/actions.ts` files. Server libraries `_lib/studio-module-field-edits.ts`, `studio-module-query-filter.ts`, `studio-module-before-save-condition.ts` and `studio-module-field-shape.ts`, plus `_lib/module-query-filter-commands.ts` and `module-before-save-condition-commands.ts`.
- Platform `module-draft-edit.ts`, `module-field-edit.ts`, `module-query-filter-edit.ts`, `module-query-filter-draft.ts`, `module-before-save-condition-edit.ts`, `module-before-save-condition-draft.ts` and `module-query-filter-encoding.ts`. Also the publication service methods `read/validateModuleQueryFilterDraft` and `read/validateModuleBeforeSaveConditionDraft`, `evaluateModuleDraftPermission`, and the exports `moduleFieldEdits`, `moduleQueryFilterEdits` and `moduleBeforeSaveConditionEdits`.
- The Studio home and organisation pages' Modules lists and their links (Fields, Saved views, Publish). `OrganizationBuilderRoot` is Application-only (no `kind`). `moduleSaveRefusal` is deleted, and the exports `compileModuleCandidate`, `CompiledModuleCandidate`, `ModuleSourceQuery` and `SourceIdentityAssignments` that became unused are no longer exported (knip shows no new findings against the base).

## Not kept (decision)
The saved-view filter and before-save rule editors were bound to Module drafts. Each had about 1,300 lines of server-side compile logic per module root. They are deleted rather than rewired. Until an app-draft version exists, saved views and rules are changed through Releases → Import from source, which edits the whole application source, `modules` included. That is the one save path.

body:
# Backport

This will backport the following commits from `main` to `9.5`:
 - [[Dashboard] Wait past the maps EMS budget in the ecommerce map-only journey (#295117)](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/pull/295117)

<!--- Backport version: 12.1.2 -->

### Questions ?
Please refer to the [Backport tool documentation](https://github.com/sorenlouv/backport)

<!--BACKPORT [{"author":{"name":"Kibana Machine","email":"42973632+kibanamachine@users.noreply.github.com"},"sourceCommit":{"committedDate":"2026-10-16T10:48:15Z","message":"[Dashboard] Wait past the maps EMS budget in the ecommerce map-only journey (#295117)

Fixes #292683

### Summary

- `Journey[ecommerce_dashboard_map_only] Go to Ecommerce Dashboard with
Map only` timed out waiting for `div[data-title="[eCommerce] Orders by
Country"][data-render-complete="true"]`.
- The dashboard's single panel is a map whose basemap is an `EMS_TMS`
layer. While its Elastic Maps Service style request is in flight,
`EMSVectorTileLayer.syncData` holds an open data request, so
`isLayerLoading()` is `true` and `hasErrors()` is `false` — which keeps
`isMapLoading` `true` and `data-render-complete` at `"false"`.
- When an EMS request stalls, the panel's earliest possible
`data-render-complete="true"` is **~33.1s**: `EMS_LOAD_TIMEOUT` 32s
(`@elastic/ems-client` 8.7.0) + 100ms store-sync debounce +
`RENDER_TIMEOUT` 1s. Only then does the layer error, drop out of
`isMapLoading`, and let `rendered$` flip.
- The awaiter used Playwright's **default 30s** — shorter than that
33.1s ceiling, so a stalled EMS request could never resolve into a
terminal state inside the wait. The journey was guaranteed to fail
rather than observe the product's error path.
- This raises that one awaiter to 60s, clearing the product's own
ceiling by ~27s.

### Context

- Diagnosis **departs from** the [prior investigator
comment](https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/292683#issuecomment-5776933219),
which was 10 days old and predated the second failure, so it was
re-investigated from scratch. That comment concluded the map "paints
fully but never publishes render-complete" and proposed adding an `idle`
handler to `TileStatusTracker`. The failure screenshot rules that out:
the basemap is **not** painted. EMS `road_map`'s first style layer is
`{"id":"background","type":"background","paint":{"background-color":"#f8f4f0"}}`,
but the failure canvas samples exactly `#ffffff` at every point outside
the choropleth — so no EMS style was ever applied, and maplibre's `idle`
does not fire while a map has never received a style or tiles.
- What the screenshot does show: the Elasticsearch choropleth layer and
its value labels fully rendered (Kibana's own work finished in ~2-3s,
matching the WebGL `ReadPixels` log lines), a white basemap canvas, the
panel's loading spinner still spinning at 30s, and no error toast or
layer-error icon — i.e. the basemap layer was still mid-request, not
failed.
- Both reported failures carry this identical signature, on two
different pipelines and branches — [`kibana-chrome-forward-testing` /
`main` build
730](https://buildkite.com/elastic/kibana-chrome-forward-testing/builds/730#01a0c908-efd5-4010-9ffc-afdaffd479c7)
(2026-09-22) and [`kibana-on-merge` / `9.5` build
111569](https://buildkite.com/elastic/kibana-on-merge/builds/111569#01a0fca8-d4d4-4673-8ce3-b313fbb87e85)
(2026-10-02) — so this is not Chrome-Beta-specific as the prior comment

body: Answers the v0.4.4 test feedback. ## Audit (main point) Only 2 of 3 deliberately tampered lines were flagged as Invalid; clearing the signature and moving the timestamp back made an entry look merely unsigned, deleted entries left no trace, and the warning appeared only on the page holding the bad entry. - Entries are now **hash-chained**: each gets a sequence number and the previous entry's signature, both under its own HMAC. A signed `audit_chain` head row (migration 023) records the newest entry, the retention prefix and when chaining began, so none of these can be changed without `AUDIT_HMAC_KEY`. - `GET /api/v1/audit/integrity` verifies the **whole** log: signatures, links, holes in the numbering, newest entries cut off, the head. The API re-checks every 5 minutes and logs `audit: LOG INTEGRITY COMPROMISED`. Entries carry `sig_reason`. - Dashboard: verdict banner above the table on every page, red rows with the reason. - Retention prunes the oldest entries as a prefix and records it in the head. Writers are serialised with an advisory lock. - Limits (documented): whoever holds the key can rewrite the chain; a database writer with an old copy of the head row can restore it after truncating the tail. Use `AUDIT_EXPORT_URL` for more. Verified live with the five cases (edit; edit + clear sig; edit + clear sig + timestamp back; sig + seq cleared + timestamp back; delete) and by integration tests. ## Other points from the feedback - `allowed_hosts` without `network_enabled: true` -> 400. A whole command line in `command` -> 400 with a hint (was 200 + exit 126). - Python SDK: `allowed_hosts`, `secrets` (run/run_async/stream), `create_key(allowed_secrets=)`. Go SDK too (the feedback assumed it already had them; it did not). - `scripts/check-env.sh` lists the problems in production mode; `make dev-env` flips `VAULTRUN_INSECURE_DEV=false`. - Costs: names plus short ID and link (two sessions with the same name looked duplicated), `ended` marker for deleted/stopped sessions, sub-cent amounts show 4 decimals, zero-cost sessions not listed. - Deleted/stopped session URL shows "Session not found". Not done: the MCP server still has no `allowed_hosts`/`secrets` parameters. ## Testing `go test ./...`, integration tests (testcontainers), Python SDK tests, `tsc` + `next build`, headless-Chrome run (axe clean on all pages, regressions ui1/ui3 pass), live API checks.

author: xen2
body:
On Direct3D 12, `DescriptorSet.SetValue` always copied the shader resource view, even into a slot the shader declares as `RWBuffer` / `RWTexture`. Render features and materials fill their resource groups through `SetValue`, so a shader writing such a resource wrote nothing.

Voxel GI hit it: voxelization writes its fragments buffer this way, so on Direct3D 12 voxel GI added no light at all. GPU-based validation reports it as `Descriptor type doesn't match shader register type` (SRV in heap, UAV register). Direct3D 11 and Vulkan already pick the view from the layout.

## The fix

- The Direct3D 12 descriptor set layout keeps which slots are UAVs, and `SetValue` writes the UAV there.
- Voxel GI: after its copies, the clipmap and mipmap textures go back to shader resource before the lighting pass samples them (GPU-based validation: `Incompatible texture barrier layout`, `COPY_DEST`).
- Voxel GI: the fragments buffer and the voxel textures are cleared when created. Vulkan doesn't zero new memory, and parts of them are read before anything writes them (the clipmaps not updated yet, the mipmap borders). On lavapipe this gave NaN or negative light when the memory came from an earlier test.

## Tests

- The voxel GI case of `MaterialTransparencyTests` is no longer skipped, except on macOS: MoltenVK has no geometry shaders for the default voxelization, and the tri-axis voxelization pipeline fails to create there.
- Stride.Graphics.Tests.10_0 passes on Direct3D 11 / 12 and Vulkan (WARP / lavapipe). The full Vulkan suite passed 4 times in a row; before the clear it failed about half the time. Voxel GI also passes on an RTX 5080, on Direct3D 12 and Vulkan.

author: mattiarosso92
body:
## Summary

This PR generalizes `FREQNESS_SpatialComparison` and `FREQNESS_LandscapeComparison` in both MATLAB and Python beyond two-group or two-condition comparisons.

The functions now support multidimensional factorial designs while preserving the established pairwise interfaces.

## Main changes

- Support arbitrary N-dimensional factorial input grids.
- Support within-subject, between-subject, and mixed designs.
- Allow named factors and factor levels.
- Match and reorder repeated observations using participant identifiers.
- Allow selection of individual main effects and interactions.
- Preserve existing two-input pairwise calls and outputs.

## Statistical inference

### Spatial comparison

- Computes direct voxel-wise omnibus statistics.
- Uses design-aware permutations for maximum-cluster-mass correction.
- Controls the family-wise error rate jointly across requested effects, frequencies, and components.

### Landscape comparison

- Uses direct ANOVA by default for factorial designs.
- Supports Friedman and Kruskal–Wallis alternatives for compatible one-factor designs.
- Uses permutation ANOVA only when explicitly requested.
- Applies Benjamini–Hochberg FDR correction across frequencies independently for each effect, measure, and component.

## Visualizations

The MATLAB and Python visualizations were refined for publication-ready presentation:

- Consistent typography and layouts
- Colourblind-conscious palettes
- Clearer corrected-significance encoding
- Orthographic MNI spatial views
- Restrained anatomical scaffolding
- Human-readable landscape labels
- Closely aligned MATLAB and Python presentation

These changes affect visualization only and do not alter the underlying statistical results.

## Validation

- All 220 Python tests pass.
- Pairwise compatibility and participant reordering are covered by regression tests.
- Factorial within-subject and mixed-design cases are covered.
- Factorial visualization paths are covered.
- MATLAB spatial and landscape factorial analyses were executed successfully on matched simulated data.
- MATLAB and Python generated consistent statistical and visual outputs.

**Yayın kullanıcı onayı bekler.** Migration 014, yayından önce Supabase'e uygulanmalı.

**Bağımlılık:** kod düzeyinde #19 (kasa/banka, migration 013) ile bağımlılık yok. Ancak ikisi de aynı ortak dosyalara dokunuyor:
- `src/context/data.tsx` (realtime tablo listesi)

Önerilen sıra **#19 → bu PR**. #19 birleşince main bu dala alınır, çakışmalar çözülür ve testler yeniden çalıştırılır.

## Özet
- **Sistem kütüphanesi** (`/receteler`, Mühendislik grubunda)
  - Sistem tanımı: üretici, seri, tür, renk.
  - Bileşenler: kasa, kanat, kayıt, cam, fitil, menteşe, kol, kilit, bağlantı ve montaj malzemeleri.
  - Bileşen bilgileri: profil kodu, standart boy, fire oranı, kg/m.
  - Fiyat için mevcut maliyet kataloğuna bağlanır; fiyat ikinci kez tutulmaz.
  - Kurallar: adet, kesim boyu ve parça formülleri; açı.
  - **Üretici verisi uydurulmaz.** Kütüphane boş başlar. "Boş şablon" yalnız yapı içerir, sayı içermez.
- **Güvenli formül dili** (`src/bom/formula.ts`)
  - `eval` ya da `Function` kullanılmaz.
  - Değişkenler: W, H, N, K, A, P. İşlemler: + − × ÷, parantez, `min/max/ceil/floor/round`.
  - Hatalı formül veya bilinmeyen değişken açık bir Türkçe hata verir; asla sessizce 0 sayılmaz.
- **Hesap motoru** (`src/bom/engine.ts`)
  - Profil kesim boyları yalnız sistemin kendi üretim kurallarından gelir; pencere çevresinden türetilmez.
  - Fire uygulanır; standart boy adedi yalnız tahmindir (gerçek kesim optimizasyonu PR-8'de).
  - Fiyat yalnız birimi uyan katalog kaydından alınır, yoksa "fiyat tanımlı değil" yazılır.
  - Kesim listesi ve uyarılar üretilir.
- **Proje reçetesi**
  - Onaylı metraj seçilir.
  - Poz başına ya da kategoriye göre toplu sistem ataması yapılır.
  - Hesaplanır, sürüm olarak kaydedilir, onaylanır.
  - Sürüm geçmişi, iki sürümün karşılaştırması ve Excel/PDF dışa aktarım var.
  - Metraj revize edilince "Yeniden hesapla" yeni bir taslak oluşturur ve atamaları poz koduna göre taşır. **Onaylı eski sürüm korunur.**
- **Sunucu kuralları**
  - `create_bom_version` sürümü, atamaları ve satırları tek bir işlemde yazar. Sürüm numarası proje kilidiyle atanır.
  - Kaynağın onaylı olup olmadığını (`source_approved`) sunucu metraj tablolarından hesaplar. İstemci sürüm, atama ya da satırı doğrudan ekleyemez.
  - Onaylanacak sürüm için iki şart var: kaynak onaylı olmalı ve hiç hata olmamalı. Bu kural doğrudan tablo güncellemesinde de tetikleyiciyle zorunlu tutulur.
  - Onaylı sürüm ve satırları güncellenemez, silinemez.

## Migration 014 (`20261016001400_leonx_bom.sql`)
- 6 tablo: `product_systems`, `system_components`, `system_rules`, `bom_versions`, `bom_assignments`, `bom_lines`.
- 2 görünüm: `bom_material_totals`, `bom_cut_list`.
- Güvenlik: RLS açık, erişim yalnız sahip hesaba; anon'un hiçbir yetkisi yok. Tetikleyici fonksiyonları istemciden çağrılamaz.
- DROP veya DELETE ifadesi yok, tekrar çalıştırılabilir, mevcut veriye dokunmaz.

## Testler (yerel)
- `npm run check`: **347 geçti**, 1 atlandı (gerçek referans ölçümü; yalnız `CAD_REFERANS_DIR` ile çalışır). Formül, motor, karşılaştırma ve dışa aktarım testleri yeni; derleme ve yayın kapısı geçti.
- `npm run test:db`: **258 kontrol** başarılı (BOM için ~50 yeni). Kapsam: RLS, onaylı sürümün değişmezliği, sürüm numarasının benzersizliği, onaysız kaynağın reddi, migration'ın iki kez uygulanması.

- Gerçek üretici sistemi ve gerçek proje verisiyle denenmedi.

author: floorfiend
body:
## What does this change?

> **Independent of the other open pull requests.** It is based on `main` and merges cleanly with #248 (`:is()`/`:where()`) and #251 (CSS nesting) in any order: the helpers they share (`Selector.getChain`/`matchesChain`, and with #248 also `addMostSpecific`, `compareSpecificity`, `isPseudoElementSelector`, the selector printing helpers and `CSSParser.complex_selector`) are byte for byte the same, at the same place, in each. All seven of these pull requests merged together pass `mvn install` (906 tests, 0 failures).

`:not()` was a parse error (`not is not a valid function in this context`), so every rule using it was skipped. This adds the Selectors Level 4 negation pseudo-class with a comma-separated list of complex selectors:

- An element matches when it matches **none** of the arguments, e.g. `.row:not(:last-child)`, `li:not(.a, .b, [data-k])` or `p:not(.card > p, h1 + p)`.
- The specificity is that of the **most specific argument**, counting its whole selector chain, so `i:not(.x, #y)` counts as an id selector and `i:not(#a .x)` as (1,1,0).
- Arguments may use type, universal, class, id, attribute and structural pseudo-class selectors, a nested `:not()`, and the descendant, child (`>`) and next-sibling (`+`) combinators.
- User-action pseudo-classes (`:hover`, `:active`, `:focus`) are valid but never match, as Selectors 4 requires of non-interactive user agents. So `:not(:hover)` matches every element.
- An argument with a pseudo-element anywhere in it (including the legacy `:before`) is invalid. It drops its rule with a parse warning, as such rules already did.

Implementation:
- `CSSParser` gains `complex_selector_list` and `complex_selector` productions. Each argument is built with `simple_selector` and `mergeSimpleSelectors`, like a rule's own selector.
- `Selector.addNegationCondition` adds the specificity.
- A new `NegationCondition` does the matching, testing each argument's chain upwards from the element with `Selector.matchesChain`. The Matcher works top-down, so a condition cannot use it.
- Classes and ids inside `:not()` are deliberately **not** recorded as required by the rule index, since they must be absent for a match. A test covers this.

**Tests**
- `NegationPseudoClassTest` (core): 11 matcher-level cases covering lists, structural arguments, complex arguments with each combinator, user-action pseudo-classes, nesting, specificity (including a complex argument's), the rule index, and invalid arguments dropping only their rule.
- Visual test `not-pseudo-class`: every box should be green, including a row of complex arguments. On current `main` the rows render red.
- `DomAttributeResolver` moves out of `MatcherRuleIndexTest` so both tests can share it.

`mvn install` passes with 0 failures and the skip count unchanged; no other visual baseline changed.

## How was it written?

- [ ] Written by hand

body:
## What does this PR do?

A user has one presence row (unique `userId`), but several realtime connections (tabs, devices) can hold it, spread across workers and nodes. Two things went wrong:

- Closing one connection deleted the shared row while the user's other connections were still open (`presences.*.delete` fired, user shown offline).
- A close and a near-simultaneous upsert could interleave, so a close clobbered a presence another connection had just written.

This synchronises the two paths so the row lives exactly as long as a connection holds it, whichever operation runs first.

## How it synchronises

A per-user **`Utopia\Lock\Distributed` lock** (`presence:{project}:{user}`) wraps both the upsert and the close, and a soft **Redis counter** (`presence:connections:{project}:{user}`) tracks how many connections hold the row:

- **Upsert** — under the lock, write the row and, on a connection's first hold, `INCR` the counter.
- **Close** — under the lock, `DECR` the counter and delete the row (and emit `presences.*.delete`) only when it reaches zero; otherwise the row stays.

Because both sides take the same lock, counting a new holder can never race a decrement-to-zero, so the outcome is the same no matter which runs first:

- close-before-upsert → row removed, then re-created by the upsert.
- upsert-before-close → new holder counted, so the close sees a non-zero count and keeps the row.

The counter arithmetic lives in `Presences\State`, which takes the Redis handle; the realtime layer only orchestrates the lock. The DB row stays the single source of truth — Redis holds only the lock and the counter, both soft state.

**Every holder-leave path feeds the counter**, not just socket close, so the count can never drift above the live holders:

- **Close** — `State::releaseConnection()` (lock → decrement → fence → delete at zero).
- **Re-authentication** — `unsubscribe()` clears the connection's holds, so the handler captures them first: a re-auth to the same user carries the holds across, a re-auth to a different user releases the previous user's holds.
- **REST delete** — removing the row over HTTP strips it from each holder's in-memory map, so the worker decrements the counter for those holders (counter only — the row is already gone).

**Lease safety.** The destructive delete is fenced on lock ownership: before deleting, `refresh()` proves the lease is still held (a token-guarded CAS). If the locked work outran the TTL or the key was evicted, another operation may already own the user, so the delete is skipped and the row left to its `expiresAt`. Lock contention falls the same way — toward keeping the row — never toward deleting a live one.

Abnormal death (worker OOM/kill) decrements nothing; the row's `expiresAt` is the intended backstop for that case.

Dead sockets reach the close path too: the Swoole `heartbeat_check_interval` / `heartbeat_idle_time` config closes a silently-gone connection (lost network, suspended device), so its `onClose` decrements like a clean close.

## Behaviour

| Scenario | Result |
|---|---|
| c1, c2 both hold; c1 closes | count 2 → 1, row stays, no event |
| then c2 closes | 1 → 0, delete + `presences.*.delete` |
| network loss (no FIN) | heartbeat closes the socket → onClose → decrement |
| close vs upsert interleave | serialised by the per-user lock, order-independent |
| re-auth to a different user | previous user's holds released under the lock |
| REST delete of the row | holder counter balanced so a later upsert isn't a phantom holder |
| lease lost mid-delete | delete skipped; row left to `expiresAt` |
| worker OOM / kill | row reclaimed by `expiresAt` |

Covered by `testPresenceCloseKeepsPresenceHeldByAnotherConnection`.

Fixes appwrite/appwrite#14342
Fixes appwrite/appwrite#14343

## Intent

MVP2 VM step 4: vss-agent search route with an always-on critic. POST /api/v1/incidents/search per search-contract-v1; the critic is always on; queries and query_results are persisted through the data layer.
Context: MVP2 is natural-language evidence search with object crops for the dev-profile-incident profile (deploy/docker/developer-profiles/dev-profile-incident/). The plan is the private report ~/workspace/firstmate/data/vss-mvp2-plan-v2/report.md (sections 3 crops, 4 search system, 5 roadmap). It was amended after a box-accuracy pilot (~/workspace/firstmate/data/vss-box-pilot/report.md): VLM bounding boxes were 0% well-framed while VLM timestamps were over 95% accurate, so boxes come from a separate open-vocabulary detector at the VLM timestamp, never from the VLM report. The merged contracts are on main: contracts/search-contract-v1 (search request and response) and incident-contract-v3 (adds per-item timestamp_seconds and a short label a detector can search for), plus mock-backend/base_profile_mock and search_profile_mock serving search-contract-v1. Teammate workstreams own the other layers: PR 118 frontend (search, chat, theming), PR 119 eval, PR 120 data and search layer (Supabase migration for evidence_crops and query_results, search_evidence_items RPC, R2 key layout and presigned URLs, hexagonal ports for incident-console-v2 database access). Read those PRs (gh-axi pr view / diff) so your work meets what they need.

## What Changed

- Implemented the `POST /api/v1/incidents/search` route in `services/agent` adhering to `search-contract-v1`, registered unconditionally in `CustomFastApiFrontEndWorker`.

- Introduced a hexagonal `SearchStore` port for candidate retrieval and query audit trail persistence, covered by unit tests and updated MVP2 profile documentation.

## Risk Assessment

✅ Low: The search route conforms to search-contract-v1, gracefully degrades critic errors without dropping hits, and decouples data persistence cleanly through hexagonal ports.

Exercised the incident search route (POST /api/v1/incidents/search) and always-on critic against the live running FastAPI service and mock VLM Switchyard across natural language search, distractor rejection, 500 failure degradation, schema rejection, and audit persistence, with all 5 live scenarios and 23 unit tests passing.

author: timdaub
body:
## What it solves

Resolves: —

Since [#8988](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-wallet-monorepo/pull/8988), pure UI components live in `@safe-global/views`. Nothing tells the agents that write most of our code about it. So new UI still lands in `apps/web`, mixed with hooks and data, and reviewers have to read everything line by line.

## How this PR fixes it

**`AGENTS.md`** gets a section, "Keep presentation in `@safe-global/views`":
- **Why:** separating presentation from business logic makes reviews faster, keeps concerns apart and lets us isolate UI code. Code in `@safe-global/views` only turns props into markup. Hooks, state, data and handlers stay in `apps/web` and reach the views as props.
- **Scope:** new code only. Existing code is not refactored unless the task asks for it.
- **When a change adds UI:** reuse an existing view first. Otherwise write the markup as a view in `packages/views` and pass it data and callbacks from `apps/web`.
- **Soft, not a gate:** if splitting would make the change larger or worse, keep it together and say why in the PR description.
- **The check:** before every commit that touches UI, run `node scripts/design-check/index.cjs --base <base commit>`, whoever the change is for. It marks each changed `apps/web` file that changes behaviour. For each marked file where UI was added too, the agent moves that UI into a view or explains in the PR why it stays.

**`scripts/design-check/`** is the checker from the design scope check PR, [#8991](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-wallet-monorepo/pull/8991): `check.cjs`, `index.cjs`, `config.json` and its tests. One fix on top: the CSS rule that rejects the old scripting `behavior:` property also matched `overscroll-behavior:`. It now only matches the property itself, with a test for each case.

**`.github/CODEOWNERS`** gets the same line as in #8991, so the checker's rules stay developer-owned: `/scripts/design-check/ @safe-global/infrasec @compojoom @PooyaRaki @TimDaub`.

**What it does not add:** no workflow and nothing in CI. The check never blocks a commit or a PR. It applies to everyone's agents, not only to designers. The `Design scope` workflow, the `design-only` label and the `design.narrow` skill stay in #8991.

**This PR changes what agents do in this repository:** `AGENTS.md` instructs every agent session to run the script before committing UI changes.

## The experiment behind it

We tested five instruction variants on real tickets before choosing this one.

### Tickets

| Ticket | Task | Needs a split? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [WA-2744](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-2744) | Group imported addresses across chains in the import modal | Barely: mostly logic, one component swapped for another |
| [WA-3208](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-3208) | Show that the module vulnerability check failed (Code 621) | Yes: new state and a new warning card |
| [WA-3503](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-3503) | Say "signer of this Safe" instead of "unknown address" for co-signers | Yes: a new condition and new copy |
| [WA-3727](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-3727) | PRO tag beside the Spending limits and Proposers titles | Yes: a new condition and a new tag |
| [WA-3819](https://linear.app/safe-global/issue/WA-3819) | Batched transactions drawer does not scroll | No: layout only, no new logic |

### Setup

- Each run is a fresh checkout of `dev` from before the ticket's real fix, with dependencies installed.
- One coding agent implements the ticket the way it normally would in this repo: read the AGENTS.md files, write tests, run scoped type-check, lint and jest, commit, and write a PR description.
- The agent may not read git history, other checkouts or the network.
- Each ticket runs twice, so every variant has 10 runs.

### The five variants

- **Control:** the repo exactly as on `dev`.
- **Soft skill:** a `ui-change` skill explaining where new UI and logic go, plus an advisory script that labels files as views, logic or a mix.
- **Hard check:** a `ui-change` skill plus a strict script the agent must make pass before committing. It fails any `apps/web` file that gets new logic and new UI together. It is built on #8991's checker.
- **Paragraph only:** this PR's `AGENTS.md` section without the check.
- **This PR:** the paragraph plus #8991's check as an advisory step (fix or explain).

### How we graded

Our goal is easy reviews: a reviewer should be able to skim most of a change (presentation) and read only a few clearly separated lines of logic. So a blind grader read all ten diffs for a ticket side by side, without knowing which variant made which. It scored each diff 1–5 on:

1. Presentation separate and skimmable
2. Logic small and easy to find
3. No noise: no re-indenting, moving or reformatting of unchanged code
4. Proportionate: no extra code, no duplicated components, assets or CSS
5. Correct, with tests

It then gave a grade from A (reviewable like an ideal change) to F (wrong); a change that does not work can get at most D. To check that the scale is not too generous, we also graded [#8999](https://github.com/safe-global/safe-wallet-monorepo/pull/8999), a design-only redesign of the plans page, blind. It got a C, held back by re-indented unchanged code, display math inside the markup and no tests. So the scale is strict: a B is a good review experience.

### Results

| Variant | Grades (10 runs) | Average (A=4 … F=0) | Presentation separate | Logic easy to find | No noise | Proportionate | Correct |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Control | 2×A, 8×B | 3.2 | 3.6 | 4.3 | 4.0 | 4.5 | 4.5 |

body:
## Решение: Backend-first

Пользователь выбрал: **«Сначала добавить серверную идемпотентность и проверку статуса»**. Консервативный frontend с постоянной блокировкой и localStorage marker не выбран для реализации. Этот Draft PR содержит только анализ и зафиксированное решение.

### Причина

POST /api/v1/businesses/{id}/customers в API 0.6.0 создаёт нового клиента, возвращает 201 и не поддерживает idempotency/replay/status lookup. Одинаковые записи допустимы. Потеря ответа не доказывает ни успех, ни отказ; GET списка и ручная сверка не исключают поздний commit. Автоматический повтор POST небезопасен.

### Условие следующего frontend-этапа

Backend-владелец публикует точный commit, OpenAPI/examples и серверные проверки:

- key scope, canonical body, атомарный Customer/result, replay и конфликт другого тела;
- durable status/recovery, поздние и параллельные запросы без дубля;
- membership при create/replay/status и определённая retention политика.

Затем отдельно согласуются состав интеграции контракта/generated и recovery UX. Frontend не придумывает endpoints и не меняет Backend. Рассмотренный frontend-вариант сохранён только как история анализа; deadline/marker/блокировки не внедрены.

### База и изменённые файлы

Base: **integration/local-combined-check:58d4eb47e0d5e6d06c8d4af1e56eedbe2fd65f76**. Head: **fix/customer-post-unknown-result**.

Только docs/SELLER_CUSTOMER_POST_UNKNOWN_RESULT.md, docs/handoffs/seller-web.md и docs/DECISIONS.md. Backend, OpenAPI/generated, финансовые, public, voice и mobile source без изменений. ### Проверки и ограничения

Предыдущий анализ: read-only assertions Customer OpenAPI и ссылки — PASS. Для решения Backend-first: git diff --check, ссылки всех трёх документов и scope review — PASS. Android/HTTPS acceptance не выполнена: физическое устройство не подтверждено, adb отсутствует в PATH. В текущем AudioInput нет playback. HTTPS/live-результаты капитана не выдаются за собственные. Android остаётся отдельным последующим этапом.

author: prajwal0598
body:
## Problem
Browsers on `https://www.relayshift.in` get `Origin https://www.relayshift.in is not allowed by Access-Control-Allow-Origin. Status code: 204`. The API only allows the origins listed in `WEB_ORIGIN`, which in production holds `https://relayshift.in` alone.

## Change
- New `cors.helper.ts`: `WEB_ORIGIN` is a comma-separated list of **exact** origins, trimmed, normalised (trailing slash, host case) and de-duplicated.
- `*`, bare hostnames and non-http(s) values are rejected and logged at startup; a wildcard is never used, and credentials are only enabled together with an explicit list.
- Unset `WEB_ORIGIN` still defaults to `http://localhost:3000` (local development). It is never added on top of a configured value.
- With no valid origin configured, CORS is switched off rather than falling back to anything.
- The Razorpay OAuth redirect uses the same parser (first entry = primary origin).

## Tests
`cors.helper.spec.ts` (30 tests) runs a real Nest app with the real `cors` middleware:
- preflight (`OPTIONS`) and real requests for both `https://relayshift.in` and `https://www.relayshift.in`: exact `Allow-Origin`, credentials, methods, requested headers, `Vary: Origin`
- unrelated origins (suffix/prefix tricks, sibling subdomain, wrong scheme, wrong port, `null`) get no `Allow-Origin`
- no `*` in any configuration; localhost default preserved; requests without `Origin` unaffected
- reproduces the reported failure when only the apex is configured

Local results: API suite 604 passed (9 opt-in integration tests skipped), typecheck and build clean.

## Rollout (required)
The existing code already splits `WEB_ORIGIN` on commas, so production is fixed by the variable alone. Set on the Railway `api` service:

```
WEB_ORIGIN=https://relayshift.in,https://www.relayshift.in
```

Keep the apex first (the Razorpay OAuth redirect uses the first entry). Changing the variable redeploys `api`. Verify afterwards:

```bash
curl -si -X OPTIONS "$API_URL/api/auth/login" -H "Origin: https://www.relayshift.in" \
  -H "Access-Control-Request-Method: POST" -H "Access-Control-Request-Headers: content-type,authorization" | grep -i access-control
```

Merging this PR to `main` auto-deploys `api`, `web` and `worker` on Railway.

body: Implements #75 after pre-implementation plan in docs/plans/r1-failure-artifacts-75.md. author: amoai-tech
body:
## What changes

**Stop GitHub from accepting an AI review that says it skipped changed files.** The existing PR-Agent verifier checked that a review belonged to the current commit, but did not check whether the review itself reported incomplete coverage. This PR rejects that explicit failure, prevents an older green review from overriding a newer incomplete result, and increases the bounded size of reviews.

**Real-world example:** A developer changes 20 rental, viewing, or authorization files. The AI reads only 3 and leaves 17 out, yet the GitHub review job appears green. After this fix, a review carrying `complete=false` or nonempty `excluded_files` fails verification with `INCOMPLETE_REVIEW` instead of appearing successful. The engineer can then correct the review coverage before trusting the result.

**Important distinction:** This fixes *explicitly reported* incomplete coverage. A clean review that has **no persistent coverage-state marker** is still checked for trusted identity, but its file coverage is **unconfirmed**. Neither a green GitHub check nor `complete=true` alone guarantees the AI found all bugs.

### Links and current status

- **Tasks:** [SAN-1312 · MDE-PR-REVIEW-001 — Make PR-Agent Catch Real Defects Before Saying Safe to Merge](https://linear.app/amo100/issue/SAN-1312) (review quality/coverage) and [SAN-1522 · Make MDE PR-Agent reviews faster and reliable with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL](https://linear.app/amo100/issue/SAN-1522) (provider/reliability).
- **PR:** #349 → `main`. Current verified PR head: `9293ca98cabadd385af3919917bed6271c7e9637`.
- **Implementation:** implemented; full local gates and current-head GitHub checks pass. **Open / REVIEW_REQUIRED** — independent approving review still missing. **Not merged; not yet operationally certified.**
- **Dependencies:** [shared PR-Agent workflow PR #10](https://github.com/amoai-tech/pr-review-infra/pull/10) **merged**. Caller pins the immutable reviewed commit `263f5fb347128538ed8ecc267fc5cfc8fced22a2`.

## User journey: from PR to trustworthy review

```text
Developer opens/updates a PR
  → Existing MDE GitHub Actions caller invokes the pinned shared PR-Agent
  → Nemotron Super VL reviews changes; Gemini and Lightning remain fallbacks
  → Larger diffs can be split into up to six bounded review chunks
  → PR-Agent publishes its review and, when available, a coverage record
  → Existing verifier checks bot identity, freshness, base/head and command
  → If coverage says incomplete or files excluded: FAIL (INCOMPLETE_REVIEW)
  → If newer same-head review says incomplete: do NOT reuse older green result
  → If state is absent: identity may pass, but full coverage is UNCONFIRMED
  → Eligible human reviews findings and merges only after required checks
```

### Scope, implementation and tech stack

| Existing component / file | Change | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/pr-agent.yml` | Pin merged shared workflow commit `263f5fb...` | Immutable, reviewed GitHub Actions workflow and explicit NVIDIA/Google secret mapping |
| `.pr_agent.toml` | `[pr_reviewer]` chunk cap **3 → 6** | Review more changed files rather than silently omitting them |
| [Shared infra PR #10](https://github.com/amoai-tech/pr-review-infra/pull/10) | Bounded context **32K → 64K** tokens; six chunks | Recover from real diff truncation without creating a second reviewer |
| `scripts/pr-agent/review-policy.mjs` | Reject reported incomplete/stale/malformed coverage; reject a newer incomplete same-head review even if an older one passed | Avoid false-green reviews |
| `src/__tests__/pr-agent-review-policy.test.ts` | Regression tests for exclusions, clean state-free reviews, wrong head, duplicate state, newer incomplete result | Prove success and fail-closed behavior |
| `src/__tests__/pr-agent-shared-core-contract.test.ts` and `src/__tests__/pr-agent-skills-contract.test.ts` | Pin/security/config contract assertions | Detect workflow drift |

**Stack:** GitHub Actions reusable workflow + immutable SHA, PR-Agent v0.46, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, Gemini 3.7 Flash fallback, NVIDIA Lightning fallback, JavaScript/Node.js verification policy, TypeScript/Vitest and Node test suites, YAML/TOML configuration.

**Not changed:** rental search, viewings, bookings, Supabase, RLS, agents, the frontend, payments or business eligibility. Retain authentication, least-privilege GitHub permissions, secret isolation and human review. No new code-review engine.

## Bugs fixed, with actual evidence

1. **False green on a partial review:** [real PR #342](https://github.com/amoai-tech/mdeai/pull/342) reported `complete=false` and initially 17 excluded files; a later actual persisted result reported **20 excluded files**. The original GitHub verifier was green. Executing the corrected verifier against the real comment returned `INCOMPLETE_REVIEW` with `excluded_files=20`.
2. **Older green overriding newer incomplete:** added a failing-first test: the old code wrongly accepted an older same-head review after a newer partial one. The new selection rule rejects the newer partial state. No bypass via a stale result.
3. **Review budget too small:** shared workflow PR #10 increases the bounded context and per-review chunk cap while preserving output/time limits and existing provider order.
4. **Clean review compatibility:** PR-Agent may omit the persistent state on an otherwise clean review. Keep exact-head identity verification working but label its coverage **unconfirmed**. Do not fabricate a complete-file receipt.
5. **False-positive reviewer findings:** the latest PR-Agent review claimed the caller SHA and chunk configuration were absent. GitHub's real [six-file diff](https://github.com/amoai-tech/mdeai/pull/349/files) includes **both** files, and both contract tests pass. [Source-backed correction](https://github.com/amoai-tech/mdeai/pull/349#issuecomment-6216944787). Do not alter correct settings to satisfy an AI-generated claim.

## Pre-merge checklist — verify this exact head

- [x] Confirm the six changed files and shared commit SHA resolve to merged shared PR #10.
- [x] Regression tests: **67/67 Vitest** and **56/56 Node** passed on `9293ca98...`.
- [x] Local `npm run typecheck`, `git diff --check` and complete `npm run floor` passed.
- [x] [GitHub floor + Mastra schema-init](https://github.com/amoai-tech/mdeai/actions/runs/38910273071) **PASS**; [deterministic Chromium](https://github.com/amoai-tech/mdeai/actions/runs/38910272863) **PASS**.
- [x] [Real PR-Agent review and exact-head verifier](https://github.com/amoai-tech/mdeai/actions/runs/38910274114) **PASS** for current head. **Four chunks**, published `last_run.complete=true`, `excluded_files=[]` and the correct SHA. Review accuracy is a separate criterion.
- [x] Codacy, Kilo and Vercel checks **PASS** for this head. Sourcery skipped / CodeRabbit rate limited; do not represent these as completed substantive reviews.
- [x] Recheck two AI HIGH "missing config" warnings against the real code; both are **disproved**. Evidence is in the PR discussion.
- [ ] Obtain **eligible independent approving human review** and confirm `reviewDecision=APPROVED`. Do **not** self-approve, force-merge, or relax branch protection.
- [ ] Immediately before merge, confirm all *required* statuses still pass at the latest PR head, resolve genuine review threads and revalidate the base branch has not changed materially.

**Useful commands (in the existing checkout/worktree):**

```bash
npx vitest run src/__tests__/pr-agent-review-policy.test.ts src/__tests__/pr-agent-shared-core-contract.test.ts src/__tests__/pr-agent-skills-contract.test.ts
node --test scripts/__tests__/pr-agent-review-evals.test.mjs scripts/__tests__/pr-agent-verified-blocking.test.mjs
npm run typecheck
npm run floor
gh pr checks 349 -R amoai-tech/mdeai
gh pr view 349 -R amoai-tech/mdeai --json headRefOid,reviewDecision,mergeStateStatus
```
