author: thegorgeousivorchival
body:
## What changed
Matrix row A13 (VLESS over QUIC), leanness half. Three per-datagram buffers in `crates/ferrox-app/src/quic.rs` opened zeroed and then had every byte overwritten by the writer:

- `flush_egress`: `[0u8; MAX_DATAGRAM]` before the send loop — 1350 bytes.
- `pump_once`: `[0u8; MAX_DATAGRAM]` before `recv_from` — 1350 bytes.
- a relayed `Datagram::send_to`: `[0u8; RELAY_HEADER + MAX_DATAGRAM]` per frame — 1372 bytes.

All three take `quic::Unfilled<N>` now, a stack array of `MaybeUninit<u8>` handed out as one slice. The relay frame's two reserved bytes and fragment flag are what the hop reads *before* the target, so those three bytes are filled explicitly rather than left as stack garbage.

## Witnessed
- **Machine code**: the `mov w1, #0x546`/`#0x55c` + `bl` zeroing pair is gone from every frame that carried it. `Datagram::send_to` inlines into three frames (`flush_egress`, `serve_vless_quic_inbound`'s driver, `hysteria::flush`), so the release binary drops from **9 such sites to 4** — the four left are hysteria's own three and `pump`'s per-connection scratch, both named on the page.
- **New test** `quic::tests::a_relayed_datagram_frames_its_target_ahead_of_its_payload` asserts the whole frame (reserved, fragment, family, address, port, payload). Mutation-checked: changing the fill to `1` turns it red, which is how the `zero-filled-bytes-per-relayed-frame 3` row is known to be seen.
- **No `0` row** for the two removals: the only filter `scripts/expected-ops.txt` blesses never sends a datagram, and a loopback test sees packets, not the stores behind them. `scripts/method-ops.txt` now publishes `quic::flush_egress` and `quic::pump_once` under a filter that does send them, so CI prints the numbers where a callee's inclusive cost would carry the stores.
- **Bytes unchanged**: `quic_serves_vless_echo_over_loopback`, `socks_dials_vless_quic_to_echo`, `a_socks5_hop_carries_the_quic_carrier`, foxy's QUIC hops.

## Measured
`./scripts/check.sh`: fmt, clippy `--all-targets -D warnings`, `cargo doc`, leak surface, dependency policy, comment trace, fixture safety, windows paths, method docs (201 counts agree), ci scope (19 blocks, 34 rows), method matrix (99 rows), prompt library — all green, then `cargo test --workspace --locked`: 9 suites ok, **0 failed**.

## Test plan
- [ ] **Exact ops and RSS are CI-only from this machine**: `count-ops.sh` stops at `valgrind not installed` on darwin/aarch64, so `ops.yml` is the gate here.
- [ ] `ops.yml` blessed check: the one blessed row is `append_pem 1205`, a PEM helper this diff does not touch — but it is codegen-adjacent, so a shift would need reading before re-blessing, not pasting.
- [ ] `ops.yml` `method-ops` artefact should now print `quic::flush_egress` and `quic::pump_once` Ir for the foxy QUIC filter.
- [ ] `benchmark-matrix.yml` has no QUIC cell; `conformance.yml`/`safety.yml` unchanged in shape.
- Still open, named on the page: `pump_once` pays a `setsockopt` per datagram (`pump`, `serve_loop` and hysteria cache the armed value), hysteria's three remaining zeroing sites, and quiche's own packet build inside `send_on_path`.

author: nghia-vantrong
body:
## Why alerting-health has failed 35 of 35 runs
It reports three broken delivery paths. They are not the same kind of failure:

1. `qnsc-prod-breakglass-assumed` "EventBridge rule is DISABLED": **false positive (this PR)**. The rule's state is `ENABLED_WITH_ALL_CLOUDTRAIL_MANAGEMENT_EVENTS` (needed, because `sts:AssumeRole` is a read-only event; `breakglass-alert.tf`), and the check compared against the string `ENABLED`. It has been reported disabled since the rule was added (#153/#160).
2. `rova-prod-alarms` and `opshub-prod-alarms` "no subscriptions at all": **real, not fixed by this PR**. Develop topics and `qnsc-security-alerts` stopped appearing in the report after 2026-10-11, prod did not. Prod is applied only on a release tag or a dispatch, so the `alarm_emails` default (`devops@qnsc.vn`, already on main) has never been applied there (the comment in rova's `infra-apply.yml` describes this exact case). This resolves when prod is applied, and the address must then confirm the AWS email. Needs the owner (production environment approval); I did not dispatch it.

## What this PR does
- accepts both enabled states, with tests (4 cases; two fail on the old code) and runs them before the check;
- passes the real `region` input to `setup-aws-oidc` (`aws-region` was ignored with a warning on every run);
- **alerts**: a red scheduled run opens or updates one `alerting-health` issue and posts a Teams card (`TEAMS_ALERTS_WEBHOOK_URL`, already a repo secret); the next green scheduled run closes the issue. Pull-request runs are unchanged. Same mechanism as `drift-detection.yml`.

## Not verified
The alert jobs have only run through actionlint, not on a schedule. Dispatch the workflow after merge to see the issue appear (a dispatch does not alert, by design; the first red schedule does).

author: thegainslab
body:
## What this does

The full upgrade list in one PR, three commits. **Merge #865 first** (this stacks on it; after that lands this diff is just these changes).

**1. Ingest hardening (the four preemptive fixes):**
- The admin page uploads PDFs **straight to the storage bucket** and passes only the path — file size is never capped by the function's request body (the most likely next failure, removed).
- The repair round runs primary-only on a tighter budget so the worst case always fits the background wall clock — **no more silently killed work**; a drafting row older than 12 minutes is flagged stalled in the queue.
- Output that hits the token limit fails as *"output truncated — paper too dense for one pass"* instead of a cryptic JSON error.
- Publishing a draft that still has validator errors asks for explicit confirmation.

**2. Glossary merge on publish (pipeline step 4, the last piece):**
- `knowledge_glossary` table seeded with the 110 founding terms (public read, admin write); the app loads it once per session — tap-to-define behaves exactly as before.
- **Approving a paper now merges its proposed glossary terms automatically**: first definition wins, alternate definitions and sources recorded for reconciliation — build.py's rule, automated.

**3. Usage event logging:**
- `knowledge_events` table (anyone writes, only admins read) with fire-and-forget logging: entry views, list views, topic filters, glossary taps, chart table-views, Discuss clicks. This is the data that tells you which papers earn their keep and steers what to ingest next.

**Deploy: merge #865 then this → apply all migrations → redeploy `ingest-paper` → deploy the app.**

With this, the pipeline is complete: PDF in → draft → your approval → live, with glossary and usage data maintaining themselves. Type check, build, and migration checks pass.

body:
## What

Every preview card on a docs page now has an expand button in its top-right corner, a 28px link named "Open <docs title> <example> full page". It opens a full-page view of that one example. The components gallery and the blocks list opt out with `expandable={false}`.

- **Route:** `/preview/<base>/<item>/<example>` (`apps/docs/src/app/preview/`), outside the docs catch-alls.
  - Its `[base]` layout mounts `ProvidersForBase` only.
  - The page sets `dynamicParams = false`, and `previewParams()` gives one page per example per base, about 270 in total.
  - It shows a title, a Close button and the preview, inside a `<main>`, with no sidebar or TOC. It is `noindex`.
  - Focus goes to the `<h1>` on open.
- **Morph:** React `<ViewTransition>`. Only the card that was opened carries the shared name (`preview-origin.ts`, `preview-morph.ts`). No `experimental.viewTransition` flag is set: Next 16.2.6 does not read it at runtime, and its bundled React already runs `<ViewTransition>`.
- **Closing:**
  - When the view was opened from a card, Close and Escape run `router.back()` inside `document.startViewTransition` (`morph-back.ts`). The returning card restores the scroll, takes focus and names itself before the transition captures it. Escape inside an open dialog only closes the dialog.
  - On a direct load, Close and Escape push the docs page instead.
  - Browser Back returns to the same scroll position with focus on the expand button, but without the morph (the amendment to #120 is recorded on the issue).
  - Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, nothing animates.

## Tests

- Static params against the real content files: every registry example has a page.
- The origin store, the transition name, the scroll restore, and the Escape decision.
- `morphBack` and its fallbacks, against a fake browser environment.
- The card's href and label wiring.
- The base-isolation test extended to the route modules.

## Checked in a browser

On both bases, for a component and a block, at 1440 and 390, in light and dark:
- open and close morph, with the scroll and focus restored;
- no extra history entry;
- direct load and reload work, and bad paths answer 404;
- reduced motion;
- dialog Escape;
- no console errors, including on the data-table, kanban and calendar full pages (their hydration fixes landed separately in #152).

Not checked: Safari and Firefox.

Closes #120

body:
## Ticket

CC-102 — Chess that feels like a modern chess site (with parts of CC-041 and the first use of Motion from CC-092) · `docs/tickets/CC-102.md`

## What & why

The owner found chess "very normal": no dragging, and nothing showed the pieces could be moved. This brings the board up to what chess.com and lichess.org players expect. Web only, no server change, the engine stays pure.

- Drag and drop (mouse, pen, finger) and click or tap to move, grab and grabbing cursors, a lifted piece with a shadow, the drop square marked. An illegal drop goes back and stays picked up.
- Keyboard: one Tab stop, arrows walk the squares (mirrored for Black), Enter picks up and puts down, Escape cancels. Screen reader labels unchanged.
- Legal move dots and capture rings, last move and check tints, coordinates, flip board.
- Pieces slide into place with `motion/react` (LazyMotion strict, `domAnimation` loaded as its own file, `reducedMotion="user"`, and no slides at all with reduced motion). Castling slides the rook, stepping back slides backwards.
- A move shows at once and is taken back if the server refuses it.
- Captured pieces and material lead per player, clock red under 20 s and announced once.
- Move list in SAN with first/previous/next/latest, clickable moves and the arrow keys. View only.
- Promotion picker drawn over the board like the big sites.
- Game over panel with the reason, the winner, the score and **Download PGN** (built in the browser).
- ADR-016 (proposed) for the Motion dependency is in the ticket. Bundle: chess chunk 13.8 kB to 32.9 kB gzip, plus 17.9 kB `motionFeatures` loaded only on the chess page. The main bundle is unchanged.
- Also: the profile e2e test now waits for the guest to exist before navigating (a race seen in one full run).

Sounds and opponent popups are left to CC-103/CC-104. Chess events stay derivable from the RoomView (`moves` SAN, `lastMove`).

## Verification

- [x] CI green (lint · format · audit · `test:coverage` · `test:e2e`)
- [x] Ran it for real (what was checked): full games in Chromium desktop and Pixel 7 against the production config server (`e2e/chess.spec.js`, 18 tests: drag/tap checkmate with PGN content, finger drag illegal drop, promotion via picker, keyboard play, history navigation, flip, slide vs reduced motion, resign, draw by agreement, reload mid-game with the clock, Back/Forward, bullet low-time warning and time out). Local gates: lint 0/0, format, `test:coverage` (1673 tests, 100 % lines/functions), `test:e2e` twice on port 4988 (149 passed each time), `npm audit` 0. Screenshots desktop and mobile, light and dark, were reviewed.

## Rebase

Rebased onto 1cf744b (CC-101 durable rooms, CC-106/110, CC-046/047, CC-108/049, CC-125, CC-119, CC-095, CC-097/113, CC-186). One conflict: a comment in `e2e/screens.spec.js`, where main already had the same guest wait, so I kept main's. The board needed no changes for CC-101: it renders the same RoomView, and the restart specs pass.

Second commit, **move list clipping** (from the owner, seen in production: "10." showed as "0"): the list is one grid whose rows share its columns (`subgrid`). The number column is as wide as the widest number ("100."), the move columns are as wide as the longest move ("exd8=Q+"), and they line up in every row.
- Unit: `MoveList.test.jsx` checks 1, 2 and 3 digit numbers, and long moves (`exd8=Q+`, `Nbxd7#`, `Qa1xb2+`, `O-O-O`) rendered whole beside their number.
- e2e: `chess.spec.js` "a long game's move list…" writes a 210 move game into the stored room (it opens with `bxc8=Q+`). Both players reload, and every number and move cell is measured: `scrollWidth <= clientWidth`, the box inside the list, columns aligned, no sideways scroll. It checks light and dark, desktop and mobile, and on desktop also the narrowest side panel (just above the 48rem breakpoint). With the old CSS it reports "10." to "105." as cut off.
- `chess.js` is added as an e2e dev dependency. It was already in the lockfile, so no new package is downloaded.

Draw offers: this PR's board still has its own draw offer buttons. #42 (opponent request popups) lands after this one and will move draw offers into its popup.

Closes #161

## What
The album, playlist and artist header aligned its cover to the bottom of the row. On a phone the title block is much taller than the cover, so the cover floated at the bottom with a blank block above it. body:
Priority: P1 | Area: render | Labels: feat, P1, area:render | Milestone: 0.0.24 | Task: CTX-1272

Closes #2131.

## Summary
Yazi selects its image driver off the honest child environment plus query answers: with no known brand it sends the KGP support probe and reads `Unknown { kgp, sixel }` off the replies, mapping `(true, false)` to KgpOld. Bitty answers every clause (`a=q` OK, non-zero 16t cell probe from #2148, honest `Bitty` XTVERSION, sixel-free DA1, themed OSC 11), so kitty is selected with no manual flags; the KgpOld wire flow (`a=T`/`C=1`/`q=2`/`z=-1` display, `a=d,d=A` erase) paints and clears. This PR pins that contract with yazi-exact regression tests, and refreshes the stale CTX-0194 rationale which predates kitty support.

Chafa stays name-gated upstream (1.18.3 sends no KGP probe even with `--probe=on`; verified empirically against a pty): bitty cannot force kitty output without spoofing another terminal identity, so the bitty-side fix keeps advertising bitty itself (`TERM_PROGRAM=bitty`, sanitized outer fingerprints) and lets query-based detectors select kitty. Sixel honesty is unchanged: DA1 claims no sixel, sixel DCS stays ignored, symbols fallback untouched.

Follow-ups (not this PR): upstream recognition requests -- chafa bitty rule (ghostty #296 precedent) and/or the XTVERSION-gated `a=q` probe (chafa#349 middle path), yazi bitty `Brand` mapping to Kgp.

## Verification
- New `yazi_probe_battery_reports_kitty_capable` (terminal_queries): yazi exact detect bytes -> asserts `Gi=31;OK`, honest `Bitty` XTVERSION, non-zero 16t, exact `?6c` DA1, themed OSC 11 background.
- New `yazi_kgpold_display_paints_and_erases` (kitty_images_present): yazi-exact `a=T` chunks store+place, `q=2` suppresses replies, `C=1` holds cursor, tick paints (`last_frame_images == 1`, non-zero headless pixels), `a=d,d=A` clears placements.
- Empirical (pre-PR investigation): chafa 1.18.3 under bitty env emits symbols by default and kitty APC under `TERM=xterm-kitty`/`TERM_PROGRAM=ghostty` with identical probes -- name gate confirmed; yazi detect+display flow verified headless against Runtime.
- `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` clean; `cargo test -p bitty-runtime --lib` 1003 passed; `terminal_queries` + `kitty_images_present` + `kitty_queries` suites pass; `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu --workspace --all-targets` clean; `cargo +1.85 check` clean for touched crates (no let-chains).
- `just ci-local` (Quality gates, both shards) green first run: 3522 + 3579 passed. Local recipe notes: needed `-P ubuntu-24.04=bitty-act:latest` (recipe still maps `ubuntu-latest` while the workflow pins `ubuntu-24.04`) and sccache GHA disable.
- Headed proof staged only (`recording/headed-2131-33/staged-runbook.sh`, gitignored): owner desktop busy, never disturbed -- yazi preview + chafa renders + btop scrollback check reserved for a free desktop. Headless pixels plus exact-bytes tests cover the same paths.
- Requesting independent review; NOT merging from this session.

## Pourquoi
Sur le projet réservations-salon, chaque arrêt NON_CONVERGING a demandé un expert : lire la sortie des tests et les vrais fichiers, trouver la cause, écrire une consigne précise. Un utilisateur qui ne code pas ne peut pas le faire.

## Ce que fait la PR
- **auto_diagnosis.py** : quand le garde-fou arrête le Developer, run_workflow demande au modèle (diagnose, sortie JSON stricte) la cause et UNE consigne précise. Le dossier contient la tâche en échec, la sortie des tests, les fichiers de la tentative annulée, les fichiers du projet qu'ils utilisent (les traces .test-modules/…mjs sont ramenées au source .ts, plus un niveau de dépendances), l'index des exports avec signatures (PR #18) et les consignes déjà données.
- La consigne est ajoutée à l'entrée du Developer comme une demande humaine (marquée « Diagnostic automatique de la Factory ») et le budget est rouvert (source auto:diagnosis). **Au plus 2 diagnostics par tâche en échec.**
- Si seule une personne peut résoudre (identifiant, service payant, base injoignable, décision produit) : le run s'arrête et l'interface pose **une question en français simple**.
- Interface : carte « Corrigé automatiquement par la Factory » ; message NON_CONVERGING expliqué en français.
- agent_inputs.py : écriture des entrées d'agent partagée entre l'interface et le diagnostic.

## Vérification
Essai à blanc sur le vrai projet (sans appel OpenAI) : dossier de diagnostic d'environ 6 000 tokens pour l'échec RS-MVP-010A, contenant bookingsRoute.ts (où l'erreur se produit), contracts.ts, errors.ts et BookingService.ts.

## Dépendance
Basée sur la PR #18 (signatures dans l'index des exports) : fusionner #18 d'abord.

tests/test_auto_diagnosis.py (11 tests, dont un rejeu du cas createBookingService) et test d'interface ; 1 283 tests verts.

body:
## 概要

issue #137 backlog「セルクリックの判定を event 経由で find-path 側の listener へ集約する」の PR 4。
クリックの分類と pointer 表示を同じ元から判定し、判定の重複・ずれを防ぐ。

## 変更内容

- `classifyCellClick`（proto-03 `_lib`）を追加する
  - 同期判定できる範囲で `current` / `move` / `cancel-objective` / `objective` に分類する
  - EN 切れによる拒否・到達不能は `objective` に含める（非同期・BFS のため処理側で判定）
  - 進入可否は扱わない。`move` は隣接マスのみで判定し、進入可否は `moveTo` に任せる
  - 現在マス判定は stage-07 の `isCellSelectable` を使い、pointer 判定と共有する
- `useCellClickEventListener` を分類による振り分けへ置き換える
  - ts-pattern の `exhaustive` で分類追加時の処理漏れを型エラーにする
  - `moveTo` に拒否された場合（障害物・EN 切れ等）は目標として扱う（従来の挙動）
- stage-07 の `_lib/cell-selectable` に pointer の判定関数 `isCellSelectable` を置く
  - `GeoLayer`（`useIsCellSelectable` で actors store の現在セルを購読）と `classifyCellClick` が共に import する
  - `GeoLayer` の `isCellSelectable` prop は廃止し、`Stage07` から受け渡さない
  - 判定は従来どおり現在セル以外。依存は現在セルのみで、`GeoLayer` の再レンダリングは現状から増えない

## 確認

- `check-types`・`lint` 成功
- vitest: find-path・stage-07 で 267 件成功（`classify-cell-click`・`use-cell-click-event-listener`・`GeoLayer` の選択可能表示のテスト追加）
- Storybook（proto-03）で以下を確認
  - 表示中のセルで pointer でないのは現在セルのみ。移動で入れ替わる
  - 隣接マスのクリックで移動する
  - 非隣接マスのクリックで経路・吹き出しが出て、再クリックでキャンセルされる
  - 障害物のクリックで移動せず到達不能の通知が出る

## 補足

- disabled 表示（EN 切れで拒否される「実行」吹き出し等）は対象外。必要が生じた時点で対応する

Both API and browser Sentry already activate through DSN configuration. Harden the capture boundary to remove sensitive headers/body/query/fragment, personal user fields, arbitrary extras/tags/contexts, breadcrumb content, frame variables and free-text exception values. All existing CI and isolated acceptance requested. Owner-approved real-event receipt remains deferred activation verification. Do not merge automatically.

author: erwanjun
body:
## 基线与风险

- Base / head：`main @ 16af07daf` → `b6fd9b232`
- 风险等级：高。理由：改了跨进程交接协议（CLI ↔ 插件 ↔ 桌面实例）、新增一个经认证的只读端点、桌面 sidecar 首次在磁盘发布一份 scoped 凭据（ADR 0008 修订）
- 标签：`risk:high` + `full-ci`
- 唯一目的：实现 ADR 0131 §六「交接三态」，让交接结果能分开报出「唤起成功」「渲染成功」「确认是目标图」
- 非目标：MSIX 数据目录错位（#1129）；HTTP 查询端点；升 protocol
- 受影响契约：同源对 `locate.PROTOCOL_VERSION` ↔ 插件 `PROTOCOL`（仍为 1）、`docs/handoff-protocol.md`、技能文本、ADR 0131 §六（补「实现」小节）、ADR 0008（追加修订小节：桌面发布 scoped 只读凭据）

## What this changes

`tavotto open --json` 返回的 `launch` 里多了一个 `render` 字段，取值 `ok | failed | unverified`：
- `ok` 带 `stem`、`registry_match`、`manifest_elements`。
- `failed` 带 worker 的稳定码，比如 `engine_files_incomplete`。
- `unverified` 带 `reason`，取值只有 `not_waited | timeout | channel_unavailable | no_target_stem | not_renderable` 五种。

另有 `verified`：只有渲染成功、stem 和目标一致、注册表里有这张图、manifest 非空，四条都满足才是 true。

插件 payload 顶层加了三个字段：
- `launch_success`
- `render_success`：true / false / null，null 表示不知道，不等于失败。
- `verified_success`

**`ok`、退出码、`protocol: 1` 都不变。**

#961 的情况现在报成 `launch_success=true, render_success=false, render.code=engine_files_incomplete`。

## 设计：经认证的 HTTP 查询（维护者 2026-10-16 定）

> 第一版用 CLI 写、实例填的回执文件；维护者改为 HTTP 查询，`7819dae18` 起回执文件通道整体删除。ADR 0131 §六「实现」已重写。

- **实例侧**：每次 `/api/engine/render` 结束（成功、override 的 `WorkerError`、取 worker 阶段的 `WorkerError`），往进程内结论表 `handoffreceipt.LEDGER` 记一条，作为旁路，没有 IO。表最多 128 条，每条保留 600 秒。
- **端点**：`GET /api/handoff/render-status?project=&stem=&since=`，返回 `since` 之后该项目和 stem 的**第一份**结论，没有就返回 `{"status":"pending"}`。响应只含 status、code、stem、registry_match、manifest_elements，不回显路径。参数错误时返回 400 `bad_handoff_query`。
- **认证**：走 `security.py` 现有的 guard，Host/Origin 校验照旧。接受 cookie、浏览器模式的完整 secret，或新的 `status_token`。`status_token` 是独立的 256 位随机值，只在 `GET` 且路径恰为该端点时有效，换不到 relaunch nonce。
- **桌面凭据（ADR 0008 修订）**：sidecar 端口实绑后、发握手前，写 `<data_dir>/session/handoff-status-<port>.json`（0700/0600，原子写），内容是 `{port, pid, token, scope, created}`，退出时删除，并清理陈旧文件。写失败不影响启动。
- **CLI**：唤起前取 `since = now - 2s`，唤起后在 `--render-wait` 的上限内轮询，用 `http.client.HTTPConnection` 直连 127.0.0.1，**带凭据的查询绝不经过代理**（Codex 安全 P2，b6fd9b232；同类旧代码记 #1132）。每轮重新发现凭据，先找 pid 存活的 `handoff-status-*.json`，再找已知端口的 `port-<port>.json`。到点时，连上过但没有结论记 `timeout`，一个实例都没连上记 `channel_unavailable`，都不是 failed。**CLI 不再往磁盘写任何东西。**
- **MSIX（#1129）**：CLI 现在只读桌面写在真实路径下的文件，预计能读到，但没在 Windows 真机验证。

## How it was verified

- [x] `ruff format . && ruff check .`
- [x] HTTP 版定向测试（含 security / session / auth / sidecar 全部相关文件）`2312 passed, 19 skipped`；回执文件版曾跑过的 622 条定向测试也在其中：
  - `test_handoff_render_receipt.py`（新增，56 条）
  - `test_handoff.py`、`test_desktop_launch.py`、`test_open_script_route.py`、`test_install_locate.py`、`test_codex_plugin.py`、`test_claude_plugin.py`
  - `test_agents_rules_index.py`、`test_error_codes.py`、`test_import_architecture.py`、`test_foundation_facade_ledger.py`、`tests/native/test_native_inconsistent.py`
- [ ] 后端全量 pytest：本地串行还在跑（本机没装 xdist），以本 PR 的 full-ci 为准

兼容矩阵：
- 新插件 + 新 CLI：pytest 覆盖。
- 新插件 + 老 CLI：pytest 覆盖，`render` 补成 `{"status":"unverified","reason":"cli_without_render_signal"}`。
- 老插件 + 新 CLI：手工对比过，多出的键被忽略，输出不变。

### 定向测试与反证

| 变异 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| `verified` 去掉 manifest 非空或 stem 一致的条件 | 红 |
| 超时返回 failed | 红 |
| 去掉 `/api/engine/render` 里的回执钩子 | 红 |
| 放开「第一份结论有效」 | 红 |
| unverified 时 `render_success` 给 false | 红 |
| `renderable` 恒为 True（不可参数化也去等） | `test_a_figure_without_a_script_is_not_waited_for` 红 |
| scoped token 不限路径/方法 | 2 failed |
| 去掉 `since` 过滤 | 3 failed |
| 取 worker 阶段失败不记录 | 1 failed |

### 未验证范围

- **Windows 真机，以及 MSIX（Store 版 Codex）下的端到端**：CLI 写的期望文件可能被重定向到 `Packages\<pkg>\LocalCache`，那样 #961 的情况会一直是 `unverified/timeout`。结果只会是「没有信号」，不会误报。另记在 #1129。
- 真桌面窗口里的端到端（交接 → `openFastEdit` → 渲染 → 写回执）
- Python 3.10 的 worker 钩子
- 结论表在进程内，实例重启后丢失

### 回滚

`git revert` 即可。scoped 凭据文件在 sidecar 退出时删除，残留的超过 30 天自动清理。

After: spins top out at 6 rad/s (`TRICKS.spinRate`). The wind-up rate (`spinSet`) is unchanged, so a spin still starts as quickly as before.

How: 6 rad/s is the lowest top rate at which a snowboarder's flat-ground hop still has time for a 180. At 5 rad/s the hop falls short and the board test fails. The slopestyle bot still lands its 360, its 360 the other way and its 720.

`tests/tricks_test.ts` changed in two places:
- The "let go in the wrong place" test now sweeps short holds, which still end crooked. Holds of 0.3 s or more all reach the top rate, so every one of them lands square.
- Two absolute spin-speed floors were scaled down to match the slower spins.

`make sim`: 8/8 home, 0 wipeouts, digest line unchanged.

Replaces #368: the same tree (8f9980cedd84de16d08e6a95ae3926a4b5e1f80d), re-authored with the account's no-reply e-mail (hard rule 8, the repository is public). Its review history is on #368.

## What

Task D15: the CVs and letters the command line made become the documents of their postings. `api/app/documents/legacy.py` reads each posting's legacy `cv.json` and `letter.json` (attached by the jobs import as `job_files` with origin `legacy`) and makes the posting's CV or letter: template `classic`, the draft written by `import`, version 1 with origin `legacy`. A sent posting keeps its `cv.pdf` and `letter.pdf` byte for byte: version 1 points at the file (`legacy_file_id`) and is frozen with `legacy_applied`. `python -m app.documents.cli import-legacy <email> [--dry-run]` runs it in one transaction; `./deploy.sh documents import-legacy <email> [--dry-run]` runs it on the Jetson.

## Why

Decision 5 of SPEC-documents.md: the command line's documents become the postings' documents, and an applied posting keeps its sent PDF byte for byte, frozen.

## Spec and task

SPEC-documents.md, Decisions 5 and 7, "Data model" (`origin legacy`, `legacy_file_id`, `legacy_applied`), "Versions and freezing". tasks/documents/todo.md, D15.

## Acceptance, line by line

| Acceptance | Built | Test or evidence |
|---|---|---|
| for each posting holding legacy `cv.json` or `letter.json`, version 1 with `origin = legacy` and template `classic` | `legacy.import_legacy` | `test_every_shape_of_posting_is_imported_as_the_plan_says` |
| employer keys matched to the profile's; an unmatched key kept and noted, never guessed | exact match against the profile's keys (the ones the template prints for a document with no base CV); unmatched: kept, note `unknown_employer` (the existing `rules.employer_keys`) | `test_an_employer_key_is_kept_exactly_or_left_out` (15 neighbours: longer, shorter, glued, singular, typo, word order, case, underscore, space, accents, full width, empty), `test_the_unmatched_fixture_keeps_its_entry_and_notes_it` |
| applied posting: version points at the legacy PDF and is frozen with `legacy_applied` | `store.snapshot(..., legacy_file_id, pdf_sha256)` then `store.freeze(..., FreezeReason.legacy_applied)`; "applied" is the jobs module's `is_sent` (status `applied`, or an `applied_on` date: an `interview` that was sent is frozen too) | `test_every_shape...` (applied and interview), `test_the_api_serves_the_legacy_pdf_byte_for_byte_to_its_owner_only` |
| the others: PDF not attached, the version can be rendered again | version 1 without PDF; a render of the unchanged draft gives version 1 its PDF | `test_a_found_postings_draft_renders_into_its_version_1` |
| idempotent | a posting that has a document of that kind is left as it is; the person's row is locked for the whole import | `test_the_run_twice_changes_nothing` (every column of every row compared), `test_two_imports_at_once_make_each_document_once` |
| a dry run prints counts only | the CLI rolls the transaction back; output is counts | `test_the_dry_run_counts_what_a_run_does_and_writes_nothing`, `test_the_command_dry_run_then_import_then_nothing` (exact output) |
| imported postings count as having documents, D10 never writes them | already true: `eligibility` refuses a posting with legacy files | `test_imported_postings_are_never_written_automatically` |
| the line in `./deploy.sh` | `./deploy.sh documents import-legacy <email> [--dry-run]` | `tests/deploy_test.sh` (argument refusals, remote command, `--dry-run` passed on, exit code) |
| journey `documents-d15.spec.ts` through the api | jobs import api with invented legacy files, the command in the api container (dry run first), the applied CV and letter frozen with `legacy_applied` serving the PDFs byte for byte, the found CV rendered then edited and rendered again, a second run changing nothing | written and typechecked, NOT run (below) |

## Edge cases

Covered, all with invented files under `api/tests/documents/fixtures/legacy/`:
- a JSON and no PDF: imported, counted `json_without_pdf`, renders like any draft;
- a PDF and no JSON: nothing imported, counted `pdf_without_json`;
- JSON that does not validate: the document is made, its draft holds every field and list item that validates on its own, each one left out is a note `legacy_invalid` with its path in the file and the content code, and the file stays attached to the posting; no version, except on a sent posting with its PDF, whose PDF is frozen all the same (`test_what_does_not_validate_is_left_out_and_noted`, 20 rows; `test_the_invalid_fixture_keeps_every_valid_part`; unreadable files: 11 shapes, both kinds);
- a role field (Decision 7): leaves the entry and becomes one line of `notes` ("Role in the imported CV for example-corp: Senior Platform Engineer"); a role that is not text is noted (`test_a_role_is_never_content`, 10 rows);
- an applied posting's legacy PDF bytes compared before and after (every `job_files` row identical, `freeze.pdf` and the api return the same bytes);
- B's postings untouched (`test_b_imports_only_his_own_and_a_is_untouched`, and 404 on every route for B);
- the run twice; a document already there (made by a writer before the import) left as it is;
- a JSON with origin `upload` is not read (`test_a_json_file_of_the_person_not_from_the_command_line_is_not_imported`);
- a status change during the import waits for it (`test_a_status_change_waits_for_the_import`);
- the canary planted in a headline, a role, an employer key and an unknown field never reaches the logs or the command's output (`test_the_canary_never_leaves_the_files`).

Not covered: the real files of the owner (never read here). See open points.

author: davidstephengrant
body:
Resolves: #21480

Creating tuplets from a selection outside note input (e.g. <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>3</kbd>) now leaves a predictable selection.

### Before

- A range selection was lost. Only one note or rest stayed selected, so you had to reselect the music for the next step.
- Which element stayed selected depended on the order in which the elements had been created, not on their position in the score. For a bar of quarter notes turned into triplets, the selection could end up on any of the new rests.
- A single note and a single rest gave different results: from a note, the rest _after_ it was selected; from a rest, the first rest of the tuplet.

### After

| Selected before | Selected after |
|---|---|
| Range (one or more bars, one or more staves) | The same range |
| A single note or rest | The first note or rest of the new tuplet |
| A list (e.g. <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+click on several notes) | The first note or rest of the first new tuplet in the score |

If the first element is a chord, the whole chord is selected.

A range stays a range, as it does when you change the duration of a range. You can then go on working on the same music, for example by changing the voice or making another tuplet. For a single element or a list, the first element of the tuplet is where you would usually start filling it in: pressing <kbd>N</kbd> starts note input there, with the tuplet's note value.

Creating a tuplet during note input is unchanged.

### Demo

1. Enter four quarter notes in a bar, select the bar and press <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>3</kbd>. The bar stays selected.
2. Undo, click the first note and press <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>3</kbd>. That note is selected, not the rest after it.
3. Undo, <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+click the third and then the first note, and press <kbd>Cmd</kbd>+<kbd>3</kbd>. Only the first note is selected.

author: rellwood
body:
## What changes

**Unit prices on tax-inclusive lines.** A taxed document's line table shows "Unit price (ex. tax)" and "Amount (ex. tax)". For a tax-inclusive line, the PDF backed tax out of the unit price and rounded it to the cent, but the amount comes from the whole line, so the two could disagree by a cent. For example, $10.00 incl. 15% GST × 3 printed **$8.70** × 3 beside an amount of **$26.09**.

- The unit price before tax is now the line's pre-tax amount ÷ quantity, shown with the fewest extra decimal places (up to four) that multiply back to the printed amount. The example now reads **$8.697** × 3 = $26.09. Prices that divide evenly still show two decimals.
- Tax-exclusive lines are unchanged: they show the price as entered, which is what the amount was computed from.
- Stored amounts, totals and tax are untouched. This only changes how the unit price is printed, on invoice and quote PDFs.

**Tax rates in the totals.** The tax summary formatted rates as "20.00%" while the line table said "20%". Both now use the same label. A rate whose name already states it isn't repeated ("VAT 20% on £100.00", not "VAT 20% (20.00%) on …"), the same rule the app's own tax labels follow. A name that only contains the digits ("VAT 120%" at 20%) still gets the rate added.

**Other**
- `fmt_money` now formats through `fmt_money_exact`, which keeps extra decimals but never shows fewer than two. Existing outputs are unchanged.
- `rust_decimal` (already in the workspace and lockfile) is now a direct dependency of the desktop crate.
- README and CHANGELOG: the PDF behaviour, and test counts of 229 (121 Rust, 108 front end).

## Tests

- New sweep: 6 prices (including a discount) × 5 rates × 100 quantities (99 whole, plus 2.5). Every inclusive unit price multiplies back to the line's pre-tax amount, with at most two extra decimals. The old rounding fails on its first case.
- New: exact money formatting (extra decimals, negatives, grouping, minimum two decimals).
- Updated: the $8.697 example end to end through the line table; summary labels for named, unnamed, look-alike and fractional rates.

## Checks

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings`, and `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` (121 passed, desktop crate included).
- `npm run check`: versions, IPC surface, `tsc`, eslint, Prettier, 108 tests and the build.

author: sp0rtsxd
body:
## TL;DR

Both deploy attempts to TRITON died at `quiesce` because `ops` opened one fresh ssh connection per remote call and burst past the host's ufw limit of 6 new tcp/22 connections per 30s per source IP. This PR fixes the client: every call now rides one ControlMaster connection, with automatic fallback to plain ssh for clients that cannot multiplex. Docs record the diagnosis and the `TETHER_OPS_SSH` escape hatch.

## What happened

Both `ops deploy` runs failed reporting `units still active (state unknown)` and then `ROLLBACK FAILED` when the readiness probes also could not get an answer. In reality the rollback had already converged: units were active and readyz returned 200 on the old release. The deploy process was blind, not the host broken.

## Root cause

Not fail2ban (not installed), not the cloud security group, not link flap. `ufw status` on TRITON lists `22/tcp` with the `limit` action: a source IP opening more than 6 new SSH connections in 30 seconds is rejected by the `recent`-module rule. `ops` spent one ssh connection per remote call, so the quiesce/readiness poll loops burst straight through the budget; every fresh handshake was refused or dropped until the window decayed, reading as intermittent connectivity. `kern.log` showed ~300 ufw limit-block drops on `DPT=22` over the failure window.

## The fix

`ops/remote.py`: every `SshRemote` call now carries `ControlMaster=auto` plus a per-process `ControlPath` under the temp dir and `ControlPersist=120`, so a whole run costs one handshake regardless of how many remote calls it makes. `auto` also self-heals: a dead master's stale socket is replaced by the next call. An atexit hook sends `ssh -O exit` and unlinks the socket.

Clients that cannot multiplex (Windows OpenSSH, e.g. the `~/bin/ssh` 1Password interop wrapper under WSL) fail before connecting with signatures like `getsockname failed: Not a socket`. That is a pre-connect failure, so the remote command never ran: `_ssh` drops the mux args once, retries the same call plain, and stays plain for the life of that `SshRemote`. Ambiguous mid-session failures (connection reset, `packet_write_wait`, empty stderr) still never retry, preserving the existing mutation-safety contract.

`TETHER_OPS_SSH` overrides the ssh binary so WSL operators can point at `/usr/bin/ssh` without shimming PATH (`TETHER_OPS_SSH=/usr/bin/ssh uv run --frozen python -m ops status all`).

## Changes

- `ops/remote.py`: mux argv on every call, one-shot plain fallback on mux-unsupported signatures, `TETHER_OPS_SSH` override, atexit socket cleanup.
- `tests/test_ops.py`: regression coverage for mux argv, the fallback (including permanent plain mode after one failure), per-instance socket paths, and the existing timeout/retry contract.
- `docs/how-to/deploy-tether.md`, `docs/how-to/troubleshoot.md`: the diagnosis, the automatic behavior, and the WSL configuration path.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q -rs`: 2271 passed, 7 skipped (opt-in live proofs)
- [x] `ruff check .`, `mypy --strict src tests examples`, `basedpyright`: clean
- [x] `git diff --check`: clean
- [x] Live proof: `TETHER_OPS_SSH=/usr/bin/ssh ops status all` twice against TRITON, both `ok: true` in a fraction of the earlier runtime through the same flapping link
- [ ] Next real deploy rides the mux (not attempted; deploy needs its own authorization)

author: noonghunna
body:
From paulp83's 2× 5090 report in [Discussion #1700](https://github.com/noonghunna/club-3090/discussions/1700#discussioncomment-18971548): `maya.sh --calibrate --plain --yes` didn't exit when it finished; it started a normal server on the Docker bridge address with no API key.

**Why:** starting the model after tuning is Maya's documented default (`--calibrate`: "then start the model (with --no-start: only tune)"). Run inside our image, Maya reads the config our launcher writes (`maya_prepare.py`: host `0.0.0.0`, no key), which is right for the server the compose starts and publishes, not for a second one started by hand. Our engine page named the calibration knobs but never said how to run the calibration.

**What changed:** `docs/engines/STRATA_MAYA.md` gets a "Tuning for your PC" section:
- boot the slug first (the calibration reads the config that boot wrote, and all topologies of a quant share one folder, so the last boot decides one card vs two), then stop it, since the calibration refuses while a server holds the GPUs;
- the one-off command, with `--no-start`, then a `compose down` for the network the run creates;
- how to keep the result: the launcher writes Maya's config afresh at every boot, so the printed `STRATA_GLM_*` values go into `MAYA_PCIE_SHARE` / `MAYA_CPU_LANE` settings.

**Checked live** on the reference rig, `strata-maya/glm53-flash-single-maya-s`, with the command exactly as documented:
- exit 0 after ~10 min; it printed every split and thread count and `tuned for this PC: STRATA_GLM_PCIE_SHARE=0.10 (32.3 tok/s)` (the same 0.10 the native one-card run found on 2026-10-14);
- afterwards: no Maya container, both GPUs at 1 MiB, nothing new listening;
- `compose run --rm` leaves the project network behind; the documented `down` removes it (checked, exact line);
- a saved `MAYA_PCIE_SHARE` / `MAYA_CPU_LANE` reaches the rendered compose (`settings.sh compose-env-file` + `docker compose config`, scratch config dir).
The page cache held ~150 GB during the run, so that tok/s is a procedure check, not a measurement.

**Not changed, found:**
- `switch.sh --set <maya slug> MAYA_PCIE_SHARE=…` is refused: the two knobs aren't in `launch-knobs.json`, so they can only be saved globally (every Maya slug, every quant and card count). Registering them is a separate change, so the page says `--set` doesn't take them yet.
- The nine Maya compose headers still say "Maya's `maya.sh --calibrate` result … goes in MAYA_PCIE_SHARE / MAYA_CPU_LANE". Still true; not edited.

**Checks:** `test-docs-slugs-resolve`, `test-docs-slug-tables`, Tier 0 (28): pass. Diff and body leak-grepped.

author: kaloyantanev
body:
The builder API defines `BuilderRequestAuth`, `SignedBuilderRequestAuth`, `BuilderEntry` and `BuilderConfig` as regular SSZ `Container`s ([builder-specs](https://github.com/ethereum/builder-specs/blob/main/specs/gloas/validator.md), [beacon-APIs](https://github.com/ethereum/beacon-APIs/blob/master/types/gloas/builder_entry.yaml)). Their `ssz-index` tags make dynamic-ssz hash them as EIP-7495 progressive containers instead. Serialization is the same for both kinds, but the hash tree roots differ.

This matters for `BuilderRequestAuth`, whose root is the message signed under `DOMAIN_BUILDER_REQUEST_AUTH`: a signature made with this library does not verify at a builder, and a validator's valid signature does not verify here.

This drops the `ssz-index` tags from the four types and regenerates their codecs, so they merkleize as regular containers. The Gloas consensus types, which are progressive in the consensus specs, are unchanged.

The new test pins both auth roots for fixed values. They match `eth-ssz-specs` (the consensus-specs SSZ library), Prysm's generated code and Lodestar's `@chainsafe/ssz`. KaloyanTanev/prysm#1 adds the same test to Prysm, with the same values and expected roots; it passes there unchanged. Without this change, go-eth2-client returns `4b7aa1a1…23bdc` instead of `6ad33c94…fd6c9` for `BuilderRequestAuth`.

author: mithulpranav24
body:
## Problem
Trying to reserve while in a cancellation cooldown showed the raw database exception in the UI:

> Couldn't reserve the port — (psycopg2.errors.RaiseException) User is in cancellation cooldown for this station CONTEXT: PL/pgSQL function sp_createreservation(...) line 106 at RAISE [SQL: CALL sp_CreateReservation(...)] [parameters: {...}]

The cooldown itself is correct, expected behaviour (DD-24: a 60-minute per-station cooldown after a cancellation). The bug is that this and several other `sp_CreateReservation` guards fell through to the catch-all `else`, which dumped the full SQLAlchemy/psycopg2 error — statement and bound parameters included — to the client.

## Fix
- Map the known RAISE conditions to friendly, correctly-coded HTTP errors: cancellation cooldown (409), connector mismatch (400), active session (409), unpaid invoices (400), held waitlist offer (409), suspended/banned account (403), closed/closing station (409).
- The fallback now strips everything after `CONTEXT:` / `[SQL:` and the `(psycopg2.errors.RaiseException)` prefix, so a raw query dump can never reach the UI again.

No change to the cooldown logic — a cancellation still enforces the per-station cooldown; it just reads as a clear message now.

## Testing
Backend `pytest tests/test_reservations.py` → 3 passed (DB-backed cases skipped without Postgres).

F-206（DEC-560，issue #376）：`GET /pending-entries` 四视图每项新增 `cancelRemark`。

## 覆盖的 AC
`tests/acceptance/AC-EN-F206-cancel-remark.test.ts`（7 条）：
- 取消带说明 → 已取消视图读到说明；未取消记录为 null；
- 取消不带说明 → null；
- 取消 → 改期恢复（换新 ID）→ 再次取消带新说明：新记录不继承旧说明，只读到新说明；
- 同一记录有多条 cancel 动作时取最近一次；
- 跨租户：外租户已取消记录的说明不进本租户结果（外租户数据插入前先取基线，之后结果与基线相等且不含外租户说明）；
- 跨租户纵深防御：拆掉外键和行级安全后，仍不取外租户的行；
- 数据范围反向：范围内看到说明，范围外 / 范围为空整行不可见。

## 未覆盖的 AC 及原因
- 详情接口：不适用，未新建（见下）。
- 前端“取消说明”列：本单不改 apps/web，由 #377 在本单合入后续作（DEC-560 方案 B）。

## 偏离规格之处（附 DEC 或差异编号）
无偏离。

字段定义与取值（`apps/api/src/modules/employment/entry-views.ts`）：
- `cancelRemark: string | null`：该记录（`business_id = r.id`）最近一次 `action='cancel'` 的动作日志 remark；没有 cancel 动作、或 remark 为空白，返回 null。
- 排序：`created_at DESC, id DESC`（表上已有 `(tenant_id, business_id, created_at)` 索引，不加迁移）。
- 一条 LEFT JOIN LATERAL 子查询，四个视图共用同一份 SQL；子查询带 `tenant_id` 条件。
- 可见性：沿用 `employmentScopePredicate`，行可见即可见，不另做字段权限（DEC-560、DEC-402）。
- 路由：`cancelRemark` 与 probation、合同起止日一样属于控制项，不在任职字段目录，裁剪前摘下、裁剪后放回（`entry-routes.ts`）。
- 改期恢复会换新记录 ID，动作日志按 ID 取，所以新记录天然不继承旧说明。

**详情接口处理结论**：没有待入职专用的详情读接口。前端详情是用通用的 `/businesses/:id`、`/records/:id`、`/employees/:id` 拼出来的（`apps/web/src/entries/model.ts` 的 `readEntry`），probation 也是从列表行带入。通用接口服务全部任职业务，把取消说明加进去会改动通用字段目录，超出本单范围，所以只做列表。#377 如需详情里的说明，沿用 probation 的做法从列表行取。

## 变异证明（不提交，两个变异均在 PGlite 与真 PG16 上验证）
1. 去掉子查询的 tenant_id 条件：
   `sed -i 's/WHERE a.tenant_id=r.tenant_id AND a.business_id/WHERE a.business_id/' apps/api/src/modules/employment/entry-views.ts`
   → 失败用例：`跨租户纵深防御：动作日志即使带着本租户记录的业务 ID，别的租户的行也不被取到`
2. “最近一次”改成“最早一次”：
   `sed -i 's/ORDER BY a.created_at DESC, a.id DESC/ORDER BY a.created_at ASC, a.id ASC/' apps/api/src/modules/employment/entry-views.ts`
   → 失败用例：`同一记录有多条取消动作时取最近一次`

## 参考的 `reference/` 文件
无

## 新开的“需取证” issue
无

## 核心门禁变化（F-072 D-5，DEC-374①）
无

## 恢复点
- 做了什么：见上，改动 3 个 api 文件（+15/-2）和 1 个新测试文件；不改前端、不加迁移、不改恢复点文档。
- 验证：`pnpm lint`、`pnpm typecheck` 通过；`AC-EN-*` + `guard-*` 共 17 个文件 / 145 个测试，PGlite 和真 PG16 各跑一遍全绿（新增测试在两边均 7/7）。未跑全量 vitest（DEC-351）。
- 疑点 / 遗留：
  1. 业务 ID 是全局主键且动作日志有组合外键，正常数据里造不出“外租户同 ID 的动作行”，所以 tenant_id 条件的变异只能在拆掉外键和 RLS 的测试库里观察到；它是纵深防御，不是靠约束兜底。

body:
Resolves **drafting ticket 08** — the first ticket off the `to-tickets` breakdown (frontier was 08, 09, 10, 12, 19; 08 was recommended first because it unblocks 11 → 13).

**Stacked on #2** (`to-tickets/paper-draft-2026-10-16`), which is still open. Base is that branch so this diff shows only ticket-08 work; if #2 merges first, GitHub retargets this PR to `main` automatically.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `GLOSSARY.md` | **New.** 22 terms in 4 groups (control paradigm, control chain, evaluation, working conventions). |
| `issues/08-*.md` | `Status: ready-for-agent` → `resolved`; criteria checked; `## Answer` with reasoning + verification. |
| `map.md` | Ticket 08 recorded under Decisions so far. |
| `AGENTS.md` | Domain-docs line now names the real ADR directory. |
| `docs/domain.md` | New "This repo's paths" section overriding the generic layout. |
| `AGENTS.md`, `WORKFLOW-paper-development.md` | Added to the mirror (were local-only). |
| `README.md` | Layout + current status. |

## The 22 terms

The 12 the ticket required — teleoperation, fine mode, coarse mode, condition A, condition B, release-to-hold, gain reduction, pre-registered target, grid cell, 2-second hold, open-loop, PS2 controller — plus 10 the paper would otherwise leave undefined: **stick**, **fallback**, **operator**, **placement error**, **one-way latency**, **expected result**, **team estimate**, the control-chain terms **receiver ESP32** and **sender-side ESP32**, and the **`-dingleberry`** convention.

## Judgement calls worth reviewing

1. **`Fine mode` explicitly excludes "smoothing"/"filtering" and "clutch."** The intervention is a gain reduction, not a filter, and release-to-hold is what replaces the literature's hardware clutch. Conflating them would import the unsupported claim that smoothing alone improves accuracy (prior-art finding 1).
2. **`2-second hold` carries "project-defined" inside the definition** so no drafting pass can cite it as a standard metric (spec Testing Decision 8).
3. **`sender-side ESP32` records the retention question as OPEN (ticket 09), not settled** — the glossary does not pre-empt ticket 09.
4. **No prohibited interface string appears anywhere**, including in `_Avoid_` lines: the `PS2 controller` entry points at `spec.md` Testing Decision 7 for the list rather than spelling the strings out, so even the glossary is clean for ticket 20's forbidden-content grep.
5. **`pre-registered target` and `team estimate` are defined as evidence statuses, not values**, so ≤ 200 ms and Rp40k–70k can be written down without becoming claims.

## Verification (run, not asserted)

- All 12 required terms present.
- Zero hits for `aplikasi web` / `smartphone app`.
- No camera-autonomy plan asserted (ADR 0001); web joystick appears only as the documented fallback (ADR 0002).
- Sender-ESP32 left open (ticket 09).
- Every figure in the file is carried from the tracker or the locked protocol — `5-DOF`, `8 of 10`, `200 ms`, `Rp40k–70k` — with no invented value.
- `verify_blocking_edges.py`: no cycles, no dangling refs; frontier recomputes to 09, 10, 11, 12, 19 (11 newly unblocked).

## Not in this PR

The title (ticket 10) and the sender-ESP32 re-decision (ticket 09) stay open. Nothing here decides them.

author: lathiyamagpiexyz
body:
**⚠️ Post-merge steps:** None.

## Summary

A customer who signed up successfully could be told their confirmation link was invalid — while their account existed, was confirmed, and worked.

Reported from a real signup on **16 Oct**, the day paid traffic started.

## What was happening

Confirmation links are single use, and the customer is often not the first to open one. Corporate mail scanners pre-fetch links before delivery, and that request **spends the token and confirms the account**. The customer then clicks their own link:

1. Scanner fetches the link → token spent → **account confirmed**
2. Customer clicks → token already used → **"That confirmation link is no longer valid"**

They're confirmed and able to log in, but the screen says signup failed. Most people don't then try the login form on a hunch — they leave. That's a drop at the very top of a funnel we are now paying for.

## Root cause

[`route.ts:129`](src/app/auth/callback/route.ts#L129) and [`:152`](src/app/auth/callback/route.ts#L152) — Paths 1 (PKCE) and 2 (token-hash) redirected to the error page the instant an exchange failed, without asking whether the user was already signed in.

The check they needed was **already in the route**, at Path 3. But Path 3 was only reachable when the URL carried no `code` and no `token_hash` — and a spent link still carries its token, so it never got there.

## What Changed

- **`src/app/auth/callback/route.ts`** — Paths 1 and 2 fall through to the session check instead of short-circuiting past it. The header comment map is updated to match.
- **`src/app/login/page.tsx`** — a note on the `link_invalid_or_expired` mapping, which the callback no longer emits but which is retained for old tabs and bookmarks.
- **`tests/auth-callback-spent-link.test.ts`** (new) — 8 tests.

## Why this is safe

**It grants nothing.** The user reaching the fall-through is already authenticated; this is the same `getUser()` check Path 3 has always made. We only stopped jumping over it.

**A real failure still fails.** A spent link with no session falls to Path 4 and still errors — with the `missing_or_expired_link` message, which already says *"log in if your account is already confirmed"*. That is the better message for this case anyway.

**The open-redirect guard still runs.** The fall-through reaches the same `redirectInto()` as every other path, so `?next=` goes through `safeInternalPath`. Tested against the protocol-relative, backslash and absolute-URL forms.

## How to Test

1. Sign up with a new email
2. Open the confirmation link **twice** — the second open simulates what a mail scanner leaves behind

Before: the second open showed the red "no longer valid" error.
After: it takes you into the dashboard, because you are confirmed and signed in.

A genuinely expired link in a browser with no session still shows an error, as it should.

## Checklist

### Scope
- [x] Only builds/changes what's in `experiment/experiment.yaml`
- [x] No new features, libraries, or frameworks beyond scope
- [x] No unrelated changes bundled into this PR

### Analytics
- [x] All new/changed pages fire correct events from `experiment/EVENTS.yaml`
- [x] All required event properties are included
- [x] `project_name` and `project_owner` are attached (via the analytics library)
- [x] No existing analytics were removed or broken

Events added/modified:
- None. `signup_complete` still fires from `onAuthenticated` with the same 60-second recency guard, so a fall-through on an older account does not re-fire it.

### Build
- [x] `npm run build` passes with zero errors
- [x] No hardcoded secrets (all in env vars)
- [x] `.env.example` updated if new env vars were added — no new vars

### Verification
- [x] `verify.md` ran in full — **503 tests across 28 files**, `npx tsc --noEmit` clean, `npm run lint` clean
- [x] design-critic verdict: n/a — no UI changed
- [x] ux-journeyer verdict: removes a dead end that told a successful signup it had failed

## A note on one of the tests

The open-redirect test builds its backslash with `String.fromCharCode(92)` rather than writing it as an escape. Written as `"/\evil.com"` through a shell heredoc it collapsed to `"/\evil.com"`, and JS resolves that unknown escape to a plain `e` — so the test was asserting against `/evil.com`, an ordinary same-origin path. It passed the guard correctly, and the test read as a security failure that was not one. The comment in the file records this so the next person does not re-simplify it.

author: sholadev-1
body:
# Four robustness fixes: partial releases, graceful shutdown, access logs, error boundary

## Summary

Four small, self-contained hardening fixes across the backend and the frontend.
They were assigned together, so they ship together:

- **#25** — a partial milestone release no longer marks the milestone fully released.
- **#26** — the API drains and exits cleanly on `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT`.
- **#27** — every request is logged as one structured JSON line.
- **#28** — a render error shows a fallback with a reload control instead of a blank app.

Closes #25
Closes #26
Closes #27
Closes #28

---

## #25 — a partial release must not complete the milestone

**Root cause.** `escrow.release_partial` emits the same `MilestoneReleased` event
as `release_milestone`, and the event's `amount` is only what *that* call paid.
`handleMilestoneReleased` treated every `milestone_released` event as "this
milestone is done", so a half-paid milestone was written as `RELEASED` and — once
each milestone had seen at least one event — the job flipped to `COMPLETED` while
the freelancer was still owed money.

**Fix.** `Milestone` gains a `releasedAmount` column (migration
`20260107000000_add_milestone_released_amount`). The handler adds each event's
amount to the running total and flips to `RELEASED` only once the total reaches
the milestone's amount; the job completes only when **every** milestone is
`RELEASED`. Amounts are compared in integer base units (`lib/assets`), never as
floats — money arithmetic in `number` is exactly the class of bug this project
already avoids elsewhere.

**Why not just compare the event amount to the milestone amount.** Because
`release_milestone` emits only the *remaining* amount after earlier partials: pay
4 of 10, then "release the rest", and the event carries 6 — less than the
milestone total. Comparing to the total would classify that completing release as
a partial and strand the job forever. It would pass the obvious test and hide the
symptom; a running total is the only thing that is actually correct.

## #26 — graceful shutdown

**Root cause.** `server.ts` discarded the `app.listen` handle, the indexer's
interval and `prisma.$disconnect()`. A Render `SIGTERM` during a deploy left a
dangling interval and an open connection, and the container was killed rather
than stopped — cutting in-flight requests and leaking the poller.

**Fix.** `startIndexer()` now returns an `IndexerHandle`: `stop()` clears the
interval and awaits the poll already in flight, so a shutdown never races a
cursor write. The drain sequence lives in `lib/shutdown.ts` behind injected
collaborators — stop the indexer → close the HTTP server (letting in-flight
responses finish) → disconnect Prisma → exit `0` — with a watchdog that forces a
non-zero exit if draining overruns, and a guard so a second signal cannot start a
second drain.

## #27 — structured request logging

**Root cause.** The API emitted no access log at all: no record of what was
requested, or how long it took.

**Fix.** A `requestLogger()` middleware emits one JSON line per request with
`method`, `path`, `status` and `durationMs`, and `createApp()` does not install
it when `NODE_ENV=test` so the suite's output stays the assertions' output.
`path` is `originalUrl` (query included) because the router rewrites `req.url`
before `finish` fires.

## #28 — error boundary

**Root cause.** A render error in any page blanked the whole app with no message.

**Fix.** An `ErrorBoundary` wraps the routes. The nav stays mounted so the user
can navigate away, and the failed page is replaced by a short message and a
Reload button.

---

## How it was tested

Mirrors `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

Backend (`cd backend`):

```
npm ci             # ok
npx prisma generate
npx tsc --noEmit   # clean
npm test           # 115 passed (14 files)
```

Frontend (`cd frontend`):

```
npm ci
npm run lint       # clean
npx tsc --noEmit   # clean
npm test           # 122 passed (19 files)
npm run build      # ok
```

New tests, one group per issue:

- `backend/src/__tests__/indexer.test.ts` — a partial release leaves the
  milestone `PENDING` and the job `ACTIVE`; partial-then-full flips to `RELEASED`
  and completes the job; one full release out of two milestones does **not**
  complete the job; a replay of an event cannot double-count.
- `backend/src/__tests__/shutdown.test.ts` — drain order (indexer → server → db),
  exit `0`, a second signal is ignored, non-zero exit on failure and on timeout.
- `backend/src/__tests__/startIndexer.test.ts` — polls immediately and then on
  the interval, `stop()` halts polling, and `stop()` waits for the in-flight poll.
- `backend/src/__tests__/requestLogging.test.ts` — exactly one JSON line with the
  four fields, and the logger absent under `NODE_ENV=test`.
- `frontend/src/components/ErrorBoundary.test.tsx` — children render normally; a
  throwing child yields the `role="alert"` fallback with a Reload button; the
  button calls `location.reload`.

**Not run:** the contracts job (`cargo fmt/clippy/test`, `stellar contract
build`). No Rust toolchain was available in the environment I worked in. This PR
does not touch `contracts/`, so that job's outcome is unchanged from its base.

---

## Note on the base — please read

This branch is based on `1a6a491`, the last commit where `main`'s CI was green
(it is also what my fork was at). **`main` is currently broken, and not by this
PR:**

- CI on the current tip `a91b766` (merge of #121) is red on all three app jobs.
- `backend/src/indexer.ts` no longer parses — that merge kept **both** sides of
  several functions (`dispatchEvent`, `handleDisputeOpened`, `handleRefunded`,
  `handleRaised`) and left a stray doc-comment body in the middle of a function,
  so `tsc` errors from line 372.
- `backend/src/__tests__/indexer.test.ts` and `backend/src/__tests__/assets.test.ts`
  fail to parse too (TS1005).

As a result this branch **conflicts with the current `main`** in
`README.md`, `backend/src/app.ts`, `backend/src/indexer.ts`,
`frontend/src/App.tsx` and `frontend/src/styles.css`, and will need a rebase
once `main` is repaired. I deliberately did **not** bundle a repair of #121's
merge into a PR about #25–#28. Happy to rebase onto a fixed `main`, or to send
the indexer repair as its own PR — whichever is more useful.

## Follow-ups worth filing separately

- The three pre-existing failures on `main`: the merge corruption above;
  `backend/package-lock.json` being out of sync with `package.json` (`npm ci`
  fails on `swagger-ui-express`, `openapi3-ts`, `yaml`, `swagger-ui-dist`); and
  `cargo clippy` failing on `contracts/escrow/src/test.rs` (`vec!` used without
  importing the macro).
- `Milestone.releasedAmount` is stored in the asset's human units to match
  `amountUsdc`; if the UI later surfaces it, read from that column rather than
  recomputing from events.
- The indexer now serialises polls (one at a time) instead of allowing overlap —
  worth revisiting if a slow RPC ever makes the poll interval too tight.
- `requestLogger` writes via `console.log`; if log shipping is added later,
  swapping in a real logger is a one-line change behind the same middleware.

## Checklist

- [ ] Contracts: `cd contracts && cargo fmt --all && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test` — not run (no Rust toolchain); `contracts/` untouched
- [x] Frontend: `cd frontend && npm run lint && npx tsc --noEmit && npm run build`
- [ ] New contract functions have tests for both success and failure paths — no contract changes
- [x] Behaviour changes are reflected in `README.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md`
- [x] Contract reference tables in `README.md` / `CONTRIBUTING.md` still match `contracts/*/src/lib.rs` — untouched
- [x] No secrets committed; testnet only

author: hua0512
body:
Slow notification storage or endpoints could accumulate dispatch tasks and concurrent sends. Synchronized platform checks also woke every waiter for each token, while historical runtime errors grew until shutdown.

- Use a 1,024-event ingress queue, at most 16 event passes, and a shared 16-send limit while retaining four sends per event. Async listeners wait for room; synchronous failure callbacks drop the newest event before persistence when full, with a counter and sampled warnings. Existing source broadcasts can still lag. Accepted ingress retains event logging, web push keeps its separate admission policy, and eviction cancels active sends. Per-event panic containment keeps ingress available.
- Queue blocking token acquisitions per platform so only the head sleeps. Rates, bursts, cancellation, route backoff and operation deadlines stay unchanged; opportunistic `try_acquire` still bypasses the blocking queue.
- Retain the latest 128 historical failure details per diagnostic cache, capped at 2,048 UTF-8 bytes each, with total/omitted counts. Fatal shutdown failures retain their complete reports.

The plan records the isolated F07/F13 measurements and their limits. F07 remains unchanged after measurement. Native mid-copy interruption, lifecycle-safe historical-ID cleanup, and the optional combined remux/metadata preset remain open; existing metadata placeholders are literal and need a separate contract. F03/F09/F10 remain deferred.

Validation on Linux/Rust 1.98.1: formatting and diff checks passed; all 2,614 default-feature backend library tests passed (six ignored); affected-package Clippy with all targets and `tls-native-fallback` passed. Integration-test binaries, ignored tests and other platforms were not run locally. CI has not been used as evidence of these results. No production database or provider requests were used for the probes.

author: ybelmekk
body:
Closes #1099.

`exp` is set from the token provider's clock (`systemTime` or `timeProvider`), but `expires_in` was computed against `Instant.now()`. With the clock set in the past, `expires_in` came out negative. RFC 6749 §5.1 defines `expires_in` as the lifetime of the access token, so it should match the token the server actually issued.

- A new `internal` overload, `SignedJWT.expiresIn(now: Instant)`, truncates `now` to whole seconds, because JWT times have whole seconds. All six grant handlers pass `tokenProvider.systemTime ?: Instant.now()` to it. The public `expiresIn()` is unchanged, so the JVM signature is the same.
- The client assertion lifetime check in `requirePrivateKeyJwt` still uses the wall clock, because that assertion comes from the client, not from our clock. Same reasoning as the `auth_time` fix in #1090.

### Tests
New `ExpiresInIntegrationTest`, with `systemTime` set one day back:
- `client_credentials`: the grants that use the access token
- `authorization_code`: the grants that use the ID token
- a clock with sub-second precision (`2020-01-21T00:00:00.123456789Z`) gives `3600`, not `3599`

Before the fix both returned `-82801`; now they return `3600`. `./gradlew build` passes locally.

### Live check
Standalone server (`./gradlew run`) with `JSON_CONFIG={"interactiveLogin":false,"tokenProvider":{"systemTime":"2020-01-21T00:00:00Z"}}`:

| | `master` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `client_credentials` `expires_in` | `-212587479` | `3600` (= `exp - iat`) |
| `authorization_code` `expires_in` | `-212587480` | `3600` (= `exp - iat`) |

author: akurteshi-guardentra
body:
## Scope and traceability - Issue: #196 - Requirement/source IDs: #196 comments 6213380210 (diagnosis), 6214268246 (local candidate), 6216061164 (publication authorization), review 5548730904 (this correction) - Summary: Bounded correction on the published candidate at `4d1c7b9eb53304910f13fb4d011f92cab540f0f4`. AuthProvider clears `disposedRef` when the auth effect is set up again, so a StrictMode setup-cleanup-setup replay can refresh verification. Cleanup still increments `refreshGeneration`, so work from the previous lifetime stays stale. Resend success requires the same Auth user object; a replacement with the same uid is `session-changed`. The banner binds in-flight, dismissal, and cooldown state to that user object. An older `finally` does not release a newer guard. author: abdul-khaliq-khalid
body:
`ssh2_userauth_publickey()` returns the `userauth_key_sign_algs()` error without freeing `session->userauth_pblc_method`, which happens when the server's `server-sig-algs` has none of the RSA algorithms we can upgrade an RSA key to. The next call sees the non-NULL method and skips parsing it from the new key, so when iterating agent identities an ed25519 key is offered as `ssh-rsa` and every later key fails with "No signing signature matched" (the fromfile/frommemory/sk paths overwrite and leak it instead). Free it there like the other error returns in the function do; the new `test_simple` case fails without the fix.

I checked the open PRs and found none touching this path.

author: alphakits
body:
A fully paid historical checkout could permanently reserve a rounded whole-USDT option. The scanner found a later deposit within the approved tolerance but rejected it as a reference conflict, leaving the new commission unpaid until manual intervention.

This change:
- Raises the allowance from ±1 to ±2 USDT once per combined base commission total, with shared application/UI constants and matching SQL enforcement.
- Allows a fresh independently verified receipt to reuse an old rounded option only when every original member was verified paid before the new checkout was issued.
- Retains original exact references, receipt uniqueness, network/recipient verification, receipt-time ambiguity checks, atomic revalidation, and historical reservations.
- Adds an explicit runtime check for the new database policy. No historical commission or payment is rewritten by the migration.

Validation:
- Checkout release gate: 113 policy tests and 119 application/database/API/UI tests pass.
- Batch policy/integration: 68 tests pass; batch application/database/API/UI: 151 tests pass.
- Additional discovery/verifier/automatic-settlement/recovery tests: 60 pass.
- TypeScript checks pass. The regression fails on the old workflow and passes on this change for TRC20 and BEP20.
- English/Arabic phone and desktop browser coverage includes both ±2 boundary amounts. Required CI will run the browser tests; the local browser binary download was unavailable.

Deploy the included backwards-compatible database migration before the application release. Confirm the database allowance is 2,000,000 micros and inspect scheduled checkout scans after production rollout.

author: kimjisub
body:
## Why

The sixth keySound column is the chain to move to after a pad's sound. Since #220, when that value names a chain the pack does not have, loading drops the move and the pad stays on its chain. iOS, the web and every released Android build go to the nearest chain the pack has instead (the first, or the last), so the same pack would behave differently on Android only once #220 ships.

## Change

- `UniPackFolder` keeps the `wormhole is incorrect` warning, but now moves an out-of-range value to the nearest chain (`coerceIn(0, chain - 1)`) instead of dropping it. `0` still means no move.
- Because the target is now a chain the user can select, autoPlay, guide and step practice follow it to the end. The out-of-range guard #220 added in `AutoPlayRunner` stays as a second net.
- `UniPackFolderWormholeTest`: chain count + 1 and 40 now move to the last chain, -1 to the first.
- `TransportAndLifecycleTest.stepPracticeContinuesPastAMoveToAChainThePackLacks`: on a two-chain pack whose first autoPlay pad moves to chain 40, the warning shows once, the press moves to chain 2, chain 2's button is lit as the selected chain, and step practice hints and accepts the next pads on chain 2.

## Local verification

| Check | Base (`c68a1125`) | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest --tests '*UniPackFolderWormholeTest'` | 3 of 5 fail (`expected:<2> but was:<-1>`, `expected:<0> but was:<-1>`) | 5 pass |
| `stepPracticeContinuesPastAMoveToAChainThePackLacks` (API 35 emulator) | fails: `Step practice did not continue on the last chain, at 2 1: chain 0, hint 8` | passes |

- `./gradlew :app:testDebugUnitTest :design:testDebugUnitTest assembleDebug :app:compileDebugKotlin :app:compileReleaseKotlin :app:processReleaseManifest :design:compileDebugKotlin :design:compileReleaseKotlin :app:compileDebugAndroidTestKotlin lintDebug` → BUILD SUCCESSFUL; app 852 / design 10 unit tests, 0 failures; no new Kotlin warnings; lint clean.
- `scripts/check_debug_telemetry_manifest.py` → PASS; `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests` → 33 OK.
- `ANDROID_SERIAL=emulator-5554 bash scripts/ci-connected-tests.sh` (API 35) → `exit_code=0`, app 164/164 discovered, design 1/1, 0 failures, 0 skipped, `verdict=pass`.
- Merged with the current `main` (two newer commits) locally: unit tests app 870 / design 10, 0 failures; androidTest sources compile.

## Risk

Only packs whose sixth keySound column is outside 1..chain are affected, and they return to the behaviour released Android builds, iOS and the web already have. Reverting this commit restores "stay on the current chain".

Closes #530, closes #533 ## Resumo O gate de worktree passa a reconhecer duas famílias de escrita no checkout principal que antes saíam 0 a partir de um worktree. ``` alvosBashEscrita(comando, cwd, ehPowerShell) ├─ PowerShell: junta continuação de linha por crase (incerto se houver # fora de aspas, here-string ou aspa tipográfica) ├─ por segmento │ ├─ resolverMovedor: {cd,X}/{pushd,X} no começo do segmento (só Bash) vira `cd X` ← #530 (D1) │ ├─ alvosDeCmdlet (só PowerShell): Set-Content, Add-Content, Out-File, New-Item, ← #533 (D2, D5) │ │ Tee-Object, Copy-Item, Move-Item e aliases; pula &, ., atribuição; parâmetros │ │ resolvidos pelo conjunto de cada cmdlet; variável/splat/desconhecido = incerto │ └─ iex/Invoke-Expression com texto literal: o texto é analisado como comando └─ alvosNetDoComando: [IO.*]::Metodo( — só a lista de leitura passa (D3) main: alvos de escrita somados aos do verbo git (D4) ``` ## Evidência - **Antes** (`origin/main`): a partir do worktree, `{cd,

} && echo x > f`, `Set-Content

/f x` e `[IO.File]::WriteAllText('

/f','x')` saíam 0. **Depois:** `bash hooks/testa-gate-worktree.sh` termina com `== resultado: 436 ok, 0 falha(s) ==`, e `bash hooks/testa-cwd-efetivo.sh` com `== resultado: 59 ok, 0 falha(s) ==`. A bateria nova, rodada contra o gate da `origin/main`, falha nos casos que discriminam. - **Mutação do plano:** `if (ehPowerShell) alvosDeCmdlet(...)` virando `if (false)` deixa a bateria vermelha (`verificar`: "tarefa 1: vermelho"). - **Revisão:** 5 rodadas. Na 4ª e na 5ª o teto foi liberado por Luís (impasse em `docs/rainforest/portoes/2026-10-16-gate-worktree-brechas-impasse.md`). A 5ª saiu `VEREDITO: ok`. ## Perigo de merge **Porta:** mão dupla. É um hook, e um revert desfaz. **Raio de impacto:** médio. O gate pode barrar comando PowerShell legítimo de subagente no worktree quando há alvo incerto: variável, splat, parâmetro desconhecido, comentário de bloco, ou continuação de linha com `#`. É proteção por desenho (falha fechada); o agente escreve com caminho literal. ## Deixado para depois nada ficou para depois O gate reconhece a escrita por uma lista de formas conhecidas. A cauda medida nas revisões está na #552: remoção, `New-Object`, parênteses, pipeline, provedor, outros cmdlets, indireção .NET, texto executado fora do `iex`, aspas aninhadas em `$( )` e pai inexistente com `-Force`. Dívida sem cenário de falha medido: `gate-fechar-issue`, `gate-staging-total`, `gate-subagente-sem-gh` e `gate-mensagem-commit` chamam `segmentosComAspas` sem `ehPowerShell`, então `{cd,X}` num comando PowerShell vale como expansão neles. É inferido, mais conservador, e não foi medido. ## Decidido sem você - P2 da #530 (toda escrita depois de cd nao resolvido vira incerta)? → nao; so a expansao de chaves em posicao de comando (D1). Porquê: Luis autorizou as recomendadas; P2 barraria cd $X e { ...; } > f dentro do proprio worktree, e as grafias medidas fecham pelo D1 - [IO.File] com caminho nao literal? → incerto: barra dentro de repo (D3). Porquê: Luis autorizou as recomendadas; sem literal nao ha como saber o destino, e o ramo de CLI ja barra o incerto - Achados de seguranca e regressao da rodada 1 do gate (chaves no PowerShell, cmdlet sem falha fechada, .NET por lista de escrita, Select-String barrado, verbo git com escrita) → emendas D1-D3 com falha fechada e D4 novo neste PR. Porquê: Luis autorizou as recomendadas; deixar a falha aberta reabriria a brecha que o fluxo fecha, e o D4 e a mesma classe no mesmo trecho - [design] 1a revisao do gate: alvo incerto (variavel) barra tambem dentro do worktree, e todo posicional virou candidato (falso positivo em Copy-Item P/a . e Set-Content a $t) → candidato volta a ser o que o D2 diz (1o posicional; Copy/Move: -Destination ou ultimo); incerto segue barrando; brechas baratas (aspas no -Path:, & e $null =, splat, espaco no ::, iex com cmdlet, chaves apos A=1/then/!/aspas, mascara so sem crase/#/here-string) neste PR; cauda longa (parenteses, pipeline, provedor, outros cmdlets) para a #552. Porquê: Luis autorizou as recomendadas; o falso positivo trava agente, o incerto e a protecao que o gate existe para dar, e a cauda longa da lista de negacao do PowerShell nao fecha neste PR - 2a revisao do fluxo: achado [design] 9 (texto executado por Invoke-Command/[scriptblock]::Create/InvokeScript/AddScript, metodo de instancia de [IO.FileInfo]) e desvios do tokenizador que nao e de PowerShell (aspa escapada por crase na segmentacao, aspas aninhadas em subexpressao) → vao para a #552; nesta rodada entram os achados 1, 2, 3, 6, 7 e 8, e do 4 e do 5 as partes baratas (crase no nome do cmdlet, comentario de bloco, elemento citado com espaco nas chaves).
