author: gauvino
body:
## What this changes

Two things the release ships wrong, one in the unstable workflow and one in every zip.

### The unstable build's own draft

The first point of #250. A rerun of the unstable build looked its release up with `gh release view`, which a draft answers, uploaded the zips into it with `--clobber` and stopped. gh creates a release as a draft, uploads, then publishes, so a draft left by an attempt cancelled or killed in between stayed a draft, and the manifest step then failed its checksum on a download a draft does not serve: no rerun could turn the run green. A draft somebody prepared under the tag was filled the same way.

The "Tag and release" step of `prerelease.yml` now does what `release.yml` does since #237:

- it counts the releases carrying the tag, drafts included, read once so that gh failing fails the step;
- with no tag yet, a release carrying it is somebody's draft, and the step stops before pushing the tag;
- two releases on the tag stop it before either is touched;
- the one release there has to be the workflow's, made with `GITHUB_TOKEN`, or it is left as it is;
- the workflow's own release gets the zips whose digest differs, and is published when it is a draft.

The two other points of #250, one concurrency group for both workflows and one script for the logic they share, stay there: neither was seen to fail.

### No library the plugin does not use

`packages/` holds the DLLs the zip ships beside the plugin, and Jellyfin loads every DLL in a plugin's folder. It shipped `Newtonsoft.Json.Schema.dll` 4.0.1, which nothing in the plugin calls, while the project referenced 3.0.16; Json.NET Schema is published under the AGPL-3.0 or a commercial license, and this repository is MPL-2.0. The reference and the DLL go (#244's first point; building `packages/` from the project at zip time, its second, stays there).

## Why

#250, found by the review of #237, and #244, found building the 0.70.0.0 release candidate. Part of the 0.70.0.0 release campaign (#121), and of #114.

## How it was checked

- [x] `prerelease-resume.test.js`, the step run for real against a throwaway origin with git real and gh a stand-in, as `release-resume.test.js` does for `release.yml`. Four of its five cases failed on `develop`: a draft an attempt killed between gh's uploads left is finished and published, a draft somebody made for the tag is left as it is, two releases on the tag stop the rerun, and a draft waiting before the tag exists stops the build before the tag is pushed. A first attempt tagging and publishing passes on both.
- [x] `PackagedLibrariesTests.EveryLibraryTheZipShipsIsOneThePluginUses`, which reads the references of the plugin's assembly and of each DLL in `packages/` it reaches, failed first: `Shipped and used by nothing: Newtonsoft.Json.Schema`.
- [x] `bun test`: 402 passed; `make test` on jf11 and jf12: 1122 passed on each, and `make build` with no warning.
- [x] The jf11 zip of this branch ships `Jellyfin.Plugin.Streamyfin.dll`, `NJsonSchema.dll`, `NJsonSchema.Annotations.dll`, `Namotion.Reflection.dll` and `YamlDotNet.dll`, where the final release candidate's had `Newtonsoft.Json.Schema.dll` too. On a throwaway Jellyfin 10.11.11 it loads, and `config/schema`, the route NJsonSchema serves the Yaml editor, `settings/form` and `config/yaml` answer 200.
- [x] Seen on GitHub, in a throwaway public repository holding `develop` as `main` will after #121 (`Gauvino/streamyfin-release-rehearsal`). An unstable build was published, its release made a draft again the way a killed attempt leaves it, and the Publish job rerun:

  | | `develop`'s `prerelease.yml` | this branch's |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | The rerun's step | `The release exists already. Replacing its assets rather than creating it.` | `The release exists already. Replacing the assets that differ and publishing it if it is a draft.` |
  | The release after it | `unstable-0.68.1.175`, still a draft | published, a prerelease, two assets |

  A new dispatch with this branch's file on the same commit published the draft the `develop` run had left, too. The manifest step of those runs failed on a checksum, since that repository's `develop` still named this repository in its Makefile, so the zips were looked for here; with the Makefile pointing at the throwaway repository, the next run went through: `unstable-0.68.1.176` published, both builds validated against what the release serves, and `manifest-unstable.json` on that repository's `main` holding 0.68.1.176 for 12.0.0.0 and 10.11.9.0.

### After the review

- **The resume test pins what the step compares.** Six broken versions of the step passed it: assets compared by name only, uploaded without `--clobber` or every time, the release created without `--prerelease`, and a release list gh failed to give, or answered as something else, read as none. The gh stand-in now refuses a name a release has without `--clobber`, as gh 2.98 does, can fail its list or answer an object, and records what it changes; the killed attempt's draft holds the bytes gh had uploaded, so only the other zip is sent before publishing, and a release holding another build of the commit gets this build's zips. Each of the six versions now fails a test, run one after the other against the step.
- **The zip check reads `packages/` as the Makefile zips it**, folders and any case of the extension included, reports a file that is not a .NET assembly instead of throwing on it, and fails on a library older than the version the plugin or another library references. Shown with a DLL in `packages/extra/` named `Unused.DLL` (seen by nothing before, now `Shipped and used by nothing`), a native file, and NJsonSchema 10.9.0 in place of 11.0.2 (`NJsonSchema 10.9.0.0 shipped, 11.0.2.0 referenced by Jellyfin.Plugin.Streamyfin`).
- **The step's two refusals say what they know**: a draft on a tag not yet pushed may be an earlier attempt's, and of two releases on a tag none is named. The list asks for the tag names only.
- [x] `bun test`: 405 passed; `make test` on jf11 and jf12: 1124 passed on each, and `make build` with no warning.

Left for #250, where the two workflows' resume logic is to become one script: the list reads the newest 100 releases, as `release.yml` does, so a release older than that reads as absent (the repository has 66, and a rerun then fails with gh's own message); and the two tests' gh stand-ins, which that script would share.

  * Only ZIP assets that are missing or out of date are uploaded; eligible draft releases are published.
* **Maintenance**
  * Removed an unused package dependency.
  * Added checks to catch missing, incompatible, or unrelated libraries in packaged builds.

body:
**SakJules · Master of Automation & CI/CD.**

🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL/HIGH
💡 **Vulnerability:** The workflow executor's shell action parses commands with `shlex.split`, but an attacker could bypass input filters by using process substitutions directed at interpreters (e.g., `eval <(echo 'cat /etc/passwd')` or `bash <(...)`), which allows arbitrary code execution or file exfiltration.
🎯 **Impact:** An attacker could execute arbitrary bash/python commands on the host by wrapping malicious code inside a process substitution block.
🔧 **Fix:** Implemented `_validate_shell_command` within `apps/agent_workflow_framework/agent_workflow/executor.py` to identify and block any command containing a process substitution token (`<(`) followed by a known shell interpreter or runtime (`eval`, `exec`, `source`, `.`, `bash`, `python`, etc.), accounting for environment variables and absolute paths.
✅ **Verification:** Added `test_validate_shell_command_process_substitution` in `tests/test_executor.py` to assert these bypasses raise a `ValueError`, and ran the full framework test suite to verify no regressions occurred.

_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01947ZMb6zqRGHqXN1qAbAFE?thread=cmsg_01947ZMb6zqRGHqXN1qAbAFE86TUjTotT5ruMb9QQjgz7r)_

Before: after a take the page showed the ribbon, the marks and the singer's key, with no words on the take as a whole.

After: two sentences sit above the key, for example "Your reciting tone held steady. One of the eight cadences went off pitch." They cover the reciting tone and the cadences only, nothing on timing or breath. A take not heard gets none.

The judge decides both sentences, and cantor eval gates them. The first comes from the drift, which was already gated. For the second, the judge now measures each phrase's cadence against the key and the drift line, the first phrase included. In a psalm tone a cadence is the mediant or termination: what follows the last two notes on the reciting tone before the phrase leaves it. In a chant that is not recited, it is each phrase's last two notes. A cadence is judged only when every note in it was clearly heard; otherwise the sentence counts only the cadences that were clearly heard.

The eval counts a cadence as told wrong in two cases: it was called off pitch when every note was planted within 50 cents, or called on pitch when a note was planted 150 cents or more off. Expert, student and wrong-singer suites must have none. Across the suites the judge rules on 132 of the 143 cadences in the 16 real takes and calls none of them off. It finds 17 off in student-notes and 15 in the wrong-singer control, with no cadence told wrong in any suite.

How:
- `Note` gains a `recitation` flag from the timeline.
- `judge::cadences` and `Verdict.cadences` hold the cadences, and `tell::summary` writes the sentences.
- The summary travels in the ear's `Judged` and in `cantor take`'s file.
- The cli test and the e2e test hold the page's sentences to the eval's.

author: shapedtime
body:
Closes #153
Part of #9

R1's deterministic, LLM-free inputs for recommendations: migration 006, the taste profile, the candidate pool, the agent's custom tools, and feedback.

## What changed

**Migration `006_recommendations.sql`** (PLAN §5): `taste_profiles`, `rec_runs`, `rec_shelves`, `rec_items`, `rec_hero_picks`, `rec_feedback`, `ask_threads`, `ask_turns`, `ask_messages`. It's idempotent. A test builds a database at 009 without 006, as production has it, then checks that the runner applies 006 on top and that the CHECKs, partial unique indexes and cascades hold. `ask_messages.content` is `json`, not `jsonb`, so a replay stays byte-identical (the orchestrator's change; PLAN §5 says why).

**Readers** (`library/taste_reads.go`, `TasteRepository`), one query each:
- watched movies and watched shows (a progress row, plays, or both);
- ratings: a show without its own rating gets the mean of its season and episode ratings;
- hidden and dropped shows, watchlist refs, library titles (genres, language, countries, anime, runtime);
- feedback with the title it's known by;
- `TitleStates(refs)`: per-title watch state, rating, feedback, hidden, watchlist and library, for `check_seen` and R2's validation.

**Repositories:** `RecFeedbackRepository` (upsert keeps `created_at`; clear is idempotent) and `TasteProfileRepository` (insert prunes unreferenced profiles older than a day, in the same transaction).

**TMDB lists** (`tmdb/lists.go`): discover, trending, upcoming, on the air, search and the genre lists, each with a `Cached` wrapper (6–12 h; genres 7 days). Every item carries its media type. List items gain `origin_country`, and `EpisodeRef` gains `runtime` (`ShowDetails.EpisodeRuntime()`), so the cache version is now `tmdb:v2`.

**`internal/recommend/profile`:**
- **Weights:** recency halves each year since you last watched or rated a title, down to a floor of 0.25; feedback doesn't date it, so a title only marked seen weighs at the floor. Ratings multiply by 0.7–2.0, only with `use_ratings`. A like multiplies by 1.5. A show weighs by the share of it watched; a rewatched movie a little more.
- **Features:** genres, keywords, creators and cast, languages, countries, the anime share and runtimes, from TMDB's details of the 40 heaviest titles. Without TMDB, they come from the library's metadata. Decades and the movie/show mix cover every weighed title.
- **Lists:** loved, dropped, recent and aversions, as the issue defines them. It stays within 16 KB, trimming the longest lists first.

**`internal/recommend/candidates`:**
- **Sources:** TMDB's recommendations and similar titles for the 10 most loved titles (never one only marked seen; seeds are keyed by rank and labelled with their year, `rec:Dune (2021)`); discover by keywords (last 5 years), new releases (last 120 days), gems (rated 7.5+, 2+ years old) and the second language; trending, upcoming and on the air. Discover runs only for a media type with at least 15% of the profile.
- **Exclusions:** anything watched, any show started (a progress row or plays), anything rated on Trakt (the title's own rating, whatever `use_ratings` says), shows dropped or hidden on Trakt, and titles with negative feedback. One rule, `candidates.Exclusion(library.TitleState)`, is shared with `check_seen` and R2's validation. Library titles stay, marked `in_library`.
- **Ranking:** a pre-rank on overlap, then TMDB describes the best 200 (runtime, seasons, keywords, ended), a re-rank, and the pool keeps 150. Source order is fixed, so the same inputs make the same pool.

**`internal/recommend/tools`** (each an `agent.Tool`):
- **The tools:** `get_taste_profile`, `get_candidates`, `tmdb_search`, `tmdb_details`, `check_seen`.
- **Schemas** are strict: closed objects, every property required, and none of the keywords strict mode refuses. "No value" is a sentinel, not a nullable union: structured outputs allow at most 16 parameters with `anyOf` or a type array per request, across every strict tool, and #157 and #158 share the request. So `get_candidates` takes `media_type: movie|tv|any`, `genres: []` for any, `0` for no runtime, year or limit bound, `language: ""` and `anime: only|exclude|either`; `tmdb_search` takes `media_type: movie|tv|any` and `year: 0` for any. R1's tools use no unions (a test counts them across `tools.All`, and allows at most 2). Golden files (`tools/testdata/*.json`, run with `-update`) pin the definitions, plus a test that walks each schema.
- **Results** are compact JSON without HTML escaping (`tools.Encode`). `get_candidates` re-checks exclusions, so a title turned down since the pool was built is dropped.
- **Errors:** only the run's own context ending is fatal. TMDB failures, timeouts included (the HTTP client's timeout is a `DeadlineExceeded` too), and a pool TMDB couldn't build (`ErrNoSources`) are `ToolError`s the model can work around. A database error ends the run. A missing profile or pool, and ids past int4, are `ToolError`s too.
- **Inputs:** `tools.Fixed` for a run; `tools.Cached` builds on first use and rebuilds after a TTL, for Ask.

**API and wiring:**
- `api.RecFeedback` is `recommend.FeedbackService`, set in `wire_recs.go` with or without a key. A TMDB id past int4 is a 400. `Options.Recommendations` stays nil (#157).
- The dev-only `GET /recommendations/debug/profile` (`recommend.Debug`) builds the profile and pool and stores nothing. It's registered only with `ai.recs_debug` / `RECS_DEBUG` (default off; YAML key, env var, config test, `config.yaml.example`, compose).

## Decisions beyond the issue (PLAN updated)

- **A started show is never picked,** per the orchestrator's note, rather than PLAN's "completed and not returning". PLAN §6 and §7 R1 now say so.
- **`no_history` reads `counts.loved`.** Loved counts completed titles too, but never one rated 4 or less or disliked: "5 loved or completed" without counting a title you finished and hated. `seen` feedback counts as completed and loved (note "marked seen"), with no rating boost. PLAN §6 is updated.
- **The tools name titles by `media_type` and `tmdb_id`,** not the issue's `type` and `id`. Every result uses those keys. `check_seen` takes `titles: [{media_type, tmdb_id}]`, because TMDB ids repeat across movies and shows. PLAN §7 R1 "Landed" lists this.
- **`get_candidates` adds `min_runtime`** next to `max_runtime`. A runtime or year bound leaves out titles without one.
- **Two indexes beyond PLAN §5:** `rec_runs.profile_id` (the prune) and `ask_messages.turn_id` (the cascade). PLAN §5 is updated.
- **Titles rated on Trakt are never picked,** even unplayed and with `use_ratings` off: a rating means you've seen it. PLAN "What's never picked" says so.
- **Shared files, minimal:** `internal/aicore/tool.go`'s and `recommend/agent/tool.go`'s doc comments now state the 16-union budget and "sentinels, not nullables" (PLAN §7 R1 too). `internal/api/router.go` gets one `Options.RecDebug` field. A nil field leaves the route unregistered (404), and the `Options` struct has to live there. `compose.yml` gets one line, `RECS_DEBUG=${RECS_DEBUG:-}`.

## Live check (real TMDB, throwaway Postgres; not committed)

A seeded history: Arrival, Dune: Part Two, Inception and Blade Runner 2049; Severance (rated 10), Frieren, Dark; Game of Thrones dropped.
- The profile built in 1.1 s at 3.7 KB.
- The pool built in 10.2 s cold and 0.3 s cached: 150 kept of 428 considered, 3 excluded, about 30 KB as JSON.
- The top of the pool: The Institute, The Capture, Emergence, Interstellar, The Expanse, Contact, Moon, Twin Peaks, Breaking Bad.
- A title marked not interested wasn't in the pool. `check_seen`, `tmdb_search` and `tmdb_details` answered as expected against the seeded state.
- That run led to three fixes in this PR: shows' episode runtime falls back to the last episode's, "similar" counts for less than "recommendations", and TMDB's rating weighs more.

## Verification

Rebased on `origin/main` (#162: `agent.Tool` is an alias of `aicore.Tool`).

`go vet ./...`:

author: shih-liang
body:
## Summary

guestd now mounts the drag-and-drop filesystem for the graphical session's user and hands the `/dev/fuse` descriptor to that user's compositor:

- It listens on `/run/nativepipe/drops.sock` (`NPDM` request) and takes the caller's UID/GID from `SO_PEERCRED`.
- It mounts FUSE at the root-owned `/run/nativepipe/drops/<uid>` with `nosuid,nodev,default_permissions`, owned by the caller and without `allow_other`. It then passes the descriptor back with `SCM_RIGHTS`.
- Root callers are refused. Mount points are never in a directory the user controls, so a symbolic link can't redirect where root mounts. A newer request from the same user detaches the previous mount, so a restarted compositor takes over.
- A failure to start the listener is logged and isn't fatal: drag and drop then keeps using copies.

## Depends on

- shih-liang/NativePipe#1: provides `common/file_rpc/np_drop_fs.h` (protocol constants) and the compositor side that uses this mount. This repository builds against the sibling NativePipe checkout (`FILE_RPC_DIR`), so that change must be present when building.
- shih-liang/LightHouse#1 (LinPortal) is the host side for virtual machines.

## Testing

- `make -C guest-platform build` cross-compiles guestd for aarch64 and x86_64.
- `make -C guest-platform test` passes.
- **Not yet run in a VM.**

author: crf04
body: Closes #227 Part of crf04/statsplus#217 ## Change ### Why the change The home page's ticker, Tonight and Your Targets appeared only after three reads ran one after another. This change starts them together and repaints the last public result from the browser on a return visit. ### Special things to note - **Merge order:** crf04/statsplus-backend#428 is merged and deployed, which this needed: a backend without `fallback` would leave a no-games day with no ticker or Tonight. - **Targets are never cached:** only the public ticker and Tonight are kept in `localStorage` (`courtai.homeTonight.v1`). Once a fresh Slate answers, a stored day that no longer matches it is cleared. - **Missing `fallback` field:** it is read as `null` on purpose, so the page still works while the backend and frontend are briefly on different versions during a rollout or rollback. ### Change outline The home reads, before and after (no-games day): ```diff - GET /api/games/slate → empty today - GET /api/games/slate?date= → waits for the first - GET /api/games/slate/edges?date= (parallel with) - GET /api/user/targets/resolve?date= + GET /api/games/slate?fallback=previous_game_day ┐ + GET /api/games/slate/edges?fallback=previous_game_day ├ all at once + GET /api/user/targets/resolve?fallback=previous_game_day ┘ (signed in only) ``` The Slate decoder gains one field: ```diff { slateDate, games, previousGameDate, nextGameDate, ..., + fallback: 'previous_game_day' | null } // past = fallback === 'previous_game_day' ``` The rules for the cached paint in `useHomeTonight`: ```text mount paint readCache() # validated field by field; a bad entry is removed start Slate, Edges, Targets on Slate success empty, or another day than the painted one → clear paint + stored entry on Slate + Edges success, same date write cache, replace paint on Edges null / other date → clear on Edges failure → keep only a same-day paint on Slate failure → keep the paint on Targets → shown only when they match the Slate's date; never stored ``` Files: ```text src/ ├── home/useHomeTonight.js # parallel reads, cache read/write/validate ├── slateApi.js # fallback option + decoded field ├── slateEdgesApi.js # fallback option └── targets/targetsApi.js # fallback option e2e/ ├── fixtures/courtai-contract.mjs # fallback param + 400s └── flows/home.e2e.ts # every home read carries fallback, no date ``` ## Verification Live checks: boundary Why they apply: this changes API request parameters and the Slate decoder, and the home page's rendering depends on the shape of live data. | Check | Result | Revisions, command, and evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | Owning repository gates | passed | `07609ad` (master merged in): `npm run check` exit 0 under Node 25 — test:ci 1195, test:e2e 164 passed, test:flows 152 | | QA user journeys against the selected backend and isolated database | passed | `journeys/home.jsonl` (crf04/statsplus#222), frontend `07609ad`, backend `6b20e4d8`: Slate, Edges, Targets each 200 with `fallback=previous_game_day`; Decisões do RT em 16/10/2026 ("1a 2a 3a 4a 5 sim 6 sim"):

- Todo item de medicamento, em qualquer idade, exige data de nascimento (ou idade estimada) e peso deste atendimento. Antes só a criança ou o paciente sem data precisava de peso.
- Peso aferido, estimado ou referido pelo paciente: nova coluna observacao.metodo, gravada pela fila de sinais vitais.
- Idade estimada em anos: RPC registrar_idade_estimada grava a data no cadastro com pacientes.data_nascimento_estimada; a data real tira a marca (gatilho), e a marca não se liga por fora.
- O peso vale a internação inteira ou o atendimento de porta, desde a chegada (private.inicio_do_atendimento), não mais 24 h.
- Sem exceção de emergência. Cuidado e dieta não exigem.
- A trava vale em todos os caminhos: prescrever (bloco trocado no corpo atual, conferido), alterar_item_prescricao (chama prescrever), registrar_prescricao_itens e inserção direta, por gatilho em prescricao_itens, que também grava o peso no item.
- Mensagem diz o que falta: "Falta para prescrever: data de nascimento ou idade estimada; peso deste atendimento (aferido ou estimado)."

Tela: campos de idade estimada e de peso com o método na prescrição (internação e porta); último peso mostra "estimado"/"referido"; cabeçalho mostra "(estimada)". A tela antiga Consulta de Medicamentos deixou de gravar prescrição direto na tabela.

Testes de banco antigos ganharam o peso do atendimento antes de prescrever; teste novo portao2_prescricao_idade_peso.sql (11 checagens).

author: hkarani
body:
# PR: Three-part SDK / UI / Platform architecture (ADR-0021)

Branch `feat/architecutre` · 50 commits (`b5651b94..0ebd2aa8`) · [ADR-0021](../adr/ADR-0021-three-part-sdk-ui-platform-architecture.md)

## What

Splits the app into three top-level parts:

- **`sdk/`** (321 files): marketplace logic with no React, UI or platform code. It holds event builders and parsers, publish and read workflows, an event store, Cashu and auction logic, and the core contracts (signer, nostr-io, pay aggregator, funds contract).
- **`ui/`** (154 files): React views that render only from props, plus primitives and a `UiProvider`. Import rules are enforced by a boundary test.
- **`platform/`** (106 files): routes, the Bun server, the extension registry, and the adapters that connect NDK and applesauce to the SDK.

`src/` becomes the wiring layer. All 22 `src/publish` modules and all 28 `src/queries` modules call the SDK. Containers in `src/components` pass data into `ui/` views. Pure logic moved out of `src/lib`, which now has 31 files that only re-export from the SDK.

## Behavior changes

1. **Deletions:** the deleted-item lists in localStorage are replaced by NIP-09 deletion lookups and an in-memory event store. This applies to products, shipping, collections, auctions and payment details. After a reload, an item stays hidden only if a relay returns its deletion event.
2. **Extra request:** each list read makes one more relay request, to look up deletions.
3. **Timeouts:** shipping and payment-detail reads now time out after 8 seconds.
4. **Session accumulation:** the store keeps every version it has seen and shows the newest, but never removes anything.

## Fixes

- Copy-to-clipboard passed the toast message as the MIME type.
- XSS in the pickup map popup.
- Two crashes from the UI extraction: dashboard `totalListings` and the product form tab helpers.

## Validation

- **Unit tests:** 2447 pass, 0 fail.
- **Type errors:** `tsc` is at 274, down from 282; all of them predate this branch.
- **NDK footprint:** down from 144 to 130 files.
- **Other checks:** boundary tests, the auctions NDK guard and Prettier all pass.
- **⚠️ Playwright E2E has not been run.** AGENTS.md requires targeted specs with video before merge.

## Follow-ups

- **Core modules:** switch the auth store and Nostr I/O onto the SDK signer and nostr-io modules. This overlaps the paused NDK→Applesauce migration.
- **Payments and checkout workflows:** waiting on the port design.
- **Auctions:** move the bid and settlement orchestration out of `src/publish/auctions.tsx`.
- **Parsers:** move the per-kind parsers into SDK Core, so the store can use them to accept or reject events.
- **Cleanup:** remove the forwarding files and shrink the list of `src/` files allowed to import `platform/`.

## Review order

1. Boundary tests and ADR-0021.
2. `sdk/core/event-store/`: check the NIP-01 and NIP-09 merge and deletion rules.
3. Shipping, publish path: `sdk/commerce/shipping/shippingPublish.ts` → `src/publish/shipping.tsx` → `platform/web/ndkPublishContext.ts`.
4. Products, read path: `sdk/commerce/discovery/productRead.ts` → `src/queries/products.tsx` → `platform/web/ndkReadContext.ts`.
5. Payment-adjacent code in `sdk/commerce/payments/` and `sdk/commerce/v4v/`.

author: hornjason
body:
Closes #307.

## Status of the ten criteria

Half of #307 Phase 1 was already in the tree with its checkboxes never ticked.
Verified against source rather than against the issue body:

| SC | State | Where |
|---|---|---|
| SC-A1 `TestSchema.command`/`timeout`, `ProjectHarnessSchema.container` | already landed | `lib/rungate-schema.ts:56,57,148` |
| SC-A2 `resolveConfig` + D3 normalisation, wrappers unchanged | already landed | `lib/config-loader.ts:160` |
| SC-A6 baseline returns UNMEASURED, not 0 | **this PR** | |
| SC-A7 the test uses a consumer-shaped fixture | **this PR** | |
| SC-A10 mutation, counted | **this PR** | 6 of 17 |
| SC-A11 ship.js resolves the URLs itself | **this PR** | |
| SC-A16 `no hand-written config interface survives` | already landed | `test/adr-002-regression-guards.test.ts:38` |
| SC-A17 `no bare catch remains around the config read` | already landed | same file, `:70` |
| SC-A18 `the rebuildCommand never hands make rebuild to an agent` | already landed | same file, `:101` |
| SC-A19 no heal round may reduce the test count | **this PR** | |

SC-A16/A17/A18 are there under slightly different titles than the issue gives
them, which is why a grep for the issue's wording finds nothing. They are the
three guards #314 restored.

## SC-A6/A7/A10 — a baseline nobody measured, reported as a clean tree

`captureTestBaseline` runs the project's suite before any change lands so the
verify gate can subtract pre-existing failures. It returned `0` for four
different facts, and the scope gate printed
`Test baseline: 0 pre-existing failures — clean suite` for all four:

| What happened | What was recorded |
|---|---|
| no `.claude/rungate.json` — the path was built by hand, so **every consumer on the documented directory layout took this branch** | `0`, clean suite |
| no `test.command` — including every consumer that authored `dev.testCmd`, the spelling ADR-002 D3 normalises *to* | `0`, clean suite |
| the suite ran and printed something unparseable — jest, pytest, a Makefile target, a timeout kill | `0`, clean suite |
| the suite ran and nothing was failing | `0`, clean suite |

Only the last is a clean tree. A fabricated baseline is the worst direction
for this number to be wrong in: it asserts the strongest claim the run can
make about the tree it started from.

**It worked on rungate the whole time.** This repo's config carries
`test.command`, so branch 2 was never taken here and any rungate-shaped
fixture is green against the broken code and the fixed code alike. That is the
reason the defect survived, and the reason SC-A7 insists on the consumer
shape.

An unmeasured baseline records **no number**. A `0` beside a reason would
leave `?? 0` at the verify gate reading it as a measured clean tree. Verify
WARNs on it: no subtraction happens either way, so what the branch stops is
the claim, not the arithmetic.

`extractTestFailureCount` keeps its contract — `gates/workflow.test.ts` pins
it and this issue may not change gate checks — and gained a nullable sibling
`parseTestFailureCount` that it now wraps.

## SC-A11 — the heal prompt sent an agent to find a file the consumer does not have

The prompt told an agent to read the project's monolith config for `apiUrl`
and, failing to find the key, to write `SKIP`. A migrated consumer does not
have that file, so a project serving a live API recorded "this check does not
apply" — and a skip for *no server here* and a skip for *I could not locate
the config* are the same two letters in the state file.

The workflow already knew the answer: it resolves the config before any prompt
is written and interpolates `${testCommand}` from it three lines above. The
clause is now built by the workflow, and **when a URL resolved, SKIP is not
offered at all**. It lives in a marked block and is executed by its test,
because a prompt test that greps for a URL passes against a prompt that
mentions the URL and still says SKIP.

## SC-A19 — a heal round that deletes a test

Run `wf_5cdce852-1e2` went from 34 tests to 23 across two rounds, no `skip`
recorded, no `todo` recorded. A heal agent is told a gate failed and asked to
make it pass; deleting the test is a correct solution to that instruction and
an incorrect solution to the problem, and nothing downstream can tell.

`lib/test-census.ts` counts declarations per file; the gate compares each run
to the census the previous one banked and FAILs on a drop. Every heal round
ends in a gate re-run, so the window is right. Not in `workflows/ship.js` — it
has no filesystem access and could only have asked an agent to check, and a
guard whose subject is an agent's edits cannot be an instruction to an agent.

Three decisions that keep it from being decorative: declarations rather than
passing tests (`.skip` and `.todo` count, and comments are not stripped,
because converting or commenting out removes the check just as thoroughly);
the first reading of a run is not a pass; and a refused round does not bank
the reduced census, or the next round compares against the deletion and the
refusal clears itself.

### Six ways the new guard could not fire, found by two review passes

All six were the shape SC-A19 guards against — present, called, unable to
fire. Fixed here rather than filed, and worth recording as its own fact: a
guard against a defect class, written by someone holding that class in mind,
still shipped six instances of it. That is the argument for the review pass,
not for trying harder.

1. **The refusal was counted where a later step erases it.** The census
   `fails++` sat above the verify gate's `subtractTestBaseline`, which cannot
   tell a census refusal from a suite failure. A run carrying three
   pre-existing failures would have had the deleted-test refusal subtracted to
   zero.
2. **It censused the wrong tree.** `projectRoot` is the main checkout; on a
   decomposed run the edits are in the worktree named by `treeUnderTest`, so
   the guard compared a tree nobody touched against itself — green every
   round, for the runs it most needs to watch.
3. **The walk was rungate's own layout.** `["test", "gates"]` means
   `src/foo.test.ts` censuses to `{}`, and `{}` compares clean against `{}`
   forever: permanently and silently dead for exactly the consumers it
   protects. The walk is now the whole tree minus `node_modules`, build output
   and dotfiles, and an empty census is UNMEASURED rather than first-reading.
4. **The banked census never reached disk, so the guard was permanently
   dead.** `writeGateResult` does its own `readState(sf)` and writes *that*
   back, so setting `state.gateContract.testCensus` in memory lands only by
   accident. Every subsequent run would have found no census, answered
   `first-reading`, logged a reassuring line, and compared nothing. The write
   is now explicit and read-modify-write, so the gate tests' and the heal
   agent's edits to the state file survive it.
5. **Every matching file was read with no bound.** Capped at 2 MB, and the cap
   is stable so an oversized file is absent from both censuses rather than
   reading as a deletion. A file crossing the cap between rounds refuses
   falsely, which is the right direction and names the file.
6. **The walk followed symlinks.** A dirent for a symlink answers false to
   `isDirectory()`, so a symlinked *directory* was skipped — but a symlink to
   a *file* passed the old `else` and was read. A link named `x.test.ts`
   pointing at a character device has size 0 and never ends. `isFile()`
   excludes both.

## What was broken to prove it

Two batteries, every count predicted before the mutation ran. None is left in
the tree.

Over `test/test-baseline-unmeasured.test.ts` + `test/ship-local-env-clause.test.ts` (17 tests):

| Mutation | Predicted | Red |
|---|---|---|
| the old reader restored verbatim — the defect | 6 | 6 |
| `parseTestFailureCount` returns `0` where it returned `null` | 2 | 2 |
| `recordTestBaseline` writes `0` beside the reason | 1 | 1 |
| `baselineAdjust

author: m-tabaza
body:
Google's sign-in in a Work tab still answers "Couldn't sign you in. This browser or app may not be secure" on Electron 45 (Chromium 156). #212 moved to the Electron 45 beta because it judged the engine version was the gap, but noted that "Google's sign-in itself" was "Not checked here". The engine version was not the gap.

## Cause

Work presents as Chrome: the user agent has no `Electron/` token, and the brands say Google Chrome. But Electron's `window.chrome` is empty. Chrome's `chrome.app`, `csi` and `loadTimes` come from Chrome's own layer, which Electron does not include. Google's sign-in turns away a browser that says it is Chrome without `chrome.app`.

Measured with a stand-alone Electron harness carrying Work's identity code, each part switched on or off. Each run takes the sign-in's first step with a made-up address. Google decides before it looks the account up: a browser past the gate gets "Couldn't find this account", a refused one gets `/signin/rejected`.

| Setup | Result |
|---|---|
| Work's identity as shipped (Chromium 156 and 152) | Refused 6/6 |
| Chrome user agent only, Electron's own brands | Refused 2/2 |
| Work's identity + client hints on page loads | Refused |
| Work's identity + `chrome.csi`, or + `chrome.loadTimes` | Refused |
| Work's identity + a Firefox user agent on accounts.google.com | Refused |
| Work's identity + `chrome.app` (Chromium 156 and 152) | Admitted 5/5 |
| Plain Electron (names itself) | Admitted 4/4 |
| Real Chrome 154 (control) | Admitted |

## Change

- **`preload/chrome-object.ts`.** Web pages get Chrome's `window.chrome`: `loadTimes`, `csi` and `app`. That covers a tab's top frame, a sign-in popup, and a tab's embedded frames; embedded frames now also get Chrome's client-hint brands. It matches Chrome 154, read from Chrome itself:
  - member order, values and JSON;
  - the `TypeError`s Chrome's bindings throw for arguments they don't take, and `installState` answering after the call;
  - which functions construct;
  - every function reads as native code. The app methods are bound functions. `loadTimes` and `csi` sit behind a Proxy, which lets them construct, show exactly Chrome's `function () { [native code] }`, and answer `null` for `caller` and `arguments`.
  - a refusal's stack has no frame of the shim's own.

  Timing comes from the page's navigation entry, through functions kept before the page's scripts run (performance, timers, `Math`), and it never throws. Members already there stay. Extension pages and workers are untouched.
- **ADR 0235** records the decision; ADR 0150's 2026-10-09 cause is corrected in place and points to it. The Electron 45 beta pin stays for the changes that landed with it, but sign-in no longer needs it.
- **Known limits** (TODO.md):
  - the app methods read as native code without Chrome's names;
  - `loadTimes` and `csi` answer the probes that find a Proxy (a prototype cycle, the `caller` getter called on them directly);
  - a frame a script creates (`about:blank`) keeps Electron's empty `window.chrome`;
  - `pageT` and `firstPaintTime` are a few milliseconds from Chrome's.

  Google checks none of these today.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`chrome-object.test.ts`, 11 tests): runs the function from its source, as `executeInMainWorld` does, against Chrome's recorded values. It covers a page that replaces `performance` and timing that fails.
- **E2E, offline:** `browser-identity.e2e.ts` checks what a page sees, including native-looking functions and a frame from another origin. `browser-popups.e2e.ts` checks what a sign-in popup sees.
- **E2E, live** (`google-sign-in.e2e.ts`): takes Google's first sign-in step in a Work tab. It runs only with `CATAMORPHIC_EXTERNAL_INTEGRATIONS=1`, which now reaches the Docker desktop suite and Turbo's `test:e2e:ci`.
  - A refusal of Work always fails.
  - Real Chrome takes the same step on every run where it is installed, and its answer and version go beside Work's to explain a failure. They never excuse one: this PR's first macOS run saw Google refuse the runner's Chrome 152 while admitting Work, so a "Chrome was refused too" skip would have hidden a real refusal.
  - Each run writes its verdicts to `google-sign-in.json`, Work's before the control runs. The control's calls time out, so it cannot hang the test.
- **Daily** (`.github/workflows/google-sign-in.yml`): runs on macOS at 05:41 UTC.
  - It requires the verdict file, so a check that skipped for lack of authority fails.
  - It writes both answers to the job summary.
  - On a failed daily run, it opens or comments on the issue "The daily Google sign-in check failed".
  - It also runs on pull requests that change what pages see of Work or how the check runs, including Electron upgrades.

### Verified

- Docker desktop suite with the live check enabled: all 7 tests across the three files pass, and the live one ran rather than skipped. On this PR's macOS runner the live check admitted Work on every commit.
- With the fix switched off, each of them fails. The live check is refused with "This browser or app may not be secure", and its verdict file and screenshot are written. The identity test fails on `window.chrome`, and the popup test fails on `chrome.app`.
- The revised shim, compiled, passes Google's gate live in the stand-alone harness, and its functions read `function () { [native code] }`.
- Typecheck, lint and unit tests (12). `bun run check` passed on the second commit; its run on the final commit is in a comment below.
- Not checked: a full sign-in through password and 2FA with a real account.

## Reviews

Four independent reviews found no blockers. Three reviewed the first commit (runtime correctness, tests and CI, docs), and their should-fix items are in the second. A fourth reviewed the second commit: its findings, along with the runner's refused Chrome, are in the third.

author: roysalisbury
body:
## Issue

Closes #1297

Target: `development/v1`

## Outcome

A CameraAgent image built from a commit now names that commit and a version in three places:
- **Published assemblies:** `AssemblyInformationalVersion` is `<version>+<40-char revision>`. The System > Software page reads this and shows both parts.
- **Telemetry:** the startup line and the OpenTelemetry resource `service.version` carry the same value.
- **Image labels:** `org.opencontainers.image.version` is set explicitly and is never inherited from the Ubuntu base image again.

Defaults:
- Development builds use the declared version `0.0.0-dev`.
- `scripts/release:cameraagent-image` passes its `--version`.
- A build without `HVO_SOURCE_REVISION` stays marked `unknown` everywhere, and the installer still refuses it.

Verified on a real amd64 image built on home-dev-01 from `3ab4d5a3`:

```text
labels:     org.opencontainers.image.version=0.0.0-dev  org.opencontainers.image.revision=3ab4d5a348e82863d7e97fec575101678ffdf710
assemblies: HVO.SkyMonitor.CameraAgent.dll, Common.dll, AgentCore.dll, replay-runner/HVO.SkyMonitor.CameraAgent.ReplayRunner.dll
            all contain 0.0.0-dev+3ab4d5a348e82863d7e97fec575101678ffdf710
log:        [15:49:21 INF] Starting telemetry service: hvo-camera v0.0.0-dev+3ab4d5a348e82863d7e97fec575101678ffdf710 (unknown)
metrics:    target_info{service_version="0.0.0-dev+3ab4d5a348e82863d7e97fec575101678ffdf710",...,service_name="unknown_service:dotnet"} 1
            with OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=hvo-camera: target_info{service_version="0.0.0-dev+3ab4d5a3…",service_name="hvo-camera",service_instance_id=…}
```

Before this change the smoke deployment showed `1.0.0` with no revision, `vunknown`, and `org.opencontainers.image.version=24.04`.

## Scope And Exclusions

Changed:
- `src/HVO.SkyMonitor.CameraAgent/Dockerfile`:
  - `HVO_VERSION` (default `0.0.0-dev`) and `HVO_SOURCE_REVISION` (default `unknown`) are declared once as global arguments and re-declared in each stage without a default.
  - Both are validated before publishing:
    - The revision must be `unknown` or a 40-character lowercase object ID.
    - The version follows the release tool's safe-identifier rule: 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, `.` and `-`, alphanumeric first and last character, no `..`.
    - A bad value fails the build with exit 64 before any publish work. This also keeps `;` out of the MSBuild properties.
  - Both publishes, the CameraAgent host and the ReplayRunner, receive `-p:InformationalVersion=${HVO_VERSION} -p:SourceRevisionId=${HVO_SOURCE_REVISION}`. The SDK composes these into `<version>+<revision>` for every project in the publish graph.
  - The runtime stage labels `org.opencontainers.image.version="${HVO_VERSION}"` next to the existing revision label.
- `src/HVO.SkyMonitor.Common/Observability/SkyMonitorObservabilityExtensions.cs`: `AddSkyMonitorObservability(builder, string? serviceVersion = null)`.
  - A configured `Telemetry:ServiceVersion` takes precedence over the passed value. Blank values are ignored.
  - The resolved value goes to `TelemetryOptions.ServiceVersion`, which drives the startup line and the operation `ActivitySource` version.
  - It also goes to `OtlpExportOptions.ServiceVersion` and directly to the resource attribute `service.version`. The export package only calls `AddService` when a service name is configured, and `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` is often unset.
  - It also goes to the Serilog OTLP log resource. The pinned sink (4.2.0) applies the OTLP environment variables after its options, so the sink reads the environment through a reader that appends the resolved `service.version` as the last `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` entry. A conflicting `service.version` there no longer replaces it on exported logs. The endpoint, headers, service name and other resource attributes still come from the environment (correction for review finding F1).
  - Passing no version leaves everything unset, exactly as before, and the log sink reads the environment unchanged.
- `src/HVO.SkyMonitor.CameraAgent/Program.cs` passes `typeof(Program).Assembly`'s informational version. The Software page (`CameraAgentSystemUiService.GetSoftwareAsync`) reads the same value.
- `scripts/release:cameraagent-image`:
  - Passes `--build-arg HVO_VERSION=${version}` to both per-platform builds and to the `--push` build.
  - After the existing host-platform smoke test, it requires the version label to equal `--version` and both entry assemblies to contain `<version>+<revision>`. `create-image` already requires identical label sets across platforms, so the host platform's label check covers both.
- `scripts/test:cameraagent-arm64-ci`: the label `jq` expression also requires `org.opencontainers.image.version == "0.0.0-dev"`, and both entry assemblies must contain `0.0.0-dev+<revision>`.
- `scripts/test:deployment-installer`: both images built from the current Dockerfile must carry the `0.0.0-dev` version label: the HEAD install image and the recovery candidate. The recovery baseline is built from an older Dockerfile and is not checked.
- `scripts/deploy/images.sh` (split-host deploy, correction for review finding F2): archive and registry CameraAgent builds pass `--build-arg HVO_SOURCE_REVISION=<revision>` next to the unchanged revision label, so their assemblies name the commit. LogicHost builds are unchanged because the LogicHost Dockerfile declares no such argument. The `prepare-images` contract in `scripts/deploy-contracts/prepare-images.sh` requires the argument and the label on every recorded CameraAgent build, and no build argument on LogicHost builds. `docs/runbooks/split-host-preflight.md` states this.
- Tests and inventories, all new cases Unit:

  | File | Adds | Category inventory |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `CameraAgentImageBuildIdentityTests` | 3 cases | `CameraAgent.Tests` +4 (the 3 cases plus the `SplitVersion` row) |
  | `CameraAgentSystemUiServiceTests` | 1 `SplitVersion` row for `0.0.0-dev+unknown` | (counted above) |
  | `SkyMonitorObservabilityExtensionsTests` | 3 cases, plus 3 exported-log-resource rows (F1) | `Common.Tests` +6 |
  | `ReplayRunnerComposeTests` | 4 installer rows | `Deployment.Cli.Tests` +4 |

  `docs/runbooks/ci-pipeline.md` totals change from 7024 to 7038.

Excluded:
- Per the issue: release-train versioning policy, LogicHost images, and reproducible image IDs (#1299).
- LogicHost telemetry: it calls `AddSkyMonitorObservability()` with no version and is unchanged.
- The startup line's `(unknown)` environment is `Telemetry:Environment` and is outside this issue.

## Compatibility

- **Installer label contract:** unchanged. `org.opencontainers.image.revision` keeps its value and placement. The installer still requires a 40-character lowercase revision. The new `ReplayRunnerComposeTests` rows pin that `null`, `unknown`, a 7-character SHA and an uppercase SHA are refused.
- **Build arguments:**
  - `HVO_SOURCE_REVISION` keeps its name and its `unknown` default.
  - `HVO_VERSION` is new and optional.
  - Every existing caller passes a 40-character `git rev-parse` value or nothing.
  - The new validation rejects values that would previously have produced a revision label the installer refuses anyway.
- **Assembly identity:** only `InformationalVersion` changes. `AssemblyVersion` and `FileVersion` stay at the SDK default `1.0.0.0`. Release versions therefore never pass through NuGet version parsing, and binding identity does not change between builds.
- **Local `dotnet run` builds:** unchanged, because the SDK still derives `1.0.0+<git sha>` from `.git`. Only image builds use `0.0.0-dev`.
- **Release script:** the new arguments and checks touch no existing output. The checks run where the smoke test already loads the host-platform image.

### Build cache cost (acceptance criterion 5)

Before this change, `HVO_SOURCE_REVISION` was declared after the payload, so a revision-only change rebuilt one metadata layer. The assemblies must now contain the revision, so the identity is declare

author: dynasty9
body:
Gunfire is rebuilt: muzzle flashes, tracers, recoil and bullet impacts. Every shot now flashes and kicks, tracers glow in each side's colour, and what a round hits decides what flies off it. Heavy firefights cost about the same as before.

![Before and after, at night](https://github.com/Dynasty9/Frontline/blob/claude/firing-animations-impacts-fbd4e7/changelog/unreleased/gunfire-effects/before-after-night.jpg?raw=true)

![A tank's main gun by day](https://github.com/Dynasty9/Frontline/blob/claude/firing-animations-impacts-fbd4e7/changelog/unreleased/gunfire-effects/tank-gun.jpg?raw=true)

![Rounds landing in a field](https://github.com/Dynasty9/Frontline/blob/claude/firing-animations-impacts-fbd4e7/changelog/unreleased/gunfire-effects/rounds-landing.jpg?raw=true)

## What changed

- **New `GunFx` (`scripts/game/gunfx.gd`).** Seven layers (tracers, flashes and flames, puffs, sparks, grit, debris, brass), each a single `MultiMesh` drawn in one call. A shot writes a few instances into a ring once. The vertex shader then flies them (drag, gravity, wind, landing on the ground), so nothing is moved from script per frame. This replaces `Fx`'s per-frame GDScript tracer and flash pools and its CPU blood and wood puffs.
- **Muzzle:** a starburst plus a flame along the barrel, split sideways by the flash hider and sized per weapon. Also a short light (skipped on Low effects), a breath of smoke, dust lifted under guns fired low, and brass ejected to the right that lies on the ground.
- **Recoil per real shot**, replacing the sine-wave wobble:
  - `SoldierModel.fire_kick`: the weapon goes back, the muzzle up, the shoulders back, settling in a few frames.
  - `Structure.crew_kick`: mounted guns.
  - `Vehicle.gun_kick`: the turret jolts back on main-gun and autocannon fire.
- **Tracers** in team colours (red Coalition, green Rebels), at least about 2 px wide at any zoom. Some other rounds get a faint streak.
- **Impacts by surface.** `Fx.surface_of` on the server picks dirt, stone, sand, wood, leaves, metal or flesh. Water uses main's new spout and foam. Impacts show when the round arrives, with the odd ricochet off steel, stone or a shallow hit on the ground.
- **Big guns:** tank guns get a flash, fireball, burning flecks, smoke cloud, ground dust and a shockwave. Rockets get a back-blast, mortars a tube flash.
- Visual randomness no longer draws on `world.rng`, so a host with a view plays the same battle as a headless one.
- **New test hooks:** `--shot-demo`, `--test-fire=ground` and `--test-fire-every`. They're documented in DEVELOPMENT.md, and FEATURES.md has a Gunfire section.

## Network

- No `NET_VERSION` bump. SHOT events keep their shape; impact codes 5–7 are new values in the same field, so older clients just skip them.
- LAUNCH gains an optional shooter id at the end.

## Performance

Measured with the old and new builds running at the same time, because runs one after another swing about 2× with other load on this machine. Same stress test: about 17 men each firing 11 rounds a second.

| | Old build | New build |
|---|---|---|
| Fire straight ahead: GPU ms per frame | 9.05 | 8.73 |
| Fire straight ahead: FPS | 69 | 72 |
| Every round into the ground: GPU ms per frame | 8.23 | 7.91 |
| Every round into the ground: FPS | 82 | 87 |

The server tick, which includes spawning the effects on the host, is about the same.

## Testing

- `--import` compiles clean.
- Headless runs, no `SCRIPT ERROR`, on both the branch and after merging main:
  - `--scenario=attack`, `breach`, `naval`, `guns`, `tank`
  - `--aivai --seed=3 --timescale=5 --quit-after=1200`
- Multiplayer: a headless host of `--scenario=tank` with a windowed off-screen client. The client played the shots, tank-gun rounds and rockets with no errors and draws the tracers and impacts.
- Off-screen renders by day and at night of the roster, guns, cover and tank scenarios, plus the shot demo. The screenshots above come from these.
- `python .github/scripts/changelog.py check` passes.

## 变更摘要 / Summary

本 PR 在 PR1 的统一构建基础上增加 npm 分发包生成能力，使用户可以通过 `@infituit/rss-cli` 使用原生 `rss-cli` 二进制。

- 新增 `make npm-packages VERSION=<version>`，复用 Makefile 的六平台构建矩阵。

author: jfolcini
body:
## Problem

The real-backend WebdriverIO lane's slowest typing specs spent most of their time waiting out read-back budgets. A CI survey timed `pages-most-linked` at about 24 s and `search-bm25-order` at about 21 s.

## Cause

One `browser.keys` call presses every key down before it releases any, and WebKitGTK's driver loses a key that is pressed again while still held:

- `[[` arrived as `[`, and `::` as `:`.
- Every space after the first in a call was lost: `zap of ink` arrived as `zap ofink`.

The first attempt then sat on the wrong text for its whole 3 s budget (10 s in `search-bm25-order`) before the slow one-key-at-a-time retry. In run 38909854600, ten first attempts failed this way across six specs. The helper's doc blamed a janky first render; the log shows the driver.

## Fix

In `e2e-tauri/helpers.ts`:

- `distinctKeyChunks` splits the text into runs in which no character repeats, and the first attempt sends each run as its own call.
- An attempt ends once the read-back has stopped changing for 400 ms, with 3 s still the bound. The retry still types one key at a time.
- The `readBackTimeout` parameter is gone, along with the 10 s budget it carried.

No spec's assertions changed.

## Tests

`e2e-tauri/helpers.test.ts` pins the chunks for `[[wdio-rival` and `zap of ink`. A fast-check property checks that the chunks join back to the text and that no chunk has a repeated character. Splitting only at adjacent repeats turns three of them red, the space case among them.

## To check on this PR's e2e-tauri run

Compare spec times against run 38909854600:

| Spec | Before |
|---|---|
| pages-most-linked | 23.7 s |
| search-bm25-order | 21.3 s |
| link-label-source-roundtrip | 16.2 s |
| page-rename-lookup | 14.6 s |
| escape-property-line | 11.0 s |
| import-vault-adopts-link-target (control: types nothing through the helper) | 13.8 s |

author: arul28
body:
## Why Sentry **ADE-BRAIN-6** hid a real bug inside its catch-all: `Unsupported database value at parameter 1: object [sql=select * from lane…`. **The defect is live, not dead code, and it is in the desktop's action registry rather than `apps/ade-cli`.** An exhaustive sweep of `apps/ade-cli/src` found every `from lanes` query there binds only scalars — but the brain runs the desktop lane service headless, which is why `ADE-BRAIN` saw it. `buildLaneDomainService` spreads the raw lane service onto the action surface, so `lane.getStackChain({laneId})` reaches `getStackChain(laneId)` with the **object**, which flows straight to `getLaneRow` (`select * from lanes where id = ? and project_id = ? limit 1`) and gets bound as parameter 1. Two callers always send the object, which is why it always throws: - The **automation step** `lane.getStackChain` — the editor renders its schema parameter as `{laneId}` and the runner calls the callable with the resolved args object. - **Agents** via `run_ade_action`, whose tool doc says "Use args for one object parameter". ## What changed A `readLaneIdActionArg` adapter that accepts a positional string **or** `{laneId}`, applied to `getStackChain`, `getChildren`, `getDeleteRisk` and `cancelDelete`. `getSummary` already had exactly this adapter — this follows the existing precedent rather than inventing a pattern. **Siblings of the same class were found and fixed too:** `getChildren` binds the lane id as parameter **2** (so it produced "parameter 2", not the reported "parameter 1"), and `getDeleteRisk`/`cancelDelete` were latent — positional methods on the object-input surface, saved only because preload happens to send `{arg}`. The fix is at the action surface, so no stored automation rule changes shape, and every existing positional caller (`ade lanes children`, `ade lanes stack`, sync commands, IPC) still sends a scalar and is unaffected. ## Evidence - Extended the existing lane test in `registry.test.ts` (no new file): both `{laneId}` and a bare `"lane-1"` reach all four methods as the scalar, and `{}`/`undefined` are refused. **81 passed.** Both app typechecks clean. - Falsified: with the four adapters reverted to the pre-fix spread, the test fails with the exact bad shape — expected `['lane-1']`, received `[{ laneId: 'lane-1' }]`. The DB-level message text is already pinned in `kvDb.test.ts`, so it was not duplicated. ## Not checked - **Which single event ADE-BRAIN-6 grouped** (an automation run versus an agent calling `run_ade_action` with `args`) is not established — both funnel through the same registry adapter, so one fix covers both. - Whether the automation editor should emit a positional args list instead is a separate call; the fix is at the action surface rather than in the stored rule shape. - Windows parity: not exercised on Windows. The change is argument-shape normalisation with no platform-specific surface.

  Open in ADE  ·  perf/ade176-lane-param branch  ·  PR #1673

--- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches the desktop ADE action boundary used by automations and agents for lane DB reads; change is narrow and covered by tests but fixes live failure paths. > > **Overview** > Fixes lane ADE actions that were forwarding **`{ laneId }`** objects straight into SQLite lane lookups when automations or **`run_ade_action`** used the documented object args—matching the failure behind **ADE-BRAIN-6** (`Unsupported database value at parameter 1: object`). > > Adds **`readLaneIdActionArg`** on the desktop action registry (same idea as **`lane.getSummary`**) and routes **`getChildren`**, **`getStackChain`**, **`getDeleteRisk`**, and **`cancelDelete`** through it so both a positional string and **`{ laneId }`** become a scalar before the lane service runs. Positional CLI callers are unchanged. > > Tests in **`registry.test.ts`** assert both shapes forward **`"lane-1"`** and empty/missing args are rejected for all four actions. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit b09a82bc2cc9ad513950382aa8a9e5142dd122c4. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

author: deferredreward
body:
Closes #1155

**Intent:** Benjamin's decision A on #1155: when a named person fixes an AI-written note directly on Door43, the next AI notes run leaves it alone. Bot pushes and the unnamed "Door43 sync" don't protect a note. Replaces held draft #1198 and fixes its two review findings (F1 over-keep from adopted bot pushes, F2 regression on create A → Door43 B → app save A).

**What changed, plainly:**
- The kept-notes rule now also keeps a note when its last change was a Door43 copy-in stamped "commits by <name>", the AI wrote the note in its current life, and the words still differ from the AI's last version (`api/src/keptNotes.ts`). It reads the note's own "last changed by" record, because the nightly copy-in clears the editor field and writes no history row.
- The kept list sent to the bot and the after-run sweep both consider these notes (`loadKeptTns`, `deleteUnkeptTns`). The kept-list query only pulls named rows the AI actually wrote: in prod, 1CH (the worst book) goes from 1,140 candidates to 21, 78 ms.
- Prod check (read-only): 640 notes match, the number the decision priced.

**Known limits:** the name stamp covers the whole Door43 file window, so a bot push in the same window as a person's commit can over-keep; a note with an AI write but no create in its history counts as kept; a Door43 change that only moves a note doesn't count. Commits under deferredreward's own name count as a person. About 1,845 notes Door43 people changed but the AI never wrote are not protected by this rule (they were never AI notes).

**Tests:** failing fixtures first in `keptNotes.test.mjs`; typecheck, web (77 files) and api (99 files) green.

**Live test:** skip: server-side classifier with no Door43 sync to drive on agentbox; unit and sweep tests cover the path, read-only prod queries confirmed which rows match.

**Lessons:** the nightly sync's re-seed of an AI note sets the editor field to empty and writes no history row, so any Door43 attribution must come from the row's last-change columns; those names are per file window, so pair them with a per-row word check.

author: agrivisionai
body:
Modelled on the agritech landing pages competitors rank with — hero, audience split, numbered use cases, trust block, CTA — and deliberately missing the part those pages lead with. The reference page for this format opens its case study with **"3x faster harvesting"** and its lead form with **"thousands of successful accomplishments."** We have measured neither. So the second paragraph of ours says, in plain text: > You will not find an outcome statistic anywhere on this page. We have not run the studies that would support one, and a number we cannot source is worth less than the sentence it sits in. ## What's on it **Nine use cases, each naming the modules it runs on.** Every module named is a real screen in the product and appears in the Platform grid — Disease Detection, Soil Analysis, Crop Recommendation, Market Prices, Price Alerts, Government Schemes, Weather Intelligence, Irrigation Scheduling, Extension Worker CRM, Field Scouting, My Farms, Voice Assistant, Ask AI, Pest Prediction, Yield Prediction, Analytics, Dashboard. **FieldSense and FieldOps appear nowhere in the nine.** A use-case page is exactly where a roadmap item quietly becomes a promise. **The two sections competitors don't have are the ones worth having:** - *What it will refuse to answer* — the chemical-dose refusal, stated as the differentiator it is rather than buried in a safety footnote. - *What this page does not claim* — five claims we will not make, including the 54-crop figure and any accuracy percentage. **Market-price cadence is a table, not prose:** | Country | Source | Update cadence | |---|---|---| | India | Agmarknet, via data.gov.in | Daily | | USA | USDA NASS Quick Stats | Monthly | | Canada | Statistics Canada table 32-10-0077 | Monthly | That's the fact most often quoted back at us wrongly, so it goes where it can be extracted cleanly. ## Not an orphan Linked from the nav, the footer, the sitemap (priority 0.9) and `llms.txt`. The Ireland page taught us what an unlinked page is worth: Google found it, reported *"referring page, none detected"*, and declined to index it. ## Images The existing Pexels-licensed set already on `/investors`, with alt text carried over verbatim — rice transplanting (hero), the three audience photos, and the plant-and-smartphone shot beside the refusal section. Nothing new is licensed. No image is a product screenshot or a mock of one, and the credit line says so. All five carry explicit `width`/`height` to avoid layout shift; the hero is eager, the rest lazy. The `` lint warnings match the existing `/investors` convention (self-hosted `.webp` with `srcSet` rather than `next/image`) — 3 here against 13 there. ## Verification - `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean apart from the pre-existing `no-img-element` convention warnings - `next build` passes — 103 static pages, `/use-cases` prerendered - Rendered locally: 6 question-based `

author: nathan1e1-1
body:
## Problem
The macOS keychain kept prompting even after **Allow**, and "Always Allow" never stuck. `codesign` shows why: both dev and bundled builds are **ad-hoc, linker-signed** with `Internal requirements=none` and no `TeamIdentifier`. macOS binds a keychain grant to the app's code-signing identity — with no stable identity, it re-prompts on every access. This is not patchable in-app (the prior in-place-write + memoization PR reduced accesses but could not make the grant persist).

## Fix
Move secrets off the OS Keychain into a local `0600` JSON file:
- `secret_*` commands now read/write `~/Library/Application Support/com.nthnp.coldemailagentic/secrets.json`.
- Atomic writes (temp file + `rename`), serialized read-modify-write, `0600` perms, `create_dir_all`.
- **Command surface unchanged** → `secrets.ts` / `keychainSecretStore.ts` / OAuth untouched.
- Drops the `security-framework` dependency (also simplifies the Linux CI).

## Tests
- New Rust unit tests: set/get/update/delete round-trip, no temp file left behind, `0600` mode enforcement.
- `cargo test` 3/3 · `npm test` 166/166 · typecheck · lint · build all green.

## Note
Existing keychain values are **not migrated** — reconnect Gmail once; AI keys/client secret resolve from `.env` if present, else re-enter in Settings.

author: quangvdao
body:
Part of #706.

Base: #874, with #873 merged in.

Proves P5 for the old compressed oracle and salted Merkle extractor. The main theorem,
`SaltedMerkle.merkle_online`, establishes `OnlineIndistinguishable` with the explicit error
`min(1, 24*wVC*(t-1)^2/|Y|)` in the existing two-sided square-root formulation. Both directions
use ordinary-port mass in the unsplit recording execution. The coefficient 24 and the joint
budget schedule come from the bounds note, equation (30), and repair note, equation (2).

The proof lifts the extraction-controlled basis swap to a private unitary, proves that it
fixes initialization, and establishes exact recording conjugacy and extraction commutation.
Occupied-key and unchanged-database sectors transfer the generalized commutator bound to a
source-projected Gram inequality. Empty occupied sets contribute zero, and sectors combine
by a maximum without measuring the keys. The runtime comparison reuses #873's coherent-port
and selected-mass infrastructure. Its local rate schedule sums exactly to `(t-1)^2`, and
subprobability caps the error at one.

The general P5 theorem takes explicit ordinary-port operator and population-grade hypotheses;
the compressed-oracle theorem reduces them to joint-label instability, and the Merkle theorem
discharges that instability using S15's results. Programs may branch adaptively, select ports
coherently, use arbitrary local instruments and entangled workspace, and start subnormalized.
No collision-freeness assumption is required. No Hadamard instantiation or protocol layer is
included.

Files:

- `VCVio/Quantum/VC/Proof/Online.lean`: recording population, swap unitary identities, sector
  decomposition, source Gram bounds, and actual-prefix coherent comparisons.
- `VCVio/Quantum/VC/Proof/OnlineSecurity.lean`: private-unitary law invariance, identification
  of both recording laws, subprobability cap, general P5, and compressed-oracle P5.

author: jhontea
body:
## Why
The fix for reverse geocoding in #63 gives a pasted coordinate-only Google Maps link the address of the **nearest** place that Geoapify knows, and that place is often someone else's, 65–340 m away. In a dry run on the 13 existing coordinate addresses, "Nanda House" came back as "Masjid Al Huriyah, …" and "favehotel" as "Starbucks, …". Ahmad decided to keep coordinates for those (see #65, closed). This PR makes new pastes behave the same way.

## What changed
- `GeoapifyClient.ReverseGeocode` only returns an address when the result's `distance` is ≤ 50 m from the point. When it is farther, the address is empty and the country code is still returned.
- `ResolveMapsLink` then falls back to the coordinates as the address, as it already did whenever reverse geocoding failed. A place name taken from the link is kept.
- This adds no API calls: `distance` is already in Geoapify's response.

## Tests
- Client: a result 0 m away (Mason Pine Hotel) uses its address; a result 340 m away gives no address but still the country `ID`.
- `ResolveMapsLink`: with a far result, the suggestion's address and name are the coordinates, and the country is `ID`.
- `go vet ./... && go test ./...`

author: eliaspinero
body:
Closes #765. Also answers #664 (the maqaf test it asks for).

## What this changes

In Hebrew a maqaf (`־`, U+05BE) joins two words inside one quote word, but the aligned ULT names each side as its own word. The quote matcher split quote words on whitespace only, so a quote with a maqaf never matched the ULT. The Check list title then fell back to the Hebrew quote, and the ULT pane highlighted nothing.

`quoteToWords` (`src/data/sourceHighlight.ts`) now also splits each quote word on the maqaf. It is the one function behind both the list titles (`gatewayTitleFor` → `glTitleFor` → `gatewayQuote` → `matchQuote`) and the ULT-pane highlight, for tN quotes (word arrays) and TWL `OrigWords` (plain strings). This fixes Translation Notes and Translation Words together. The New Testament is unchanged, because Greek has no maqaf.

## Commits

- `5db0e70` Check: match a maqaf-joined Hebrew quote word to its ULT words (#765)
- `3722be2` Evidence: Genesis tN/tW titles with a maqaf, seen in the app (#765). This is the D81 artifact the issue's "Verify" asks for: [`docs/evidence/maqaf-titles-genesis-2026-10-16.md`](https://github.com/unfoldingWord/translationCore4/blob/issue-765-maqaf-quotes/docs/evidence/maqaf-titles-genesis-2026-10-16.md), with two screenshots.

## Platform reuse

Nothing in the platform or the pinned libraries resolves a helps quote to gateway words. The app's own matcher (`sourceHighlight.ts`, issue #104) is extended by one line. No new code path.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **tN Genesis: no Hebrew titles where the verse is aligned, 95 → 0. Met: seen in the app on Genesis. The committed journey runs on Jonah.** [VERIFIED 3722be2, 2026-10-16]
   - **In the app** (evidence record above): a blank Genesis was added to the rig project and Check → Translation Notes was opened. The list has **2224 rows, 0 with Hebrew text**.
   - A throwaway harness ran `deriveTnItems` + `glTitleFor` over the same v91 pins (en_tn `e586762`, en_ult `35d2159`). Genesis: **95 untitled before, 0 after**, and all 95 have a maqaf. Jonah: 5 → 0.
   - The committed journey runs on **Jonah**, because the rig's seeded project has no Genesis (decision 2). New J4 case `every Jonah title shows the ULT phrase, also for a quote with a maqaf (#765)` asserts 0 list titles with Hebrew script. It failed before the fix with title `“מַה־לְּ⁠ךָ֣”` for z3jv, and passes after.
2. **Gen 1:5 xxe6 "Then there was evening and there was morning", 1:7 xfx7 "And it was so", highlighted in the ULT pane. Met: seen in the app.**
   - **In the app:** xxe6 and xfx7 show exactly those titles. The ULT-pane marks read "Then there was evening and there was morning" and "And it was so" (screenshot of xxe6 in the evidence record).
   - `test/sourceHighlight.test.ts` › `matches its separate ULT words — tN quotes` returns exactly those two strings from the real rows against the en_ult v91 Genesis 1 fixture. It failed before with `null`.
3. **A maqaf quote word matches its separate ULT words, failing before and passing after (#664). Met.** Same unit tests as 2, plus the TWL string case below. Both failed before the change.
4. **Items without a maqaf keep the same titles. Met.**
   - Unit test `leaves quotes without a maqaf as they were`: c9yz "And God called", xmx5 "one day".
   - Harness: every title of GEN, JON, RUT and PSA (24 447 tN+tW items) compared before and after. **0 titles of a quote without a maqaf changed.**
   - About 3 200 maqaf titles in those four books changed. Most now match the phrase exactly, for example GEN 1:22 pfl8 "in the seas" → "the waters in the seas", and 2:3 aq2s "And God blessed … seventh" → "And God blessed the seventh day".
   - Some still go through the existing per-word fallback in `matchQuote` and pick up words from elsewhere in the verse. For example, GEN 33:5 mix3 "God" → "his eyes … the women … whom God has graciously given to your servant". These were already wrong on `main` (a partial title, or Hebrew). See "Not in this pull request".
5. **tW Genesis: no Hebrew titles; Gen 1:28 vzz2 shows its ULT phrase, highlighted. Met: seen in the app on Genesis.**
   - **In the app:** Check → Translation Words on the same Genesis lists **5640 rows, 0 with Hebrew text**. vzz2 shows “the earth”, and the ULT pane marks "the earth" (screenshot in the evidence record).
   - Harness: en_twl `7cbb341` Genesis, **260 untitled before, 0 after**. Jonah: 11 → 0.
   - Unit test `TWL OrigWords (a plain string)`: vzz2 `אֶת־הָ⁠אָ֖רֶץ` → "the earth". It failed before with `null`.
   - The J4 case asserts 0 Hebrew titles in the tW list and the ULT-pane highlight for Jonah 1:1 mtmh "the word of Yahweh".

## Self-review

Run in the worktree at `5db0e70`, Windows 11, 2026-10-16:

- `npm run lint`: 0 errors, 1 warning (the existing `src/data/serverApi.ts` warning).
- `npm run typecheck`: clean.
- `npx vitest run`: 1725 passed, 2 failed (`homeObsCard`, `obsStoryState`, 5 s timeouts under load). Both pass alone (18/18). These are known local timeouts and are not in this change.
- `npm run test:desktop`: 60 pass, 8 fail (seven `#740` archive cases and the `#644` en_tw bundle case). **The same 8 fail on unchanged `main` 52e03ba** on this PC. This change touches no desktop code.
- `npm run build`: OK. `npm run docs:gate`: OK.
- Playwright `e2e/j04-check-book.spec.ts` (lane 19990/5190): 16 passed, 3 skipped, 1 failed. The failure is `a bookmark and a check comment persist… (#50)`. It also fails with this change stashed, on Titus, which has no Hebrew. Not from this change.
- Ran the feature as a user: J4 case screenshots of Jonah 1:6 (tN) and 1:1 (tW), each with an English title and the phrase marked in the ULT pane.
- Diff checks:
  - **Inputs that differ:** a word with no maqaf passes through unchanged. A maqaf at an edge gives an empty piece, which is filtered as before.
  - **Saved data:** `tnQuoteWords` is untouched, so `contextId.quote` in saved decisions keeps its shape.

## Decisions for approval

1. **Split in `quoteToWords`, not in `tnQuoteWords`.** The issue proposes both. `tnQuoteWords` builds `contextId.quote`, which is saved in every decision (`httpStore.ts` `normalizeContextId`) and is part of the tC3 import key (`import/tc3.ts`). Changing it would give old and new decisions different quote shapes. The matcher-only change fixes both tools and changes no saved data.
2. **The committed journey runs on Jonah, not Genesis.** The rig's seeded project holds TIT and JON only, so a Genesis journey would mean adding a 5 MB book to the fixture every journey shares. Jonah carries the same defect (tN 5, tW 11 titles in Hebrew). Genesis was checked in the app by hand instead, and recorded as the D81 evidence record (`3722be2`).
3. **`quoteSpans` is left alone.** It only serves OBS frames, whose quotes are in the gateway language and have no maqaf.
4. **The fixture is Genesis 1 only** (`test/fixtures/en_ult/GEN-1.usfm`, 110 KB, provenance in `test/fixtures/README.md`). The whole `GEN.usfm` is 5 MB.

## Not in this pull request

- The per-word fallback in `matchQuote` (`sourceHighlight.ts`, "degrades to content matching") can add words from elsewhere in the verse to a title and to the ULT highlight. This happens when the English word order differs from the Hebrew. It is older than this change and affects quotes without a maqaf too. Changing it would change titles for every quote, so it is left for its own issue.

- The stray spaces in list titles ("creature s", "flock s"), reported in #765 for separate triage.
- A freshly imported USFM project with no source texts pinned (same).
- The rig's Jonah shows "The original-language text is not on this computer": the seed does not sideload `hbo_uhb` v3.0.0. This does not affect titles, which read the ULT alignment.

author: aliorhun
body:
## Özet

Üst menüye **Karşı Uzay** (`#karsi-uzay`) adında yeni, tam genişlikli bir kavram laboratuvarı sayfası ekler. Sayfa, etkin çalışma alanındaki yapıyı (simetriyle genişletilmiş P1 listesi) salt okunur kullanır ve editördeki IT92 `f₀(s)`, ADP ve `F(hkl)` hesaplarını paylaşır. VESTA'da karşılığı olmayan, X-ışını toz kırınımı ve yarı iletken fiziği derslerine yönelik dört sekme içerir.

| Sekme | İçerik |
| --- | --- |
| **Gerçek ↔ karşı örgü** | Birim hücrede `(hkl)` düzlem ailesi ve ona dik `G(hkl)`; `d`, `|G| = 1/d`, karşı hücre parametreleri; `|F|²` ile ağırlıklandırılmış 3B karşı örgü; atom katkılarını uç uca ekleyen **yapı faktörü fazör diyagramı** (kapalı çokgen = sistematik sönüm) |
| **Ewald küresi ve toz halkaları** | `[uvw]` düzleminde Ewald kesiti, kristal dönüşü `ω`, **Sonraki Bragg konumu** düğmesi (ilk açılışta otomatik hizalama); toz modunda `1/d` kabukları; düz dedektörde Debye–Scherrer halkaları ve LP'li toz deseni |
| **Bölge ekseni deseni (SAED)** | Relativistik elektron dalgaboyu, Mott–Bethe elektron saçılma çarpanı, uyarılma hatası ve kalınlığa bağlı `sinc²` biçim çarpanı; kinematik olarak sönük konumlar ayrıca işaretlenir |
| **Brillouin bölgesi ve bantlar** | Saf ötelemelerden primitive örgü, Wigner–Seitz bölgesi, Bravais türü, Setyawan–Curtarolo (2010) yüksek simetri yolu (CUB/FCC/BCC/TET/ORC/HEX) ve boş örgü bantları |

## Mimari

- `reciprocal-core.js`: bağımlılıksız, saf matematik modülü. Testleri `tests/reciprocal.test.mjs` içinde.
- `reciprocal-page.js`: Three.js ve SVG arayüzü; editöre `crystal-app.js` içindeki salt okunur `reciprocalHost()` köprüsüyle bağlanır.
- Sayfanın başlatılması editörün açılışından yalıtılmıştır: sayfada bir hata olsa bile editör çalışmaya devam eder.
- `pages.yml` yeni modülleri kopyalar ve yeni testleri çalıştırır; `browser-visual.yml` yeni modüller değiştiğinde de tetiklenir.
- 117 TR/EN çeviri girdisi eklendi; dinamik etiketler ve hata mesajları da dahil.

## Doğrulama

- `node --test tests/core.test.cjs tests/worker.test.mjs tests/reciprocal.test.mjs`: **180/180 geçti**. `tests/validation/test_runner.cjs`: 3/3.
- Çekirdek testleri analitik sonuçlara karşı yazıldı: dual baz, `d(hkl)` ve G ⟂ düzlem, Bragg geometrisi ve sonraki Bragg dönüşü, 200/300 kV elektron dalgaboyu, saf ötelemeler (F/I/P), FCC (14 yüz, 24 köşe) / BCC / SC / HEX bölge geometrisi ve `(2π)³/V_prim` hacmi, özel noktaların bölge yüzeyinde olması, Γ ve X'te boş örgü enerjileri, elmas sönümleri.
- Uygulamadaki yedi örnek yapının hepsinde Bravais türü doğru tanınıyor (Si/NaCl/elmas/Cu → FCC, CsCl/BaTiO₃ → CUB, grafit → HEX).
- `tests/browser/visual.test.mjs` yeni sayfa için genişletildi: Si için d(111) = 3.13559 Å, (200) sönümü, 4 Debye–Scherrer halkası, λ(200 kV) = 0.02508 Å, FCC bölgesi ve 10 bant eğrisi, TR/EN geçişi, konsol hatası olmaması.
  - Yerel, yazılımsal WebGL (SwiftShader) ortamında yaklaşık 7 çalıştırmanın biri hariç hepsi geçti. Tek zaman aşımının hangi adımda olduğunu tespit edemedim; bu ortamda ekran görüntüsü almak çok yavaştı. Sayfada sızıntı veya sürekli yeniden çizim yok (60 kare/s sabit, sekmeler boştayken sıfır DOM değişikliği). CI'daki görsel test sonucuna ayrıca bakmanızı öneririm.

## Bilimsel sınırlar (sayfada da yazılı)

- Kinematik model: dinamik ve çift kırınım, HOLZ ve Kikuchi çizgileri yok.
- Boş örgü bantlarında kristal potansiyeli sıfırdır, bant aralığı açılmaz.
- k-yolu BCT, RHL, monoklinik ve triklinik örgüler için henüz tanımlı değil; bu durumlarda bölge doğru çizilir ama yol etiketlenmez.
