body:
Adds device classes for two Xiaomi fans that currently fall back to generic handling.

### dmaker.fan.p39 (Xiaomi Smart Tower Fan)
- Power, fan level 1–4 (`fan:fan-level`) and stepless speed (`fan:speed-level`)
- Modes: Straight Wind / Natural Wind / Sleep
- Horizontal swing plus angle (30/60/90/120/150)
- Manual move left/right (`fan:motor-control`, write-only)
- Off delay (`fan:off-delay-time`, minutes), LED (`fan:brightness`), buzzer (`fan:alarm`), child lock

### xiaomi.fan.p85 (Mijia Smart Standing Fan Pro Slim)
- Power, fan level 1–4, stepless speed (`dm-service:fan-level`)
- Modes: Straight Wind / Natural Wind
- Horizontal swing plus included angle (30/60/90)
- Manual move left/right. This device has no step-move property, so it overrides `supportsHorizontalMove()`/`moveLeft()`/`moveRight()` to fire the `fan:turn-left` / `fan:turn-right` actions.
- Off delay (`delay:delay-time`), indicator light, buzzer, child lock

### Testing
Both fans ran on Homebridge 2.4.0 with homebridge-miot 2.0.0 over a local miIO connection, with `offDelayControl`, `moveControl`, `fanLevelControl` and `horizontalAngleButtons` enabled. I watched the device properties change for each control: modes, levels, swing, angle, off delay, LED and buzzer. Move left/right was confirmed physically, since `motor-control` is write-only and can't be read back.

### Not included: p85 "natural breeze scenes"
The Xiaomi Home app has eight scenes (Lakeside, Putting Green, Camping, …). Selecting one changes no readable property. The fan just steps `fan-level` over time. `dm-service:natural-list` (`a_b_c_d_e_f_g_h_i_j_k_l`) only changes when the scene order is edited in the app, so it looks like a display order, not a selector. Because of that, I didn't map the scenes.

body:
- Closes #4702
- Closes #4796

## Summary

Routes the role-delegation `Offer(CaseParticipantRole)` through the case's CASE_MANAGER: the Case Owner addresses it to the CASE_MANAGER only, which checks the sender, role and target, commits the Offer and forwards it to the target; the target acts only on the CASE_MANAGER's forward and answers the CASE_MANAGER. The CASE_MANAGER no longer accepts on the target's behalf or grants the role on Offer receipt. The trigger body now requires `role`, with no `CASE_MANAGER` default (#4796, maintainer-approved API change).

Issues: closed 2, opened 2 (#4796 separate-defect, #4814 separate-defect)

## Changes

- **`vultron/core/use_cases/triggers/actor.py`**: `SvcOfferCaseParticipantRoleUseCase` resolves the case and its CASE_MANAGER, raises `VultronNotFoundError` before building anything when no CASE_MANAGER resolves (PCR-08-011), and builds and queues the Offer `to: [case_manager_id]` through the shared `send_case_actor_activity` helper (`sender_side_bt`, PCR-08-001); a factory fault raises `VultronValidationError` with nothing queued. Queuing is part of sending it: the trigger previously persisted the Offer but never put it in any outbox, so nothing was delivered. It stays outside `SvcBTTriggerBase`, so `RoleOfferResult` keeps its shape (ADR-0110).
- **`vultron/core/use_cases/received/actor/case_participant_role.py`**: declares `SenderRule.to_case_manager(CASE_OWNER)` in place of the #4522 exemption (CM-33-002, CM-33-004); refuses a misaddressed copy at the door via the shared `unaddressed_copy_refusal` (HP-01-005); drops the `CVDRole.CASE_MANAGER` default for a missing role (CM-33-003); refuses an Offer naming no case after intake; reports a redelivered Offer `SKIPPED`.
- **`vultron/core/behaviors/case/offer_case_participant_role_received_tree.py`**: rebuilt on `create_receive_activity_tree` with the sender guard, the `RoleOfferAdmissibleNode` precondition guard, the guarded commit, a CASE_MANAGER-gated `ForwardRoleOfferToTargetNode`, and the answer in the participant-replica arm behind `IsRoleOfferTargetNode`. `GrantCaseParticipantRoleNode` leaves this tree (CM-33-001); the class stays for #4703, which composes it on the committed Accept.
- **`vultron/core/behaviors/case/nodes/role_offer_guard.py`** (new): `RoleOfferAdmissibleNode` refuses a missing role, `CASE_OWNER`/`CASE_MANAGER`, a non-participant target, a role the target already holds, and a target that is the case's CASE_MANAGER (CM-33-003, BT-17-008). A redelivery is an Offer whose id is recorded with the same role and target; an Offer reusing a recorded id for another role or target is refused (ID-02-001). A redelivery whose forward is already stored fails the guard and changes nothing; one whose forward is not stored (it failed after the commit) is admitted, so the commit reuses the recorded entry and the forward is built under its derived id.
- **`vultron/core/participants/role_offer.py`** (new): reads the ledger's `offer_case_participant_role` entries (`recorded_role_offer`, `entry_names_role_offer`) and derives the forward's id (`role_offer_forward_id`); #4703 can extend it for open-Offer reads. It and `ownership_offer.py` now share `sync_helpers.recorded_entries_for_case` rather than each scanning the ledger.
- **`vultron/core/behaviors/case/nodes/delegation.py`**: new `ForwardRoleOfferToTargetNode` (delegated authorship via `delegated_authorship`, `to: [target]`, `in_reply_to` = recorded Offer id, derived id for OX-06-002; a fault after the commit escapes as an internal error rather than reading as a refusal) and `IsRoleOfferTargetNode`; the answer base now addresses the CASE_MANAGER resolved from the case and fails before sending when none resolves; its CASE_MANAGER-only commit branch is removed, since the answer now runs only on a participant replica.
- **`vultron/core/ports/trigger_activity.py`**, **`vultron/adapters/driven/trigger_activity_adapter/actors.py`**: `offer_case_participant_role` takes `attributed_to`, `in_reply_to` and `id_` for the forward.
- **`vultron/core/use_cases/received/_bt_verdict.py`**: `role_offer_verdict` maps a run the guard flagged as a redelivery to `SKIPPED`, whether the guard stopped it or admitted it to finish the forward.
- **`vultron/core/behaviors/replica_emit_exemptions.py`**: the `offer-role` exemption's reason now says the answer runs only at the target and goes to the CASE_MANAGER.
- **`vultron/semantic_registry/actor.py`** and the regenerated `vultron/metadata/msm/occasions.yaml` / `docs/reference/messages/_occasions/*`: the Offer is sent to the case manager by the Case Owner; the Accept and Reject are sent to the case manager.
- **`vultron/wire/as2/vocab/examples/case.py`**, **`vocab_examples.py`**, `docs/reference/examples/*_case_participant_role.json`: examples route through the case actor; new `forward_case_participant_role.json`.
- **`vultron/core/use_cases/triggers/request_bodies.py`**, **`vultron/adapters/driving/fastapi/routers/trigger_actor.py`** (route description), `test/adapters/driving/fastapi/openapi_trigger_snapshot.json`: `OfferCaseParticipantRoleRequest.role` is required, with no `CVDRole.CASE_MANAGER` default (#4796: the CASE_MANAGER refuses that Offer, CM-33-003); snapshot regenerated, a missing role returns 422.
- **`specs/case-management.yaml`**: CM-33-003 adds a target that is the CASE_MANAGER itself to the refused shapes (see Spec amended); the learning that recorded the gap is removed.
- **Docs**: `docs/howto/activitypub/activities/role_delegation.md` (AC-7), `docs/reference/messages/case_management.md` Routing and Who may send bullets (AC-8; now also the CASE_MANAGER-target refusal), `role_delegation.md` also says the trigger request must name the role, `docs/reference/glossary.md` Role Delegation row (it still described offering the CASE_MANAGER role).
- **`vultron/core/use_cases/received/actor/accept_reject_case_participant_role.py`**, **`vultron/core/models/events/actor.py`**, **`vultron/wire/as2/extractor/_instances.py`**, **`vultron/core/behaviors/sync/nodes/role_grant_effect.py`**: docstrings and pattern descriptions no longer say the offering actor receives the answer or that the Offer tree grants the role.
- **`specs/sync-ledger-replication.yaml`**: SYNC-09-002's `verification:` drops the deleted CASE_MANAGER-answer test (the answer no longer runs at the CASE_MANAGER); no statement changed.
- **`test/architecture/test_ledger_event_types_are_replayed.py`**: `AWAITING_COMMIT` holds `accept_case_participant_role` and `reject_case_participant_role` for #4703, which commits them at the CASE_MANAGER; nothing commits them until then.
- **Tests**: `test_role_offer_routing.py` strict `xfail` marks on CM-33-001 to CM-33-004 removed (AC-6) and new cases for the forward's shape, redelivery, misaddressed copies, a CASE_MANAGER target, a non-target addressee and an Offer naming no case; the CM-33-005/006 `xfail`s stay, with reasons updated to what still fails. `test_delegation.py`, `test_case_participant_role.py` and `test_actor_triggers.py` updated for the new routing.

## Specs

Loaded (floor): CM-33-001, CM-33-002, CM-33-003, CM-33-004, CM-24-005, PCR-08-001, PCR-08-011, PCR-03-001, HP-01-006, HP-01-007, HP-01-008, BT-17-008, CLP-09-001, CLP-10-006, SYNC-09-002, OX-06-002, CM-02-016

author: thiagokimo
body:
## Summary

Steps 3 and 4 of moving the whole configuration to the dendritic pattern, following #17. Every `.nix` file is now a flake-parts module, except the generated hardware configurations and `lib/colors.nix`.

**Step 3: hosts with flake-parts, no `specialArgs` (`812023e`)**
- `modules/flake/hosts.nix` replaces `lib/builders.nix`. It builds `nixosConfigurations`, `homeConfigurations` and the checks for each host in `vars.hosts`, from the host's own NixOS module and the features it lists. It sets `networking.hostName` itself, and in Home Manager a new `host.name` option.
- Each `hosts/<name>/default.nix` is a flake-parts module, loaded with `import-tree`, that sets the new `vars.hosts.<name>.nixos` option. The `nixos-hardware` imports move there from the generated hardware configurations.
- The generated hardware files are renamed `_hardware-configuration.nix`. The underscore keeps `import-tree` from loading them.
- No module receives `specialArgs` any more:
  - `vars` and `inputs` come from the flake scope.
  - fastfetch imports `lib/colors.nix` directly, so `lib/default.nix` (`myLib`) is removed with the builders.
  - Noctalia finds the host's display through `host.name` instead of `hostname`.
  - `user` was passed but never read.

**Step 4: README (`b8e8169`)**
- The architecture text and diagram show `features/` and `hosts/` loaded by `import-tree`, the typed `vars` option and `modules/flake/hosts.nix`. A section on `hosts.nix` replaces the one on the old builders.
- The hosts section explains each host's own module and lists which features each host gets.
- Paths in the system, Nixvim and CLI sections point to `features/`, and the directory layout is redrawn.

## Testing

- The NixOS and Home Manager derivations for framework, t14 and t14s are identical to `main`, including t14s's `nix.conf`, so deploying restarts nothing.
- The list of checks and the flake outputs are the same as `main`.
- A misspelled feature still fails: "Host t14 lists unknown features: zhs".
- No file mentions `specialArgs` or `myLib`.

- `nix flake check --no-build` passes.
- `nix fmt -- --check .` passes.

body:
**Lane:** LW-1g, the launch session's /earn calculator. It implements hand-off Part A's "/earn Ready-Made Trip calculator" and F2 2b, built after CP-2 (R481) as the launch brief orders.
**Ledger:** `2026-10-16-lw1g-earn-calculator`. It stays `R?` until the post-merge stamp.
**No schema change, no migration.**
**Order:** this merges after #1481. It shares no files with it except `docs/DECISIONS.md` and `build.yml`, and main gets brought in under the ledger rule before it merges.

## What changed
- **Rate:**
  - `GET /api/fee-policies/keep-rates` (the public path `/earn` already reads) now also returns `readyMadePlatformRate`.
  - That value comes from `resolveReadyMadeTakeRate()`, the one function a Ready-Made purchase is charged by: the `ready_made_trip` band, with that function's own fallback. Nothing is typed.
  - A rate outside [0, 1) means no calculator.
  - Note: this adds fields to `earn-keep-rates.service.ts` (CP-2's file, since rebuilt by FE-2 on main), as the brief directs ("through the same public path"). It changes nothing in the existing fields.
- **Calculator** (`client/src/components/earn/ReadyMadeCalculator.tsx`, words and arithmetic in `client/src/lib/ready-made-calculator.ts`):
  - Heading: "Write it once, sell it again and again."
  - Two boxes, "Your price (USD)" and "Your guess: sales per month", both empty with no placeholder.
  - Results: "You keep $X per sale" and "At your guess: $Y a month", rounded to the cent once per sale.
  - Marketing's fixed label: "Your estimate, based on the numbers you entered. Not a prediction."
  - An empty or non-numeric box shows nothing, never $0.
  - Nothing is stored or sent.
  - No "typical", "average", "top experts", "passive income" or "make $" wording.
- **The $20 example line** (Leon, Oct 16, 2026: build it behind the flag, off by default, the amount from the `ready_made_trip` band):
  - The hand-off's line, "Example: you set a 3-day Ready-Made Trip at $20 and keep $X. The traveler pays $20."
  - Drawn only while `earn_ready_made_example_enabled` (seeded `false` by migration 381) is `"true"`. The keep-rates read carries it as `readyMadeExampleEnabled`; a missing row or a read error is `false`.
  - $X is worked out from the same rate the calculator uses: whole dollars print as "$17", anything else with cents. $20 is the example's price, not a fee.
- **Shown only** when the rate is usable **and** the launch market has at least one Ready-Made Trip on sale. That's checked against the public `/api/ready-made` feed, matched to `launch_market_slug` or its city name. So it's hidden in markets without Ready-Made Trips.

## Tests
- **`server/__tests__/earn-keep-rates.db.test.ts`** (E1–E4 are main's):
  - **E5:** the Ready-Made rate equals `resolveReadyMadeTakeRate()`; editing the `ready_made_trip` band moves it; the band is restored afterwards.
  - **E6:** the example flag is `false` for `"false"` and for any value other than `"true"`, and `true` only for `"true"`; the setting is restored afterwards.
- **`client/src/lib/__tests__/ready-made-calculator.test.tsx`:**
  - **C1:** both boxes start empty with no placeholder, no result is shown, and the label is exact.
  - **C2:** the kept amount follows the rate given, and an unusable rate gives nothing.
  - **C3:** a non-numeric box shows nothing.
  - **C4:** no average, typical or earnings-claim wording in the copy module, the component or the page.
  - **C5:** hidden without Ready-Made Trips in the launch market; the page mounts it only with a usable rate and a match, passes the flag, and never pre-fills a box.
  - **C6:** the example line is hidden by default and with the flag off; with it on, the exact line with $X from the rate ($17 at 15%, $16 at 20%, $17.50 at 12.5%); an unusable rate gives no example.
- **Local results:**
  - E1–E6 6/6 on two runs; the setting is left `false`.
  - C1–C6 10/10.
  - TypeScript 117 (the baseline), none in touched files.
  - The fee-literal gate and decision guards pass.

- [x] **CLAUDE.md delta:** none.
- [x] **Expired:** none.
- [x] **`superseded@<sha>`:** none.
- [x] **Ledger append:** `2026-10-16-lw1g-earn-calculator`.

author: zhouyanliang
body:
## Why

Studio's side panel becomes My Agent: the agent sessions on the person's own computer, opened beside whatever page is open. The session page, the new session and the list were laid out by the screen's width and navigated to `/agent-sessions/...`, so they could not live in another application's panel, and nothing told an application which sessions a record is tied to.

## What

- `@nocobase/app-plugin-agent-sessions/client/panel` exports `AgentSessionsPanel`: one session, a new session or the list, chosen by the host (`view`, `onViewChange`), with buttons between them and to the full page (`onFullScreen`), and the host's own buttons (`actions`). In the panel a new session and a session picked in the list open in place, a session's details open over the conversation, and a record tied to a session opens at its own `href`.
- The session, the new session and the list are laid out by their container's width (container queries named `agent-session`, 448 px) rather than the screen's, so the page itself looks as before and a narrow panel looks as a phone does.
- `attach` puts what the host attached, such as the record the panel was opened beside, in the shown draft once per `id`. It shows above the message, can be removed, and goes with the next message: an attachment with a `reference` as a `#` mention, one with `text` as text. `projectId` is the project a new session starts with.
- `GET /api/agentSessions/sessions?linked=<kind>:<refId>` lists the viewer's own sessions tied to one record, latest activity first; `useLinkedSessions(kind, refId)` reads it.

## Checks

`@nocobase/app-plugin-agent-sessions`: lint, typecheck, test (183, including the new panel and `linked` route tests), build. `validate-changesets`, `require-changesets`. Checked in Studio's browser: the panel beside a task, the task attached and sent as a mention, the new session tied to the task, the list at phone width.

body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes three unused-export findings in the dependency check after the MCP test-facade cleanup and Enterprise identity work.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior changes. Enterprise sign-in keeps its trusted-proxy and issuer checks, and MCP catalogs keep their current merge behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

These functions are live internal helpers, not dead implementations. Make them private to their owners, and move the MCP test's direct helper call through the existing combined runtime while preserving every assertion.

History and source audit found no lost trust check: #173513 introduced the Enterprise helpers together with their current caller in `createAuthenticatedGitHubIdentitySync`. Both HTTP profile resolution and WebSocket admission still use that entrypoint. It validates successful trusted-proxy authentication, the configured principal header, issuer host and account ID before accepting metadata. #174347 removed the MCP testing facade but retained production calls to the merge helper in catalog loading and peeking. Deleting these functions would remove required behavior.

## Evidence

- Before: `pnpm deadcode:dependencies` failed on exactly these three exports (78.78s). After: both dependency/unused-export scans pass (168.77s).
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/github-user-identity.test.ts src/gateway/github-user-identity.enterprise.test.ts src/gateway/github-user-identity.authority.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: all 97 tests pass (138.97s). This includes rejection of issuer mismatch, token authentication and invalid account IDs, profile persistence, public/Enterprise ID collision isolation, and the MCP safe-name/policy-tool contract.

The initial test-type command used invalid shorthand graph names and stopped before compilation; the corrected canonical graphs passed without configuration changes.
- `pnpm deadcode:exports` passes production and script scans but reports two unrelated full-tree namespace members: `shouldIgnoreBoundThreadWebhookMessage` (`preflightRuntime`) and `processDiscordMessage` (`processRuntime`) in the Discord message-handler modules. Those owners and all Knip configurations are unchanged from the base; this audit is not claimed green. The patch retains the same module import graph.

Parent: usaturn/agent-workspace#662（child `srw-verify-script`）

## 概要

公開 CI（`.github/workflows/ci.yml`）の `lint`・`test`・`docs`・`audit-and-package` と同じ検査を、ローカルで 1 回で実行する `scripts/ci/verify.sh` を追加する。変更はこのファイル（mode `100755`）だけ。

```bash
./scripts/ci/verify.sh [full]   # 省略時は full
```

- `full`: 下の 13 手順を順に実行し、最初に失敗した手順で止まり、その終了コードで終わる。すべて成功したときだけ 0
- それ以外（未知のプロファイル名・空文字列・引数 2 つ以上）: 標準エラーに理由と `usage:` を出し、何も実行せずに 64
- 標準入力を閉じ、`COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0` を設定するので、対話の確認で止まらない
- `sphinx-build` と `uv build` の出力は一時ディレクトリに置き、終了時（失敗・シグナルを含む）に消す。追跡対象のファイルと既存の `dist/` には触らない

| # | 手順 | CI のジョブ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `uv lock --check` | （準備） |
| 2 | `uv sync --locked --all-groups` | （準備。`lint`・`docs` の `uv sync --all-groups`） |
| 3 | `uv run --no-sync ruff check` | `lint` |
| 4 | `uv run --no-sync ruff format --check` | `lint` |
| 5 | `uv run --no-sync mypy src` | `lint` |
| 6 | `corepack yarn install --immutable` | `lint` |
| 7 | `corepack yarn lint` | `lint` |
| 8 | `corepack yarn test` | `lint` |
| 9 | `uv run --no-sync pytest` | `test`（実行している Python 1 つだけ） |
| 10 | `uv run --no-sync sphinx-build -W docs <一時ディレクトリ>/html` | `docs` |
| 11 | `uv audit --locked` | `audit-and-package` |
| 12 | `uv build --out-dir <一時ディレクトリ>/dist --clear` | `audit-and-package` |
| 13 | `uvx twine check --strict <一時ディレクトリ>/dist/*` | `audit-and-package` |

対象外: tox による複数版の実行（py311〜py313 は CI の `test` ジョブで確かめる）、CodeQL・zizmor、ブラウザを使う検査、CI の workflow から `verify.sh` を呼ぶこと、ほかのプロファイル。

## 設計の決定と理由

| 項目 | 決定 | 理由 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 手順の順 | 準備（lock の確認と sync）の後、CI のジョブの順（`lint` → `test` → `docs` → `audit-and-package`）にジョブ内の順を保つ | どのジョブの手順が失敗したかが CI の画面とそのまま対応する。`uv audit` を最初に置くと、外部の advisory の状態でコードの検査が 1 つも動かなくなる |
| 出力先 | `mktemp -d` の一時ディレクトリを `EXIT` の trap で消す | リポジトリの `dist/` を使うと `uv build --clear` が利用者の配布物を消す。`build/` に前回の出力が残ると sphinx の差分ビルドになり、CI の新しいビルドと条件が変わる |
| uv の実行 | 手順 2 の後は `uv run --no-sync` | 手順 2 で入れた環境を変えずに、全手順が同じ環境を使う |
| yarn | `corepack yarn …` | `package.json` の `packageManager`（yarn 4.17.0）を使う。PATH の `yarn` が corepack の shim でない環境に依存しない。`corepack enable` はグローバルな変更なのでしない |
| 対話の防止 | `exec </dev/null` と `export COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=0` | corepack は、`COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=1` の環境や古い版では、端末から未取得の yarn を使うときに確認を出す。標準入力を閉じれば、未知の確認でも止まらない。上書きする環境変数はこれだけで、uv の Python の選択は呼び出し元に従う |
| 引数 | 引数なしか `full` だけを受け付け、ほかは 64 | 呼び出し側の変数が空になった誤りを、`full` の実行で隠さない。文言は wabun-rst-ulint の `verify.sh` に合わせた |
| 作業ディレクトリ | スクリプトの場所からリポジトリの root へ `cd`（`CDPATH` を空にして） | 呼び出し元の cwd や `CDPATH` による取り違えを防ぐ |
| シグナル | HUP・INT・QUIT・TERM を trap して 128 + N で終わる。`passed` は最後の手順まで終えて終了コードが 0 のときだけ出す | 端末を閉じるなどで打ち切られた実行を、ログで成功と見誤らせない。一時ディレクトリも消す |
| テスト | pytest・bats は足さない | Issue の指定。挙動は使い捨ての worktree で実行して確かめた（下の「検証」） |

## 実行方式

単一のセッションで計画の Task を順に実行した（inline）。変更は 1 ファイルで、検証の Task はその成果物を順に使うため、Task を分けて並行に進める利点が無い。実装の後に、別のレビュー担当（読み取りのみ）が branch 全体をレビューし、指摘された 2 件（シグナルで打ち切られた実行の表示、`CDPATH`）を、失敗を再現する確認を先に作ってから直した。

## 検証

すべて head `5c366c7`（この PR の最終の commit）で実行した。ローカルは Python 3.14（`UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=system`・`UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=manual`）、uv 0.13.1、Node 24、corepack 0.36.0。

| 確認 | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| `.venv`・`node_modules` の無い新しい worktree で `./scripts/ci/verify.sh full </dev/null` | 終了コード 0。13 手順の見出しが順に出て `verify.sh: full passed`。pytest 245 passed、`yarn test` 342 pass、`sphinx-build -W` 成功、`uv audit --locked` 0 件、sdist・wheel の `twine check --strict` PASSED。実行の前後で `git status --porcelain` が同じ。gitignore 済みの `dist/` に置いたファイルは残る。一時ディレクトリは残らない |
| `./scripts/ci/verify.sh unknown`・`""`・`full extra`・`quick` | どれも 64。標準エラーに理由と `usage:`。一時ディレクトリ・`.venv`・`node_modules` を作らない |
| 端末（pty）から `docs/` で `../scripts/ci/verify.sh full`。呼び出し元が `COREPACK_ENABLE_DOWNLOAD_PROMPT=1` を設定し、`COREPACK_HOME` は空（yarn は未取得） | 終了コード 0、ダウンロードの確認は出ない。`docs/` は ignored なファイルを含めて変わらない。対照として、同じ条件でスクリプトを通さない `corepack yarn --version` は確認で止まる（`timeout` の 124）。標準入力を閉じることと環境変数の二重の防御の組み合わせで確かめた |
| 壊した写し: `src/sphinx_riddle_whisper/__init__.py` に未使用の `import os` | 終了コード 1。`ruff check` で止まり、後の手順を実行しない。`verify.sh: full failed (exit 1)` |
| 壊した写し: `docs/index.rst` に存在しない `:doc:` の参照 | 終了コード 1。`sphinx-build -W` で止まり、`uv audit` 以降を実行しない |
| 偽の `uv` を眠らせた実行に、プロセスグループへ HUP・INT・TERM・USR1 | 129・130・143・138 で終わり、どれも `passed` を出さず、一時ディレクトリを消す（レビューの指摘で直した。直す前の commit では HUP と USR1 で `passed` を出した） |
| `CDPATH` に `scripts/ci` を持つ別のディレクトリがある状態で `bash scripts/ci/verify.sh` | リポジトリの root で実行する（レビューの指摘で直した。直す前は別のディレクトリへ移って続けた） |
| `bash -n`、`shellcheck`（shellcheck-py） | 警告なし |
| 既存のローカルの検証（tox `py314,lint`、`sphinx-build -W`、`uv build`、`twine check --strict`、`yarn install --immutable`・`yarn lint`・`yarn test`）と `uv audit --locked` | 成功 |
| push の前の秘密検査（Gitleaks、既定の規則） | no leaks found |

公開 CI の必須チェックの結果は、この PR の checks を参照。

## 作業時間

着手から PR の作成まで約 40 分（2026-10-16 15:45Z〜16:25Z）。

| 作業 | 時間 |
| --- | --- |
| Issue・依存・競合の確認、作業場所の準備 | 約 5 分 |
| 設計と計画（設計の別の読み手による確認を含む） | 約 11 分 |
| 実装（`verify.sh`、引数の確認） | 約 3 分 |
| 受け入れの確認（新しい worktree、pty、壊した写し） | 約 4 分 |
| 全体のレビュー、指摘 2 件の修正と再確認 | 約 15 分 |
| 秘密検査、push、PR の作成 | 約 2 分 |

## マージ後

#51 の完了のコメントで、インターフェース `./scripts/ci/verify.sh [full]`（未知のプロファイルは 64、対話で止まらない）を固定する。登録の検証の入口の差し替えは usaturn/agent-workspace#667 で行う。

父eecd7d4唯一复现的两项GameTest失败、图形启动超时及约89.7GB重复日志耗尽磁盘证据保留；新HEAD通过不代表这些故障已修复。下一Review核对软件诊断范围与两处文字修正，正式放行仍需合法非作者审批。PR保持draft，未合main、未force push、未推进PR2/3/4。

## 前轮 FPS 交付（历史 eecd7d4）

关联 [ZER-1542](https://linear.app/zerodotsix/issue/ZER-1542)。仅补 PR1 报告和证据，不实施 cap/config、缓存或渲染优化，不合 main、不 force push。

前轮 HEAD [eecd7d45e7ab177e28296cced7df9e14810b0c8a](https://github.com/ZeroPointSix/sound-isolating-eraser/commit/eecd7d45e7ab177e28296cced7df9e14810b0c8a)，直接父提交 df9cb7a，同一分支 `docs/zer-1542-t2-pr1-perf-baseline`。新增/更新14份 docs/perf 文件：FPS 报告、8份原始CSV、全精度摘要/环境/生命周期及 README/runbook。版本维持同一PR已提升的 **0.14.2**；运行时、Mixin、CI未改。独立PR53保留，不在本轮推进。

## 客户端 FPS 补证

复用前轮成功 [run38992181049](https://github.com/ZeroPointSix/sound-isolating-eraser/actions/runs/38992181049)，不是本轮新采样。准确运行时 bb325dc，独立只读 harness37fdce8，原before世界来自既有制品12077285827。各120秒预热、约300秒正式窗口。

| 场景 | 平均 FPS | 1% low FPS | 秒数 | 全局实体 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| A1 驻足1玩家 | 11.046 | 7.930 | 300.005781 | 216至257 |
| B1 雨寂 | 9.725 | 7.243 | 300.039039 | 273至277 |

**这是优化前 llvmpipe 软件渲染诊断基线，不是硬件 GPU 基准、优化收益或独立审批。** 1280x720、Fancy、视距8/模拟6、FOV70、VSync关闭、上限260；由11,034个真实世界帧端点重算，不将上限当FPS。A1不等于0玩家服务端A。C最大位移10.016格、末图有遮挡；计数命令聊天叠层开销在全部窗口中保留。FPS与旧spark不是同步采样。

- [完整方法、站位、环境、限制与复算命令](https://github.com/ZeroPointSix/sound-isolating-eraser/blob/eecd7d45e7ab177e28296cced7df9e14810b0c8a/docs/perf/evidence/2026-10-17-client-fps-baseline.md)
- [永久原始CSV与全精度JSON](https://github.com/ZeroPointSix/sound-isolating-eraser/tree/eecd7d45e7ab177e28296cced7df9e14810b0c8a/docs/perf/evidence/client-fps-38992181049)
- [原制品12086881569](https://github.com/ZeroPointSix/sound-isolating-eraser/actions/runs/38992181049/artifacts/12086881569)，33,355,071 bytes，SHA256 `fea86cd8c6c0e314ea0cfc263bc4544d5511664a14ec0e741a141ebd6e21e4b0`，2026-11-16到期。含8张截图、原日志及复用快照。

## eecd7d4 验证（历史）

本地固定源码原Mixin脚本14/0 exit0；统计测试6/6；4帧CSV、1204行实体记录、4快照哈希及4次正常停服全部核验。提交范围14文件全部在docs/perf。新HEAD CI最终 **7 success / 1 failure**，不是8/8。默认434/434及清洁世界复跑434/434、FLARE_TWO_PROCESS_RESTART_PASSED已核验。Gravity飞翼入水步骤失败：water=false而deployed=true；后续motion-only通过不抵消失败。失败制品已校验，原始日志、八项终态和最小下一步见[本轮验证评论](https://github.com/ZeroPointSix/sound-isolating-eraser/pull/43#issuecomment-6229168250)。未放宽门禁、未盲目重跑取绿。

## 真实专服基线

生产代码来源 **bb325dc9ccf3d99565d8a1eedb7efee372fdcd45**，验证脚本 **013f97061b004248a2ca6510536daa35522807e8**。独立GitHub runner正常解析原依赖、构建生产reobf jar、安装官方Forge47.2.0并持续运行专服。不是仍等待foojay/TLS；没有修改证书校验/网络权限或借用高负载测试机。8次启动及正常stop/exit0均有记录；这是隔离专服，不是线上生产部署。

| B2永夜城市 | [Scz8kd12Ic](https://spark.lucko.me/Scz8kd12Ic) | 300.089s/6000 | 3.785/4.799 | 永夜8–11；全局252–255 |

MSPT为spark结束时last5m滚动摘要；每窗口实体CSV300行，按维度 `@e[distance=0..]`，子实体按实际YujiSummoner NBT计数。先预热120s，服务端/客户端固定不同物理核心；数据不是本次文档补充重新采出的。

[完整报告](https://github.com/ZeroPointSix/sound-isolating-eraser/blob/df9cb7acc7c9d8bfea86c0d933aacd6d3abb8586/docs/perf/evidence/2026-10-16-four-window-baseline.md) / [全精度JSON](https://github.com/ZeroPointSix/sound-isolating-eraser/blob/df9cb7acc7c9d8bfea86c0d933aacd6d3abb8586/docs/perf/evidence/2026-10-16-four-window-metrics.json) / [成功采集run38966307507](https://github.com/ZeroPointSix/sound-isolating-eraser/actions/runs/38966307507) / [原始制品12077285827](https://github.com/ZeroPointSix/sound-isolating-eraser/actions/runs/38966307507/artifacts/12077285827)。
制品68,723,631 bytes，SHA256 `e0a5505f00f9fd0aeccf85dedf7c4c9990a0a201c2f33bf14bb6755ad718de88`，回源确认未过期，2026-11-15到期；含profile、CSV、日志和8份世界快照。

## 验收边界

- **FPS已补独立窗口**：见上方软件渲染逐帧证据。旧20和新260均只是配置上限；硬件GPU、客户端sparkc/allocation尚缺，不把它们说成已完成。
- **C原基线采样前发生碰撞推位，未逐秒记录坐标**。四窗口是真实诊断负载，不是严格固定站位前后验收。单玩家/早期城市/16父实体不覆盖多人或晚期波次。
- 亮度读取不等于光照重建；setDirty不等于每tick写盘；BrickrotTrail已有192点边界、冷却表已有清理，不能统称永久增长。
- 客户端分配新增证据仍属静态候选，不声称JIT不能消除，也不换算成FPS/MSPT改善。
- 主线仍是先基线后独立PR2、PR3、PR4，不能将PR1报告或其他PR的结果混成整体GOAL已验收。

## Summary

Adapts `@huanlin/dsh-plugin-sleep` to dsh **0.2.0-rc.2 → 0.2.1-alpha.5** (version-jump edge, 1912 commits). Source code and `cordis.patch.yml` needed **zero changes** — the plugin's entire face is `inject: ['tools']` + `defineTool` + `ctx.tools.register`, all verified compatible against alpha.5 `packages/core/tools` by hand (shadow ambient types don't compile against the host, so typecheck alone is not a safety net).

## Changes

- **`package.json`**
  - `version` 0.2.1 → 0.2.2
  - peerDependencies: `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` / `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm` `^0.2.0-rc.1` → `^0.2.1-alpha.5`; `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `^4.0.1` → `~4.0.5-alpha.2` (J1-01 recipe B; prerelease hosts need same-tuple comparators)
  - dependencies: vendored `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` `^3.18.4` → `~3.18.5-alpha.2` — the J1-18 "vendored-as-dependency" escapee that the batch peer bump missed. `^3.18.4` refuses the prerelease host, and a 3.18.4/3.18.5-alpha.2 dual copy re-opens the global `Schemastery` namespace merge this plugin already hit in its 0.1.7 migration. Mirrors the official published pin (`3.18.5-alpha.2` is on npm; `~` also admits `3.18.5` final).
- **`src/types.d.ts`**: header note recording the alpha.5 verification (`defineTool` DSL unchanged — per-property `required: true`, `output.schema` as explicit `ObjectValueSchemaSpec`; `ToolRunContext` gains `deferContext`/`concludeTurn` additively; `schemas()` gains optional `scope`; `ContentBlock` text variant intact). Shadow signatures unchanged.
- **`docs/plans/2026-10-17-dsh-0.2.1-alpha.5-migration.md`**: full migration record (cards, 7-touchpoint scan, manual API diff table, junction probes, verification).

No `src/*.ts` or `cordis.patch.yml` changes; `lib/` rebuilt byte-identical (externals-only bundle — all `@deepseek-ai` imports external, resolved from the host module table at runtime).

## Cards hit

| Card | Verdict |
|---|---|
| J1-01 (peers/engines + prerelease trap incl. vendored peers) | hit — peers bumped + schemastery dependency aligned |
| J1-18 (Windows fleet mechanics; junction false-green) | hit — schemastery link resolved stale store `3.18.4`; range bump + relink now probes `3.18.5-alpha.2` |
| J1-14 (dsh-tools requires dsh-working-directory) | plugin side N/A (only `inject: ['tools']`); hand-rolled compositions mounting this plugin must ensure `dsh-working-directory` — shipped bundles already do |
| J1-02/03/04/05/06/07/08/09/10/11/12/13/15/16/17/19/20 | not hit — grep-verified zero references; no client half, no fixtures, no session persistence, no CLI scripts, no presets |

## Verification

- Junction probe (every `@deepseek-ai` link, absolute paths, layered attribution):
  - `cordis` → `dsh/vendor/cordis` ⇒ `4.0.5-alpha.2` ✅
  - `dsh-tools` → `dsh/packages/core/tools` ⇒ `0.2.1-alpha.5` ✅

  - `dsh-llm` → node_modules-unresolvable by design (ambient shadow + type-only import; host provides it in profiles)
- Baseline (pre-change): `pnpm test` **40/40 green — zero pre-existing failures**
- Post-change: `pnpm typecheck` ✅ · `pnpm test` 40/40 ✅ · `pnpm run build` ✅

author: quwisky
body:
## What

On phones, the room list no longer moves when the global banner slot settles after Rooms renders on a restart. The slot is decided before the live encryption status arrives, from what this device last needed, and the expected prompt holds its real space, hidden, until the status confirms it. This covers a prompt replacing the storage notice and a prompt arriving in an empty slot.

- **Press latch.** While any pointer is pressed (each finger is tracked, so lifting one of two keeps the press), `CapabilityStatusService` holds the slot and the encryption prompt it holds together, and applies any change on release. No banner swaps in or out, and the prompt never changes kind or height, under a tap in flight. A held prompt the live status no longer supports (for example a shown prompt whose status turns `ready`) becomes a hidden, inert placeholder of the same kind until release, so nothing stale stays visible, announced or clickable.
- **Forecast.** `TrustSlotForecastService` keeps an account-scoped device preference, `trinity.trust.slot-forecast`. It records which prompt this device last needed: `none`, `needs-setup`, `needs-recovery`, `needs-verification` or `setup-elsewhere`. The preference is private and excluded from config export.
- **Slot from the forecast.** While trust is unknown, the slot owner claims the slot from the forecast with the live priority rules. `deviceConfirmationGuard` loads the forecast before Rooms opens. An Account switch loads it too.
- **Hidden banner.** `trn-encryption-banner` renders only the prompt the slot owner holds (`bannerPrompt`), never the live status. It lays out a placeholder prompt inside a frame that is `visibility: hidden`, `aria-hidden="true"` and `inert`, and keeps its live region empty. When the live status confirms the prompt, the same banner node is revealed in place.
- **Journeys and docs.** New browser journeys cover the restart at 320 and 390 px, at 100% and 200% text, a restart at 390 px into an empty slot (persistent storage granted, so no notice), and a keyboard check. A paragraph in `encryption-and-trust.md` describes the forecast.

Closes #1433.

**Start-up cost.** On a guarded first navigation to Rooms or Settings, `deviceConfirmationGuard` waits for the stored forecast alongside its existing device check, for at most 300 ms (`FORECAST_HYDRATE_MS`), and then lets the route through whether or not the read finished. The read is one local device-preference lookup, so it normally finishes well inside that bound.

## Why

#1430 kept the notice-to-prompt swap from moving the list. Three cases in #1433 still moved it:

- taller encryption states taking the slot from the storage notice (18–66 px);
- 200% text, where the reserved height no longer matched the prompt;
- a prompt arriving in an empty slot.

All three happen because the slot changes after Rooms has drawn its first row. A forecast lets the slot hold the right banner, at its real height, from the first frame.

## How

- **One slot owner.** `CapabilityStatusService.bannerSlot` stays the only owner. While the live status is `unknown`, it decides from `slotTrust()`, which uses the forecast. It latches `{ slot, trust }` together behind the press and exposes the held prompt as `bannerPrompt: { kind, placeholder } | null` through `WORKSPACE_SYSTEM_STATUS`. `placeholder` is true for a forecast, and for a held prompt the live status does not (or no longer) confirm; a confirmed forecast is revealed on release, not under the press. The port defines its own `SlotForecast` union, so `application-workspace` does not depend on `data-access-trust`; the composition fails to compile if the two unions diverge.
- **The forecast never makes a decision.** `TrustService.status` and `TrustHealth` are unchanged. The device-confirmation gate, the encryption flows and Security settings never read the forecast.
- **When the forecast ends.** The forecast is only the stored value, used while the status is still unavailable, as at start-up. It ends:
  - when the live status arrives (it then governs);
  - at once when Trust reports a failure (a `trust:projection` problem, dismissed or not), so the "Encryption trust status is unavailable" notice and its Retry take the slot;
  - at a `FORECAST_HOLD_MS` backstop of 10 s, if the status neither arrives nor fails.

  A slow start keeps the forecast while the status is loading, up to the 10 s backstop, so a correct forecast is revealed in place rather than collapsing first. A stale snapshot (a read that failed mid-session) forecasts nothing, so mid-session failures show the notice as on main.
- **Lifetime.** The preference stays on the device after the Account is removed, like the other account-scoped device preferences; an installation reset removes it. `hydrateActive()` waits for an Account to become active when none is yet, still bounded by the guard's 300 ms. A run in which the Account changes records nothing.
- **Reveal in place.** The frame is a plain block `div`, so `trn-banner`'s container query measures the same width as before. Revealing removes the frame's attributes on the same node, so the box cannot change.

## Testing

Browser journeys ran against native Synapse with `--retries=0`. The GPU restart count stayed at 20.

**Failing first.** Tasks 2–4 were reverted in the working tree only (Task 1 kept), with the new journeys applied: **25 failed, 25 passed** (`--repeat-each=5`).
- All 20 restart journeys failed. The storage notice held the slot when the first row was drawn, instead of the prompt's space, so the slot went `status → encryption` instead of `forecast → encryption`. The 100%-text journeys failed on that sequence, not on movement: their row did not move. The 200%-text journeys also moved the list:
  ```
  320px, 100%: slot changes [status t=443 row=170.875] → [encryption t=1365 row=170.875]
  320px, 200%: [status row=340.5] → [encryption row=328.5]   (list moved 12 px up)
  390px, 100%: [status row=170.875] → [encryption row=170.875]
  390px, 200%: [status row=284.5] → [encryption row=328.5]   (list moved 44 px down)
  ```
- The 5 keyboard runs failed: `expect(locator('trn-encryption-banner [data-forecast]')).toBeAttached()`. There was no hidden prompt.
- The 25 existing first-sign-in journeys passed, as before.
- For this run only, the precondition that waits for the stored forecast was disabled. Without that, the committed journeys stop there on the reverted code, before they measure anything.

**With the fix.** `workspace/startup-banner.spec.mts --repeat-each=5`: **55/55 passed** (after the latest round). In every restart journey the slot went `forecast → encryption`, and the row and the prompt's box did not change:

| Width, text | Row top (px) | Prompt box, hidden → shown (px) | Root font |
|---|---|---|---|
| 320, 100% | 170.875 | 320 × 69.875 → 320 × 69.875 | 16px |
| 320, 200% | 328.5 | 320 × 195.5 → 320 × 195.5 | 32px |
| 390, 100% | 170.875 | 390 × 69.875 → 390 × 69.875 | 16px |
| 390, 200% | 328.5 | 390 × 195.5 → 390 × 195.5 | 32px |

The forecast held the slot from the first row, at about 440 ms, until the reveal, at about 1360 ms.

**Empty slot (persistent storage granted, 390 px, 100%).**
- On main's code (this branch's `libs/` reverted, the new journey kept, its stored-forecast precondition disabled for that run), the journey failed **5/5**. The slot went `[null] → [encryption]`, and the first row moved from 101 px to 145 px, 44 px down.
- With the fix it passed **5/5**: `forecast → encryption`, row at 145 px throughout, prompt box 390 × 44 hidden and shown.

**Keyboard.** While the forecast prompt is hidden:
- the prompt reads as hidden;
- Tab from the element just before it skips its action and lands on the next control, "Recent activity";
- after the reveal, Tab from the same place focuses "Set up".

**F1 regression.** These journeys from #1430 ran with `--repeat-each=5`, in the same batch as the startup journeys: **90/90 passed**.

author: jvhtec
body:
**High risk (database):** three new migrations, one of which merges a duplicate skill row in production data, plus a staffing-orchestrator change. Please give it a deliberate second read before merging.

## Summary
- [x] I described what changed and why.
- Affected route/feature: `/project-management` job cards, `/job-assignment-matrix` (job columns, required personnel, technicians, skills filter), Settings › skill catalog, the user "manage skills" dialog, the staffing orchestrator, and the per-minute scheduler crons.

Follow-up to #1007. Everything left from that session goes into this one PR.

**1. Staffing campaigns stop once their job is over** (`supabase/functions/staffing-orchestrator`)
- Each tick stops an active campaign, with a `staffing_campaign_events` row, when its job:
  - is missing,
  - is cancelled (`cancelado`/`cancelled`),
  - is marked complete (`completado`/`completed`), or
  - has an `end_time` that has passed.
- Before this, past campaigns stayed `active` forever. Every tick rewrote their role rows, which caused write churn and realtime traffic.
- Role rows are now written only when a counter, stage or wave changed.
- `campaignClosureReason` / `campaignRoleChanged` live in `orchestrationUtils.ts`, and the writes in `campaignTickWrites.ts`, which keeps `index.ts` within its file-size budget.

**2. Idle scheduler ticks skip early** (`20261016150000_skip_idle_scheduler_ticks.sql`)
- `festival.feed.tick` returns early unless a subscription with stages has artists or shifts within Madrid today ±2 days.
- `programa.feed.tick` returns early unless a job overlapping now ±2 days has an approved or final Hoja de Ruta programme.
- `invoke_staffing_sweeper` returns early unless an active campaign is due.
- The guards run before the pg_net call, so idle minutes no longer make an HTTP round-trip to an edge function.

**3. Job cards and the matrix stay live**
- `useJobScopedRealtime` goes through the unified subscription manager.
  - Each change refreshes only the affected job's queries, throttled per key on the leading edge.
  - It is used by `useJobCardsRealtime` for folders, required roles, tasks, artists and rider files, tour documents, transport requests and items, logistics events, WhatsApp groups and requests, and calculator defaults.
- `useMatrixJobsRealtime` covers:
  - job columns (`jobs`, `job_departments`, `job_date_types`): a newly created job appears without a reload;
  - required personnel (open-slot badges and the staffing summary);
  - technicians and fridge state. This replaces two raw channels, `rt-technician-fridge` and `rt-matrix-profiles`.
- `CreateJobDialog` invalidates the card and matrix job lists after a create.
- `20261016160000_publish_job_surface_tables.sql` publishes the 10 tables those surfaces read but that never sent events.

**4. Skills: real catalog, per-department creation, live everywhere**
- **Matrix skills filter:**
  - It reads the active catalog through the shared `useActiveSkills` query (`['skill_catalog','active']`) instead of hardcoded lights/sound presets.
  - It lists every skill once, ignoring case, with Spanish category headings: the selected department first, then General, then the rest.
  - It adds a search box and matches selections case-insensitively.
- **Settings › skill catalog:**
  - Department management could already create skills only in their own categories plus General. This now has pgTAP coverage.
  - A name that already exists in any case is rejected before the insert.
  - Duplicate (23505) and RLS (42501) rejections are explained in Spanish, and categories are labelled in Spanish.
- **Manage-skills dialog:** it reads the shared live catalog and offers every skill the profile lacks. Before, sound profiles could only be given sound skills.
- **Realtime:** `useSkillCatalogRealtime` (settings, the profile picker) and a matrix source keep `skill_catalog` and `role_skill_mappings` live.
- **`20261016170000_merge_case_duplicate_skills.sql`:**
  - It merges skills whose names differ only in case and makes `lower(name)` unique.
  - It publishes `skills` and `role_skill_mapping` to realtime.
  - On production this keeps the `PA` row (54 holders), moves the 6 holders of `pa` onto it (none held both), deletes `pa`, and renames the kept row to `pa`. I checked this with a read-only query; `role_skill_mapping` already matches case-insensitively.

## Risk Assessment
- [x] I assessed functional, data, and deployment risk.
- Risk level: high (database migrations, including one data merge)
- Main risks:
  - **Skill merge is data-changing and cannot be undone by a revert.** It only affects the `PA`/`pa` pair; holders are kept, and no technician loses a skill.
  - **Campaign closure:** a campaign whose job is over, cancelled or complete becomes `stopped`. A past job will not restart its campaign; start a new one if needed.
  - **Realtime load:** 12 more published tables (10 job-surface tables plus `skills` and `role_skill_mapping`). All are low churn and covered by RLS SELECT policies, so deliveries respect row visibility.
  - **Scheduler guards:** if a guard is wrong, a feed tick is skipped while it shouldn't be. Each guard's conditions mirror what the edge function would select, and pgTAP covers them.
- [x] If this touches database (migrations/RLS/grants/RPC/SQL functions) or money (timesheet/rates/payroll) paths, I flagged it high-risk and confirmed compensating scrutiny per `docs/release/production-release-checklist.md` (CodeRabbit fully resolved + a deliberate second read — this is a solo-maintainer repo, there is no CODEOWNER/two-approver gate).

## Impact Checklist
- [x] Migration impact assessed: three additive migrations. The only data change is the skill merge above, and there are no schema changes to existing columns.
- [x] Realtime/subscription impact assessed: all new subscriptions go through `UnifiedSubscriptionManager`, with route-owned cleanup and leading-edge coalescing. No new raw channels; two raw matrix channels were removed.
- [x] RLS/security impact assessed: no policy or grant changes. I verified the per-department `can_manage_skill_category` results for each department's manager (read-only).
- [x] Performance impact assessed: fewer orchestrator writes and fewer idle pg_net calls. Refreshes are throttled per job key, and matrix cell data is untouched (rendering contract kept).

## Test Evidence
- [x] I ran relevant tests and confirmed expected results.
- Commands executed:
  - `npm run lint`: 0 errors
  - `npm run typecheck`: exit 0
  - `npm run lint:functions`: 0 errors
  - `npm run governance`: exit 0. The lint-warning baseline was rewritten with reductions only (`no-explicit-any` −1).
  - `npm run ci:db:migrations`: "OK: 268 Supabase migrations have unique ordered timestamps."
  - `npm run test:critical`: 29 files / 144 tests and 11 files / 71 tests passed
  - `npm run test:run`: 548 files passed (11 skipped); 3,755 tests passed (95 skipped)
  - `npm run build`: exit 0
  - `npm run budget:bundle`: exit 0
  - `npm run test:e2e`: not run locally; runs in CI.
- Results: all of the above pass. New tests:
  - Vitest:
    - `orchestrationUtils.test.ts` (closure reasons, role change detection)
    - `useJobScopedRealtime.test.tsx` (scoping, throttling, prefix fallback, cleanup, matrix and skill-catalog sources)
    - `SkillsFilter.test.tsx`
    - `ProfileSkillsEditor.test.tsx`
    - `SkillRoleMappingManager.test.tsx` (duplicate guard, Spanish RLS error, catalog invalidation)

author: lunarchy107
body:
## Problem

`msync_wait_multiple()` registers the thread with the wineserver's msync thread for every object, then spins until the server answers. If an object becomes available during that spin, the client returns early without telling the server. The server still processes the registration and, when nothing is signaled yet, adds the thread to each object's waiter list. Nothing removes those nodes until the object is signaled.

On an object that is rarely signaled (a quit event, say) every lost race adds another node for the same thread. Under load the 524,288-node pool runs out, the server prints `msync: warn: node memory pool exhausted` on **every** further allocation and falls back to `malloc`, and the wineserver keeps growing.

## Fix

`add_tid()` in `server/msync.c` skips a thread that is already on the object's list, so an object holds at most one node per thread. One node is enough to wake the thread; a stale one can still cause a spurious wake later, as today, and the wait loop already retries on those. The pool warning prints once.

The client (`dlls/ntdll/unix/msync.c`) is unchanged on purpose. Unregistering from the client on every early return also stops the leak, but in my testing that version left a Unity game (Endfield in this case) ignoring keyboard and mouse under MSync, so I kept the fix on the server side.

## Testing

`tests/fixtures/msync-wait-stress.c` (new) reproduces the leak: a worker sets an auto-reset event in a loop while the main thread waits on {quit, work}. A second thread pair measures how long a signaled wait takes to wake. Build and run instructions are in the file.

| | wineserver over 30 s | pool warnings | wake latency p50 / p99 / max |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 18 → 54 MB | 5.2 M | 0.16 / 0.26 / 86 ms |
| after | no growth | 0 | 0.009 / 0.04 / 0.15 ms (15 s run) |

Message-queue waits (`MsgWaitForMultipleObjects` + `PostThreadMessage`) and alertable waits show the same pattern.

- The full series (44 patches + this one) applies cleanly to CrossOver 26.3 with `git apply`; no other patch touches `server/msync.c`.
- `tests/test-msync-waitall.py` still passes (11/11).
- Tested on an Apple M1, macOS 26.6.2, **in a full CrossOver 26.3 Wine build used as a Sikarugir engine, not in CrossOver itself**: the stress test above, and about 30 minutes of Endfield (Steam version) with MSync on, input working. I don't have CrossOver, so the patched-CrossOver path is untested beyond applying the series.

## Contributing

Done with Claude Opus 5.5's assistance; I checked the results on my own machine.

author: amatsuda
body:
## Summary

`Dir[*patterns]` with a splat whose length is known only at run time did not compile:

```ruby
class Watcher
  def initialize(globs) = @globs = globs
  def watched = @globs ? Dir[*@globs] : []
end
# error: passing 'sp_PolyArray *' to parameter of incompatible type 'sp_RbVal'
```

There are two causes:

- **The analyzer splits by length.** It dispatches a splat of unknown length on its length, against the arity it knows for `glob`: a pattern and an optional flags argument. With a single element, the spread array went to the one-pattern arm as its path. With two elements, the arm took them as (pattern, flags), and two boxed patterns fell through to "undefined method 'glob'". More than two raised ArgumentError. `Dir[]` takes any number of patterns.
- **The emitter has no splat arm.** When the splat was kept, as it is when a user `[](*args)` stops the dispatch, the one-argument arm received the `SplatNode` and emitted it as a single path.

The fix covers both:

- In `analyze.c`, a splat into `Dir[]` or `Dir.glob` is kept whole when its length is not static, as `File.join(*parts)` already is.
- In `codegen_call_module.c`, the glob arm handles a splat, or more than one positional argument, by gathering every pattern into one list and handing it to the existing `sp_dir_glob_multi`. A trailing Integer flags argument or a keyword keeps the arms that were already there.

## Test

`test/dir_glob_splat_patterns.rb`: `Dir[*@ivar]` holding two patterns, nil (guarded), one pattern and a bare String, plus `Dir[a, b]` and a literal splat. The tests that call `Dir[` / `Dir.glob` or `File.join(*` (16), and every test named for splats (223), give the same results as on master.

author: slabbdev
body:
## What

New ADR 026, docs-only. Makes **admissions** (semantic promotions) first-class sealed events — the contract for `admission/0.1`, `check_admission_basis`, and the SCAR-BENCH admission axis.

## Source

You-An Lin, *"Capability Is Not Authority: Semantic Ownership Architecture for Persistent Conversational Agents"* — [DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23315265](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23315265) (2026-10-12, CC BY 4.0), fourth independent arrival in this corridor after SCAR (Randal), W231 (Mike Mol), and this journal — and the first at the **authority** half (who was entitled to originate the act) where the ladder so far covers the **witness** half (who wrote it). Paper I (23171351) left control and ownership questions out of scope; Paper II is that scope.

The load-bearing finding (§6.3): a live agent correctly attributed foreign history while **using it** — attribution correct, admission invalid, every output-level metric green. Check-vs-proof, one floor up.

## Decision summary

1. `admission/0.1` receipt: `{actor, source, transition, basis, decision, participation_ownership, scope}` — transitions named after Lin's four invalid promotions (`visibility→admission`, `capability→move`, `relevance→payload`, `style→stance`); basis = independent (instruction ref / prior receipt seq / scope grant), never presence-relevance-plausibility.
2. `admitted | denied | admission_undecidable` — undecidable never clean; skipped check = `admission_check_not_run` (ADR 019 lineage).
3. `participation_ownership ∈ {same, foreign, shared}` — FFPO guard as field discipline: a receipt proves an earlier actor's decision, never the citing actor's autobiography.
4. `check_admission_basis`: foreign-sourced payload content without an admitted receipt reads `admission_gap` (receipt_gap, one transition deeper).
5. SCAR-BENCH admission axis per Lin §6.3 — vary admission rights and actor identity at fixed task; grade receipts of the PATH, never the answer text. His ceiling-parity null (§6.1–6.2) is the Level-0 lesson restated by a fourth team.

## Scope

Contract only — schema, reconciler check, and bench fixtures land in 0.22.0. Docs change carries no code risk; the required checks should be a formality.

Credit: Lin, CC BY 4.0, cited inline with both DOIs.

author: andrescmg06-hue
body:
## Qué cambia

Tres fallos que se encontraron probando en un Redmi Note 13 (Android 15, HyperOS 2.0), más el endurecimiento y los dos huecos que salieron de la prueba en emulador:

- **Reabrir rápido una app bloqueada:** ya vuelve a bloquear (la visita se decide con toda la secuencia de eventos, no con el último; la pantalla de bloqueo se redibuja si desaparece).
- **Regla nueva con la app ya abierta** (bloqueo, horario o límite): se evalúa en cada latido de reglas y bloquea sin cerrar la app; si la regla se quita, desaparece el bloqueo.
- **Con NetProtect cerrada:** los servicios ya no se paran al cerrar la pantalla; `START_STICKY`, receptor de arranque y `SyncWorker`/`EnforcementWatchWorker` como vigilantes.
- **T5:** el backend rechaza con el 404 uniforme los envíos de un dispositivo sin vínculo activo (así el teléfono detecta una desvinculación con la app cerrada); cerrar sesión borra vínculo y cachés; un fallo pasajero del Keystore ya no cierra la sesión.
- **T6:** pide «Permitir todo el tiempo» (decisión del dueño, revierte los Sprints 13/14) para que la ubicación revive tras la muerte del proceso.
- **T7:** el servicio de reglas envía el latido y la sincronización de apps/uso con la app cerrada (antes solo con la pantalla abierta).

Detalle y decisiones: `docs/sprint-73.md`. Evidencia con comandos y salidas reales: `docs/sprint-73-evidence.md`.

## Verificado

author: andreas-froyland
body: Closes #462 ## Approach Posted on the issue first. A Registry edit becomes active without a manual step when the fetched, valid candidate differs from the active revision only in `RegistryType`/`RegistryEntry` resources. The policy lives next to activation in `fleet-application/src/source.rs` and goes through the same authorized, serialized, audited path (`activate_as`). - **System principal**: the audit actor is `system:fleet-controller` (the actor skill-catalog seeding already uses). The authorizer decides for the controller's internal caller principal, as the fetch executor and Lab sweeper do, because `LanAllowAllAuthorizer` only knows LAN/Tailscale principals. The audit event carries the commit SHA, the triggering fetch operation, and per-kind `+added/-removed/~changed` counts; never resource contents. - **Registry-only**: candidate resources vs the active snapshot per (kind, id). No active revision, an empty diff, or any non-Registry change means the candidate waits. An auto-activation failure never fails the fetch. - **Settings**: no settings store existed, so migration 0055 adds a STRICT `controller_settings` table behind a `SettingsPort`. `GET/PUT /api/v1/desired/settings`, `fleetctl desired settings [set ...]`, and a self-contained Registry block in the Desired state settings section. Read needs `source.fetch`, write needs `source.activate` (existing catalog entries; the pinned catalog count is unchanged), each write audited before it lands. - **Periodic fetch**: `FLEET_DESIRED_FETCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (off by default, minimum 30). `SourcePoller` resolves the remote HEAD (`git ls-remote`) and queues the ordinary `source.fetch`; it skips while any `source.fetch` is pending or running and retries failed ones. - **Fetch-now**: `POST /api/v1/desired/fetch` already exists; documented for webhooks rather than duplicated. - **CI workflow**: `docs/guides/registry-validate.workflow.yml` plus `docs/guides/registry-workflow.md`, written against the planned `fleetctl registry validate` (FM-1013). ## Changes - `fleet-application/src/source.rs`: policy, diff, settings, `auto_activate`. - `fleet-storage-sqlite`: migration 0055 and `SettingsPort` impl. - `fleet-api`: settings endpoints; OpenAPI and generated client regenerated. - `fleet-controller`: executor reports `autoActivation`; `source_poller.rs`; wiring. - `fleet-provider-git`: `resolve_head`. `fleet-config`: the interval setting. - `fleetctl`: `desired settings`. - `apps/web`: `RegistrySettings.vue` embedded in the Desired state section (one import and tag, to stay clear of the FM-1001 Provider accounts section). - Docs: desired-state architecture, deploy README, the guide and workflow example. ## Verification Commands: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --all-features`, `cargo xtask verify` (includes web lint, typecheck, tests, build), all passed. New tests: mixed revision not auto-activated, Registry-only revision activated with audit actor and counts only, invalid revision never activates, auto-activate off keeps it manual, first activation manual, settings authorization and audit, poller serialization and retry, config floor, fleetctl parsing, web component and workflow-doc checks. Screenshots from an isolated controller (placeholder data only), Settings > Desired state > Registry: ![dark desktop defaults](https://github.com/Frogbyte-io/fleet-manager/blob/c7a1ae1e5bc85a4e8eee30f00d6f97934f08a7a2/pr-fm-1014/registry-settings-defaults-dark-desktop.png?raw=true) ![light desktop defaults](https://github.com/Frogbyte-io/fleet-manager/blob/c7a1ae1e5bc85a4e8eee30f00d6f97934f08a7a2/pr-fm-1014/registry-settings-defaults-light-desktop.png?raw=true) ![dark narrow defaults](https://github.com/Frogbyte-io/fleet-manager/blob/c7a1ae1e5bc85a4e8eee30f00d6f97934f08a7a2/pr-fm-1014/registry-settings-defaults-dark-narrow.png?raw=true) ![light narrow defaults](https://github.com/Frogbyte-io/fleet-manager/blob/c7a1ae1e5bc85a4e8eee30f00d6f97934f08a7a2/pr-fm-1014/registry-settings-defaults-light-narrow.png?raw=true) ![changed through the UI, with the fleetctl equivalent](https://github.com/Frogbyte-io/fleet-manager/blob/c7a1ae1e5bc85a4e8eee30f00d6f97934f08a7a2/pr-fm-1014/registry-settings-changed-dark-desktop.png?raw=true) ![persisted after reload, dark](https://github.com/Frogbyte-io/fleet-manager/blob/c7a1ae1e5bc85a4e8eee30f00d6f97934f08a7a2/pr-fm-1014/registry-settings-persisted-dark-desktop.png?raw=true) ![persisted after reload, light narrow](https://github.com/Frogbyte-io/fleet-manager/blob/c7a1ae1e5bc85a4e8eee30f00d6f97934f08a7a2/pr-fm-1014/registry-settings-persisted-light-narrow.png?raw=true) Not verified: the T3 browser tools were unavailable, so screenshots were captured with headless Chromium (Playwright). Console showed two 503s per page from other settings endpoints not wired in the isolated controller; none from the new endpoints. The narrow layout clips long text at the right edge in the existing Desired state section too (pre-existing). The webhook path and periodic fetch against a live remote were tested with a local repository only; the CI workflow cannot run until `fleetctl registry validate` (FM-1013) exists. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic A fetched, valid revision that changes only Registry resources now activates without a manual step when `registry.autoActivate` is on, through the same authorized, serialized, audited activation path. Previously every valid candidate waited for explicit activation. The step is compare-and-set: within one serialized transaction the controller re-checks the active revision and re-reads the setting before switching, so a concurrent activation is never clobbered, and a failure never fails the fetch. A rollback puts auto-activation on hold until a manual activation releases it. **Settings and API** - Adds a STRICT `controller_settings` table (migration 0055) plus `GET/PUT /api/v1/desired/settings`, `fleetctl desired settings`, and a Registry settings section in the console UI; reads need `source.fetch`, writes need a new `source.settings` permission, and every write is audited. - Adds `registry.changeMode` (`direct` or `pull-request`) as fleet-managed guidance; the repository host's branch protection is what actually enforces it. - Auto-activation now requires the candidate commit to be a descendant of the active commit, and changed files are classified by document kind — not just assumed Registry-only from the diff. Git operations run with process-group timeouts, and file comparison is bounded (1 MB per file, 500 files). **Fetching and CI** - Adds an optional periodic fetch behind `FLEET_DESIRED_FETCH_INTERVAL_SECONDS` (default off, minimum 30): the poller resolves the remote HEAD and queues the ordinary `source.fetch`, skips while a fetch is pending or running, and retries failed ones. - Adds a Registry workflow guide and an example GitHub Actions workflow that validates Registry changes on every pull request; both reference `fleetctl registry validate`, which lands separately in FM-1013. Written for commit d4b456fb85cb66236d86b05043d2e6df42ca64ac. Summary will update on new commits.

author: kevmo314
body:
CI wall time per PR goes from about 9.5 minutes (567, 559 and 629 s on the last three runs on main and PRs) to 3.5 minutes (212 and 210 s on this PR's two runs). The main e2e shard used to run about 1,450 s of scenarios in 4 lanes, finishing in about 445 s, while recovery finished in 60 s. CI now runs a pr shard, which is main plus recovery, split four ways with e2e.py --split. The splits are balanced from a COST table rebuilt from measured CI times (the old table left exec_background, arrival_overtaken, reconcile_kill and exec_pause_grace at the 2 s default). Each split's e2e step takes 97 to 121 s, and each split builds only the templates its scenarios use. The root networking tests now run in the check job: they are built as the runner's user and run under sudo through cargo's runner. That takes 35 s and an apt install off every e2e job. I also measured a thin-LTO release build at about half the fat-LTO time but kept the shipped profile.

Slow scenarios got faster without changing what they check. exec_background goes from 152 to 106 s: it arms the sweeper knob at the default wait at the start, so sweeps already come every second when the wait is shortened, and it starts the stalled client first. Its pause is 12 s instead of 20 s, still longer than the 8 s wait. exec_pause_grace goes from 55 to 41 s: a 27 s pause still passes the 30 s grace on the wall clock. arrival_log goes from 12 s to 0.5 s: it backdates the logs instead of sleeping out the 5 s grace.

Removed scenarios: gen_zero is covered by forged_peer, which already sent the gen-0 arrival and now also sends the route message without a generation. quarantine_reboot_ls is covered by resume_mark_fails, which runs the same faults and reboot and now also checks that ls lists the VM as suspended after the reboot. Scenarios go from 180 to 178 (PR CI runs 162 of them plus the 7 cases). Also removed from faults.py: the dead FAULTS tuple, a shadowed children(), the no-op skippable(), and 75 trailing cleanup() calls that the runner already does. There is a new name_free() helper, used by forged_peer, nothing_left and unlend_retry.

Removed Rust unit tests: uffd remove_during_fetch_skips_the_copy is covered by install_runs_past_partial_copies_eexist_and_discards and remote_accounting_adds_up. template rehash_is_remembered_across_opens is covered by stamps_written_back_elsewhere_spare_a_rehash. compat older_metadata_cannot_silently_skip_new_checks is covered by host_cache_reprobes_corrupt_and_incomplete_entries. Two pairs were merged into table-driven tests, shared helpers went into several test modules, and redundant TempDir removals are gone. host.rs is untouched. Unit tests go from 544 to 539. Test code goes from 25,116 to 24,881 lines: faults.py and e2e.py from 10,333 to 10,243, and Rust test code from 14,783 to 14,638.

Flakes: the three root networking tests now hold a shared lock. Run in parallel, one test's fork inherited another's /dev/net/tun descriptor and kept the tap attached, so TUNSETIFF failed with EBUSY. unlend_retry now waits until B's aborted arrival has given up the name before each retry.

Closes #552. Closes #559.

author: arnaudmaillet
body:
Closes #1296 (follow-up of #1271). Base develop, not stacked. One commit: 4c89f3cb.

## Owner decisions (2026-10-16)
- **10 cards at most per row** (`PostShelfSection.rowLimit`), the default for the model and the shelf.
- **Each row ends on a chevron card**: narrow (56pt), on a ground, no words (`ShelfViewAllCell`). It is sized through the flow layout's delegate and is as tall as the row. It is the shelf's "View all": it runs the title's action, and it is drawn only while the title has one.
- **An empty shelf disappears** (unchanged).

## Loading skeleton
`isLoading` (and `Model.isLoading`) draws the title over a row of `SkeletonBoneView` cards, at the media cards' size and gap, until posts land. A shelf that loads nothing then disappears.
- **For You**: until its Following state leaves `.loading`.
- **Place page**: until the place's posts land.
- **Search/hashtag lead row**: while its posts hydrate.

## Also
`PostSetSurface`'s lead title, and so its chevron card, acts only once the host sets `onLeadRowTitleTapped`; before this, the closure was installed unconditionally.

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Every host draws at most 10 cards per row: `ShelfHostsTests` (For You, place page, lead row) and `PostShelfSectionTests.aRowDrawsTenCardsByDefault`.
- [x] Each row ends on the chevron card, which runs the title's action, on every host:
  - `eachRowEndsOnTheChevronCardRunningTheTitlesAction` checks the narrow width, the row's height and that it opens no post;
  - `ShelfHostsTests` checks it on each host.
- [x] A loading shelf shows the skeleton under its title, at the media row's height: `aLoadingShelfShowsItsTitleOverSkeletonCards`. For You, the place page and the lead row show it until their posts land (`ShelfHostsTests`).
- [x] An empty shelf is zero tall (`anEmptyShelfIsZeroTall`, plus the loaded-nothing case).

## Verification
- Feed: 1810 tests green.
- Release build (CI's command): green.
- Simulator, `#foodie`: the Recent row ends on the chevron card, and a tap pushes the Recent list.
- The skeleton could not be filmed: under `-mock-latency` the whole sign-in waits too. It is pinned by tests.

author: koraydozdemir-commits
body:
## Problem
The Browser page is served at `/`, but the proxy service worker is scoped to `/frog/ixl/`. Calling `navigator.serviceWorker.ready` from `/` waits for an active worker associated with the current page, so it can wait forever. The address stays on a blank iframe and the status never advances.

## Fix
- Show startup progress before registering the worker.
- Wait for the `ServiceWorkerRegistration` returned by `register()` to activate instead of waiting on the out-of-scope global `navigator.serviceWorker.ready` promise.
- Add a bounded timeout and clear error messages for unsupported browsers and activation failures.

## Validation
- `node --check proxy/public/app.js`
- `git diff --check`
- Ran the proxy locally and loaded `https://www.google.com/` through the Browser iframe. Google rendered its homepage and cookie consent prompt inside the proxied frame; the Browser status reached `Ready`.

author: musthaf-bughunter
body:
The dashboard's `GET /profiles/new` handler passes the `service` and
`namespace` query parameters straight into the ServiceProfile
text/template and into an unquoted `Content-Disposition` filename. A
link such as

    /profiles/new?namespace=default&service=x%3B%20filename*%3DUTF-8''run.sh%0A---%0AapiVersion:...%0Akind:%20ClusterRoleBinding...

returns a download whose body contains attacker-supplied YAML documents
(for example a ClusterRoleBinding to cluster-admin) next to the
ServiceProfile, and whose `filename*` parameter overrides the intended
`<service>-profile.yml` name. The dashboard only checks the Host header,
so a top-level navigation to the port-forwarded dashboard is enough to
trigger the download.

`linkerd profile --template` already rejects these values by requiring
the service to be a DNS-1035 label and the namespace a DNS-1123 label
before calling the same renderer. Apply the same checks in
handleProfileDownload and return 400 when they fail.

Validation: added TestHandleConfigDownloadInvalidParams, which fails on
main (200 with the injected header and body) and passes with this
change. `go test ./web/...` and `go vet ./web/...` pass.


Signed-off-by: mushtaf saheb <musthaf@medios.digiscrypt.com>

author: debens
body:
`🟠 risk: medium (author call, no review)` · `⏱ review: ~15 min` **In short:** pages load faster and stay usable while they load. ### Why this matters Each page waited on a chain of steps that could have run at the same time. Some checks also ran twice, once for the page frame and once for the page. The database is a network hop away, so every extra step adds a delay you can feel. ### What changes for you - **Checks run once per page load**, not twice. - **Steps run side by side** instead of one after another. The security check still has the final say: nothing is shown until it passes. - **A contact record appears straight away**, and its notes and properties fill in a moment later. - **Every section shows a placeholder while loading**, instead of a blank "Loading" screen. - **Less is sent to the browser.** Two forms no longer download a 428 KB security library they never used. Branch dropdowns no longer receive staff names and email addresses they do not show. Contact searches fetch 20 rows instead of 100. Nothing about who can see what has changed. ### How to check it works 1. Sign in and open a contact record. 2. The record should appear first, with notes and properties following. 3. Click around the dashboard: pages should feel quicker.
For reviewers: what changed in the code - React `cache()` per request for the signed-in session, the `staff_mfa` decision, `getWorkspaceAccessContext` and `getCustomerProfile`. - `requireMfaUserWith` starts a page's reads alongside the MFA check; the check settles first (redirect wins even if a read failed) and data is returned only after it passes. Used by the workspace layout and 12 pages. Four tests cover it. - Member security settings are sent in one parameterised `set_config` statement instead of four. - The contact record streams notes and properties in ``; workspace and platform `loading.tsx` added. - Reference generators moved to their own files, so client forms no longer bundle `node:crypto`. - `toActiveBranchOptions` sends `{ id, name }` only; `table.tsx` is a Server Component; list searches take 20 rows and skip addresses. - Deferred: caching the verified identity per request. It changes how row-level security learns the user, so it needs its own security review.
Review status: no agentic or human review yet Checked locally: 186 tests, 180 database tests and a production build pass. The build's browser files no longer contain the crypto library. Speed gains are estimated from counting database round trips, not timed against the real database.
