author: potrock
body:
feat(mcp): webhook-mode MCP events client (experimental)

## What does this PR do?

It adds client support for the webhook delivery mode of the MCP events design sketch (modelcontextprotocol/experimental-ext-triggers-events, `docs/design-sketch-proposal.md`). An MCP server can then notify Hermes when something happens upstream, and each event starts an agent run like any other webhook route.

Hermes already had most of the pieces this needs. The gateway's webhook listener verifies Standard Webhooks `whsec_` signatures and loads dynamic routes, and those routes can deliver results anywhere. What was missing was the MCP side: `events/list`, `events/subscribe`, `events/unsubscribe`, a refresh loop, and the verification challenge.

Before this change, a webhook route registered with an events server by hand fails verification. Hermes treats the server's signed `{"type":"verification"}` POST as an ordinary event: it starts an agent run and returns `202` without echoing the challenge, so the server rejects the subscription with `CallbackEndpointError` / `challenge_failed`.

The feature is opt-in per server with `events: true`. That is the only workable gate: `mcp_types.ServerCapabilities` has `extra="ignore"`, so the server's `events` capability never reaches `initialize_result`.

## Related Issue

None found. I searched the source for an existing implementation. I could not search the issue tracker from my environment, so please check for a duplicate before merging.

## Type of Change

- [x] ✨ New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

## Changes Made

- `tools/mcp_tool_events.py` (new):
  - The `list_events`, `subscribe_event` and `unsubscribe_event` utility handlers.
  - The subscription store: one dynamic webhook route per subscription, with a per-subscription `whsec_` secret and an `mcp_event` block that holds the grant, the callback URL and the cursor.
  - `run_refresh_loop`. On a fresh connection it re-subscribes every route. After that it refreshes each route once 80% of its grant has elapsed, and drops a route on `Forbidden` or `NotFound`. Before subscribing it re-reads the route under `_rpc_lock`, so an unsubscribe that ran in the meantime is never undone.
  - `subscribe_event` asks for approval on every call, because a subscription is a standing trigger for unattended runs.
- `gateway/platforms/webhook_mcp_events.py` (new). It acts only on routes that carry an `mcp_event` block:
  - It echoes the verification challenge without starting an agent run.
  - `terminated` removes the route and notifies the `deliver` target.
  - `gap` stores the fresh cursor.
  - Event occurrences are deduplicated by `eventId` instead of the per-attempt `webhook-id`.
- `gateway/platforms/webhook.py`: one control-envelope hook after the body is parsed, and `eventId` takes precedence when deriving the delivery id.
- `tools/mcp_tool_schema.py` and `tools/mcp_tool_registration.py`: three new utility specs, gated on `events: true`. They are appended at the end, so the bytes of the existing utility schemas do not change.
- `tools/mcp_tool_transport.py`: the refresh task starts once a session is serving and is cancelled with that session.
- New config keys: `mcp_servers.<name>.events` and `platforms.webhook.extra.public_url` (the HTTPS origin servers POST to).
- Docs and `cli-config.yaml.example`: a new section, "MCP Events (experimental)".

Not included: the `poll` and `push` delivery modes, and subscriptions made from a secondary profile under `gateway.multiplex_profiles`. Dynamic routes load from the launch profile's home. The docs list both gaps.

## How to Test

1. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp_events.py tests/gateway/test_webhook_mcp_events.py` should report 15 passed.
2. `scripts/run_tests.sh tests/tools/test_mcp*.py tests/gateway/test_webhook*.py` should report 1007 passed and 1 failed. The failure is `TestDualStackBind::test_default_bind_serves_both_families`, and it fails on `main` too in an environment without IPv6.
3. End to end: run a Python SDK `MCPServer` over Streamable HTTP that implements `events/list`, `events/subscribe` and `events/unsubscribe` the way the sketch describes. On subscribe, it POSTs a signed verification challenge to the callback, then POSTs one occurrence.
   - Connect it with `register_mcp_servers({"x": {"url": ..., "events": True}})` and run the real webhook adapter.
   - Result: the challenge was answered with `200`, the occurrence was admitted (`202`, `delivery_id: mcp-event:<eventId>`), the rendered prompt reached `handle_message`, and unsubscribe removed the route.
   - Before upstreaming, it is also worth testing against a production events server. Ambush Feeds (`feed.emission.created`) is the one we built this for.

- [x] My commit messages follow Conventional Commits
- [ ] I searched for existing PRs to make sure this isn't a duplicate: **not done, see Related Issue**
- [x] My PR contains only changes related to this feature

- [x] I've tested on my platform: Ubuntu 24.04, Python 3.14.7

### Documentation & Housekeeping

- [x] I've updated `cli-config.yaml.example`
- [x] N/A: `CONTRIBUTING.md` / `AGENTS.md`

author: spy4x
body:
<!-- agent -->
## In short

Every product built on the template refuses forwarded-client headers (`X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `CF-Connecting-IP`) from any peer that is not its own proxy, so a neighbour container cannot mint a fresh sign-in rate-limit bucket per forged address. That check lived in the template only (`apps/api/middlewares/proxy-peer.ts`, template#469). It now lives here as `@spy4x/server/http/trusted-proxy`, with two fixes: a request never waits on a DNS lookup any more, and a failing error reporter cannot drop the trusted addresses.

Security review: yes. This module decides which peers a host trusts to name the client in forwarded headers.

## Why it matters

Generic code left in the template is copied into every product and drifts. The template's version also awaited a DNS lookup inside the request every 10 seconds, so when upstream DNS was down every proxied request stalled for up to 8 seconds.

## What I did

- `@spy4x/server/http/trusted-proxy` (new): `createProxyPeers`, `requireProxyForForwardedHeaders(isProxyPeer, { remoteAddr, message? })`, `FORWARDED_HEADERS` (re-exported), `PROXY_ADDRESS_MAX_AGE_MS`, `PROXY_LOOKUP_RETRY_MS`, and the types `IsProxyPeer`, `ProxyPeersOptions`, `RequireProxyOptions`. The template's test is ported and extended.
- `@spy4x/platform/rate-limit/client-ip`: exports `FORWARDED_HEADERS`, built from the three header constants the file already had. `TrustedProxyHeader` is now derived from it (the same three names). It is defined here because `@spy4x/server` may import `@spy4x/platform`, not the reverse.
- `@spy4x/platform/rate-limit/hono`: `denoServeRemoteAddr`, which reads `env.remoteAddr.hostname` as `deno serve` hands it to Hono, and gives `undefined` for anything else. The doc example on `remoteAddr` (`({ env }) => env?.remoteAddr`) returned Deno's address object rather than a string; it now shows `denoServeRemoteAddr`. Both rate-limit READMEs and the server README are updated; `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt` and `docs/1.0-contract.md` are regenerated.

Changed from the template's code, and why:

- **No request waits on DNS after the first lookup.** The first call that needs a name awaits the first lookup, because before it there is nothing to answer from. After that, a call answers from the addresses already known and starts a lookup in the background when they are 10 s old, or when the peer is unknown (at most once a second). One lookup runs at a time, so a hung resolver is not started again and again.
- **The last good addresses survive a failure.** A thrown lookup keeps the name's addresses (as before). New: an `onError` that throws is caught, so it can neither drop the addresses nor leave an unhandled rejection from a background lookup.
- **No Deno call in the module.** The peer address comes from a `remoteAddr` resolver (the same type as the rate limiter's), and the DNS lookup goes through `@spy4x/net`'s `defaultResolver`, the existing adapter. `remoteAddr` is required and checked when the middleware is built; `message` sets the 403 wording and must not be empty.

Decisions:

- **A recreated proxy is refused for one lookup's time.** The template awaited the lookup for an unknown peer, so a recreated Traefik's first request waited and passed. Now that request is answered at once and refused; requests after the background lookup ends (milliseconds with Docker's DNS) pass. I took this because the brief asks that a request never wait on DNS, and the alternative (await only for unknown peers) still stalls every forged or new-peer request when DNS hangs.
- **A stale address stays trusted until its refresh ends.** The request that finds the addresses 10 s old is answered from them while the refresh runs. With DNS down, the last good addresses stay trusted until a lookup succeeds, which is what the template did too.
- **The first lookup is awaited.** Refusing every proxied request until the first lookup ends would answer the first users after each deploy with 403. If DNS hangs at boot, those first requests wait for the resolver's own timeout, once.
- **An empty answer is not a failure.** A name that resolves to no address (a container that is stopped) trusts nothing, as in the template: keeping its old addresses would trust whichever container gets them next.

Nothing in the verified list was false: `hono.ts:175` returned the address object, and `client-ip.ts` held the three names as private constants.

## Done when

- [x] `@spy4x/server/http/trusted-proxy` exports the functions, constants and types above.
- [x] A request is answered while a lookup hangs (test "answers from the known addresses while a lookup hangs").
- [x] `denoServeRemoteAddr` is exported and the doc example uses it.
- [x] `deno task check` and `deno task check:cold` pass.

Refs https://github.com/spy4x/template/issues/137

## Mutations

Each run broke the implementation in a throwaway worktree and ran only the test file named.

- Mutation: server/http/trusted-proxy.ts:132 `void lookUp()` → `await lookUp()` → "answers from the known addresses while a lookup hangs" → `error: Promise resolution is still pending but the event loop has already resolved.`
- Mutation: server/http/trusted-proxy.ts:126 first lookup `await lookUp()` → `void lookUp()` → "trusts the address a proxy's name resolves to, and no other" (and six more) → `AssertionError: Values are not strictly equal.`
- Mutation: server/http/trusted-proxy.ts:102 `resolved.delete(name)` added in the failure branch → "keeps a name's last addresses when a lookup fails, and reports the failure" → `AssertionError: Values are not strictly equal.`
- Mutation: server/http/trusted-proxy.ts:103-107 try/catch around `onError` removed → "keeps the last addresses when the failure reporter itself throws" → `error: (in promise) Error: logger down`
- Mutation: server/http/trusted-proxy.ts:92 `fixed.add(ip)` → `fixed.add(host)` → "trusts an IP address in the list without a lookup, in any spelling" → `AssertionError`
- Mutation: server/http/trusted-proxy.ts:90 `normalizeIp(host.trim())` → `normalizeIp(host)` → "trusts an IP address in the list without a lookup, in any spelling" → `AssertionError`
- Mutation: server/http/trusted-proxy.ts:131 `age >= PROXY_ADDRESS_MAX_AGE_MS ||` → `false ||` → "stops trusting a proxy's old address once it is looked up again" → `AssertionError: Values are not strictly equal.`
- Mutation: server/http/trusted-proxy.ts:131 `!trusted && age >= PROXY_LOOKUP_RETRY_MS` → `!trusted` → "looks up again for an unknown peer, at most once a second" → `AssertionError: Values are not equal.`
- Mutation: server/http/trusted-proxy.ts:122 `if (ip === null) return false` → `return true` → "refuses a forwarded header on a request with no peer address" → `AssertionError: Values are not strictly equal.`

author: bjo004
body:
## What

- **`godspeed self update`**: checks GitHub for the latest release, downloads this machine's build and `SHA256SUMS`, checks one against the other, runs the new binary (`--version` must name the new version), and only then swaps it in with a single rename. On Windows, the running binary is renamed to `.old` and a later run removes it. A checksum mismatch, a binary that doesn't run, or a folder it can't write leaves everything unchanged.
- **`godspeed self uninstall [--yes]`**:
  - Lists what it will remove, then asks first: the binary, `~/.godspeed` if it ends up empty, and the PATH entries the installer added (the profile lines on Unix, the user PATH entry on Windows).
  - On Windows, the registry value is edited as stored, so `%VAR%` entries stay unexpanded and the value keeps its type.
  - **Keeps the config directory** (signing key, tokens, trust records) and says where it is.
- A copy installed with `cargo install` is left to Cargo; both commands say so (exit 22).
- New exit code **29, cancelled**: the user declined, or there was no terminal to ask and `--yes` wasn't given.
- The update notice, `doctor` and the `godspeed update` refusal now point to `godspeed self update`.
- README and site: an Updating and Uninstalling section, a "This CLI itself" command table, and exit codes 19 and 29.

0.1.0 doesn't have this command, so 0.1.0 users update once more by re-running the installer.

## Tested

- New integration tests run against a local stand-in for GitHub Releases:
  - unchanged when already at the latest release;
  - a checksum mismatch replaces nothing (exit 17);
  - a verified file that doesn't run replaces nothing (exit 11);
  - a full swap (Unix);
  - a cargo-installed copy is refused;
  - uninstall without `--yes` and with no terminal changes nothing (exit 29);
  - uninstall removes the binary, its folders and the profile line, and keeps `signing-key.toml`.
- On Windows by hand: a real installed 0.1.0 updated itself to a real 0.1.1 build. The `.old` copy was removed on the next run.
- The Windows PATH removal was run against a throwaway registry key. It matches case-insensitively, keeps `%USERPROFILE%` entries unexpanded and the value's type, and touches nothing else.

author: hypforge
body:
Fixes #2583.

## What changed

- A pid file naming a live process no longer blocks `hyp daemon run` when that process's command line lacks the `daemon run` arguments. Every daemon launch carries them: the launchd plist, the systemd unit, and a foreground `hyp daemon run`.
- If the command line can't be read (no `/proc`, `ps` fails, empty output), the start still refuses, as it did before (fail-closed).
- A pid file naming the starting process itself is treated as a previous incarnation's. A container restarts as the same pid.
- The process that holds the pid is never signalled, adopted or waited on. The stale file is simply overwritten.
- The pid-file read, the check, the control-request clear and the pid write now all run under the LLP 0417 cross-process guard, keyed on the pid file (`<run>/.hypaware.pid.mutation-lock`). Of two concurrent starts, one wins. The other gets either `daemon start already in progress` or `daemon already running`.
- Clearing a stale pid file (`hyp daemon stop` and every `requestDaemonStop` branch) is now a compare-and-delete under the same guard: re-read, and unlink only if the named pid is gone. Before this, a clear that read a dead pid could unlink the file a start had just written for a live daemon, and a second start would then pass (review r1 F1; the same race exists on master). A clear that finds the guard held leaves the file to that start. The one behavior change: an unremovable stale file no longer makes `requestDaemonStop` throw.
- The claim lives in a new `claimDaemonStart` in `src/core/daemon/gateway.js`, so it can be tested without booting a gateway.
- The guard moved from `src/core/cache/partition.js` to `src/core/util/mutation_guard.js`, verbatim, so the pid module can take it without loading the cache. `partition.js` re-exports it, so its callers don't change.
- LLP 0515 records the identity rule and the claim. Forward-refs were added on LLP 0417 and LLP 0017.

## Credit

This builds on #2587 by @CRYPTONIKAV. Their commit is kept as the first commit. It adds the command-line reader (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline` on Linux, `ps` elsewhere).

The second commit makes three changes:

- It drops the program-name test. A `hyp` shim or global npm bin path doesn't have to contain `hypaware`, so a real daemon could be read as foreign and a second one started beside it.
- It replaces the program-name test with the `daemon run` argument test.
- It makes the check and the replacement atomic.

## Tests

- `test/core/daemon-pid-identity.test.js`:
  - a non-daemon child gives false;
  - a `daemon run` child gives true;
  - a missing pid gives null;
  - a reused pid is overwritten and its holder left running;
  - a self-pid file is replaced;
  - a live daemon still refuses;
  - a guard held by a live owner refuses;
  - a stale clear leaves the file while a live owner holds the guard, and clears it once the guard is gone;
  - six concurrent starts over a stale file give exactly one winner, and the pid file names it.
- The reviewer's real two-gateway race driver (a gateway boots between the clear's read and its unlink) admits two gateways on master and at a8927ea7. At this head the gateway that boots inside the clear refuses with `daemon start already in progress`.
- Results:
  - `npm test`: 8356 of 8360 pass. The one failure is `test/plugins/ollama-setup.test.js:162` (`384 !== 416`, file mode 0600 vs 0640 under umask 077). It fails the same way on clean master, and #2594 tracks it.
  - `npm run typecheck`: clean.
  - `npm run smoke -- daemon_foreground_start_stop`: ok.
  - `npm run smoke -- status_diagnostics`: ok.

## CPU and memory

Per start, and per stale clear, the claim does one guard directory create and remove, one owner file, and one pid file read and write. When the pid file names a live process other than this one, it adds one `/proc` read on Linux or one `ps` exec (5 s bound) elsewhere. There is no runtime or per-row cost and nothing that grows.

## Not in this PR

- The gateway's and the processor's own pid-file removal at shutdown don't take the guard. Each runs while that daemon is still alive, and a start meanwhile reads its live `daemon run` pid and refuses (LLP 0515#scope).
- The processor child's pid write is unchanged.

author: aman678317
body:
## Summary
This branch implements a first, testable tranche of Issue #52 without rebuilding the existing UI, authentication, meeting flow, or database schema.

### Changes
- Pass bounded source-text context to document segment translation.
- Persist completed segment outputs incrementally and skip already translated segments on retries.
- Add document block/page/character coverage diagnostics and fail the document QA gate if any eligible block is empty or a page with source text has no translated text.
- Add configurable, opt-in OCR for scanned PDF pages using PyMuPDF + Pillow + pytesseract; host OS must also have Tesseract and matching language packs installed.
- Preserve URLs, email addresses, phone-like numbers, and inline code across deterministic writing corrections.
- Add targeted regression tests and include them in the backend CI workflow.
- Document new configuration values in `.env.example`.

### Validation status
- Changes are pushed to `fix/issue-52-translation-quality`.
- Targeted automated tests are included in CI but have **not been executed from this session**.
- Live provider, real-time browser/mobile call, and production PDF/OCR tests still require GitHub Actions/runtime providers and actual deployment configuration. Do not interpret this PR as evidence that all end-to-end acceptance tests have passed.

### Known scope remaining
- The current document translation loop intentionally keeps AsyncSession use sequential; the configured batch size controls checkpoint granularity, not parallel provider concurrency. Safe parallel translation needs a per-task DB session/pure-provider split and is not claimed here.
- Context-aware grammar still uses the current deterministic engine with safer protected spans; provider-backed LLM/grammar integration, debounce/cancellation, and accept/reject UI remain to be implemented separately.
- PDF OCR requires Tesseract installed at the host/container OS layer; Python package installation alone does not install the Tesseract binary.
- Full realtime observability/readiness, independent outage simulations, TURN/mobile network E2E, PDF visual/layout QA and the full language-pair benchmark remain open follow-up work.

Closes #52 (initial implementation tranche; see known scope remaining).

body:
Related to DOTCOM-18833

## Proposed Changes

* Reset the global `blockquote` box on the review quote. On the Themes page, the classic Calypso stylesheet (`client/assets/stylesheets/_main.scss`) gives every `blockquote` a grey background, padding and a 10px top margin. The quote showed in a grey box, away from its title. The dashboard does not load that rule, so only the Themes modal was wrong.
* Add the 8px gap under the title. The `Text` component's own class resets the title's margin, so the gap now sits on the quote's top margin.
* Set the gap under the quote to 16px, as in the design.
* Style the "Trustpilot" link as plain 12px/16px text in the card text color, with no underline and no external-link icon. The link stays, so a user can check that the review is real. It does not pull the user out of the request step. It underlines on hover and on keyboard focus.
* Make the reviewer name grey with the `muted` `Text` variant. The `Text` component's color overrode the card's class, so the name showed in the quote's dark color. `muted` is `$gray-700`. The design's `#979797` is about 2.9:1 on white, which fails WCAG AA for 11px text.
* Set the reviewer name to weight 400 and the design's letter spacing.

## Why are these changes being made?

Design feedback on the review cards: the spacing between the title and the quote was off, and the name and Trustpilot line did not match the design. The Trustpilot link is for credibility only, so it should not look like a call to action.

## Testing Instructions

1. Use a free site that is less than 7 days old, with an English account.
2. Assign yourself to any treatment arm of `calypso_difm_free_with_upgrade_wpadmin_202610_v1`.
3. Open `/themes/<site>` on this PR's Calypso build. Click **See the offer** in the banner, then **Tell us about your site**.
4. Check that the quote has no grey box and sits 8px under the title, and that the reviewer name is grey.
5. Check that "Trustpilot" is plain black text, with no icon. Hover it: it underlines. Click it: the review opens in a new tab and the modal stays open.
6. Repeat on the site overview at `/sites/<site>?difmOffer=open` in the dashboard.

## Pre-merge Checklist

- [x] Has the general commit checklist been followed?
- [ ] Have you written new tests for your changes? (Style only. The existing tests cover the link, its label and its new-tab target.)
- [x] Have you tested the feature in Simple (P2, WordPress.com) sites?

author: smartinsdev
body:
Gives `AuthenticateUser` its token and the three real adapters behind its ports: Prisma for `UserRepository`, bcrypt for `HashComparer`, and JWT for `TokenSigner`. It also brings the database, environment and CI setup they need.

This is the infra half of the `POST /sessions` slice planned in `docs/architecture.md` §8. The HTTP half (controller, route, factory, server) comes in the next PR. Until then, nothing in production wires these adapters together.

## What changes

- **`AuthenticateUser` returns `{ accessToken }`** on success. It signs `{ sub: user.id }` through a new `TokenSigner` port, tested with `FakeTokenSigner`.
- **`UserPrismaRepository.findByEmail`** restores a stored user through `UserPrismaMapper`, with identity and credentials intact.
- **`BcryptHasher`** implements `HashComparer` with the async `bcrypt.compare`. It implements only `HashComparer`, because no use case asks for `HashGenerator` yet.
- **`JwtSigner`** implements `TokenSigner` with `jose`: HS256, `sub` from the payload, and `exp` 15 minutes after `iat`.
- **`Clock`** is a new application port (`now(): Date`). `JwtSigner` reads the time from it.
- **Infra:**
  - PostgreSQL 18 runs in Docker Compose. One server holds `mydb` (dev) and `identity_test`, which an init script creates.
  - Prisma is reached through `src/shared/infra/prisma`.
  - `env.ts` validates the environment with Zod.
  - Vitest is split into `unit` and `integration` projects.
- **CI:**
  - A new `integration` job runs `pnpm test:integration` against a disposable `postgres:18-alpine` service.
  - The existing matrix job now runs `pnpm test:unit` explicitly.

## Decisions worth reviewing

**Adapter tests speak the standard, not the library.** The bcrypt test checks a digest produced outside the codebase (Python `bcrypt`), stored as a literal. The JWT tests read claims and recompute the HS256 signature from RFC 7519/7518 with `node:crypto`. Because of this, the JWT tests stayed green unchanged when `JwtSigner` moved from a hand-written `createHmac` to `jose`.

**The secret and the clock are injected; the adapter reads no configuration.** `JwtSigner(secret, clock)` never touches `env`. Only the factory will pass `env.JWT_SECRET` and a system clock. The adapter tests therefore need no environment variables, and they control time with a stopped clock instead of `vi.useFakeTimers()`.

**`iat` and `exp` come from one reading of the clock.** `exp = iat + 900` is computed by hand rather than with `setExpirationTime("15m")`. `jose` resolves string durations against the system clock, not against the `iat` you set, so the two claims could come from different instants. `iat` is rounded down so it is never in the future.

**HS256, a symmetric algorithm.** The same process signs and verifies, so a shared secret is enough. An asymmetric algorithm such as RS256 only pays off when another service verifies tokens it must not be able to issue.

**`new SignJWT(payload)` signs the whole port payload.** `TokenPayload` stays a `type`, not an `interface`. A `type` gets an implicit index signature, which lets it be assigned to `jose`'s `JWTPayload`. If `TokenPayload` gains a claim, the adapter signs it too and does not drop it silently.

**`bcrypt` (native) over `bcryptjs`.** `bcrypt@6` ships prebuilt binaries for linux-x64 and darwin-arm64, among others, so CI needs no C++ toolchain. `allowBuilds: bcrypt: true` is set in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`.

**Integration runs once, on Node 24.** It checks how the domain maps to the database, which does not depend on the Node version. The service container starts before checkout and cannot run the init script, so `POSTGRES_DB: identity_test` creates the database directly.

## Known gaps

- **Timing (carried over from #11).** An unknown email still returns at once, while a wrong password runs bcrypt. The response time can reveal which emails are registered. The real adapter now exists, so this can be addressed in the use case.
- **No `SystemClock` and no `JWT_SECRET` in `env.ts` yet.** Both arrive with the factory. `jose` accepts HMAC keys shorter than 256 bits, so the Zod schema should enforce `JWT_SECRET.length >= 32`.
- **Prisma 8 is a release candidate** (`prisma@8.0.0-rc.22` with `@prisma/orm-postgres@8.0.0-rc.17`). `pnpm peers check` reports unmet peers for vitest 5, typescript ≤6 and effect ^4.0.3. They all come from `prisma → @prisma/composer-cli → alchemy`, deploy tooling the project does not load. Staying on 8 or moving back to stable 7 is decided after the slice works.
- **Email case.** A non-normalized email written straight to the database is never found by `findByEmail`. If it needs guarding, the guard should be a database constraint, added once something writes users.

## Tests

- **Unit:** 106 tests, now including `BcryptHasher` (2) and `JwtSigner` (4).
- **Integration:** 2 tests (`env`, `UserPrismaRepository`).
- `pnpm validate` is clean.
- The `integration` job was simulated locally in a clean worktree, with no `.env.test`, against a throwaway `postgres:18-alpine`.

author: justin13888
body:
## Summary

- `crates/gamut-dng/src/encoder.rs`: the lossless-JPEG chunk encoder no longer hands a CFA strip/tile
  to `lossless_jpeg::encode` as one full-width component (where predictor 1 differences each
  photosite against a neighbour of a different colour). It now declares the chunk as
  `repeat-cols` interleaved components at `width / repeat-cols` wide — `(width/2, height, 2)` for
  Bayer — so every prediction is across like colours. DNG 1.7.1.0 p. 20 permits this ("Only the
  total sample counts need to match. It is common for CFA images to be encoded with a different
  width, length or component count to allow the JPEG compression predictors to work across like
  colors"). No sample is reordered: an interleaved scan already reads the row `c0, c1, c0, c1`.
  New private helpers `horizontal_cfa_period` and `lossless_jpeg_geometry`; `encode_chunk` takes the
  period. A chunk the split does not fit (more than 4 components — T.81 caps a scan at 4, e.g. an
  X-Trans 6-column repeat — or a width the period does not divide) keeps its own geometry. LinearRaw
  has period 1 and is unchanged. Two inline tests: the geometry rule row by row, and an end-to-end
  check that an encoded CFA strip is a 2-component half-width SOF3 frame whose samples are the
  mosaic in raster order. A third inline test,
  `cfa_lossless_jpeg_width_ceiling_is_twice_the_frame_limit`, pins the width ceiling the reshape
  moves (see decision 5): a 131 070-wide untiled Bayer strip encodes and our decoder reads it back
  exactly; 131 072 wide is refused with the 65535 dimension error.
- `crates/gamut-dng/STATUS.md`: P13 row records the reshape; the #163 harness section marks #584
  fixed, notes the fixture table now prints 508 112 for `cfa/lossless-jpeg`, notes the decode
  timing tables were taken against the pre-reshape stream, and records the real-corpus measurement
  below.

Decoder side needs nothing: `decoder.rs` already follows the total-sample-count rule.

### Measured gain (real-camera corpus, as the #617 correction asks)

Each CFA file in `third_party/gamut-dng-samples` decoded with gamut and re-encoded with
`Compression::LosslessJpeg`, same samples (ad-hoc, uncommitted measurement program):

| file | codestream before → after | whole DNG before → after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Canon 5D3 5920×3950 | 36 298 966 → 24 962 613 (−31.2 %) | 53 838 242 → 42 501 889 (−21.1 %) |
| Leica M10 5984×3992 | 41 785 281 → 32 398 714 (−22.5 %) | 59 702 425 → 50 315 858 (−15.7 %) |

Synthetic fixture (`cargo bench -p gamut-dng --bench codec -- zz_no_such_bench`, table only):
`cfa/lossless-jpeg` 618 800 → **508 112** (now below `cfa/uncompressed` 541 440);
`linear-raw/lossless-jpeg` unchanged at 1 262 560. No size is pinned in a test, per #617.

## Validation

- `cargo test -p gamut-dng` — pass (lib 213; all 12 integration binaries incl. `oracle_adobe` 18 and
  `roundtrip` 29, where the Adobe DNG SDK validates and decodes the reshaped strips and tiles
  pixel-exact: `lossless_jpeg_roundtrips_and_validates` covers even width 64 (reshaped) and odd
  width 33 (fallback); `adobe_validates_and_decodes_tiled_dngs_exactly` covers 32×32 tiles).
- After the width-ceiling repair: `cargo test -p gamut-dng` — pass again (lib 214, all
  integration binaries).
- `cargo clippy -p gamut-dng --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — pass.
- `rustfmt +nightly --edition 2024 --check crates/gamut-dng/src/encoder.rs` — pass.
- `convco check origin/master..HEAD` — pass.
- Not run: `mise run fmt` / `mise run test-dng-real` — both fail before doing any work in this
  checkout because it is nested under another checkout of the repository, so cargo resolves the
  outer workspace for the excluded `tooling/` crates (unavailable, environmental). `test-dng-real`
  only decodes the corpus and does not call the encoder; the corpus measurement above is what
  exercised it. Mutation survey not run; CI's gate covers it.

## Coverage gaps

- The 131 070-wide ceiling is proved against gamut's own decoder only; the Adobe SDK differential
  does not reach widths past 65 535.

- No test exercises a 4-column-repeat or X-Trans CFA through the full encoder; the geometry
  function's unit test covers those branches, and the Adobe differential covers only 2×2 Bayer.

## Risks and rollout

- Output bytes change for every CFA lossless-JPEG DNG gamut writes (smaller, still conformant; the
  Adobe SDK reads them). Readers that ignore the DNG total-sample-count rule and assume
  JPEG width == tile width would mis-read them; the Adobe SDK and real camera converters write this
  same shape, so such readers already fail on common files.

Closes #584

## Decisions taken

Issue 584 - gamut-dng: lossless-JPEG CFA encode expands the payload past uncompressed

1. **General rule vs Bayer-only.** Took `components = spp × CFA repeat cols` when it is ≤ 4 and the
   period divides the chunk width, else the chunk's own geometry. Rejected a Bayer-only `(w/2, h, 2)`
   special case: the issue asks for the general rule for 2×4/4×4 patterns. Reverse: make
   `lossless_jpeg_geometry` return `(cols, spp)` unconditionally.
2. **No size gate.** Per the #617 correction folded into #584, no test pins the synthetic fixture's
   bytes; the gain is recorded in STATUS.md from the real-camera corpus instead. Reverse: add an
   assertion on the `cfa/lossless-jpeg` fixture size.
3. **Fitted Huffman table split off** as #824 (sub-issue of #163): the issue calls it secondary and
   it is an independent change to `lossless_jpeg.rs`'s table emission. Reverse: implement it here.
4. **Decode timing tables in STATUS.md left as measured**, annotated as taken against the
   pre-reshape stream, rather than re-measured: re-running the eight-run matrix is out of scope for
   an encoder size fix. Reverse: re-run the `decode_dng`/`decode_lossless_jpeg` matrix and replace
   the `cfa` rows.
5. **Accept the moved width ceiling rather than re-impose the old one.** `lossless_jpeg::encode`'s
   1..=65535 check now sees the frame width `cols / 2`, so an untiled Bayer image 65 536–131 070
   px wide (even width) encodes where it used to be refused. Kept: the limit is T.81's on the SOF3
   line length, not on the DNG strip; TIFF `ImageWidth` is a LONG and DNG 1.7.1.0 p. 20 lets the
   JPEG geometry differ from the strip's, so the file is conformant, and gamut's own decoder reads
   it back pixel-exact (pinned by the new test at 131 070; 131 072 still refused). Not run against
   the Adobe SDK at that width (fixture cost); the SDK already validates the same reshape at width
   64. Odd widths past 65 535 fall back to the unreshaped geometry and stay refused. Reverse:
   check `cols <= 65535` in `encode_chunk` before reshaping.

author: danalec
body:
Fixes the hassfest rejection on `master` and four defects found reviewing that build.

## Hassfest

`master` was red on seven points. Two were runtime problems:

- **`triggers.yaml` was missing.** Hassfest requires one for a custom integration that registers device triggers. `samsungtv` is on its not-yet-migrated exemption list; `samsungtv_custom` is not, so the turn-on trigger could not be described to the automation UI.
- **`async-upnp-client==0.49.0` is incompatible with `==0.48.2`**, which is what Home Assistant 2026.10 ships. Pinning the core value forced a UPnP client version HA had not tested.

The rest: every requirement pinned with `==` a package HA already depends on (`getmac`, `samsungctl`, `samsungtvws`, `wakeonlan` now use `>=`), and `version` sat after `zeroconf`, breaking manifest key order.

Validated against the same image CI runs, before pushing:
`docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/github/workspace" ghcr.io/home-assistant/hassfest`

## Defects

**`_remote_event` raised on a malformed frame.** Upstream short-circuited on falsy `data`; the rewrite used `.get("data", {})`, which only substitutes the default when the key is absent, not when the value is null. A `data` of null, a string or a list reached `.get()` and raised `AttributeError`, and a non-string `message` raised on `.lower()`. This runs inside the websocket receive loop, so the exception escaped into the library's listener — on the very connection whose health the branch exists to report on. Now type-checked.

**The entity never advertised `TURN_ON` without an automation.** The method worked with a valid MAC, but `supported_features` only set the flag when a turn-on action existed, hiding the power button for exactly the users wake-on-LAN was written for.

**An app colliding with a reported input produced a duplicate label.** The name appeared twice and `select_source` checks inputs first, leaving the app unreachable.

**`service_unsupported` no longer described its own condition.** Wake-on-LAN widened the raise to "no usable MAC and no automation", but the text still said only "does not have an automation configured".

Also: the sources callback did not write state when the TV's list arrived late, so a corrected list only reached the state machine on the next poll. `info.md` said turn_on worked "instead of a wake-on-LAN packet", the opposite of what it does. `MAC_RE` ended in `$`, which in Python also matches before a trailing newline, so a MAC carrying one would have built a malformed packet; it is `\Z` now.

## Evidence

Each fix is pinned by a check that was run against the previous commit and **failed there**: four `AttributeError`s on the malformed payloads, `TURN_ON` not advertised, and the duplicated `'Netflix'` label. Full gate green locally — ruff 0.16.10, `compileall`, all seven verification scripts, and hassfest.

## Still unverified

No live TV, no installed Home Assistant. The `ed.sourcesChanged` parser remains written from a captured trace rather than executed against hardware.

Before: `libs/extras/c_preprocessor` failed with "invalid token paste" on `, ## __VA_ARGS__` whenever the variable arguments were non-empty (e.g. Linux's `static_assert(expr, ...)`), and it had no `, ## args` support for named variadic parameters. Stringizing dropped the space after any argument token that was a string literal (`"a" ;` became `"\"a\";"`), and a substituted argument kept the call site's spacing, so `.quad sym` stringized as `".quadx"`.

After: these behave as in GCC. The comma stays and the arguments follow unpasted when non-empty; it is deleted when empty, for both `__VA_ARGS__` and named `args...`. Stringizing drops only leading whitespace, and a stringized token or a substituted (non-`##`) argument takes the spacing of the `#`/parameter in the macro body.

These are fixes the w-private C-to-W transpiler carries in its own copy of the expander (`c_to_w/ctow_preprocess.w`, `c_to_w/upstream_patches/c_preprocessor_gnu_comma_paste.patch`); once this lands and its `w/` pin moves past it, that copy can go.

author: jordansmall
body:
## Summary

Go's `flag` package stops parsing at the first non-flag argument, and `parseSignalFlags` treated a clean `fs.Parse` as success. One stray token, usually an unquoted multi-word value, silently ended flag parsing, so every flag after it was dropped. For example, `driver-exec signal issue-intent -title t -type bug stray -dedup a.go:Sym` sent an intent with no dedup terms and exited 0.

No signal verb takes positional arguments, so `parseSignalFlags` now rejects any leftover argument through `signalUsageFailure`. The rejected line names the first leftover token, says signal verbs take no positional arguments, and hints that a multi-word flag value may need quoting:

```
signal issue-intent rejected (usage): unexpected argument "stray": signal verbs take no positional arguments; a multi-word flag value may need quoting
```

All four signal verbs (`comment`, `pr-intent`, `issue-intent`, `status`) go through `parseSignalFlags`, so they all pick this up.

## Changes

- `cmd/launcher/driver-exec/signal_cmd.go`: a post-parse `fs.NArg() > 0` check in `parseSignalFlags`, plus a doc comment update.
- `cmd/launcher/driver-exec/signal_cmd_test.go`: a new row in `TestRunSignal_UsageFailureRejectedLine` pins the exact rejected line. A new `TestRunSignal_StrayPositionalSendsNothing` checks exit 1 and an empty issue-intent buffer, so no partial intent reaches the socket.
- `docs/reference.md`: the signal usage-failure list now includes a stray positional.

## Reviewer notes

- A literal `--` followed by a token is now rejected too. That is intended, because no signal verb accepts positionals.
- The non-signal `driver-exec` verbs (bind-registry, probe-registry-socket/tcp, forward-registry-tcp, assemble-prompt, and the default run path) still ignore leftover positionals in the same way. That is out of scope here and has been queued for filing as a follow-up issue.

## Checks

- `go test`, `go vet`, and `gofmt` on `./driver-exec/` all pass.
- `nix build .#checks-inbox -L` passes.

author: kubanemil
body:
First part of the proof that the Pöschl-Teller potential is reflectionless (TODO in `PoschlTeller/Basic.lean`).

Scattering states have the form `Pₖ(tanh (κ x)) e^{i k x}`, where `Pₖ` is a polynomial. This PR works only with the polynomial part, an element of `ℂ[X]`. The derivative, the raising operators `-∂ₓ + n κ tanh (κ x)` and the Hamiltonian become operators on `ℂ[X]`, so the intertwining relation is an identity of polynomials, proved by `ring`. The follow-up PR transfers this to functions `ℝ → ℂ` and proves the reflectionless theorem.

## Added

`Physlib/QuantumMechanics/PoschlTeller/Scattering.lean` (new)
- `waveDeriv`, `raise`, `reducedHamiltonian`: `∂ₓ`, `-∂ₓ + n κ tanh` and `-∂ₓ² - n (n + 1) κ² sech²`, acting on the polynomial `p` of a wave `p(tanh (κ x)) e^{i k x}`.
- `reducedHamiltonian_raise`: the intertwining relation `H_{n+1} R_{n+1} = R_{n+1} H_n`.
- `waveDeriv_C`, `raise_C_mul`: small API.
- `scatteringPoly`: `Pₖ`, defined recursively by the raising operators.
- `reducedHamiltonian_scatteringPoly`: `Pₖ` is an eigenvector with eigenvalue `k²`.
- `eval_one_raise`, `eval_neg_one_raise`, `scatteringPoly_eval_one`, `scatteringPoly_eval_neg_one`, `scatteringPoly_eval_one_ne_zero`, `scatteringPoly_eval_neg_one_ne_zero`: `Pₖ(±1) = ∏ₙ (±n κ - i k) ≠ 0`, which become the asymptotic amplitudes in the follow-up PR.

`Physlib.lean`: imports the new file.

## Reviewer map

Read §A.1 (definitions) first, then §A.2 (`reducedHamiltonian_raise`, the key step), then §A.3 and §A.4.

author: jagc-siete
body:
## What was wrong

Verified against the production catalog on 2026-10-16:

- `employees_company_view` / `b2x_employees_select` let **any** signed-in user of a company, role `employee` included, read every coworker's `base_salary`, `dni`, `bank_account`, `phone` and `address`.
- `b2x_employees_update` let any user of the company **update any employee row**, including their own salary.
- `"Employees can manage their own leave requests"` (FOR ALL, no WITH CHECK) let an employee approve, edit or delete their own leave request straight through PostgREST, bypassing the API. `"Leave requests are viewable by company users"` exposed every coworker's requests.
- `PUT /api/leave/[id]` did not check the current status (a cancelled request could be approved, approved/rejected could be flipped) and let a manager or HR approve their own request.

## What changed

- **API** (`pages/api/leave/[id].ts`, `lib/leave/leave-decision.ts`): decide only `pending` requests (409) and never your own (403); the update also filters on `status = 'pending'` so two concurrent decisions cannot both win.
- **Migration** `20261016140000_employee_rls_leave_approval.sql`:
  - `employees`: employee → own row; manager → own department; company_admin / hr_manager → company; super_admin → all. B2C self branch kept; legacy `admin` role keeps company read. Company-wide writes only via `employees_admin_manage`.
  - `leave_requests`: own SELECT, INSERT only as `pending`, cancel only while `pending`; manager sees own department; admin policies unchanged.
  - `BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE` state-machine trigger for every session, service role included: `pending → approved/rejected` never by the requester; `pending → cancelled` by requester or HR/admin; `approved → cancelled` by HR/admin; anything else raises. `employee_id` is immutable.
- **Rollback** `supabase/rollbacks/20261016140000_employee_rls_leave_approval.rollback.sql`: recreates today's policies verbatim (generated from prod `pg_policy`), idempotent.

## Already applied to production

Jorge applied the migration from the Planilla SQL editor on 2026-10-16 (~20:00 UTC). It is not recorded in `supabase_migrations` history. Verified after apply: `employees` 10 policies / md5 `66681998…`, `leave_requests` 11 / `c6708ccb…` (identical to the local post-migration catalog), trigger enabled, helper functions not executable by `anon`, no Postgres errors since.

## Testing

- `scripts/test-rls-local.sh`: 36 role-impersonation tests (employee, manager, hr_manager, company_admin, super_admin, service role) on a throwaway local Postgres loaded with a snapshot of the prod catalog (`supabase/tests/rls/`, DDL + fake data only). Today's policies fail 24 of them; after the migration all 36 pass; the rollback restores both the results and the policy catalog exactly.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` pass (837/837), including `tests/leave-decision.test.ts`.
- Not tested: the real app end to end with signed-in users.

## Notes

- SQL fixtures are force-added because `.gitignore` blocks `*.sql` outside `supabase/migrations`.
- Two `manager` profiles without `employee_id` (never signed in) now see no employees or leave requests; link their `employee_id` when they start using the app.
- Out of scope, found while auditing: `b2x_user_profiles_update` lets company users edit coworkers' profiles (role/permissions); `get_supervised_employees(uuid)` is SECURITY DEFINER and executable by `anon`.

## Summary

Fixes #1231.

This PR improves `.zipper-runner/runner.py` active worktree babysitting:
- Automatically fetches remote heads and fast-forwards clean worktrees when behind the authorized PR head.
- Attempts clean rebases when worktrees have diverged local commits, cleanly publishing rebased completions.
- Protects local commits to a timestamped backup branch (`runner-backup-{branch}-{timestamp}`) when a rebase conflicts, blocking automatic merge and alerting without clobbering work.
- Verifies return codes on all git operations (`git reset --hard`, `git fetch`, `git rebase`).
- Re-verifies local CodeRabbit review gate (`_run_coderabbit_pre_pr_check`) before invoking babysit agents, immediately clearing stale failures if the tree is clean.
- Comprehensive test coverage in `test_merge_authorization.py` for behind-head fast-forwards, clean rebases, rebase conflicts, dirty worktree safety, and stale/persistent review gates.

## Release Notes

Autonomous runner now automatically synchronizes diverged or behind active worktrees against authorized remote PR heads, cleanly preserving conflicting local commits on safety backup branches. Stale review gate failures are re-verified and cleared without burning agent runs.

author: parkerhdavis
body:
Brings the listened kinds (music, audio) to the delivery ruling the video pass built (#457, walked through the Studio in #482): the processed MP3 is the upgrade that arrives, and the original is the deliverable until then.

The completed audio gate reasoned that "their processing product IS the player (a normalized rendition…)" — but the players take any address, and the meter, attention-crediting and gate ladder all ride the player rather than the rendition, so the premise does not hold: an upload's original plays today, whether or not processing has finished. Before this, the creator stared at the Processing banner (or nothing) until the job completed; a refresh never even helped.

- `/api/content/works/:id/original` widens from video-only to the listened kinds, and `originalUrl` is serialized for them in both the owner shape and the user shape — the route's existing gate ladder (access → the Public Access meter → the household limit → a fresh signed URL) unchanged.
- The public page and the embed page fall back to the processing block only where the original cannot play (`playsOriginal`); the poll still swaps the processed deliverable in when it lands. Processing failure now leaves the original playing instead of an empty slot, matching video.
- The Studio editor's `kindWaiting` stops catching the listened kinds, so the deliverable's place holds the player; the processing progress rides the Manage tab's file section, as video's does. The stale `fileReady` docblock (whose predicate no longer carried the gate it described) is rewritten.
- The original-delivery suite (renamed from `video-original` — the fixture audio case it pinned as "not a play surface" is flipped) covers the widened route, both shapes, and the 402; the meter's account-wide reach is why the listener cases sit above the spend tests. A browser walk pins the editor's and the user's view playing the original while the job row says pending, with no worker draining it.

Ebooks and comics keep their completed gate — their products (page images, the reflow reader) genuinely do not exist during processing. One stated edge: a non-deniable audio the browser cannot decode (the accepted set is deliberately wide) shows a player that cannot start until the MP3 arrives; the audio ingest has no remux pass, and the accepted-formats copy already says the conversion is coming.

body:
**#103 step 2 — evidence at the system boundary: helpers + the exemplar file** (`tests/test_config.py`). The pattern the remaining test files fan out from.

**Helpers** (`tests/evidence_helpers.py`, CONVENTIONS § Prime rule / § Helper razor): `given_alex(alex_copy, mutation, edit)` (world copy, seed attached once, mutation applied + derived yaml attached — the mutation sentence is the step name, so the value threads) · `when_bake(config, *flags)` (the ONE when step: `python -m bake` as a real subprocess; argv/stdout/stderr/data.json attached, host paths neutralised) · `verdict(claim, actual, expected, op)` (`Then: <claim> = <value>` steps that go red/green) · `then_config_error(run, msg)` (exit 1 + stderr names it + nothing written) · `item_of`, `ring`, `item`.

**Exemplar**: every labelled case in `test_config.py` (68 records, 15 rules) now proves its row through the CLI — exit code, stderr, `data.json` — instead of `load_config()` in-process. Old in-process tests deleted (each replaced 1:1; `test_command_empty_argv` kept as an unlabelled unit guard — no spec row). Assertions moved, not dropped: `pytest.raises(match=X)` → `then_config_error(run, X)`; field asserts → `data.json` verdicts. Tightened where the row says more (no-artifact on config errors; the noexec row names the file; `config-error-aborts-whole-bake` now uses the row's exact inputs).

**Head stamp**: a session hook writes `environment.properties` (`git.commit` = `CIRCLES_HEAD_SHA` or `git rev-parse HEAD`; no `image.digest` — not an image run) + `executor.json` (run URL). `evidence.sh` opens the digest with `**Stamp:**`. Seat: `ci.yaml` exports `CIRCLES_HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}` on `ci` + `e2e`; `test-browser.sh` passes it (and the run identity) into the Playwright container so the browser half carries the same stamp.

**Effect** (whole digest before → after): STEP_FLAT 61→45, THREAD_BROKEN 61→45, BARE_ROW 230→178; for test_config's 15 rules STEP_FLAT 19→3 (the 3 left are test_adapters'). Rows proven unchanged — now CLI-earned. Suite 6.5 s → 16.4 s (test_config +9.5 s of subprocesses).

Verified: `devbox run ci` exit 0 (313 passed), scan-secrets clean, browser 28/28 with a populated stamp. Red/green: config error exiting 0 → `Then: exit code = 1` reds on two rows.

body:
From TestFlight feedback: "Created trip for 8pm and in driver app it's showing 8:30".

## Cause
The driver app formatted trip times in the **phone's** time zone (`toLocaleTimeString(undefined, …)`). The server, web and operator app use the company time zone (Riyadh). A phone left on India time (+5:30) showed a Riyadh 20:00 trip as 22:30.

## Change
- `shared/lib/dates.ts`: company time zone with Riyadh as the default. Both apps refresh it from `GET /settings/public` at start. New helpers: `inCompanyZone`, `formatTime`, `companyDayKey`. `formatDay` and `formatDayTime` now use the company zone too.
- These driver-app screens now use it:
  - Home
  - trip details
  - Trips list
  - new-trip acknowledge prompt
  - trip completed
  - driver charges
  - POD photos
  - navigation ETA
  - geotag stamp and preview
- Unchanged: greeting and night-mode logic (still the phone clock), and document expiry dates (already UTC calendar dates).

## Testing
- `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint` pass for driver-app and operator-app.
- On a machine set to `TZ=Asia/Kolkata`, 17:00Z formats as 20:00.
- Needs new driver and operator builds.

author: reubentechery
body:
The Dungeons sheet looked great but was crowded. This builds direction **B, At the door**, from the
[Dungeon Finder Redesign proposal](https://claude.ai/artifact/N6tzSmkT9boCf2TEdNuM2u), in the eight steps it
planned, with one change asked for mid-way: **practice is gone from the game**.

## What changed

1. **Say it once.** The tier cards repeated the picture under them. The dungeon's numbers are one line (clears, KC, best time); item levels moved to the loot and the coming-soon dungeons.
2. **Five sizes, lines on what you tap, 44px targets.** 28, 23, 17, 14 and 12, nothing smaller. A black line with a shadow now means you can tap it.
3. **The loot gets its own page.** The log's line opens a Loot page (back arrow; your role's drops first, marked "yours"). On desktop the loot sits in its own column instead.
4. **Your party at the door.** Your three heroes stand in front of the Barrow's arch in their own gear with the Gravekeeper in the doorway. It replaces the role tabs, the hero card, Change and the Warband sentence. Tap a hero's name plate for **Who goes in**: every hero by role, who you're playing, who comes along, an empty bed to make one. On Heroic the other spots are dashed and marked Friend, and the gold button stays locked.
   - Every dungeon now has a door in its content: `DungeonStage` in `<dungeon>/stage.ts` (the door, the final boss in the doorway, the light, three spots for the heroes). The Barrow has one, and **`src/content/_template/stage.ts`** is a documented one so every new dungeon gets one. `tests/meta.test.ts` checks each has its final boss in the doorway and room for the heroes; `docs/dungeons.md` says how to make one.
5. **One brew button.** The bottle, its name, what it does in a few words (new `short` line per recipe; a test checks each fits a phone and only states numbers its card states) and the count. It opens **Your brew**, with every bottle and its full words.
6. Practice beside the gold button (built, then taken out in the practice commit below).
7. **Every dungeon behind the name.** The tabs go; the dungeon's name opens **All dungeons**: each with its log, clears and Heroic progress, and coming-soon ones with the item level they'll want, what they drop and what their log gives.
8. **Docs.** `docs/design.md` describes the sheet as it is now; `AGENTS.md`'s code map names the stage files.

**Practice is gone, as you asked.** No Practice button or page; no Heroic practice, so Heroic stays locked until online play unless "Everything open" is on; and the Settings switch that played a walkout at the end of practice runs is gone with it. The engine still treats a run started past the entrance or in test gear as one that doesn't count, because the Crypt Trial and the testing hooks (`highfell.startRun`) need that; such a run now says "Test run". With practice gone the foot is one wide gold button, and the door fits every screen without scrolling (stage shrinks first on short phones; on desktop the loot column matches the left column and scrolls inside only on a 1280×720 laptop).

Main was merged in (Heroic's gilding kits, sounds and music). The Loot page now says Heroic drops "everything Normal drops, plus a gilding kit for every piece", and main's Kit preview stays in Settings.

## The numbers (everyday view, 390 × 844 phone)

| On screen | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Words | 140 | 33 |
| Font sizes | 11 | 4 |
| Black-outlined boxes | 30 | 15 |
| Bits of text under 12px | 24 | 0 |
| Buttons under 44px | 5 | 0 |
| Phone screens tall | 1.3 | 1 |

Checked without the sheet scrolling, Normal and Heroic, at 375×667, 390×844, 1280×720, 1440×900 and 1920×1080.

## Checks

- `npm run all` passes: 123 tests (2 new: the stage test, the brew short lines), build clean.
- Phone and desktop screenshots of every state at each step; clicked through in the built game: the Loot page and back (a drop's card returns to the Loot page; Escape goes back, then closes), Who goes in (playing Wenna makes Thorgrim come along), choosing a brew, All dungeons, and Enter starting a run.

## For you, before it goes live

- Play it: `npm run preview`, then the big Dungeons button.
- Thimblebriar and Moonmere still borrow the Barrow's picture in All dungeons, as they did before; each needs its own once it's built.
- The claude.ai Claude: please copy the `docs/design.md` changes to the Dungeon Systems doc and update "Where it's at" in Start Here when you publish.

author: junidmoh-code
body:
Junid's decisions on the per-till staff slip (16 Oct 2026), server side. Companion PR in marathon-pos-app: `feat/card-recon-supporting-slips-drift`.

## 1 — A staff slip is never refused because the machine's report is in
Before: Yasmin's slip on Marathon Till 2 after the machine's/manager's report was refused "already in from the card machine", and nothing was kept.
Now: when today's record for the till is a **better figure** — the machine's report (emailed PDF / photographed) or **Junid's** (typed total, or a manual entry) — the slip is accepted and kept on that record at `card_batches/{store}/{tid}/{key}/supportingSlips/{id}`: typed cents, photo (`cardRecon/slip-{id}/photo-0.jpg`), who, when. The record's figure is untouched and stays the verdict's. The sender gets `{ ok, received }` only.

## 2 — Precedence: machine report > Junid > staff typed
- Staff slip **after** Junid's figure → attached beside it (was: a correction that replaced it).
- Staff slip **first**, then a better figure takes over (the machine's report of its filing number, Junid's typed correction, or a manual "wrong" correction) → the staff slip moves onto the new record as a supporting slip (`carriedSlips`, same SAST day only), so the comparison is never lost. The original record stays unchanged.
- Their own second slip today, with nothing better in → still a correction (revision), as before.
- Nothing today → the slip is the day's record, as before.

The background photo check (`cardBatchReadJob`, mode `check`) reads a supporting slip's photo and writes `photoRead` on **that slip**, never on the record.

## No rule changes
All writes are Admin SDK inside `cardBatchCapture`, `cardBatchManualEntry` and `cardBatchReadJob`; the photo is under `cardRecon/**` (read needs the `card_recon` claim, so staff cannot read it). `database.rules.json` untouched.

## Tests
`card-supporting-slips.test.cjs` (11: pure rule, machine/Junid typed/Junid manual attach, two slips, photo check on the slip, Junid correction carrying Amanda's slip, manual correction carrying, machine report carrying), updated `card-slip-scope` (the refusal test now asserts acceptance). Card suite: 613 pass, 0 fail. Mutation-checked: attach rule, same-day carry, carry in submit, carry in manual entry, photoRead target — each caught.

## Deploy (by name)
`functions:cardBatchCapture,functions:cardBatchReadJob,functions:cardBatchManualEntry`.

## Also: hosting deploy fixed
`deploy.yml` failed on every push since at least 15 Oct (`Input required and not supplied: firebaseServiceAccount`). A dedicated service account `hosting-deploy-ci@marathon-club.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with **only** `roles/firebasehosting.admin` was created, proven on a throwaway preview channel with only its key, and set as the `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` secret; the local key file was deleted. This PR's merge is the first run on it.

body:
## Cosa cambia
Ridimensionando la finestra le aree grafiche diventavano nere e si ridisegnavano in ritardo. Causa: ogni evento `<Configure>` (decine per frame di trascinamento) riavvolgeva etichette, ridisegnava la topologia e rilayoutava l'intera pagina; ogni modifica cambiava la dimensione richiesta e generava altri eventi. Tk ridipinge solo a cascata conclusa, quindi su Windows l'area appena esposta restava nera.

- **`ui.on_width_change`** (nuovo): reagisce solo a cambi di larghezza, al massimo una volta ogni 40 ms con l'ultima larghezza; la dimensione finale viene sempre applicata.
- **`ui.set_wrap`** (nuovo): cambia `wraplength` solo se diverso.
- **`ScrollFrame`**: la larghezza del contenuto segue la finestra al massimo ~1 volta per frame (16 ms); `scrollregion` calcolata dall'evento invece di `bbox("all")`.
- **`Topology`**: ridisegno solo su cambio larghezza; altezza riconfigurata solo se cambia.
- **Form Gateway / passi del piano**: un handler per contenitore invece di un binding per etichetta; i passi non si riavvolgono più sulla propria larghezza (loop wrap → resize → wrap).
- `Callout` e barra modifiche usano gli stessi helper.

Nessuna nuova dipendenza, nessun cambio a NAT/rete/rollback.

## Verifica
- Trascinamento simulato (234 passi, Xvfb, Tk 8.6): chiamate Tk −35% su Panoramica e −73% su Gateway; tempo totale −20% / −28%.
- Layout finale dopo il trascinamento identico a `main` su Panoramica, Gateway e Informazioni (315 widget confrontati: dimensioni e `wraplength` uguali).
- Nuovo `tests/test_resize_helpers.py` (coalescenza, solo larghezza, widget distrutto, `set_wrap` senza no-op); suite completa verde.

author: kaboomfox
body:
**Merge before #90.** #90's one failing check, "moves into VectorCraft (stable)", is this bug, which #89 brought to `main`. Once this is merged, a rerun of that check passes.

## The bug

`build.rs` named the commit of whatever repository git found above the sources. The rehearsal of the move into VectorCraft (`compat.yml`, "moves into VectorCraft") builds StitchCraft from a copy inside VectorCraft's checkout. So the build named VectorCraft's commit, which holds none of StitchCraft's sources. The test of `REQ-CLI-001` failed there, because it took a tree without StitchCraft's own `.git` for one without a commit. Sources unpacked in a home folder kept in git would name that folder's commit too.

The rehearsal runs only on pull requests that touch `xtask`, manifests or tooling. #89, which brought the commit in (CLI-14), touched none of them, so #90 was the first pull request to run it since.

Reproduced on a copy of `main` (053f6be) inside a new repository, as the rehearsal places it. The build named commit `fbe457f176ea`, the enclosing repository's, which `stitch --version` showed too (`stitch 0.0.1 (commit fbe457f176ea)`). The test failed with `commit "fbe457f176ea"`, as in #90's run.

## The fix

`build.rs` names the commit only when git tracks `build.rs`, and the test asks git the same. A checkout names its commit as before. A copy without git, as cargo-mutants builds, and a copy that git does not track name none.

## Tests (conformance first)

`binary.rs::req_cli_001_a_bundle_names_the_commit_its_stitchcraft_was_built_from`, changed first, failed on the copy inside a new repository with the old `build.rs` (`left: true, right: false`). It passes there with the fix, with no commit named, and in a checkout, where `stitch --version` names the checkout's commit.

## Golden files and the machine

Nothing that sews changes.

## Docs

`build.rs`'s comment defining a checkout, the test's, and the changelog.

author: davidmeirlevy
body:
## Problem
Mongoose creates missing indexes but never drops old ones. After #222 replaced `{ tenant, indexes }` with `{ tenant, blueprint, indexes }`, the old `tenant_1_indexes_1` stays on every entity collection (legacy, 16 buckets, 4 log collections) and keeps costing writes, unless someone drops it by hand in every environment.

## Change
`dropObsoleteEntityIndexes()` (new `entity-index-cleanup.service`) runs once at startup, in the background (`index.ts`, right after `connect()`):

- For each registered entity collection it waits for `model.init()`, i.e. for the schema's own indexes (including the replacement) to be built.
- It drops an obsolete index only if its replacement already exists, so queries are never left without an index.
- Dropping an index that is already gone is ignored (several instances can start together); any other failure is logged and never fails startup.
- Rolling deploys are safe: the replacement serves every query the old index did.
- Future replaced indexes are one line in `OBSOLETE_ENTITY_INDEXES`.

## Notes
- On a large production legacy collection, the new index is built on the first start after deploy, and the old one is dropped only once that build finishes. That can take a while on millions of rows; the service stays up meanwhile because the work is in the background.
- The legacy collection's two other stale indexes (`tenant_1`, `tenant_1_blueprint_1`) are not touched: they are prefix-redundant, not replaced. They can be added to the list if wanted.

## Testing
- 81 unit tests in apps/no-code (4 new: drop when the replacement exists, keep while it is missing, nothing to do when already gone, never target an index the schema still defines).
- Live against the dev stack: recreated the old index on the legacy collection, a bucket and a log collection, restarted the service, and all three were dropped while all 21 collections kept the new index. A second restart stayed healthy. The relation and cross-collection scenarios still pass.
- Not exercised live: a collection whose replacement is missing (Mongoose builds it first); covered by a unit test only.

## Summary

The agent and the connector each carried a copy of the update loop, paced by `time.Sleep(24h)`, so no test could get past the first check. Both now call one `selfupdater.Watch` that waits on a tick channel and owns the `latest` gate:

```diff
 agent / connector (main.go)
-  if AgentVersion != "latest"
-    go loop: check, apply if newer, time.Sleep(24h)
+  ticker := time.NewTicker(24h)
+  go selfupdater.Watch(ctx, logger, AgentVersion, current, check, updater, ticker.C)

+selfupdater.Watch
+  return if version is "latest"
+  loop: check, apply if newer, wait for a tick or ctx
```

`TestWatch` passes a channel it sends on. I picked this over a `SHELLHUB_` interval variable, which would have let `tests/` drive a real agent, because nobody outside the tests needs that setting. The existing `TestAgentUpdateCheck/a_versioned_agent_checks_the_server's_version_as_it_starts` still proves that `main` wires `Watch` in, because the startup check runs through it.

Log lines keep their messages and fields, except the line logged before each wait: it now reads "Waiting for the next update check" instead of "Sleeping for 24 hours", because `Watch` does not know the interval it is handed. `TestAgentUpdateCheck` matches the new text.

Two behaviour changes:
- The next check comes 24 hours after the previous tick, not 24 hours after the previous check finished.
- The loop ends when the command's context ends.

Part of shellhub-io/team#243 (Self-Update: "Agent checks for updates every 24 hours").

## Evidence

`TestWatch` in `agent/pkg/selfupdater`, run in `golang:1.26.9-alpine3.24` with `-tags docker -count=5`:

```text
a versioned agent checks again after the interval
  start Watch at 0.20.0, server reports 0.21.0
  expect 1 check
  send one tick
  wait for 0.21.0 to be applied twice, expect 2 checks

an agent reporting latest never checks for updates
  Watch returns before its context ends
  expect 0 checks, 0 applies
```

- **Before (break 1: return after the first tick, never check again):**
  ```text
  --- FAIL: TestWatch/a_versioned_agent_checks_again_after_the_interval (1.00s)
      Error:    Condition never satisfied
      Messages: the agent did not check again after the interval
  --- PASS: TestWatch/an_agent_reporting_latest_never_checks_for_updates (0.00s)
  ```
  **Before (break 2: remove the `latest` gate):**
  ```text
  --- FAIL: TestWatch/an_agent_reporting_latest_never_checks_for_updates (1.00s)
      Error:    the latest agent is watching for updates
  --- PASS: TestWatch/a_versioned_agent_checks_again_after_the_interval (0.00s)
  ```
  **After (restored):**
  ```text
  --- PASS: TestWatch/an_agent_reporting_latest_never_checks_for_updates (0.00s)
  --- PASS: TestWatch/a_versioned_agent_checks_again_after_the_interval (0.00s)
  ok  github.com/shellhub-io/shellhub/agent/pkg/selfupdater
  ```
- The integration test still passes against the new wiring (one-off `test` runner):
  ```text
  --- PASS: TestAgentUpdateCheck (44.47s)
      --- PASS: TestAgentUpdateCheck/a_versioned_agent_checks_the_server's_version_as_it_starts (10.73s)
      --- PASS: TestAgentUpdateCheck/an_agent_reporting_latest_never_checks_for_updates (9.77s)
  ```
- `golangci-lint` v2.14.0 on `agent/` and `agent/pkg/selfupdater`, with and without `-tags docker`: 0 issues.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Nothing changes on the wire, on disk or in the API. Reverting restores the old loops.

**Blast Radius:** self-update

If something goes wrong, agents stop checking for updates or check at the wrong cadence. The unit test covers both cases, and the integration test covers the check at startup.

author: forstmeier
body:
# Overview

## Changes

- `parse_ticks <provider> <kind> <session> <raw file> <parquet file>` streams a local copy of a raw tick object (Massive flat file or Alpaca tee) through the existing parsers into Parquet, one million rows per row group, in the raw file's order.
- `archive::ticks` holds the trade and quote schemas: every vendor code as served, a one-sided quote's unpriced side null, and read-back for the seam.
- The seam reads the written file back, folds it through `TradeFold` (the archive's newest conditions table) or `QuoteFold` (the session's hours from Alpaca's calendar), and compares with the archive's one-minute bars; any one-sided bar, difference, or unfoldable tick exits non-zero.
- No S3 transfer code: copying in and out is the job script's, and the output goes under a scratch prefix no lifecycle rule touches.
- Reverting this commit undoes it.

## Context

Second of two pull requests for parsed ticks (formulation task F56), after #1320 (merged); replaces #1322, closed when its base branch was deleted. The permanent key, storage class, nightly writer and sort order wait until a study shows the data earns them. Runs in-region on the researcher host (#1321, merged) next.

## Measurement

Laptop, release build, against `oscm-fund-archive` raw objects restored from Deep Archive, session 2026-10-09:

| Input | Ticks written | Refused | Seam (both / ticks only / archive only / differing) | Time |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Alpaca trades, 1.5 GB gz | 108,751,349 | 0 | 2,868,163 / 0 / 0 / 0 | 341 s |
| Alpaca quotes, 3.3 GB gz | 367,352,215 (11,611 one-sided) | 29,931 (quote) | 4,900,398 / 0 / 0 / 0 | 1,520 s |

Massive sessions are untested here: the archive holds no Massive minute bars after 2026-10-05 yet (F2 derives them), so their seam would read as not checked.

author: roninsightrx
body:
closes #577

## Why
`ferx_save_fit()` copied the model file at `fit$model_path` as it was at save time. If the file was edited after `ferx_fit()`, the bundle's `model.ferx` no longer matched its own `model_hash`: on reload the theta level layout could not be made (#531), and `ferx_sir()` / `ferx_covariance()` refused the fit. #576 added a save-time `ferx_model_edited_warning` that made this visible. This PR removes the cause: the bundle always carries the bytes that were fitted, as ferx-core's own `io::fitrx::save_fit()` does with its in-memory source string.

## What changed
- **Glue (`ferx_rust_fit`)**: `model_hash` and `model_text` now come from **one** `std::fs::read()` of the model file (`sha256_bytes` over those bytes, `model_text` = the same bytes as UTF-8). Before, they were two separate reads (`sha256_file` + `read_to_string`), so the text was not guaranteed to be the hashed bytes. A model file that is not UTF-8 gets no `model_text`, as before.
- **Glue, new binding `ferx_rust_sha256_text(text)`**: the engine's `sha256_bytes` over a string's UTF-8 bytes. Internal (`@keywords internal`, not exported); wrapper added to `R/extendr-wrappers.R` in the existing style.
- **Writer (`ferx_save_fit()`)**: new `.fitrx_fitted_model_text(fit)` returns `fit$model_text` only when its bytes hash to `fit$model_hash`. If so, `model.ferx` is written from it with `writeBin()`, byte for byte (CRLF, BOM and a missing trailing newline included). Otherwise the old path runs unchanged: copy the file, with #576's `ferx_model_edited_warning` when it no longer matches; with no file, `writeLines(fit$model_source)`.
- **Loader (`ferx_load_fit()`)**: `fit$model_text` is now the bundled `model.ferx` bytes exactly (`.fitrx_read_model_text()`), not `readLines()` + `paste()`. A reloaded fit therefore re-saves the same bytes through the new path. `fit$model_source` is unchanged. The `readLines()` text is still the fallback when the bytes are not a valid UTF-8 string.
- **Docs**: `?ferx_save_fit` paragraph rewritten; NEWS bug-fix entry.

The issue suggested a new raw `fit$model_bytes` field. I reused `fit$model_text` instead: the glue already filled it with `read_to_string()`, which keeps every byte of a UTF-8 file. A second copy of the model on every fit would add nothing. Checking the text against `model_hash` before writing it is what tells a fitted text apart from a lossy one. Those are fits loaded by an older ferx (`readLines()` text), or hand-edited fits.

## Alternatives considered
- **A new `fit$model_bytes` raw field** (the issue's proposal). Not needed, see above. It would also carry no extra guarantee, because a field can go stale too. The hash check covers that for `model_text`.
- **Hash the text in R with `tools::sha256sum()`**: needs a temp file and R >= 4.5. The glue binding uses the exact function `model_hash` was computed with, and works on every R.
- **Trust `model_text` without a hash check**: an old loaded fit's `readLines()` text would then be written over the exact file bytes and drift from `model_hash`, which is the #576 bug in another form.

## Cross-repo dependency
| Repo | PR | Status | Must merge first |
|------|----|--------|-----------------|
| ferx-core (engine) | none | not needed (uses existing `io::hash::sha256_bytes`) | — |

## Breaking changes (R users)
- [ ] Function signature changed
- [ ] Output column names / types changed (add migration note below)
- [ ] New minimum ferx-core version required
- [x] None

<details>
<summary>Migration notes (if breaking)</summary>

None. A loaded fit's `fit$model_text` now keeps the bundle's line endings (`\r\n` for a CRLF model), as a live fit's already did.

</details>

## Output changes
<details>
<summary>Before / after (if applicable)</summary>

```r
fit <- ferx_fit(model, data)              # model has a [STUDY] level block
# ... model file edited (theta lines swapped) ...
ferx_save_fit(fit, "f.fitrx")
# before: Warning ferx_model_edited_warning; bundle carries the edited file
loaded <- ferx_load_fit("f.fitrx")
# before: Warning ferx_levels_unavailable_warning "model hash mismatch";
#         loaded$theta_levels is NULL, ferx_sir(loaded) refuses
# after:  no warnings; bundle's model.ferx == the fitted bytes,
#         loaded$theta_levels laid out, ferx_sir(loaded) runs
```

</details>

## Tests
- [x] `testthat` tests added / updated
  - **T17k (new, `test-theta-levels.R`)**: for an LF, a CRLF and a no-trailing-newline two-level-block model: fit, then edit the file (theta lines swapped plus a comment). Save is quiet. The bundle's `model.ferx` is the fitted bytes and hashes to `model_hash`. Load is quiet, with the level layout made and `model_text` the exact bytes. A re-save writes the same bytes. `ferx_sir()` runs on the reloaded fit.
  - **#576 test (`test-ferx_save_fit.R`)**: an edited file no longer warns for a current fit. The warning still fires, naming the file, for a fit without `model_text` (the fallback).
  - Mutation checks (in-process, against the installed build). Mutant writer (`.fitrx_fitted_model_text` -> NULL): T17k fails on every variant. Mutant loader (`.fitrx_read_model_text` -> NULL): T17k fails on CRLF and no-EOL.
  - Full suite (`NOT_CRAN=true`, default features, `FERX_NO_AUTODIFF=1` install of this head): **8498 passed, 0 failed**, 6 skipped.
- [ ] `R CMD check` passes (no ERRORs or WARNINGs): not run locally.
- [x] Test against real ferx-core binary (not mocked)

## Example (user-facing features only)
- [ ] `@examples` block added / updated in the relevant roxygen docs
- [ ] Standalone example added to `inst/examples/` or inline below
- [x] Not applicable (internal / refactor / fix with no new API surface)

## Docs
- [x] `roxygen2` docs updated: `man/ferx_save_fit.Rd`, new `man/ferx_rust_sha256_text.Rd`. The roxygen 8.1 churn in `DESCRIPTION` / `ferx_fit.Rd` / `ferx_model_inspect.Rd` was reverted.
- [ ] Vignette updated if relevant

- [x] Not applicable (no ferx-core dependency change in this PR). `tools/check-ferx-core-pin.sh` passes at `e9156c98`.

## Reviewer hints
- The core of the change is the `model.ferx` block in `R/ferx_save_fit.R` and `.fitrx_fitted_model_text()`. The hash check is what decides between "fitted bytes" and "fallback + #576 warning".
