body:
## What changed
- Cap embedded glTF texture decoding at 1024 px per side / about 1 megapixel before bitmap allocation.
- Recycle the original decoded bitmap when a format conversion creates a replacement.
- Upload embedded textures through `GLUtils` instead of allocating an additional full-size direct `ByteBuffer` copy.
- Apply the same sampled-decode cap to standalone PBR textures and the HD texture manager, including Android resources.

## Deliberately not changed
- No `android:largeHeap="true"` without evidence of Java-heap OOM; it does not solve GPU/native-memory pressure.
- No NNAPI dependency; avoid a new dependency on a deprecated Android inference API.
- No blanket direct-buffer rewrite; direct buffers can still consume native memory.

## Verification status
This PR is not marked verified until CI/build checks pass. Physical-phone install, GL renderer stability, and end-to-end chat/image/3D workloads remain unverified and require device testing.

author: jaredklopstein
body:
## Summary
Adds five optional tool-call fields to the receipt's `provenant` extension: `issuer_kind`, `run_id`, `turn_id`, `attempt_id` and `provenance_class`. `appendReceipt` can now set them. Adds ADR 0004, which explains what the fields mean and what a receipt proves and does not prove. If a receipt is appended without the new fields, its bytes and hash are exactly what they were before this change. `pnpm run ci` passes.

**One part is not finished:** the ADR's table mapping our fields to draft-noa-scitt-ai-agent-receipt-01 has no confirmed draft-side names. The draft isn't in the repo and I couldn't fetch it (network access was denied in this run). I didn't want to guess the names, so each one is marked "(to confirm)" and the ADR says so. Someone needs to check them against the -01 text before #16 relies on them.

## Root Cause
The `ProvenantExtension` schema had nowhere to put an issuer kind, run/turn/attempt ids or a provenance class, and `AppendInput` couldn't pass them in. Simply adding the keys to a receipt would not have worked either: `verifyChain` re-hashes the zod-parsed receipt, and zod drops keys it doesn't know. Those receipts would have failed verification with `HASH_MISMATCH`. The new tests showed this failure before the fix.

## Implementation
- `packages/core/src/receipt/schema.ts`:
  - New `IssuerKind` (`sdk` | `gateway`) and `ProvenanceClass` (`attested` | `observed` | `claimed`) enums.
  - `ProvenantExtension` gains `issuer_kind`, `run_id`, `turn_id`, `attempt_id` and `provenance_class`. All are nullish, and the three ids must be non-empty strings.
  - Comments on `input_hash` and `output_hash` say that for tool calls they cover the JCS of the arguments and of the result. No new hash field names were added.
  - The AAT top level is unchanged.
- `packages/core/src/chain/append.ts`: `AppendInput` gains `issuerKind`, `runId`, `turnId`, `attemptId` and `provenanceClass`. Each one is spread into `provenant` only when it is not `undefined`, the same way the existing optional fields are handled.
- `packages/core/src/index.ts`: exports `IssuerKind` and `ProvenanceClass` next to the existing enums, because the public `AppendInput` now uses them.
- `docs/adr/0004-tool-call-receipts.md`: field meanings, the (unconfirmed) mapping table, what a receipt proves (the issuer signed it, the recorded bytes are unaltered, it is linked into the chain) and what it doesn't (that every call was captured, that the tool's effect happened, that anything was correct, legal compliance).
- The new fields are not part of the idempotency fingerprint. This is on purpose: `attempt_id` changes on every legitimate retry. The ADR explains this.

## Tests
- `packages/core/test/receipt.test.ts`, in a new `tool-call fields (ADR 0004)` block:
  - A receipt with all five fields parses without losing any of them.
  - It hashes the same way after a canonical-JSON round trip, and its signature verifies.
  - Changing any of the five fields breaks both the signature and the hash.
  - Every documented enum value is accepted; invalid `issuer_kind` and `provenance_class` values are rejected.
  - Empty or non-string ids are rejected.
  - A receipt without the new fields still validates.
- `packages/core/test/chain.test.ts`:
  - A receipt appended with all five fields, between two plain receipts, passes `verifyChain` with no failures, and none of the fields appear at the top level.
  - A receipt appended with all five inputs explicitly `undefined` matches a hand-built receipt in today's shape (same key set, signed with the same key): its stored `canonical_json` and its `self_hash` are both identical.
- `pnpm run ci` passes: boundaries, typecheck, 350 tests across all packages, and 66 offline verifier tests.

## Risks
- **Draft mapping is unconfirmed** (see Summary). The rest of the ADR doesn't depend on it.
- `issuer_kind` and `provenance_class` are what the issuer says about itself. They are signed, but nobody checks them independently; the ADR says this too.
- Old readers: a core version from before this change would drop the new fields when parsing, so `verifyChain` there would report `HASH_MISMATCH` for receipts that carry them. Receipts without the fields are not affected. The standalone verifier hashes the raw record, so it handles them either way.
- The ADR list in `AGENTS.md` still names only 0001–0003. I left it alone to keep this change scoped.

## Deployment Notes
None. The change only adds things, and existing chains need no migration. Publishing to npm is still a human step.

## Verification Plan
1. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm run ci`.
2. Check the two byte-identity assertions in `chain.test.ts`: identical `canonical_json` and `self_hash`.
3. Check the mapping table in `docs/adr/0004-tool-call-receipts.md` against the text of draft-noa-scitt-ai-agent-receipt-01, and fill in the "(to confirm)" entries.
4. Optionally, append a receipt through the library with all five fields set and run `provenant verify` on the store.

author: tamnd
body:
## Summary

The engine now shows values of the type `record[]`, for example `ARRAY[ROW(1, 'x')]` and `ARRAY(SELECT ROW(...) ...)`. Before this change, such a query gave the error that the output of `record[]` is not supported yet.

## Changes

- `record[]` is a pseudo-type, so its category in `pg_type` is `P` and not `A`. The function that finds the element type of an array now also accepts `record[]`. The text output, the binary output and the binary input of arrays now apply to it.
- The text input of `record[]` still gives the error of PostgreSQL, because the input of `record` is not implemented there.

## Known differences

None known.

## Tests

- `record_array` runs a script and compares the output with the output of PostgreSQL 19. The script has rows with null fields, quoted fields, nested rows and arrays, rows of no fields, arrays of two dimensions, `ARRAY(SELECT ...)` of rows, a subscript, a cast to text, the error for the input and the error for a view.
- fmt, clippy, the workspace tests and the checks of xtask pass on server1.

body:
## Why

PR #917 told sessions to give the owner the command that approves each waiting run. The same evening showed two gaps in a bare list of approve commands.

1. The merges of PR #914 and PR #915 left two deploys waiting. The older one carried nothing the newer one did not, so approving it would have spent an approval on a run that skips once it finds `main` has moved past its commit.
2. The newer deploy reached the VM at 18:52 ET, after the nightly stop had powered it off. It sent nothing, and needed a start, a re-run and a second approval.

The owner asked for both checks to come before the commands from now on.

## What

The "Deployment approvals" section of `CLAUDE.md` gains one paragraph with two numbered checks and two commands:

1. Suggest cancelling a deploy that a newer one covers, confirmed with `git merge-base --is-ancestor`, and give the owner the `gh run cancel` line. The same holds for a deploy whose commits change nothing the VM runs, unless an infra apply has changed the VM's tags since its last deploy.
2. Say whether the nightly stop will have powered the VM off, using the stop and start times `infra/README.md` gives, and when it will have, give the commands that start the VM and wait for it ahead of the approve command.

## Notes

The session still never approves, rejects or cancels a deployment. The cancel and the start are commands for the owner to run.

This pull request closes no issue.

author: realsyncdynamics-spec
body:
## Änderung

Folge-PR aus der Claim-to-Execution-Matrix (#1869, `docs/qa/landing-to-runtime-parity.md`, Abschnitt Website-Chatbot).

`bot-chat` ist der öffentliche Chat-Endpoint des Web-Widgets (`verify_jwt = false`). Bisher genügte das Paar `(tenant_id, bot_id)`, und beides steht im Seitenquelltext jedes Kunden mit Widget. Ein Skript in Schleife hat je Anfrage eine Einheit `limit.bot_messages_monthly` verbucht und einen bezahlten Modellaufruf ausgelöst. So ließ sich das Monatskontingent eines Mandanten leeren, und sein Bot war danach für echte Besucher aus (402).

Neu ist `supabase/functions/_shared/bot-chat-guard.ts` (Deno-frei, getestet). Alle Schranken laufen **vor** `consumeUsage` und dem Modellaufruf. Abgelehnte Anfragen kosten also weder Kontingent noch Geld.

| Schranke | Wirkung |
|---|---|
| Eingaben | `tenant_id` und `bot_id` müssen UUIDs sein. `conversation_ref` ≤ 128 Zeichen aus `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]`, `contact_label` ≤ 200 Zeichen, Nachricht ≤ 4000 Zeichen. |
| Quelle | `anonRateLimit` (Bucket `bot-chat`, 20 pro Minute je IP-Hash). Gilt nur im Arbeitsspeicher einer Instanz, also nur als Bremse. |
| Herkunft | `bots.config.allowed_origins` (opt-in). Ist eine Liste gesetzt, muss der `Origin`-Header exakt passen. Ohne Header (Skript, curl) gibt es 403. Eine **leere oder ungültige Liste sperrt**. Ohne Eintrag bleibt der Bot offen wie bisher, die Antwort meldet dann `origin_unrestricted: true`. |
| Takt (dauerhaft) | Gezählt werden die Nachrichten in `bot_messages` der letzten Minute: 10 je Konversation, 120 je Mandant. Das gilt über Instanzen und Kaltstarts hinweg. Genutzt werden die vorhandenen Indizes, es gibt **keine Migration**. Überschreitung → 429 mit `Retry-After: 60`. |
| Fehler | Bei einem 500 bekommen anonyme Aufrufer keinen internen Fehlertext mehr (Tabellen- und Constraint-Namen). Der Text geht nur ins Log. |

**Bot-Builder (`/app/bots/:botId`):** In der Karte „Integration“ gibt es das neue Feld „Erlaubte Websites für den Chat“. Es zeigt laufend an, ob der Bot offen, eingeschränkt oder gesperrt ist.

Bestehende Einbettungen brechen nicht: Ohne `allowed_origins` verhält sich der Bot wie bisher, gebremst durch Quelle und Takt.

## Typ

- [ ] `feat` · [x] `fix` · [ ] `refactor` · [ ] `chore`

## Merge-Bereitschaft

- [x] auf aktuellem `origin/main` (`6d7067c`)
- [x] `merge:hygiene` ohne Befunde
- [ ] `npm run lint` und `npm test` grün. Lokal ist `npm ci` per Repo-Policy gesperrt; gelaufen ist Vitest 4.1.5 isoliert:
  - **10 Testdateien, 207 Tests grün**: neu `test/edge/bot-chat-guard.test.ts`; dazu die vorhandenen `test/governance/bot-pep-wiring`, `test/bots/*`, `test/edge/entitlement-gates`, `test/billing/bots-quota-contract` und `entitlement-catalog-parity`.
  - `tsc --strict` auf dem neuen Modul ist sauber.
  - `check:edge-syntax` und `check:edge-refs` sind grün.
- [x] Keine Migration, kein `package.json`, kein `shared/pricing.ts`
- [x] Keine Überschneidung mit offenen PRs (kein offener PR berührt `bot-chat` oder `src/features/bots`)

`check:fabrication` ist auf `main` bereits rot. Ursache ist `src/components/landing/v5/heroEuropeNetwork3D.ts`, adressiert in #1875. Das ist nicht dieser PR.

## Risiko

- [ ] öffentliche Route / `src/App.tsx`
- [ ] Migration / RLS
- [ ] Pricing / Entitlements
- [ ] Design-Lock

**Verhaltensänderungen:**
- Ab 10 Nachrichten pro Minute in derselben Konversation bzw. 120 pro Minute je Mandant antwortet der Endpoint mit 429.
- Nicht-UUID-Kennungen bekommen jetzt 400 statt einer Datenbankantwort.

**Grenze:** Ein verteilter Angriff von vielen Adressen bleibt bis zur Mandantengrenze möglich. Die Grenze deckelt aber, wie schnell das Kontingent leerlaufen kann (120 Einheiten pro Minute statt unbegrenzt).

**Offen:**
- Wer eine fremde `conversation_ref` kennt, kann weiterhin in diese Konversation schreiben. Das verlangt eine zufällige Ref im Widget; ein Widget-Skript gibt es noch nicht.
- Staging und Produktion sind nicht verifiziert.

author: u9g
body:
## What

Two fields on `SimulationRun.List.Request`, and one on `SimulationRun`:

- `optional string scenario_group_id = 8` narrows the list to one scenario group (its `SCNG_` id).
- `bool include_scenario_outcomes = 9` fills each listed run's new `repeated ScenarioOutcome scenario_outcomes = 24`: one entry per scenario with `samples`, `passed`, `failed`, the first failure's `failure_reason`, and the `job_id` to open. `jobs` stays empty on `List`; `Get` still returns whole jobs.

## Why

The Simulations dashboard is getting a page per scenario group that shows every scenario's verdict across the group's recent runs. Today that would take one `Get` per run, since `List` has no group filter and returns no jobs. With these fields it is one `List` call. A page holds 20 runs of up to 250 jobs; whole jobs (per-turn metrics, scenario text) are several KB each and would pass NATS' 8 MB message cap. Tallies are tens of bytes per scenario, plus a failure reason only where a scenario failed.

Runs created before the agent service stored the group id carry none, so a `scenario_group_id` filter never matches them; the field comment says so.

## Follow-ups

- livekit/agents-private#579: store the group id on create, honour both fields in `ListSimulationRuns`.
- livekit/web#6617: the scenario-group cards and page that call it.

body:

_Requested by **Ronnel** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_019aVWc8jps2ktLRMK8Yo2t2?thread=cmsg_019aVWc8jps2ktLRMK8Yo2t232WBgdVdX62gWAn16KMJsV)_

Before: pressing one skill and then another right after it chained them with no pause. Berserk's casting started about 30 to 50 ms after Blessing took effect, and the 0.25 s global cooldown sweep never showed on the hotbar.

After: the next skill waits for the 0.25 s global cooldown. A skill pressed during it is accepted and starts casting the moment it ends (Berserk now starts about 0.3 s after Blessing takes effect, one server tick over 0.25 s), and every hotbar icon shows the quick sweep.

The global cooldown was written when a cast locked in (0.3 s into the casting, after the grace window from #15), but counted from the start of the casting, so it was already over when it was set.

**How:** `cast_tick` starts the player's global cooldown when a cast takes effect. `start_cast` and `advance_cast` check the skill's other conditions as of the end of the global cooldown, and `advance_cast` holds a cast that is in range until it ends instead of refusing it. Emotes, jumping and crafting still start it when used, as before. `wiki/rules/skills.md` describes the new timing, including a "Changed from iROSE" note (rose-offline counts it from the start of the casting). The bot has a new `gcd` mode that measures the gap between Blessing's effect and Berserk's casting.

Tests on a local server: `rose-stdb-bot ws://127.0.0.1:3000 gcd` gives PASS on both checks with this change (316 to 377 ms) and FAIL on main (33 to 52 ms). There's also a client recording, with main and this fix side by side.

After merging, the server (Docker) needs a rebuild. ROSE.exe doesn't.

author: fybex
body:
Adds a `crawl-smart` command that signs in to smart.ukma and stores its department, teacher, discipline and teacher-discipline lists as snapshots in the existing crawl tables. Matching teachers to offerings comes in the next PR.

Part of #767. Side PR on #784, outside GitHub stack 802 for now; it joins the stack top after #792.

<details><summary>More: how it works, how to review, what is proven</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  C[New: crawl-smart] --> M[New: microsoft/session.ts sign-in]
  M --> T[Token pair read from the redirect]
  T --> S[New: SmartClient, 4 lists]
  S --> H[Sorted-key JSON, hash]
  H --> DB[(page_snapshots, kind smart_*)]
  classDef new stroke-width:3px
  class C,M,S new
```

- **How it works:** the lists go into the crawl tables with new kinds `smart_*` and source part `smart-ukma:<date>`, one run per day. JSON is stored with sorted keys, so an unchanged list hashes the same. One failed list fails the run, since it is a quarter of the data.
- The sign-in needs no browser: the Microsoft password walk САЗ uses ends on a redirect to `/get-user?accessToken=…&refreshToken=…`, read from its `Location` header and never requested, so no span or log holds the tokens. The 5-minute access token is refreshed before expiry and after a 401 or 403, under one lock.
- The walk lives in `src/microsoft/session.ts` for both clients, with one rule: a sign-in counts only when it lands on the app with a 200 (or that redirect), and a request still signed out after a fresh sign-in fails the run instead of posting the password again. #774 adds the same rule inside `SazClient`; at the merge keep this shared version. Retries wrap each request step, never the sign-in around it.
- **Review in this order:** `microsoft/session.ts`, `smart/SmartClient.ts`, `smart/crawl.ts`, `saz/SazClient.ts`, `db/migrations/0004_smart_snapshots.ts`, `smart/SmartClient.test.ts`.
- **Proven by:** `pnpm check:all` in `src/parser`: 66 tests pass. `SmartClient.test.ts` counts password posts across refresh, two requests at once, 401 then refresh, 403 twice, a broken callback and a still-refused fresh sign-in; one test checks that tokens appear in no request or span. Against the real API on a throwaway database: 12 requests, all four lists 200 with `items` equal to `total`, run 1 stored 4 snapshots in 49 s, run 2 stored 0. That live run predates the redirect change and names no commit.
- **Decisions and open questions:** at the stack merge `0004_smart_snapshots` becomes the next free number (0008 after #792's `0007_students`), and #788's `findUndecidedRuns` is limited to `saz-courses` runs. The API host is `smart.ukma.edu.ua`, not the contract's host, which answered 403. Nothing schedules `crawl-smart` yet; daily is enough.

</details>

author: brewtestbot
body:
Created by `brew bump` --- Created with `brew bump-formula-pr`.
release notes 
### Bug Fixes

- **Security: S3 remote signing signs only what it knows.** The S3 signer signs requests only with query parameters and headers it knows, and signs a copy only when its source is inside the table. Unknown parameters and headers are refused, and so are writes that use an encryption key other than the warehouse's ([#2102](https://github.com/lakekeeper/lakekeeper/pull/2102)).
- **Remote signing with Iceberg 1.12 or later.** Clients no longer get `403 SignatureDoesNotMatch` errors when they delete more than 250 files at once, or delete files several times in a row, for example in `expire_snapshots` or `remove_orphan_files`. The signer now tells clients in the `Cache-Control` HTTP header that a signature for a write must not be reused ([#2124](https://github.com/lakekeeper/lakekeeper/pull/2124)).
- **Ranged reads with remote signing.** Clients that reuse signatures, such as Iceberg's `S3FileIO`, no longer get `403 SignatureDoesNotMatch` errors on the second ranged read of a file. The signer now leaves the `Range` header out of the signature in upper and lower case (thanks @Mohil-Ahuja) ([#2104](https://github.com/lakekeeper/lakekeeper/pull/2104)).
- **Removing the last branch or tag.** A commit that removes the last branch or tag of a table, such as `main`, is now kept. Before, the reference came back when the table was loaded again ([#2117](https://github.com/lakekeeper/lakekeeper/pull/2117)).
- **Concurrent commits to one table.** When commits to the same table block each other in the database, the client gets a `409` error, which it retries. Before, it got a `503` error ([#2117](https://github.com/lakekeeper/lakekeeper/pull/2117)).
- **UI paths.** The UI no longer serves a file for a path that contains `ui/` a second time. Such a path now returns `404` (thanks @sivakumar-mahalingam) ([#2119](https://github.com/lakekeeper/lakekeeper/pull/2119)).
- **Security updates of dependencies.** Updated `rustls` and `quinn-proto` to fix security advisories RUSTSEC-2026-0338 to -0342 and RUSTSEC-2026-0346 to -0349 ([#2125](https://github.com/lakekeeper/lakekeeper/pull/2125), [#2112](https://github.com/lakekeeper/lakekeeper/pull/2112)).

View the full release notes at https://github.com/lakekeeper/lakekeeper/releases/tag/v0.14.1.

author: lenchenalc-hongda
body:
## CPC P15 — RSC auth deduplication

Goal: remove another avoidable authenticated navigation round trip without changing authorization semantics.

### Changes
- retain trusted `profileId` + `orgId` on the server-resolved CurrentUser
- add a React request-scoped cached read-only current-user resolver
- RootLayout uses the cached resolver
- CPC server-first reads reuse that same verified profile context during the RSC render
- preserve `resolveCpcProfile` as the fallback verification path for non-Supabase/test compatibility
- preserve all org filters / RLS / route mutation authorization
- extend existing CPC CI contract coverage

### Why
Before this pass, a CPC server navigation could resolve auth/profile in RootLayout and then repeat auth/profile in the page's server read. This pass deduplicates those two within the same RSC request.

No Production DB/schema/RLS/data changes.
No env/secrets changes.
No authorization weakening.

author: ragnorc
body:
Fixes #1023

## Problem

`commit publish` and `commit drop` are writes: the CLI dispatches both through `GraphClient::resolve_with_policy` with `cli.as_actor`, and the engine runs them through `publish_commit_as` / `drop_commit_as`. The plane guard in `crates/omnigraph-cli/src/planes.rs` classified every `Command::Commit` as a read and refused `--as`, so on a direct graph these two commands could only take `operator.actor`, and the `--as` path was unreachable. The GQ spelling (`mutate -e 'commit publish "<id>"' --as X`) already accepted it.

## Change

- The `--as` row of the guard now matches the `commit` subcommands exhaustively: `publish` and `drop` take `--as`; `list`, `show` and `changes` still refuse it. A new `commit` subcommand will not compile until it is classified.
- `command_label` descends into `commit`, so guard errors name the subcommand (`` `commit list` is a data command; --as … does not apply ``).
- The comment that called all of `commit` a read is corrected, as is the parity harness's read list in `tests/support/mod.rs`, which mirrors the guard.
- A served publish or drop still refuses `--as` in `resolve_with_policy_scope` before any request; the test verifies this.

## What `--as` does here

A publication records no publisher. The published commit keeps the `actor_id` and `created_at` of the write that created it, as the unpublished-commits RFC specifies, and a drop records no actor. On these commands `--as` names the actor for the engine's `commit_publish` / `commit_drop` policy check. A direct CLI open installs no policy, so nothing about the commit changes on a direct graph. The branching guide now states that a published commit keeps its original actor.

## Tests

- `planes::tests::scope_flag_matrix_matches_capabilities_issue_1023` (renamed owner): rows for `commit list`, `show`, `publish` and `drop`.
- `cli_data::commit_publish_and_drop_take_as_on_a_direct_graph_issue_1023`:
  - proposes a commit with `--as act-author` and publishes it with `--as act-reviewer`; the published commit is on `main` with `actor_id` `act-author`;
  - drops a second proposal with `--as`; it no longer resolves and the unpublished listing is empty;
  - `commit list/show/changes --as` are refused;
  - served `commit publish/drop --as` are refused before any request.
- Both tests failed before the fix with `` `commit` is a data command; --as … does not apply ``.

Run locally:
- `RUST_MIN_STACK=16777216 cargo test -p omnigraph-cli -p omnigraph-server --bin omnigraph`: 165 passed.
- The new test, the `--as`/Blob tests in `cli_data`, and all 37 `parity_matrix` rows pass. Under heavy machine load some parity rows first hit the 30 s server-readiness deadline; each passed on rerun.
- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy -p omnigraph-cli --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings -W clippy::dbg_macro`, `scripts/check-docs.py` and `typos` are clean.

No Lance domain is involved: the change is CLI argument classification only.

author: nachonorris
body: Adds the Fluxis BLE payment SDK. A POS (**collector**) hands the NASPIP token for the current sale to a nearby wallet (**payer**) over Bluetooth LE. The wallet then resolves and pays the token through the Fluxis API, exactly as if it had scanned the QR. > **Source note:** the private `TeroMinds/pos` repository was not accessible from this environment ("Could not resolve to a Repository"). Everything here was built from the protocol description in the task, not from the TeroKiosk code. Per the owner's follow-up, backward compatibility with TeroKiosk and the current Fluxis iOS app is **not** a goal. This is a clean protocol, **v3**, and receivers reject the prototype's version bytes 1 and 2. ## What's in it | Path | Contents | |---|---| | `docs/ble-protocol.md` | Normative spec, v3: one fixed GATT service (RECORD read / CONTROL write / DATA indicate), strict discovery record with amounts as `u64` minor units + `scale` + currency, ephemeral P-256 ECDH → HKDF over a transcript hash → AES-256-GCM DATA + HMAC ACK, framing (`frame ≤ MTU−3`), collector phases and re-arm rules, timeouts, security analysis (including the unauthenticated key exchange limitation), and NFC carriage. | | `packages/ble/test-vectors/` | Python reference implementation and deterministic `vectors.json`: amounts, records, framing, messages, and three full handshakes at MTU 23/185/247/517. CI fails if the file is stale. | | `packages/ble/kotlin/` | `us.fluxis:fluxis-ble-core` (pure JVM: codecs, crypto, sans-IO `CollectorEngine` + `PayerSession`) and `us.fluxis:fluxis-ble-android` (minSdk 26: `FluxisBleCollector`, `FluxisBlePayer`, `FluxisBlePermissions`). | | `packages/ble/swift/` | `FluxisBLECore` (CryptoKit on Apple, swift-crypto on Linux; `PayerFlow` over a `FluxisBLELink` protocol) and `FluxisBLE` (CoreBluetooth `FluxisBLEPayer`; the iOS collector is a scaffold only). | | CI | `sdk-ble-kotlin.yml` (vector freshness, JVM tests, Android unit tests, lint with `NewApi`/`MissingPermission` fatal, release AAR) and `sdk-ble-swift.yml` (macOS build + tests, iOS build, Linux core tests). | | Release | release-please components `ble-kotlin` and `ble-swift` (`simple`, `version.txt`, `bump-minor-pre-major`, include-paths cover the vectors and the spec). Publish jobs: GitHub Packages for Kotlin; for Swift, a mirror to `fluxisus/fluxis-ble-swift`, because SwiftPM needs `Package.swift` at the repository root. This is the same pattern as the Go SDK. | | Docs | READMEs (overview, Kotlin with Clover/targetSdk 29 permission notes, Swift), `packages/ble/CLAUDE.md`, the openspec change `openspec/changes/ble-payment-sdk/` (`validate --strict` passes), and root `CLAUDE.md`/`README.md`/`llms.txt`/`Makefile` entries. | The existing backend and frontend SDK packages are untouched. Outside `packages/ble/`, the only changes are repo-level config: release-please config, manifest and workflow, two new workflows, `Makefile`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `llms.txt`. ## Public API **Clover / TeroKiosk (Android collector)** ```kotlin val collector = FluxisBleCollector(context) // Options(txPowerLevel, rearmOnFailure, logger) collector.start(token, FluxisAmount.parse("12.50", "ARS"), "Café Tero", ttlSeconds = 120) collector.state // StateFlow // idle → preparing → ready → claimed → awaiting_ack → delivered | expired | stopped | failed collector.stop(); collector.release() FluxisBlePermissions.missing(context, FluxisBleRole.COLLECTOR) // knows API 26–35 and targetSdk ≤ 30 hosts ``` **Fluxis wallets (payer)** ```kotlin // Android val delivery = FluxisBlePayer(context).claimNearest() // or discover() + claim(candidate); scan(): Flow delivery.token // FluxisBlePayerException(reason, collectorError) on failure ``` ```swift // iOS let delivery = try await FluxisBLEPayer().claimNearest() // or discover() + claim(_:) delivery.token // FluxisBLEPayerError(reason, collectorError) on failure ``` ## Verification - **Kotlin:** 29 core tests (every vector, plus 22 `CollectorEngine` scenarios: busy, re-arm, timeouts, bad ACK, ACK before the indication confirmation, linger, expiry) and 7 permission-table tests. Android lint is clean at minSdk 26 and the release AAR builds. A local Maven publish produces a correct POM. A deliberately corrupted vector makes the suite fail. - **Swift:** 19 tests (every vector, plus `PayerFlow` against an in-memory collector built from the vectors: each MTU, busy, rejected, expired, timeout + ABORT, tamper + ABORT). They pass on Linux and on macOS (CryptoKit) in CI, and fail when a vector is corrupted. In CI, `FluxisBLE` (CoreBluetooth) compiles with no warnings for macOS and iOS (Xcode 16.4). Locally it is also clean under `-strict-concurrency=complete`. - **Vectors:** `generate_vectors.py --check` runs in CI. - **Mirror:** the Swift snapshot was tested locally the same way the release job tests it. ## Not verified - **No on-device BLE testing at all.** Advertising, GATT server and indications on Clover Flex 4 (Android 13) and PTA0010 (Android 10), real MTU negotiation, the CoreBluetooth payer on an iPhone, and Android ↔ iOS interop. The manual test plan is section 5 of `openspec/changes/ble-payment-sdk/tasks.md`. - **Android Bluetooth adapters** (`FluxisBleCollector`, `FluxisBlePayer`, `GattClient`) are compiled and linted, but there are no instrumented tests. All protocol logic underneath them is unit-tested. - **Swift `FluxisBLEPayer` / `PeripheralLink`** compile on Apple platforms. Their behaviour against real CoreBluetooth callbacks is untested. - **Release jobs** haven't run. Before the first Swift release, create `fluxisus/fluxis-ble-swift` and add the `BLE_SWIFT_MIRROR_TOKEN` secret. Kotlin consumers need a GitHub token with `read:packages` to download from GitHub Packages. ## Notes for reviewers - The base is `main`, as requested. `CLAUDE.md` says feature work normally lands on `development`, so retarget if you prefer that flow. - Security: the key exchange is unauthenticated (spec §8). Wallets **must** show the merchant and amount from the Fluxis API's resolution of the token, not from the BLE record. A core-api signature over the record is the suggested v4 follow-up.

author: lucasheriques
body:
## Problem

PostHog/charts#17629 lets managed reverse proxy domains serve hosted survey links. Without a guard, any project's survey would render on any customer's proxy domain, so anyone could put their own survey on another company's domain.

## Changes

- On a managed proxy domain, a survey renders only if the survey's organization owns that domain. Otherwise it gets the existing "Survey not available" 404.
- The app host and domains with no proxy record (self-run proxies) are unchanged.
- The guard reads the raw `Host` header. `get_host()` would trust a client-sent `X-Forwarded-Host`.
- Records count in any status, because a route stays live while its record is `DELETING` or retrying.
- Proxy registration now rejects a domain that's already registered in any case, and stores new domains lowercase. The unique constraint is case-sensitive, so a case variant could otherwise squat another org's domain, even in a concurrent race.

> [!NOTE]
> Only visible change before the charts PR ships: registering a taken domain returns a 400 instead of a 500.

## How did you test this code?

`test_external_surveys.py` and `test_proxy_record.py` pass on a devbox. Each new case was seen failing first against the code it guards against. Not yet tested on a real proxy domain. That happens after PostHog/charts#17629 deploys.

**Test rationale:** the new parameterized tests catch a dropped ownership check, trusting `X-Forwarded-Host`, filtering by status, case-sensitive matching, and case-variant registration. The closest existing test, `test_assets_load_from_app_origin_behind_reverse_proxy`, covers asset URLs only.

## Release status

- No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

- Skills: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`.
- Not added: a `Lower(domain)` index. The table holds one row per managed proxy, and the index needs a migration on a core model.
- Test data is invented (`example.com`). No duplicate PR found.

author: indenex
body:
CraftCheck fails intermittently with "Crafting check FAILED: building the ClaimMarker: Out of reach" (seen on #219 and #311; the build is refused for 60 s).

**Cause.** `BuildHere` lays the structure out, then walks to (site.X, site.Z + 2) and calls `Build`. `WalkTo` stops as soon as it is within 1.5 m of its target, so it can end up to 1.5 m short. If the bot comes from the +Z side, it ends 3 to 3.5 m from the structure's middle, outside the 2.2 m work reach (`Structures.WorkReach`). Which side it comes from depends on which candidate spot the (now hilly) land makes valid first, so the failure depends on the spawn and not on the PR under test.

**Fix.** In the `Build` loop, when the server says "Out of reach", the bot walks up to the structure (`WalkTo(s.X, s.Z)` stops 1 to 1.5 m from its middle) and carries on. Nothing is relaxed: the server's reach rule is the same, the bot just stands where the rule allows, and any other refusal still fails the check after the 60 s.

CraftCheck builds. The failing layout is spawn-dependent, so CI is the real proof. Tool only; no server change, no wipe.

body:
Las tarjetas del catálogo y el carrusel se ven a unos cientos de píxeles pero descargaban la foto original, que puede pesar varios MB. Dos commits.

### 1. Backend: al subir una foto se guarda también una copia reducida (`d6f068c`)
- Puerto `ReductorDeImagen` + `ReductorImageIO` (ImageIO de Java, **sin dependencias nuevas**): JPEG de máx. 1200 px de ancho, calidad 0.82, reducción en varios pasos, orientación del celular aplicada a los píxeles, PNG transparente sobre el fondo de la web.
- `UploadImageUseCase` guarda la original igual que antes (sin recomprimir) y al lado `<uuid>.min.jpg`. Si la copia no se puede hacer (WebP: Java no lo lee) o falla al guardarse, la subida sigue. **La respuesta de `POST /api/imagenes` no cambia** y no hay migración.
- `CLAUDE.md`: regla de las fotos al día.

### 2. Frontend: tarjetas, carrusel y tarjeta al compartir usan la copia (`55a3dc9`)
- `lib/fotos.ts` (`fotoReducida`) + hook `useFotoReducida`: copia para JPG/PNG del almacén; si no carga (fotos subidas **antes** de este cambio), vuelve a la original y la apunta para no pedirla otra vez.
- `ProductCard` y `CarruselPortada` (y su precarga) la usan. La ficha y la ampliación siguen con la original.
- `api/obra.ts`: la tarjeta al compartir usa la copia si existe (comprobada con un `HEAD`).

## Comprobado
- Backend `./mvnw test`: 154 tests en verde (ArchUnit incluido). Nuevos: copia guardada con su nombre, orientación pasada, subida que sigue sin copia o si la copia falla; reductor con imágenes reales (3000×2000 → 1200×800 y más ligera, no agranda, giro de celular 6, ancho medido sobre la foto girada, PNG transparente, WebP/basura sin copia).
- Frontend: `npm run build` pasa, `npm test` 68/68, `oxlint` sin avisos nuevos, `qa:rapido` sin hallazgos.
- `api/obra.ts` con almacén simulado: con copia → `.min.jpg`; sin copia → original.

## Ojo
Las fotos ya subidas **no tienen copia**: siguen cargando la original (con una petición fallida a la copia la primera vez por foto). Para que también vayan ligeras hay que volver a subirlas desde el panel.

author: vorstand-boris-bot
body:
## Found on the way

**A guard bypass, not a panic:** the peer client's private-address guard let `https://[::1]a/…`-style URLs through to loopback and private addresses. It ships separately in #108, with the properties of `peer_client.rs` (`authority`, `literal_is_private`, `is_localhost`, the media type) that found it. This PR doesn't touch `peer_client.rs`. No property here found a panic.

**`arbitrary_frames` never runs a handler.** I added a temporary `eprintln!` at the top of `handlers::dispatch`, and it printed 0 times over its 512 cases. Its incoming stream ends as soon as the frames are read, so the connection closes before any call task is polled. Even when a handler does run, a panic becomes an `INTERNAL` answer, and that property drops the answers. It still covers the prost decode and the connection loop. The new property covers the handlers.

## What this adds

Spec 7 §7 / D16: every decoder of input from outside the process gets a "never panics on arbitrary input" property. All properties have at most 512 cases.

### `tests/rpc_frames.rs::owner_calls` (256 cases, about 3 s)

This property runs as `Caller::Owner`, like the IPC socket, so calls get past authentication and their fields reach the handlers' parsing. Each case:

- Sets up a node in memory: `ManualClock`, `SeededRng`, a stored node key, the hostname `node.example`, its engine running (`engine::run`) and the stub ledger active, so that the methods behind the engine and Open Payments answer instead of returning UNAVAILABLE or "no hostname".
- Sends 1 to 7 `ClientMessage`s built from valid `Request`s. The fields are arbitrary or near-valid: any Unicode, control and direction characters, empty strings, strings of 257 to 70,000 characters, known values (ledger names, scheme IDs, table names, currencies, rate sources) in another case, padded, or with a character replaced, inserted or cut off; UUID-shaped IDs with odd characters, multibyte or wrong lengths; numbers at 0, 1, `u32::MAX`, `2^63` and `u64::MAX`; PEM as any text, blocks of any base64, and a real certificate or key with a character changed.
- Keeps the connection open until every call has answered, a live stream with its first item, then ends it.
- Asserts that the connection ends `ByClient` or `ProtocolError`, that every call answered, that **no answer is `INTERNAL`**, and that the engine task ended without a panic. A handler's panic is caught by `catch_unwind` and answered as `INTERNAL` ("only bugs are INTERNAL"), so the closing reason alone would never show it.

Every method in the proto is sent. Some only with fields that start no network IO:

- `GetAcmeTerms` and `ObtainCertificate`: only with directory URLs that `DirectoryUrl::parse` refuses. An empty URL means the default directory, and a valid one starts an ACME order.
- `AddSettlementScheme` and `RemoveSettlementScheme`: never the XRP Ledger's scheme, which connects to the ledger.
- `ResolveRecipient` and `QuoteSend`: only recipients the node reads without IO. These are text that is no recipient, this node's own wallet addresses and payment requests (in any case, with `:443`), or other wallets at private IP literals, which the peer client refuses before connecting.
- `SetHostname`: any text, but no valid hostname other than the node's own (another one would make "own" URLs remote).

I counted the answers per method over one run. Most methods reach their success path as well as their refusals: for example `SetDefaultLedger`, `StubDeposit` (including "the account's total would overflow"), `BanNode` (including "a node cannot ban itself"), `ResolveRecipient` for this node's own wallet address, `SetRealm`, `SetPeerSettings` and `SetRateSources`. Every live stream sends an item.

### In-module properties

| Decoder | Property | Input |
|---|---|---|
| `http::response::{header_values, header_str, header_has_token}` | `any_headers_are_read` | any bytes a header value may hold; lists of tokens with commas, quotes, space, case and parameters; repeated headers |
| `http::api` media type of `json_body` (moved into `is_json`, behaves as before) | `any_media_type_is_read` | the same, on `Content-Type` |
| `http::ws::{is_upgrade, handshake_key}` (now generic over the body, so a test can build a request) | `any_handshake_is_read` | the same, with valid handshake headers filled into some cases so that some are handshakes |
| `engine::core::incoming::parse_tag` | `any_tag_is_read_or_refused`, `tags_read_back` | any bytes, also through `admission`; round trip of `connection_tag` |
| `tls::load` / `load_valid` (the PEM from `SetCertificate`) | `any_pem_is_loaded_or_refused` | any text, PEM blocks of any base64 under any label, the real certificate and key with a character changed, the real certificate with DER bytes changed or cut short |
| `tls::inspect` | `any_der_is_inspected_or_refused` | the real DER changed or cut short, and any bytes |
| `open_payments::WalletAddresses::{ledger_of_path, ledger_of_url}`, `Urls::own_path` | `any_path_names_an_active_ledger_or_none`, `any_url_names_an_own_ledger_or_none`, `any_url_is_own_or_not` | this node's paths and near variants (case, trailing slash, `%`-escapes, query), origins in another case, with `:443`, with a suffix, over `http`, and any text |

Besides "no panic", each property asserts something cheap about the result. For example: a ledger is found only for one of the node's wallet addresses, `parse_tag` takes exactly the 16- and 32-byte tags, a handshake key is the header's, a JSON media type starts with `application/json`.

## Reachability checks

I added each panic below temporarily, checked that the property failed, then removed it:

- `rpc/payments.rs`, `CompleteIncomingPayment`: `PaymentId::parse(&request.id).filter(|_| panic!())`. `owner_calls` failed with `INTERNAL` and shrank to `CompleteIncomingPayment { id: "aAa00AaA-Aa0A-AAaA-A00A-0a00A0A0AA0A" }`. So valid-looking IDs reach the parse, with a hostname and the engine running.
- `rpc/payments.rs`, `set_default_ledger`: `assert!(request.ledger.is_empty())` just before `LedgerId::parse`. `owner_calls` failed on `SetDefaultLedger { ledger: "STUB+USD" }`.
- `engine/core/incoming.rs`, `parse_tag`: a panic in the 32-byte branch. Both of its properties failed.
- `tls.rs`, `inspect`: a panic inside the loop over the subject alternative names, for `CertificateSource::Manual` only, which is what the properties use. Both TLS properties failed, so changed PEM and DER get through the X.509 parser to the names.
- `http/ws.rs`, `handshake_key`: a panic when it returns a key. `any_handshake_is_read` failed. The first version of the strategy never made a full handshake. That is why it now fills in valid headers.
- `open_payments`, `ledger_of_url`: a panic when it finds a ledger. `any_url_names_an_own_ledger_or_none` failed.

## Known, and left for later

These decoders read the node's own data, not input from outside the process, so they are out of scope here:

- the DB row readers in `crates/dassie-node/src/store/*`
- the env parsers (`env.rs`) and the log parsers (`log.rs`)
- the `dassie-cli` parsers: `LastUpdate::parse`, `status::amount`, `Client::receive`

## Verification

`cargo test --locked -p dassie-node` (full suite), `cargo clippy --locked -p dassie-node --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`.

author: khaledsaeed18
body:
## Summary

Fixes BUG-001 to BUG-005 from `docs/plans/01-correctness-and-robustness.md` (#24). Several malformed or non-conformant tokens either crashed the CLI or verified as valid; `--json` failure paths printed human panels.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes

- Header and payload must be JSON objects (new code `invalid_json_object`); `sign` enforces the same for `--payload`/`--header`.
- `NaN`, `Infinity`, and overflowing numbers are rejected when parsing tokens and `sign` input (new code `invalid_number`). Previously a signed token with `exp: NaN` verified as valid. Deeply nested JSON and over-long integers fail as `invalid_json` instead of raw tracebacks.
- `verify`: a token is expired once `now >= exp + leeway` (RFC 7519 4.1.4); booleans are not NumericDates in `verify` or `audit`.
- `verify` rejects any `crit` header and `b64` other than `true` (RFC 7515 4.1.11, RFC 7797).
- `alg` is matched case-sensitively in `verify` and JWK selection (RFC 7515 4.1.1). `sign` now always emits the alg it signed with.
- `verify --json`, `audit --json`, and unreadable `@path` tokens emit the JSON error envelope (new codes `unsupported_algorithm`, `invalid_key_options`, `key_error`, `token_unreadable`).

Compatibility: no existing field or code changed, so `JSON_SCHEMA_VERSION` stays `0.1`. Tokens with a lowercase `alg`, a `crit` header, or `exp` exactly equal to now are now rejected; these are correctness fixes and worth a release note.

## How to test

```bash
make check
```

The reproduction script at the end of `docs/plans/01-correctness-and-robustness.md` now reports controlled errors or `invalid` for every case.

## Checklist

- [x] I read CONTRIBUTING.md and followed the branch and commit conventions.
- [x] `make check` passes locally (lint, typecheck, tests, security scan, dependency audit).
- [x] I added or updated tests for the change.
- [x] I did not introduce new runtime dependencies.
- [x] This PR does not contain real secrets, private keys, or production tokens.

author: paulbellamy
body:
These are the two changes an autoresearch loop kept, plus one bug fix the benchmark exposed. The loop proposed changes, ran headless agents against the binary, measured the result and kept or discarded each change. Its goal was to make the CLI cheaper and more intuitive for agents to use.

## Changes

1. **Slim SKILL.md and `mcp --help`.**
   - SKILL.md goes from 9775 to 3240 chars. It is embedded, printed by `mcp --skill`, and primed agents carry it on every turn.
   - `mcp --help` goes from 79 to 44 lines. Agents usually run `mcp --help | head -50`, which used to cut off the ad-hoc header hint. Now they see the whole page.
   - Auth/listen detail stays in their subcommand `--help`.
2. **New `mcp list` (alias `ls`).**
   - Prints one line per configured server with its sorted tool names, read from the cache. Servers that fail print `name: error: …`; disabled servers print `name: disabled`.
   - About 75% of agents starting cold ran `mcp --help; mcp list` first (the `claude mcp list` habit), and `list` did not exist.
   - Additive only: no existing command's output, flags or exit codes change.
3. **Fix: `warning: tools list truncated after 100 pages` printed after every complete multi-page `tools/list`.**
   - The cursor was never cleared on the last page, so any server with more than one page triggered the warning. Agents read it as "tools are missing".
   - The fix returns on the last page, the same way `listAllResources` does. The pagination test now asserts there is no warning, and it fails without the fix.
   - This one was not validated by the loop's metric (it is a stderr-only change).

## Evidence

The headless agent was `claude-haiku-5-5` with only a Bash tool and a hermetic HOME. It ran 12 fixed tasks against 9 mock MCP servers (stdio, HTTP, one broken), each task cold and with the skill preloaded, 6 reps, 144 runs per eval. Each kept change had to clear a pre-registered noise margin twice.

| | v0.13.0 | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| task pass rate | 100% | 100% |
| agent cost per run | $0.00175 | $0.00144 (−18%) |
| bash calls per run | 3.95 | 3.32 (−16%) |
| output chars read per run | 8.1k | 6.5k (−20%) |
| 5 held-out tasks (never shown to the mutators) | — | cost −14%, pass 100% |
| `claude-sonnet-5-5` cross-check | $0.0233, 3.06 calls | $0.0186, 2.65 calls (cost −20%) |

## For review

- **One regression:** lookups on resource-only servers got slightly worse, with about 0.9 more calls. `mcp list` makes a server that only exposes resources look empty. A follow-up that adds a resource count to `mcp list` replicated at +0.0055, just under the bar, so it is not included here. The ledger has details.
- **Discarded:** 11 other candidates. They include compact JSON, `call --raw`, head+tail truncation, an unknown-param warning, ad-hoc URL parity for `schema`/`-H`, help restructures and a from-scratch docs rewrite.
- **Where the full record lives:** the harness, the per-run ledger and the write-up are on the `autoresearch/agent-ux` branch, under `.autoresearch/` (`summary.md`, `results.jsonl`, `bench/`). They are deliberately left out of this PR.

`go build`, `go vet`, `go test ./...` and `golangci-lint run` all pass.

author: chelojimenez
body:
Stacked on MCPJam/inspector#6563. Inspector step **I2a** of the per-client model-context policy for plugin Apps (decision D8).

## Task, spec and plan

- **Kestral task:** None: requested directly in a Claude Code session; no Kestral task exists for this plan yet.
- **Spec:** "Per-client model-context policy for plugin Apps — implementation plan", decision D8 and step I2a (agreed before the code; not linkable from here).
- **Plan:**
  - Give `POST /api/web/apps/plugin-instances/context` and `…/model/context` their own body limit in `webBodyLimit`: the update ceiling plus 64 KiB, refused with 413 `PLUGIN_CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE`. The instance router's 512 KiB limiter skips exactly those two paths.
  - `routeUntimed` keeps the specific `PLUGIN_CONTEXT_*` / `INSTANCE_CONTEXT_*` code and returns `diagnostics` with `{budget, actual, allowed}`.
  - Add `shared/plugin-diagnostics.ts` entries for the five codes.
  - The client treats size, rate and memory refusals as known rejections, including the hosted operation limiter's `RATE_LIMITED` 429. It answers the App with `-32000 "The host could not persist the model context update"`.
  - A remove-all stops at a context refusal again, rather than re-sending it.

## User story

**As an** App author whose plugin App pushes context with `ui/update-model-context`,
**I want** an update the host can't keep to be refused cleanly,
**so that** the App can send a smaller one at once instead of being stuck until a remount.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] A refused update followed by a smaller one: the second goes through at once, and the sequence doesn't advance. Covered on the controller and through `useAppContext`, for each of the five refusal codes and for `RATE_LIMITED`.
- [x] The App receives JSON-RPC `-32000` with the host's message over the real `AppBridge`/`App` transport, not `-32603`.
- [x] An update over the byte budget is refused before it is sent, logged with `{budget: "updateMaxBytes", actual, allowed: 262144}`, and the next update succeeds.
- [x] An update the route parses and finds over a budget answers 413 `PLUGIN_CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE` with the sizes in `diagnostics`. The rate, stored-size and memory refusals keep their codes (429 / 413 / 503). An unknown outcome stays 409 `outcomeUnknown`.
- [x] A body over the context limit is refused before a stand-in for the rate limiter reads it. A body up to the limit passes, and other instance routes keep 1 MiB (outer) and 512 KiB (inner).
- [x] A remove-all stops at a `PLUGIN_CONTEXT_*` refusal, as it did when those came back as `INVALID_PLUGIN_INSTANCE_REQUEST`. The memory budget still retries, since it frees as Apps close.
- [x] Each guard was mutation-checked by disabling it in turn: inner skip, outer branch, route mapping, client mapping, known-rejection base class, pre-check, the `RATE_LIMITED` entry and the remove-all stop. Each one fails its tests.

## What this does

Before this PR, every server refusal set the controller's `uncertain` latch. `refresh()` has no production caller, so the App stayed stuck until a remount or a remove-all. The server also reported every context problem as `INVALID_PLUGIN_INSTANCE_REQUEST`, and a body over the router's 512 KiB limit surfaced as a 500.

A size, rate or memory refusal means the update was never stored. The client now treats these as `PluginContextNotPersisted`, which never sets `uncertain`. The App gets `-32000`, which is ChatGPT's answer and which the MCP SDK forwards as an integer code. `McpError` would have prefixed the message twice. Transport failures stay uncertain. The hosted operation limiter's 429 `RATE_LIMITED` counts too: it answers before the route runs, so nothing was stored.

The composer only ever shows acknowledged context, so it keeps the last accepted state. That is a deliberate difference from ChatGPT.

Admission budgets are unchanged (256 KiB, 64 blocks), so only the errors change here. The policy decides admission in I4. The descriptions say "send less context" rather than "raise the limit", because the policy has no effect yet.

**What this doesn't cover:**
- Sizes come only with a refusal the route parses (`PluginModelContextError`). The store's `INSTANCE_CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE` and `INVALID_INSTANCE_CONTEXT`, and the body-limit 413, carry no sizes. The body-limit 413 also emits no `plugin.instance.context.refused` event.
- These still reach the App as `-32603`: `PluginContextHeld` (the person removed the App's context), `INSTANCE_CONTEXT_SEQUENCE_DENIED`, and the error an App gets while an earlier outcome is unknown.
- A stored update within 13 bytes of 256 KiB that carries only `structuredContent` fails its own re-read here. MCPJam/inspector#6622, next in the stack, fixes it by re-reading against the ceilings, so the two ship together.

**Release order.** Release this before MCPJam/mcpjam-backend#2229 reaches prod. On inspector `main`, the backend's new `INSTANCE_CONTEXT_RATE_LIMITED` falls through to the `uncertain` latch, and the App is stuck until it is remounted.

**Who can reach the middleware change** (`server/middleware/` rule):
- Before: any caller of `/api/web/*` could send up to 1 MiB to the two context routes, and the instance router then refused anything over 512 KiB.
- After: the same callers, still behind the same auth and rate limits, can send up to 4 MiB + 64 KiB to exactly those two POST routes. Every other route is unchanged.

## Documentation

Nothing applicable

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  App -->|"ui/update-model-context"| Controller[model-context-controller]
  Controller -->|"over 256 KiB: -32000, nothing sent"| App
  Controller -->|"POST …/context"| Limit[webBodyLimit: ceiling + 64 KiB]
  Limit -->|"413 PLUGIN_CONTEXT_TOO_LARGE"| Controller
  Limit --> RateLimit[mcpOperationRateLimit]
  RateLimit -->|"429 RATE_LIMITED"| Controller
  RateLimit --> Route[routeUntimed]
  Route -->|"413/429/503 code + diagnostics"| Controller
  Controller -->|"known rejection: -32000"| App
```

## Screenshots and recordings

None: no UI change (the App sees a different JSON-RPC error; Logs gains a row with the budget)

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| n/a | n/a |

## Deleted

Nothing

## Reused

- `pluginErrorDiagnostic` and `describePluginError`, through a small `pluginContextRefusalDiagnostic` wrapper.
- `PluginInvocationError.diagnostics` for store refusals.
- The existing `PluginContextUpdateRejected` known-rejection path that `PluginContextHeld` already uses.
- `thread-app-api`'s existing diagnostics → Logs relay, so server diagnostics aren't logged twice.

## Production signal

`plugin.instance.context.refused`: `code`, `statusCode`, `budget`, `actual`, `allowed`, never content. A rise in its `INSTANCE_CONTEXT_RATE_LIMITED` count after B3b ships is expected. A `-32603` reported by an App on context updates should drop to zero, apart from the cases listed above.

## Checklist

- [x] I can explain every line of this diff without the agent that wrote it.
- [x] Under 400 hand-written changed lines, or labelled `large-pr` / `mechanical`. (305 per `pr-size`.)
- [x] No new `as any`, empty `catch`, `.catch(() => {})` or raw `console` on the server.
- [x] Comments say why the code is this way, not how it got here.

### Verification

- 10 test files, 149 tests: web-body-limit, plugin-context-refusal, plugin-context, plugin-model-apps, plugin-instances, model-context-controller, app-context, context-remove-all, plugin-model-context and mcp-operation-rate-limit.
- SDK: `host-app-bridge.test.ts`, 19 tests.
- `typecheck:client` is clean. `typecheck:server` has 107 errors, under its baseline of 109.
- `slop:check`: no rule went up. `repo-hygiene` warns that `plugin-instances.ts`, already over 800 lines, grows by 11.
- There's no `telemetry:check` script in this repo. The catalogs are build outputs, and the new event is typed in `server/utils/log-events.ts`.

author: everpcpc
body:
## What

Support `vertical-align: super` and `sub` as baseline shifts.

- **Parse**: the cascade now recognizes `vertical-align`. Values other than super/sub (top, middle, lengths, …) degrade to `baseline` rather than rejecting the chapter.
- **Apply**: `InlineLayout` writes the shift through `NSAttributedString`'s `baselineOffset`, so CoreText draws and positions the shifted glyphs itself. The shift amount matches WebKit (InlineLineBoxVerticalAligner): the parent box's font-size / 3 + 1 up for super, / 5 + 1 down for sub — independent of the element's own font-size, which matters for the shrunken spans EPUB superscripts typically use.
- **Line metrics**: the shifted run drags its inline box along in the line-metrics pass, growing the line box on the side it shifted towards, matching WebKit (CSS 2.1 §10.8.1).

Only horizontal writing mode shifts: vertical writing aligns runs to a central baseline where super/sub needs a different metric.

## Why

Real-world EPUBs use super/sub for footnote markers and reference glosses (found in vertical Japanese light novels and on the title pages of traditional-Chinese editions). Without the shift the markers sat on the baseline, colliding with the surrounding glyphs.

## Validation

- `xcodebuild test -scheme YueduCoreText-Package -destination 'platform=iOS Simulator,name=iPhone 18 Pro' -only-testing:YueduCoreTextTests/BrowserVerticalAlignTests` — 3 tests: superscript raises the run above the shared baseline, subscript lowers it below, and a same-size superscript grows the line box above (pushing the next line down). Assertions read the shifted run's glyph origins inside the shared CTLine, so they pin the shift itself rather than a fragment-level proxy.
- Cross-checked on this branch with the source change reverted: all 3 tests fail on the same assertions, and pass again with the change restored.
- No test-scenario adjustments were needed; the assertions hold against upstream `main` unchanged.
- The parent-font-size formula was cross-checked against WKWebView on a real EPUB title page with mixed glyph sizes: block tops/heights and line baselines match WebKit to 0.01px.

author: alexboiboi
body:
The quiver example ("Turning magnet, field arrows") stuttered while dragging on a slower Windows laptop. Every drag step redraws the arrows, and most of a step was spent building the scene in the engine. #42 already builds each colour table once; this does the rest of the studio's part, and moves the lock to the magpylib with magpylib/magpylib#1022, which is magpylib's part. Nothing drawn changes.

- **One trip a step:** the panel asked the extension host twice per drag step, once to set the pose and again for the scene it made, with a wait for the next frame in between. The pose's answer now carries the scene, as the notebook widget's already did. It does so only while the drag still redraws: once `drag.mjs` stops redrawing because a scene was slow to build, the scene is no longer built on every step for nothing, in the panel or in a notebook.
- **Lock:** magpylib at `22c727d`, which reads a sensor's pixel field once instead of three times a step here, skips it for hidden pixels, and colours pixels in one go.

```
before: previewTransform → previewDone → rpcRequest get_scene → rpcResult (scene)
after:  previewTransform {scene: true} → previewDone {scene}
```

**The engine's part of a drag step**, quiver example, on an M4:

| | per step |
|---|---|
| before #42 | 13.2 ms |
| main, with #42 | 11.6 ms |
| this branch | about 5 ms |

The crossings that go away are VS Code messages and were not measured; on the laptop they may weigh more than on the M4.

**Notes**

- The scene payload is identical before and after, for every built-in example and for the quiver mid-drag.
- The browser harness's drag check now requires one trip a step: every preview asks for the scene, and the view never asks for it on its own mid-drag. Its stub host answers with the scene, as the extension host does.
- The Python suite passes on the new lock; `npm run compile` with its checks and the browser harness pass.

## Summary

sd:4843: the machine-setup `system` stage keeps `soft=yes` and `kloglevel=1` under `[default]` in `/etc/nsmb.conf`.

- Why: two clean shutdowns stalled in `smbfs_unmount`, waiting on SMB reconnects to a NAS session that was already dead (sd:4768 decode). Soft mounts let a request to a gone server fail instead of waiting.
- Status prints `ok      nsmb.conf soft mounts` when both keys are in force. An absent file or key prints `MISSING`, which the drift grep counts, so `--fail-on-drift` sees it. The line says the setting applies at the next mount (eject and reconnect, or reboot).
- `--apply` adds only the missing keys: under the first `[default]` or `[global]`, or in a new `[default]` at the end. It keeps every other line, makes a dated `.bak-` copy first, and writes through `sudo_run`, so a refused sudo defers like the stage's other actions.
- A key set another way (`soft=no`) prints `DIFFERS` and stays: the operator's value is never replaced. A file the stage cannot read, or cannot read the way the client does, prints `DIFFERS ... state unknown` and is not written.
- `MACHINE_SETUP_NSMB_CONF` overrides the path for tests. `fixture_config.env()` points it at a fixture that is already correct, so no case reads this Mac's `/etc/nsmb.conf`.
- No new stage: the check sits in `stage_system` beside the other root-owned files.

Round 1 blocked on section semantics: the scanner lower-cased section names and ignored `[global]`. Class pass, "nsmb.conf parsing differs from Apple's parser": one awk program now serves both scan and merge and follows `rc_parse` in Apple's SMBClient `lib/smb/rcfile.c` and `readPreferences` in `lib/smb/preference.c`. Every place the stage reads or writes a section, key or value:

| Instance | Client behaviour | Stage before | Stage now | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `[global]` | same section as `[default]` | ignored; apply added a `[default]` that overrode `[global] soft=no` | read as `[default]`; keys added under it | `test_global_is_default_and_its_value_stays`, `test_global_gets_the_missing_keys` |
| section name case and spaces | `strcmp`, text between `[` and `]` kept | lower-cased, trimmed | kept; `[Default]`, `[ default ]` are other sections | `test_section_names_keep_case_and_spaces` |
| text after `]` | ignored | header not matched | ignored | `test_correct_file_is_ok_and_untouched` |
| key case | `strcmp` | kept | kept; `Soft=` does not count and `soft=yes` is added | `test_key_names_keep_case` |
| spaces around and inside a key, before a value | every space and tab in a key dropped; leading space of a value dropped | key spaces dropped | same | `test_spaces_inside_a_key_are_dropped`, `test_correct_file_is_ok_and_untouched` |
| comments | `#` or `;` first on a line only | same | same | `test_comment_lines_and_lines_without_equals_do_not_count` |
| comment after a value | part of the value | compared as text | part of the value; `yes # on` is not a boolean, so `DIFFERS` | `test_a_comment_after_a_value_is_part_of_it` |
| line with no `=` | ignored | ignored | ignored | `test_comment_lines_and_lines_without_equals_do_not_count` |
| repeated section | adds to the first; last value wins | last value in the last `[default]` | same, `[global]` included | `test_a_repeated_section_adds_to_the_first_and_the_last_value_wins` |
| key before any section, or in another section | ignored for `[default]` | same | same | `test_keys_of_another_section_or_before_any_do_not_count` |
| carriage return, no final newline | dropped; last value kept at EOF | trailing `\r` trimmed | dropped anywhere | `test_carriage_returns_are_dropped` |
| `soft` value | `rc_getbool`: first char `1`, or `yes`/`true` any case | text equal to `yes` | `rc_getbool` rules | `test_values_are_read_as_the_client_reads_them` |
| `kloglevel` value | `(int)strtol(v, NULL, 0)` | text equal to `1` | strtol base 0 with exact 32-bit halves, clamped at LONG_MAX/LONG_MIN, cast to int | `test_values_are_read_as_the_client_reads_them`, `NsmbIntPropertyTest.test_random_magnitudes` |
| `[` with no `]` on its line | header runs on to the next `]` | read as a key line | unknown; `DIFFERS`, nothing written | `test_a_header_with_no_bracket_or_a_long_line_is_unknown` |
| line over 2000 bytes | dropped past 2047 stored bytes | read | unknown; `DIFFERS`, nothing written | `test_a_header_with_no_bracket_or_a_long_line_is_unknown` |
| `~/Library/Preferences/nsmb.conf` | read first; `/etc/nsmb.conf` merged after it, so `/etc` wins for keys it sets | not read | not read, no change needed | none: no behaviour change |
| `debug_level` | read before `kloglevel`, which overrides it | not read | not read; `kloglevel=1` wins | none: no behaviour change |

The write moves state in steps. Root copies the new file beside the target, then moves it over:

| Step | State moved | Failure | Recovery | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| build the merged file as the user | temp file | mktemp or awk fails | `FAILED` line, nothing written | not covered |
| dated backup | `nsmb.conf.bak-<stamp>` | stop after | old file in place; next run backs up again and writes | `test_other_lines_kept_and_keys_added_under_default` |
| copy to `.nsmb.conf.tmp` | dotted copy beside | stop after | next run overwrites and moves it | `test_a_stop_after_the_copy_is_finished_by_the_next_run` |

## Promotion: staging -> premain (TableTheory v6, breaking major)

Staging head to promote: `5b2d5958591851a7863d0ac65f542ee23732b9fb` (merge of #723). This PR is release-intent and starts the v6 release. The operator decided on 2026-10-16 to run a full TableTheory release. It holds two breaking commits (`fix(lambda)!`, `fix(module)!`, each with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer), so release-please on premain should open a **6.0.0** RC (`versioning: prerelease`, `rc`). No CHANGELOG, manifest or version file was hand-edited.

### Why
A real consumer failed at Lambda cold start on lab (theory-mcp-server on 2026-10-16): its `facadestore` asserted `core.ExtendedDB` on the handle that `LambdaInit` returns. `*tabletheory.LambdaDB` did not implement `core.ExtendedDB`, because `LambdaDB.WithLambdaTimeout(ctx)` returned `*LambdaDB` and so shadowed the interface's `WithLambdaTimeout(ctx) DB`. No additive Go fix exists. The operator approved the breaking fix as a new major.

### Contents (#723)
- `a1e2980` **fix(lambda)!:** `LambdaDB.WithLambdaTimeout(ctx)` returns `core.DB`, with byte-identical semantics: the same 1 s default buffer, the same deadline logic and the same instance. `var _ core.ExtendedDB = (*LambdaDB)(nil)` now compiles. `WithLambdaTimeoutConfig`, `LambdaInit`, `NewLambdaOptimized` and `MultiAccountDB.Partner` still return `*LambdaDB`. TableTheory's own call sites are migrated.
- `9fe47c8` **test(lambda):** a `LambdaInit` handle used through `core.DB`/`core.ExtendedDB`, including a type assertion and `TransactWrite`, offline and against DynamoDB Local. Timeout semantics are pinned through the interface. Mutation-proven: restoring the `*LambdaDB` return fails to compile.
- `a8afe19` **fix(module)!:** the `/v6` Go module path (following the v5 precedent): every import, the docs, the examples, and the nested modules.
- `9f20512`, `22aee8c` **docs(migration):** `docs/migration/v6.md`, including a "Transitive dependencies" section.

### Compatibility and migration
- **What breaks:** the Go module path (`/v5` becomes `/v6`) and the `WithLambdaTimeout` return type. Every other exported symbol is unchanged.
- **Stored representation:** unchanged. No marshalling, key encoding or written data changed.
- **TypeScript and Python:** no API change.
- **Wave order for consumers:** a consumer can move to `/v6` only after every dependency that exposes TableTheory types in its public API has moved first, because the `/v5` and `/v6` copies of `core.DB` are distinct types. Today that dependency is AppTheory: `apptheory/v6` still takes a `tabletheory/v5` handle. The order is:
  1. TableTheory v6 is released (this PR).
  2. AppTheory adopts `tabletheory/v6` (an AppTheory major).
  3. Autheory, theory-mcp-server and TCA repin.
- **Existing v5 consumers** that do not upgrade are unaffected.

### Review and proof level
- #723 passed the paired adversary + sanity gate over 3 rounds:
  - Round 0 at `a8afe194`: adversary CLEAR, sanity BLOCK on migration-doc accuracy.
  - Rounds 1 and 2 were docs-only fixes. Both reviewers CLEAR at the final head `22aee8cf`.
- The documented v5/v6 compile error was reproduced byte for byte by the steward and by both reviewers.
- **Proof level:** source and CI only (Go, TypeScript and Python suites, contract tests, the rubric, the doc gates). No lab, live or customer-workload proof of v6 itself is claimed.

### Known follow-ups (other repos, not in this release)
- AppTheory adopts `tabletheory/v6`.
- Autheory migrates its `*tabletheory.LambdaDB` typing.
- theory-mcp-server and TCA repin later.
- `docs/migration/v4.md` and `v5.md` keep an older changelog-step pattern; this was recorded out of scope.

signed (SSH/ED25519) commits throughout.

## Summary

Creating an SSH host via `POST /host/db/host` without `authType` returned HTTP 500 "Failed to save SSH data": the route passed `authType: undefined` straight to the insert, which violates `NOT NULL ssh_data.auth_type`. Real case: the Termix CLI `hosts create --credential-id 2 ...` without `--auth-type`.

Changes (create route):
- When the body names no `authType`/`authMethod`, infer it the way the UI sends hosts: `credentialId` ⇒ `credential`, `key` ⇒ `key`, `password` ⇒ `password`.
- Host defaults still apply as before: a body that leaves auth out inherits `core.auth` from the user/folder/server defaults, so such a create keeps succeeding.
- If nothing (body, inference, defaults) supplies an auth type, answer 400 `authType is required (password, key, credential, agent or none)` instead of letting the DB constraint throw.

Create and update: a non-string `authType`/`authMethod` (e.g. an object) is now a 400 instead of a 500 from the driver. Unknown string values are still accepted on purpose, since plugin auth types may be saved while their plugin is disabled and fail at connect with a message naming the plugin.

Update was checked separately: leaving `authType` out keeps the stored value (the column is not written), so it never hit the constraint.

## Test plan
- [x] New `host-create-auth-type.test.ts` drives the real host router against in-memory SQLite: credentialId-only and password-only creates succeed with the inferred type; an auth-less create returns 400; an auth-less create inherits `core.auth` from user defaults; an update without authType keeps the stored type; an update with a non-string authType returns 400. The create/update failure cases returned 500 before the fix.
- [x] Unit test for `impliedSshAuthType`

author: evanpelle
body:
## Description:

`kickClient()` returned early when the target's persistentID was already banned, and `Roster.kick()` only dropped the one clientID it was handed. Those assumptions break after a duplicate-session replacement (prod only): the evicted record stays in `clients.all()` with the same persistentID and publicId as the session that replaced it. Kicking that stale record — e.g. an admin kick by `targetPublicID`, which resolves to the first matching record — banned the account but left the live session connected, and every later kick of the live session then logged "already kicked" and did nothing.

Fix:

- `Roster.kick()` drops every connected client holding the persistentID and returns them.
- `kickClient()` no longer short-circuits on an already-banned persistentID; it tells and closes each dropped session. The "already kicked" / "not found" warnings remain for when nothing was connected.

## Tests

- `GameServerJoin.test.ts`: after a duplicate replacement, kicking the evicted record by clientID, and an admin kick by publicId, both close the live session and leave the account unable to rejoin. Both fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- `Roster.test.ts`: `kick()` drops the replacement session when called on the left record.
- `npx vitest run tests/server` (978 passing), lint, typecheck.

body:
**Package:** WP06 (lane C, free-canvas gestures)

**Closes:** plan 311 items N1 and N2 (from the M8 round 2 re-verify).

## What changed

`shells/web/src/views/free-canvas/pinch.ts`, with three new fields on `PinchGesture` in `free-canvas/shared.ts`:

- **N1: the lift commits what was shown.** Before this change, a lift while the preview was still easing in first jumped the preview to the full transform and committed that. So fingers that stopped soon after the scale engaged committed a size the preview never reached: 202 px shown, 230 px committed in one probe case. `endPinch` now commits the frame on screen. That frame includes the lift's own point, because `onGestureEnd` applies the pending move first.
- **N2: late travel eases in.** If the travel engaged after the preview began, the midpoint's whole travel showed in one frame. That was a 7 px jump when a spread engaged it, and up to a finger's drag threshold (10 px) when the travel engaged by itself. Now a scale or a travel that engages after the preview began follows the fingers from the frame it engages on. What the fingers did before that frame ("owed", taken at the last frame) is made up over the next 14 px of finger travel. A scale and the travel it starts owe from the same frame and ease the same way, so the content under a still finger stays under it.
- **What is still owed is capped at the part's change now** (review fix, `shownPinch`). Without the cap, fingers that went just past engagement and came back to where they began left the preview, and the commit, smaller than at rest or nudged the other way, with an undo step that main never wrote. Now the factor stops at 1 and each axis of the travel stops at 0, so the preview comes back with the fingers and never passes where it began. The travel a late scale starts takes the scale's cap too, so a still finger keeps the content under it.
- Parts that had already engaged when the preview began ease in as before. A late twist is also unchanged: it counts from where it engaged, so it owes nothing. `gestures.ts` is not touched.

One choice in the cap, for review: the reviewer suggested one cap factor for the scale and its travel. I used the scale's cap for both, plus a per-axis cap on the travel alone, rather than the smallest cap across every part. With a symmetric spread, the travel owed is only finger jitter. A smallest-cap rule would let one axis of jitter cancel the scale's ease, which would bring back the jump N2 removes. With one finger still and no jitter, the caps are equal, so the still finger keeps its content either way. A jsdom probe with 0.3 px of vertical jitter on every move keeps the largest one-frame step of the left edge within twice what following the fingers exactly gives.

## Behaviour changes to existing tests

- `a quick pinch lifted just past the tap's slop ...` (`free-canvas-two-finger.test.ts`) pinned the old lift, which committed the whole spread (60 to 90 px, 1.5 times) while the preview showed under 220 px. That conflicts with N1, so the test now asserts that the commit equals the frame on screen, which is under 220 px. The trade-off: a very quick pinch that lifts the moment it leaves the tap's hold-back now keeps the small growth it showed. Before, it committed the whole spread. If you want the earlier behaviour for quick pinches, that needs a separate decision, for example a short catch-up the user can see before the commit.
- `tests/design-transform-zones.browser.test.ts`, the Scale-mode text pinch (review fix). It was the same quick pinch: fingers 60 px apart, 15 px out each in 1.5 px steps, so the preview began at the last step and the lift followed straight away. Under the new lift it committed what was shown (fontSize 42.1, not 60). Its fingers now start 120 px apart and move 30 px each, as the box pinch earlier in that test does. The spread still goes 1.5 times, so the expected fontSize stays 60. The fingers leave the tap's 14 px at the fifth step and the preview has caught up by the lift. The box pinch and the twist are unchanged.

## Tests

The scratchpad probes `m8r2-verify/pinch-{wysiwyg,jump}-probe` are now tests in `shells/web/src/views/free-canvas-two-finger.test.ts`:
- `fingers that stop soon after the scale engages: the lift commits exactly the size and place the preview showed`: the probe's 4 cases.
- `a scale that engages after the preview began brings its travel in with it: ...`: the probe's 3 cases. Each checks that the still finger's content drifts by no more than 1 px of rounding (it was 7 px), that no frame moves the box more than twice as fast as following the fingers would, and that 30 px on, the box is exactly under the fingers.
- `a travel that engages after the preview began eases in rather than jumping by a finger's drag threshold`: the travel engages by itself here.
- `fingers that go just past where the scale or the travel engages and come back to where they began commit nothing` (review fix): held past the tap's window, then fingers 100 px apart and 40 px apart spread 7 px each until the scale engages, and both fingers walk right 11 px until the travel engages. Then they come back to the start and lift. Each case checks that the preview moved, that no frame on the way back puts the box below or past where it began, that the preview ends where it began, and that the lift writes nothing and leaves the row unchanged.

Probe readings, before and after:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| One finger out 15 px, shown vs committed width | 202 vs 230 | 206 vs 206 |
| One finger out 20 px | 217 vs 240 | 225 vs 225 |
| Both fingers out 10 px | 209 vs 240 | 221 vs 221 |
| Both fingers out 15 px | 234 vs 260 | 250 vs 250 |
| Largest one-frame shift of the left edge, 100 px apart | 7 px | 1 px |
| Largest one-frame shift of the left edge, 40 px apart | 7 px | 4 px (2 px per frame is exact following there) |
| Drift of the content under the still finger | 7.25 px | 0.5 px (rounding to whole px) |

Spread just past engagement, then back to the start (committed row and writes):

| Case | main | first push of this PR | Now |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100 px apart, both fingers out 7 px and back | 100,100,200,200, 0 writes | 106,106,188,188, 1 write | 100,100,200,200, 0 writes |
| 40 px apart, both fingers out 7 px and back | 100,100,200,200, 0 writes | 115,115,170,170, 1 write | 100,100,200,200, 0 writes |
| Both fingers right 11 px and back | 100,100,200,200, 0 writes | 98,100,200,200, 1 write | 100,100,200,200, 0 writes |

The browser file's pinches, replayed through the real `initFreeCanvas` in jsdom with the browser helper's timing (second finger 40 ms after the first, 10 moves 16 ms apart, lift straight after, 1 screen px per native px):

| Pinch | Committed |
